Leaves erect to spreading, somewhat crispate above when dry, erect-spreading when wet, ovate-lanceolate, inserted in a straight line, 2–3 mm long, plane to somewhat plicate, erect-clasping at base, acuminate, ending in short hyaline hair-points, weakly auriculate, shortly decurrent; margins plane or narrowly recurved below, serrulate below, papillose-crenulate above; costae single, ending above midleaf, in cross section cells homogeneous; upper and median cells densely seriately pluripapillose, over cell walls, long-hexagonal to linear, thick-walled, porose, 30–40 # 4–5 µm; extreme basal cells elongate, porose, smooth; alar cells weakly developed, quadrate to rectangular, lightly papillose, thick-walled, porose. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown from Central America.

Protologue: Colombia. In devexis udis frigidis, montis Quindiu, super granato, altitudine 1400 hexapod. Humboldt et Bonpland.

Plants medium-sized to robust-sized, in dense or loose, yellowish‑green to gray-green, shiny tufts, to 5 cm high. Stems red, erect, hyalodermis and central strand well-developed, lightly tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth. Spores oblong to subreniform, 25–30 μm, coarsely papillose, red-brown.

Breutelia auriculata Bartr., Bryologist 49: 115. 1946.

Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. San Marcos: Finca El Porvenir along Río Chopal, south facing slopes of Volcán Tajumulco, alt. 1300–1500 m., Steyermark 37462 (F, FH).

Plants robust, in loose, glossy, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 12 cm high. Stems red,  hyalodermis and central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 3–4 mm long, moderately to well-spaced, erect-spreading to spreading, weakly flexuose when dry, erect or erect-spreading when wet, straight, oblong-lanceolate, not plicate at base; apices gradually acuminate; margins plane, minutely serrulate, long-decurrent, decurrent cells lax and enlarged; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; leaf cells with straight walls and papillae at upper ends, upper cells rectangular to long-rectangular, firm‑walled, 20–53 x 5–7.5 μm, all basal cells lax and inflated, 71 x 23 μm. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Setae flexuose, 12–14 mm long. Capsules inclined, 2.5–3 mm long, globose to subglobose, furrowed when dry, striate when wet; exothecial cells thin-walled; stomata numerous at base; opercula plano-convex; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, finely papillose below, coarsely papillose near tips, dorsal trabeculae faint, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened, endostome segments broad, yellowish, papillose, segments split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia. Spores reniform, 25 μm, coarsely papillose, red-brown.

Bryum billarderi Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 1(2): 115. 1816.

Bryum sartorii Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 200. 1872. Protologue: Mexico. Mirador, Liebmann in herb. Schimp.

Plants minute, yellow-green, gregarious or in loose tufts. Dioicous. Setae 10–30 mm long, red. Capsules 1.5–2.0 mm long, red, claviform to elongate-pyriform, constricted at neck, erect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth reddish brown, thickly papillose, endostome yellowish, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary to absent, cilia rudimentary to absent. Plants medium-sized, in dense or loose, glossy, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 5 cm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, hyalodermis and central strand present, moderately tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth or roughened. Leaves 3–4 mm long, closely spaced, erect-appressed with spreading leaf tips from an erect, plicate, clasping base with 0–3 pairs of sulci at junction of sheath and limb, obovate-lanceolate; apices long, slenderly acuminate, apices not twisted when dry; margins plane or narrowly revolute, sharply singly or doubly serrate above; costae slender, shortly excurrent; cells weakly papillose at lower ends, or from both ends, upper cells short- to long-rectangular, thick-walled, straight (occasionally somewhat porose), 17–37 x 5 μm, basal cells narrower and elongate, to 92 μm long, thick-walled, smooth or porose, alar region with 1–2 rows of enlarged, firm-walled, subrectangular to quadrate cells, extending 5–6 cells up the basal margin. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 12–20 mm long, arcuate, capsules horizontal to pendulous, furrowed when mature and dry, ovoid to ovoid-cylindric, 3–5 mm long x 1.5–2 mm wide, exostome teeth granulose below, vertically striolate above, 450–500 μm long, endostome segments nearly equaling the teeth, keeled from a moderately high basal membrane, smooth below, papillose above, cleft into 2 forks, cilia 0–3, rudimentary. Spores reniform, coarsely papillose-areolate, 20–23 μm in diameter” (Griffin 1988).

Breutelia subarcuata (C. Müll.) Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 204. 1872. Bartramia subarcuata C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 617. 1851. Protologue. Mexico. Pico de Orizaba, alt. 11000 ped.: Liebmann.

Plants robust, in loose or dense, somewhat glossy, yellowish‑green to brownish yellow tufts, to 11 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis and central strand present, moderately to densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose. Leaves 3–5 x 1.2–1.9 mm, closely spaced, secund to subfalcate, rugose, at times twisted when dry, erect-spreading to secund when wet, curved-falcate, ovate to broadly lanceolate, strongly plicate at base, not decurrent; apices slenderly acuminate; margins recurved below, plane above midleaf, serrulate; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; leaf cells porose or smooth-walled, papillose at lower ends above, from either end below, upper cells linear-elongate, thick‑walled, 17–75 x 5–7.5 μm, basal cells linear-elongate, 37–88 x 5 μm, thick-walled, alar region with 4–9 rows of enlarged, firm-walled or inflated cells at basal angles, often extending up the basal margins, intra-alar cells hyaline or orange, straight-walled, length to width ratio 1–2:1. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 4–9 mm long, arcuate, capsules subglobose, 3–3.5 mm long x 2.5 mm wide, irregularly rugulose to nearly smooth when dry, peristome inserted below the mouth, exostome teeth lanceolate, reddish orange, 480–520 μm long, granulose-papillose, endostome pale yellow, nearly equally the exostome, faintly papillose, spores subreniform, areolate-tuberculate, 30–33 μm long x 24–27 μm wide” (Griffin 1984).

Fissidens ornatus Herzog, Arch. Bot. São Paulo 1: 57. 1925. Type. Brazil, Hoehne 410 (JE).

Plants to 2.5–9 mm × to 1.5–2.5 mm. Leaves 1–2 mm × ca. 0.2–0.4 mm; apex acute; margins more or less entire to serrate; vaginant laminae more or less 1/2 leaf length, minor laminae ending on costa or intermediate between costa and margin; costa short to long excurrent; cells 18–40 µm long, marginal 2–3 rows 7–14 µm long, smooth to more or less bulging, cells guttulate, oblong to hexagonal, irregularly so at margins. Sporophytes terminal.

Fissidens polypodioides Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 154. 1801. Type. Jamaica, Swartz (S).

Plants to 8 cm × ca. 9 mm. Sporophytes terminal on short axillary branches.

Plants to 7.5 mm × to 2.5 mm. Leaves to 1.5 mm × 0.2–0.35 mm; apex bluntly acute to obtuse; margins crenulate, elimbate; vaginant laminae more or less unequal, acute, ca. 1/2 the leaf length; costa ending 4–12 cells below the apex; cells 7–8 µm, smooth, appearing bulging but convex-thickened, rounded-hexagonal. Sporophytes terminal, peristome reduced.

Fissidens scariosus Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 599. 1869. Type. Peru, Spruce 537 (NY).

Plants to 6 mm × ca. 3 mm. Leaves ca. 2.6 mm × ca. 0.4 mm; apex acute to sharply acute; margins entire; limbidia poorly defined; vaginant laminae unequal, acute, more or less 1/2 the leaf length; costa ending well below the apex; cells ca. 125 µm × 20 µm, smooth, fusiform, prosenchymatous. Sporophytes terminal.

Plants medium-sized, shiny, pale green to yellowish green, in loose or dense mats, occasionally pendent. Stems creeping, to shortly ascending, 2–5 cm long, sparsely and irregularly branched, hya-line to pale green when young, red when old, epidermal cells broadly rectangular, densely or laxly complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with outer cells somewhat smaller than the inner cortical cells, otherwise cells undifferentiated, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs fragile, 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell elon-gate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Tristichium mirabile (C. Müll.) Herz., Flora 107: 324. 1914. Tristichiopsis mirabile C. Müll., Linnaea 43: 394. 1882. Type. Argentina, Cuesta de Pinos, Lorentz.

Plants scattered, green to yellow-green, terricolous; stems 10–15 mm long, simple or irregularly branched. Leaves 0.8–1.2 mm long, keeled, narrowly lanceolate, gradually tapered from base; apex bluntly acute; margins erect, entire; cells linear, 37 µm × 5 µm, incrassate, smooth. Gonioautoicous. Setae to 4 mm long, brownish yellow, smooth; capsules inclined, ovoid, 1 mm long; annuli revoluble; opercula short-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; stomata absent. Spores spherical, 20–25 µm, lightly papillose, brown.

Plants medium-sized, in yellow green or reddish yellow mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly
branched; leaves well spaced, reduced, ovate, abruptly acuminate, erect below, squarrose-recurved
above, 0.5–0.6 mm long; cells pluripapillose; rhizoids red brown, in sparse clusters at abaxial side of
leaf insertions, not or rarely branched. Secondary stems horizontal and often transformed to stolons
at the tips or erect and loosely spreading, 3–5 cm long, irregularly branched, branches often transformed
to stolons at the tips; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, red brown, thickwalled
cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia
absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent. Secondary stem and branch leaves erect-imbricate when
dry, wide-spreading when wet, oblong-ovate, obscurely plicate, 1.5–2 mm long, shortly acuminate,
shortly decurrent; margins plane above, narrowly recurved in lower 1/2 or less, apices sparsely serrulate
to erose; costa absent; upper cells quadrate to short-rectangular, 10–14 μm, thick-walled, weakly sinuose,
pluripapillose; basal median cells long-rectangular, to 70 x 4 μm, thick-walled, porose, pluripapillose;
alar cells short-rectangular, quadrate, or oblate, 6–12 μm long, thick-walled, smooth. Autoicous.
Perichaetial leaves erect, elongate. Setae elongate, yellow, becoming red to orange with age, 7–20 mm
long. Capsules erect, cylindrical to elliptic, 2 mm long, wrinkled to irregularly furrowed when dry,
light brown, narrowed at the mouth, at times strongly constricted at neck; exothecial cells small, red,
thick-walled in 10–15 rows below the mouth, becoming lax, irregularly quadrate to short-rectangular
below, neck cells small, irregularly subquadrate to short-rectangular; stomata in neck; opercula
obliquely conic-rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, cells often clinging to capsule mouth or
operculum; peristome absent. Spores irregularly subspherical to oblong, papillose, 18–26 μm. Calyptrae
cucullate, smooth, 3.5–4.5 mm long.

Brachymenium columbicum (De Not.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 557. 1903.

Osculatia columbica De Not., Mem. Reale Accad. Sci. Torino ser. 2, 18: 445. 1859. Protologue: Ecuador (see Steere 1988). Ad flumen Napo in Columbiae meridionalis regionibus, Osculati.

Brachymenium globosum Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 112. 1875. Based on Bryum globosum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 289. 1869, non Lindb., 1866. Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, in sylva Canelos loco Pueblo de Los Jibaros (300 ped.), Spruce, n. 312.

Neobryum costatum Williams, Bryologist 28: 59. 1925. Protologue: Columbia. On log at La Cumbre, Department of El Valle, Columbia, 1800–2100 meters. E. P. Killip, May, 1922, 5556, 5932.

Brachymenium viviparum Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 77. 1928, hom. illeg. non Card., 1915. Brachymenium bulbiferum Bartr., J. Wash. Acad. Sci. 24: 472. 1934, nom. nov. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, Los Ayotes, near Tilaran, Province of Guanacaste, altitude 600–700 meters, Paul C. Standley and Juvenal Valerio, January 21, 1926, no. 45502 (FH, MICH, US).

Brachymenium svihlae Bartr., Bryologist 54: 235. 1951. Protologue: Costa Rica. Prov. Heredia: finca Isla Bonita near Vara Blanca, cloud forest, Atlantic slope, elev. about 5500 ft., Ruth D. Svihla 3056, Dec. 2–3, 1947 (FH), syn. nov.

Acidodontium grubbii Bartr., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 33: 6. 1964 [1965]. Protologue: Ecuador. On tree trunk, submontaine [sic] forest on ridge 1 mile N.E. of Borja, 5600 ft., [Grubb] 2859. 

Plants medium-sized, bright green to yellowish green above, reddish at base, in loose or dense tufts. Stems 10–40 mm long, epidermal cells quadrate, sparsely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves equally foliate, widely spaced, 2–3 mm long, appressed-flexuose and somewhat contorted when dry, occasionally lax and strongly contorted, erect-spreading when wet, concave, ovate, ovate-lanceolate, lanceolate, or elongate-triangular; apices acuminate, cuspidate; margins not or weakly bordered by 1-2 rows of rectangular cells, entire below, entire to slightly crenulate above, plane above, slightly reflexed below; costa strong, reddish, stoutly excurrent, filling the cusp, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; leaf cells thin- or firm-walled throughout, sometimes porose, upper cells broadly hexagonal to rhomboidal, 20–40 x 14 μm, basal cells rectangular to subquadrate, 20–50 x 20 μm. Asexual reproduction by bulbous axillary gemmae. Dioicous. Setae 25–35 mm long, red. Capsules 2–3 mm long, globose, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, yellow-brown, densely papillose, closely spaced and often united at base, endostome yellowish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments and cilia highly modified: cilia 2, fully united, on either side of which are fused  portions of segments, the entire structure opposite the exostome teeth. Spores 16–22 μm, spherical to oblong, lightly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Brachymenium morasicum Besch., Bull. Herb. Boissier 2: 392. 1894.

Protologue: Colombia. Auf Bäumen in schattigen Wäldern an den oberen Gehängen der Paramo de Moras. 3000 m. Cauca. 3 März 1883. [Lehmann] 2653. 

Plants small, bright-green to yellowish green, shiny, in dense tufts or mats. Stems 5-15 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 1.2–2.8 mm long, erect-appressed to imbricate not spirally twisted, erect-spreading when wet, concave, ovate, oblong to oblong-lingulate; apices short acuminate, ending in a smooth or toothed capillary hair-point, yellowish at base, hyaline in upper ½, 0.4–1.0 mm long; margins bordered at midleaf by 2–3 rows of narrow, elongate, thick-walled cells, upper marginal cells elongate, strongly toothed to denticulate or serrulate near the apex, narrowly recurved below; costa long-excurrent in upper leaves; upper cells firm-walled, hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, 40–70 x 10–14 μm, basal cells lax and bulging, oblate, quadrate to short-rectangular, 16–30 x 20–22 μm. Dioicous. Setae 7–15 mm long, red. Capsules 3–5 mm long, narrowly cylindrical, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic-apiculate; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth reddish yellow, densely papillose, endostome yellowish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores 14-22 μm, papillose.

Brachymenium niveum Besch., J. Bot. (Morot) 15: 383. 1901.

Protologue: Mexico. San Luis Potosí, Alrededores, déc. 1886, s. non. leg. 7668. 

Plants small, yellowish green to whitish, in dense tufts or mats. Stems to 10 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded, evenly foliate, 1.2–1.8 mm long (including hair-point), erect-appressed to imbricate, not spirally twisted, erect-spreading when wet, concave, triangular, ovate or ovate-lanceolate; apices short acuminate, ending in a smooth or toothed, hyaline capillary hair-point, 0.4–1 mm long; margins obscurely bordered below by 1-2 rows of narrower, elongate cells, upper marginal cells hyaline, rectangular to narrowly elongate often forming a distinct border, margins strongly toothed just below the apex to denticulate or serrulate, plane above, narrowly recurved below; costa stoutly long-excurrent, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled above, thin-walled and bulging below, cells at base of hair-point elongate to linear, thick-walled, hyaline, upper and median cells hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, 30–50 x 20 μm, basal cells oblate, quadrate to short-rectangular near the basal margin, 16–30 x 20–24 μm. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen.

Macromitrium aureum C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 15: 580. 1857.

Protologue: Colombia. Nova Granada, Cerro Pelado, Schlim 1852 legit. Collect. Linden, sine No. cum Zygogonte commixtum [NY].

Plants medium to large-sized, reddish yellow to yellowish green. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 5 cm long. Leaves erect at base, strongly keeled above, undulate, flexuose to spirally twisted above when dry, abruptly recurved when wet, 3–5 mm long, linear‑lanceolate; apices acuminate; upper margins evenly serrate or dentate, reflexed below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae subpercurrent to percurrent; upper cells 20–25 μm long, incrassate, not porose, rhombic, in longitudinal rows, strongly bulging to mammillose, basal cells long-rectangular, incrassate, porose, strongly tuberculate. Setae 10–15 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1–2 mm long, ovoid to cylindrical, furrowed; operculum not seen; exostome teeth united forming a short membrane, reddish‑orange, densely papillose, endostome segments to 280 μm long, hyaline, papillose. Spores anisosporous, 12–16 μm, hyaline, lightly papillose and 26–34 μm, yellow‑red, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 3–4 mm long.

Macromitrium carionis C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 199. 1897.

Protologue: Guatemala. Cuesta de Lovio, Aug. 1870 [Bernoulli & Cario] N° 48. (lectotypified by Goffinet 1993).

            Macromitrium altituberculosum Bartr. ex Grout, Bryologist 47: 17. 1944. Protologue: Guatemala, Sierra de las Miñas: Dept. Zacapa: oak-pine woods along the upper reaches of Rio Sitio Nuevo, between Santa Rosalia and first waterfall, alt. 1200–1500 m., on rock, Jan. 9, 1942, Julian A. Steyermark, 42274 (F, FH, NY, US).

Plants small to medium-sized, dark-green to olive‑green. Stems weakly creeping, branches 7–10 mm long, densely reddish tomentose below. Leaves plicate, erect‑appressed, weakly spirally contorted above when dry, spreading when wet, to 2 mm long, lingulate; apices rounded to obtuse, emarginate to short‑mucronate; margins crenulate above, plane or erect, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion present; costae shortly excurrent or percurrent; upper cells 6–8 μm, rounded-hexagonal, strongly bulging to mammillose, basal cells strongly tuberculate, long-rectangular, incrassate and porose, 16 μm long. Setae 3–9 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1.5–2.0 mm long, ovoid to cylindrical, plicate; opercula conic‑rostrate, 1–1.2 mm long; exostome teeth lanceolate, not fused into a membrane, papillose‑striate, 312 μm long, endostome basal membrane 117 μm high, segments 60 μm high. Spores anisosporous, to 20 μm, smooth and to 40 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 3–3.5 mm long.

Macromitrium cirrosum (Hedw.) Brid., Bryol. Univ. 1: 316. 1826.

Anictangium cirrosum Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 42. 1801. Protologue: Jamaica, Montserrat. Lectotype (Florschütz 1964): Swartz s.n., Jamaica (NY).

Macromitrium stenophyllum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 215. 1869. Protologue: Jamaica. Ins. Jamaica, Wilson, n. 607, in Herb. Hooker; etiam ex India occidentali, an Jamaica?, Herb. R. Brown. 

Macromitrium barbense Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 31(1): 157. 1893. Protologue: Costa Rica.  Forêts du Barba, mélangé à l’espéce suivante Pittier n° 5541 (NY).

Macromitrium werckleanum Thér., Recueil Publ. Soc. Havraise Études Diverses 88(4): 307. 1921. Protologue: Costa Rica. La Palma, près San José, alt. 1.500 m. C. Wercklé, avril 1910 (FH).

Macromitrium mammillosum Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 87. 1928. Protologue: Costa Rica. In tree, Cerros de Zurqui, northeast of San Isidro, Province of Heredia, Costa Rica, altitude 2,000 to 2,400 meters, Paul C. Standley and Juvenal Valerio, March 3, 1926, no. 50384 (FH, NY, US).

Macromitrium costaricense Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 88. 1928. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, La Palma, Province of San Jose, Costa Rica, Paul C. Standley, March 17, 1924, no. 38023 (FH, NY, US). 

Plants medium-sized, greenish yellow to reddish yellow 2–5 cm high. Primary stems moderately to strongly creeping, branches 2–5 cm long. Leaves keeled, erect at base, flexuose and commonly spirally twisted above when dry, abruptly recurved from a clasping base when wet, often in spiral rows, 2–4 mm long, lanceolate to oblong‑lanceolate; apices acute to shortly acuminate; upper margins serrate or dentate, at times with a weak limbidium, reflexed below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent but frequently the basal marginal cells enlarged, swollen and hyaline; costae red, shortly excurrent, occasionally percurrent; upper cells 6–12 μm long, somewhat longer than broad, incrassate, not porose, quadrate to rounded, frequently in distinct longitudinal rows, smooth to bulging or stoutly mammillose, basal cells linear, incrassate, porose, strongly or weakly tuberculate. Setae 5–10(–15) mm long, smooth. Capsules 1–2 mm long, cupulate to hemispheric, smooth, or weakly furrowed at neck; opercula shortly rostrate, 0.9–1 mm; exostome teeth united forming a short membrane, 120–152 μm long, yellow, strongly papillose, endostome segments 16, 216–240 μm long, hyaline, papillose. Spores anisosporous, 14–18 μm and 24–30 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 3 mm long.

Brachymenium radiculosum (Schwaegr.) Hampe, Vidensk. Meddel. Dansk Naturhist. Foren. Kjøbenhavn ser. 3, 9: 275. 1870.

Peromnion radiculosum Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 3(1): 250. 1828. Protologue: Brazil. Ad truncos arborum in silvis Brasiliae, Novi Friburgi lectum dedit Beyrich.

Plants medium-sized, bright-green to yellowish green above, reddish at base, in dense, shiny tufts. Stems to 15 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 2–4.5 mm long, erect-flexuose, spirally contorted when dry, spreading when wet, concave, obovate-oblong to spathulate; apices short-acuminate, ending in a smooth or toothed, reddish yellow hair-point; margins bordered below by 2–4 rows of linear, thick-walled cells, entire below, serrulate to denticulate above, plane above, narrowly revolute below; costa reddish, stoutly long-excurrent; cells firm-walled throughout, porose, upper cells rhomboidal, 30–60 x 20 μm, basal cells often reddish near leaf insertion, long-rectangular, 70–130 x 20 μm. Dioicous. Setae 15–20 mm long, red. Capsules 2–4 mm long, oblong-clavate, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic-apiculate; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth linear, whitish, densely papillose, endostome whitish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments well-developed, linear, with narrow perforation gaps, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores 22–30 μm, spherical, lightly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Brachymenium standleyi Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 77. 1928.

Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, La Ventolera, on the southern slope of the Volcan de Poas, altitude about 1,700 meters, Paul C. Standley, February 17 and 18, 1924, no. 34655 (FH, US).

Plants medium-sized, yellowish green above, reddish at base, in dense, shiny tufts. Stems 10–13 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 2–4 mm long, erect-flexuose, spirally contorted when dry, spreading when wet, concave, lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate, or spathulate; apices short acuminate, ending in a smooth or toothed, reddish yellow hair-point; margins bordered below by 2–4 rows of linear, thick-walled cells, entire below, remotely denticulate above, plane above, narrowly revolute below; costa reddish, stoutly long-excurrent, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled throughout, upper cells rhomboidal-hexagonal, 30–60 x 18–20 μm, basal cells often reddish near leaf insertion, short-rectangular, 30–40 x 12 μm. Dioicous. Setae 20–25 mm long, yellowish red. Capsules 3–4 mm long, oblong-clavate, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth linear, reddish below, whitish above, papillose, endostome reddish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores extremely variable in size and shape; 20–80 μm, spherical, ovoid, oblong, lightly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants medium-sized, in yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched; leaves
reduced, well spaced, ovate, abruptly long-acuminate, erect below, squarrose-recurved above, 0.6–0.8
mm long; cells pluripapillose; rhizoids red brown, in sparse clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions,
not or rarely branched. Secondary stems horizontal and often with lateral stolons, or erect and loosely
spreading, 3–5 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small,
red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central
strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent. Secondary stem and branch leaves erectimbricate
when dry, wide-spreading when wet, oblong-ovate, plicate, 2 mm long, shortly acuminate,
shortly decurrent; margins narrowly recurved, often to near the apex, apices sparsely serrulate to erose;
costa absent; upper cells subquadrate, short-rectangular to rectangular, 8–17 μm long, thick-walled,
strongly sinuose, pluripapillose; basal median cells long-rectangular, 100 x 4 μm, thick-walled, porose,
pluripapillose; alar cells short-rectangular, quadrate, or oblate, 6–12 μm long, thick-walled, smooth.
Paroicous. Perichaetial leaves erect, elongate. Setae elongate, yellow, becoming red to orange with
age, 7–20 mm long. Capsules erect, cylindrical to elliptic, 2 mm long, wrinkled to irregularly furrowed
when dry, light brown, narrowed at the mouth, at times strongly constricted at neck; exothecial
cells small, red, thick-walled in 10–15 rows below the mouth, becoming lax, irregularly quadrate to
short-rectangular below, neck cells small, irregularly subquadrate to short-rectangular; stomata in
neck; opercula obliquely conic-rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, cells often clinging to capsule
mouth or operculum; peristome absent. Spores irregularly subspherical to oblong, papillose,
18–26 μm. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth or sparsely hairy, 3.5–4.5 mm long.

Zygodon gracillimus Broth. ex Fleisch., Musci Buitenzorg 2: 392. 1904.

Protologue: Indonesia. An Bäumen. West-Java: bei Kandang‑Badak (2500 m.), am Gedeh entdeckt von (Wichura), (F [leischer].).

Zygodon inconspicuus Herz., Beih. Bot. Centralbl. 26(2): 67. 1909 [1910]. Protologue: Bolivia: An faulem Holz im Bergurwald bei Incacorral (Prov. Cochabamba), ca. 2200 m; Januar. 08 [Herzog].

Zygodon subminutus Broth. ex Dix., New Zealand Inst. Bull. 3: 167. 1926. Protologue: New Zealand. Thames, Auckland, July, 1896; leg D. Petrie, det. Brotherus, No. 731. Comm. D. Petrie.

Plants very slender, in dense cushions, greenish yellow above. Stems erect 1–3(–10) mm high, sparsely tomentose. Leaves erect to erect‑patent when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 0.6–1.6 mm long, lanceolate; apices acute; margins entire to weakly crenulate, plane above, recurved on one or both sides at base; costae stout, subpercurrent, ending 4–10 cells below the apex, cells on upper dorsal surface elongate; upper cells 8–12 μm, rounded or irregularly rhombic to short rectangular, incrassate, smooth, basal cells near costa 18–30 μm long, enlarged, thinner‑walled, bulging, oblong, smooth. Brood bodies not seen. Dioicous. Setae 4–6 mm long, smooth, yellow when young, becoming red‑brown with age. Capsules 1.0–1.3 mm long, obovoid to oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry, constricted at neck; opercula obliquely conic‑rostrate, to 0.5 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth16 united into 8 teeth‑pairs, red, becoming white with age, densely papillose to horizontally striate below, papillose above in vertical lines, reflexed to recurved when dry, 75–120 μm high, endostome _ to ¾ the length of the exostome teeth, white, basal membrane short, cilia absent, segments stout, vertically striate‑papillose, erect when dry. Spores isosporous, 10–16 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 0.8–1.0 mm long.

Zygodon pungens C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 20: 361. 1862.

Codonoblepharum pungens (C. Müll.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 119. 1874. Protologue: Venezuela. In cortice arborum: Moritz.

Zygodon tuerkheimii Broth. in Malta, Latv. Univ. Bot. Darza Darbi 1: 150. 1926, nom. nud. Based on Guatemala: Coban, in arb. 1310 m und Cubilgüitz (?), in arb. 350 m (Türckheim) [NY].

Plants slender, sparsely clustered or scattered, greenish yellow above. Stems erect to 1–3 mm high, sparsely tomentose. Leaves erect‑patent when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 0.6–1.6 mm long, lanceolate; apices acute; margins entire, plane; costae stout, excurrent, with elongate cells on upper dorsal surface; upper cells 8–12 μm, rounded to irregularly rhombic, occasionally oblate, incrassate, smooth, basal cells near costa 18–36 (–60) μm long, enlarged, thin‑walled, bulging, oblong, smooth. Brood bodies not seen. Autoicous. Setae 1.5–3.0 long, smooth, yellow when young, becoming red‑brown with age. Capsules 0.8–1.0 mm long, obovoid to oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry, constricted at neck; opercula obliquely conic‑rostrate, 0.5–0.7 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth16 united into 8 teeth‑pairs, red but becoming white with age, densely papillose to horizontally striate below, papillose above in vertical lines, reflexed to recurved when dry to 140–200 μm, endostome _ to ¾ the length of the exostome teeth, red, basal membrane short, cilia absent, segments stout, papillose or vertically striate‑papillose, erect when dry. Spores isosporous, 14–20 μm, smooth. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 1.0–1.5 mm long.

Weisiopsis oblonga Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 5: 95. 1932 [1933].

Protologue: Mexico. Nepantla, sur la terre (St.-P. [Marius Saint-Pierre] n° 1830). 

Plants small, light-green, 1–2 mm high. Stems evenly foliate, not branched, sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids sparse, red or hyaline, smooth. Leaves 1.0–1.5 mm long, erect at base, tubulose, incurved when dry, spreading when wet, long-lingulate to spathulate, concave; apices rounded to obtuse, narrowly but deeply grooved along the costa; margins unistratose, plane or incurved, entire to minutely crenulate by projecting cell walls, not bordered; costa subpercurrent, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band present, surface cells elongate, ventral surface layer of enlarged, hyaline cells; upper cells rounded-hexagonal to quadrate, 5–9 x 4–10 μm, mammillose-bulging on upper surface, plane to weakly convex, smooth on dorsal surface, basal cells abruptly enlarged, hyaline, 30–50 x 14–20 μm, rectangular, with thin, bulging walls. Autoicous. Perichaetial terminal. Setae 3–6 mm long, yellow. Capsules 0.6–1.2 mm long, ellipsoid to cylindric, smooth, yellow-brown, red at capsule mouth; stomata in neck; opercula 0.3–0.4 mm long, conic-rostrate; annuli of 2–3 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome of 16 red, spiculose, well-spaced, long-linear teeth, inserted within the mouth, to 450 μm long, erect, to slightly twisted, basal membrane absent. Spores 8–10 μm, smooth to lightly roughened. Calyptrae 1.0–1.5 mm long.

Brachymenium systylium (C. Müll.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 117. 1875.

Bryum systylium C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 320. 1848. Protologue: Mexico. Prope Xalapam, Deppe & Schiede.

Brachymenium brachypelma C. Müll. ex Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Beligique 31(1): 162. 1893. Protologue: Costa Rica. Chemin de la Piedra Blanca, Pittier 5562; Forêts du Barba, Pittier 5563.

Brachymenium condensatum Williams, Bryologist 26: 2. 1923. Protologue: Mexico. Michoacan, Patzcuaro, Dec. 21, 1891, Pringle 762 (MO).

Plants small, bright-green to yellowish green, in dense, shiny tufts or mats. Stems 5-30 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose, at times with red-brown, multicellular, globose propagula. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 1.2–2.5 mm long, erect-appressed to imbricate not or rarely somewhat spirally twisted, spreading when wet, concave, ovate, oval, oblong to oblong-lanceolate; apices short acuminate, ending in a smooth or toothed capillary hair-point, yellowish at base, hyaline in upper ½, 0.4–1.0 mm μm long; margins not or weakly bordered below by 1-2 rows of somewhat narrower, elongate cells, upper marginal cells short-rectangular to somewhat elongate, entire or weakly serrulate, plane above, narrowly recurved below; costa ending below the apex in lower leaves, stoutly long-excurrent in upper leaves, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled throughout, upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, 30–60 x 12 μm, basal cells often reddish near leaf insertion, quadrate to short-rectangular in up to 20 cells along the basal margin, 20–30 x 20 μm. Dioicous. Setae 15–25 mm long, yellowish red. Capsules 2.5–4.0 mm long, obovate-oblong, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic-apiculate; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth reddish yellow, densely papillose, endostome yellowish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores 18–24 μm, papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants medium-sized, in green, yellow green, or yellow brown, dense or lax mats. Primary stems creeping, at times stoloniferous, stolons with reduced leaves; rhizoids dark brown, becoming black-ish, smooth, not branched, from circular clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions. Secondary stems erect, irregularly pinnately branched, not stipitate, 4–10 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, thick-walled, central strand small; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Secondary stem and branch leaves differing in size and auricle development, erect to spreading, crispate above when dry, wide-spreading when wet, elongate-triangular to ovate-lanceolate, to 4 mm long, plicate, undulate to crispate above, erect at base, long-acuminate, distinctly auriculate at base, shortly decur-rent; margins plane, sharply serrate throughout; costae single, ending near the apex, in cross section with guide cells and single layer of dorsal and ventral stereid cells; upper and median cells with 1–2 papillae over the lumina, fusiform to elongate, thick-walled, usually porose, 18–40 # 4 µm, upper marginal cells longer, smooth, in 2–3 rows, forming a more or less distinct border; extreme basal cells elongate-rectangular, porose, smooth, 24–50 # 2–4 µm; alar cells weakly developed, irregularly quadrate to rectangular, smooth, thick-walled, porose. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown from Central America.

Bartramia potosica Mont. var. potosica, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot. sér. 2, 9: 56. 1838.

Protologue: Bolivia. Hab. in eisdem locis cum Orthotricho psychrophilo à cl. d’Orbigny lecta.

Plants medium-sized, in dense or occasionally loose, dull, green to glaucous-green tufts, to 5 cm high. Stems red, erect, hyalodermis and central strand present, tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth to roughened. Leaves 4–7.5 mm long, erect appressed or erect-spreading to weakly flexuose, sheathing at base, leaf limb fragile, often broken near midleaf, 3–6 mm long, sheathing base 1.0–1.5 mm long, not plicate; apices subulate to long, slenderly acuminate; limb margins unistratose, multistratose elsewhere, plane below, plane to narrowly recurved above, serrulate; costa excurrent, sharply toothed to spinose at back and above; limb cells mammillose, quadrate to short-rectangular, 15–25 x 5 μm, marginal cells at leaf shoulder fragile, hyaline, thin-walled, subquadrate to rhomboidal, interior cells at leaf shoulders firm-walled, not fragile, sheathing base cells linear, thin-walled, lax and bulging below, firm-walled above, not porose, 75–175 x 10 μm, alar cells reddish yellow, rectangular to subquadrate, thin-walled, bulging. Dioicous. Perigonial and perichaetial leaves 2–4 x as long as the vegetative leaves. Sporophytes not known in Central America. “Setae arcuate, yellowish brown to reddish brown, 3.2–5.8 mm long. Capsules yellowish brown to reddish brown, 1.8–3.0 mm long, globose to slightly oblong, irregular; exothecial cells moderately thick-walled; exostome teeth finely papillose below on outer surface, coarsely striate aboveendostome 0.5–0.9 the length of the exostome. Spores 29–41 μm, coarsely papillose, dark brown” (Fransén 1995).

Macromitrium fragilicuspis Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 109. 1909.

Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Vera Cruz: prés de Jalapa, 1908 n. Pringle 15168 (NY). 

Plants small to medium-sized, greenish brown to greenish yellow. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 2.5 cm long, moderately tomentose below. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, spirally twisted around stems to flexuose‑incurved above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 1.7–2.3 mm long (to 3.0 mm long with intact leaf tips), 0.5 mm wide, lanceolate; apices abruptly rounded to long (1 mm), fragile, multistratose subulae; margins entire to obscurely crenulate by bulging cell walls, recurved below, plane to weakly recurved above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion present; costae percurrent; upper interior cells 4–6 μm, quadrate, at times weakly rounded, smooth to weakly bulging, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 16–26 μm long, rectangular, incrassate and porose, tuberculate. Setae 5–6 mm long, smooth. Capsules to 2 mm long, cylindric‑ovoid, furrowed; annulus and mature operculum not seen; exostome teeth 16, short, truncate and united forming a papillose, reddish orange membrane, endostome hyaline, weakly papillose. Spores anisosporous, 17–20 μm and 32–40 μm. Calyptrae mitrate, strongly laciniate, naked, 3 mm long.

Macromitrium fulgescens Bartr. in Grout, Bryologist 47: 12. 1944.

New name for M. fuscescens Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 89. 1928, non Schwaegrichen, 1827. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, La Palma, Province of San Jose, Costa Rica, altitude about 1,800 meters, Paul C. Standley, March 17, 1924. no. 38011 (FH, NY, US).

Plants medium to robust-sized, reddish to yellowish brown. Stems moderately creeping, branches to 6 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves keeled, undulate, erect at base, crisped and contorted above when dry, erect‑flexuose when wet, 7–10 x 0.5 mm, linear‑lanceolate; apices long‑filiform acuminate; margins sinuate‑denticulate below, sharply denticulate above, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent; upper interior cells elliptic to isodiametric or rounded‑quadrate, 8–18 x 8 μm, smooth to somewhat bulging, in distinct longitudinal rows, upper marginal cells elongate, forming a distinct border, basal cells 40–48 μm long, narrowly rectangular, incrassate and porose, not tuberculate. Sporophyte unknown.

Macromitrium guatemalense C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 644. 1851.

Protologue: Guatemala, vulgatissimum et mensi Martii 1848. fruct. maturis et supramaturis: Friedrichsthal ? Ex horto dom. Van Houtte copiosissime communicavit Kegel, nuc hortulanus bot. Halensis (FH).

Macromitrium serrulatum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 215. 1869. Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, Jameson; in monte Tunguragua (7000 ped.), Spruce, n. 97.

Macromitrium tortuosum Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 189. 1872. Protologue: Mexico. Mejico, San Miguel ( Liebmann in herb. Mus. Par.); Orizaba (F. Müller).

Macromitrium verrucosum Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 82. 1928. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, oak forest near Quebradillas, about 7 km north of Santa Maria de Dota, Province of San Jose, Costa Rica, altitude about 1,800 meters, Paul C. Standley, December 24, 1925, no. 43023 (FH, NY, US).

Plants medium-sized, greenish yellow to reddish yellow. Stems moderately creeping, branches 1–2 cm long, weakly tomentose below. Leaves keeled, erect below, crisped, contorted and undulate above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 2–3 x 0.5–0.7 mm, oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate; apices acute; margins undulate above, sharply and regularly serrulate to serrate, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion present; costae ending below the apex; upper interior cells 5–7 μm, rounded‑quadrate, mammillose, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells long‑rectangular to 30 μm long, linear‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, strongly  tuberculate. Setae 4–10 (–15) mm long, smooth. Capsules 2–2.5 mm long, cylindrical, furrowed; opercula rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth 200–240 μm high, yellowish brown, densely papillose, united forming an erect, truncate membrane, endostome hyaline, papillose, basal membrane 200–280 μm high, segments rudimentary or absent. Spores anisosporous 12–14 μm, smooth, hyaline and 20–30 μm, papillose, yellow‑brown. Calyptrae mitrate, lacinate, naked or with a few hairs, 4 mm long.

Bryoerythrophyllum ferruginascens (Stirt.) Giac., Atti Ist. Bot. Univ. Lab. Critt. Pavia V, 4: 210. 1947. Barbula ferruginascens Stirt., Ann. Scot. Nat. Hist. 9: 176. 1900. Protologue: Great Britain. On the ground, Orkney, 1887, s. coll.

 

Leptodontium arsenei Thér., Smithsonian Misc. Collect. 85(4): 10. 1931. Protologue: Mexico. Morelia: Cerro San Miguel ([Arsène] 5073).

Barbula saint-pierrei Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 5: 97. 1932 [1933]. Protologue: Mexico. Cuautzin, montagne au sud de Mexico, 3200 m., c.fr. (M. Saint-Pierre, n° 1879, type).

 

Plants small, reddish brown to reddish yellow, 10–15 mm high. Stems red, erect, not or irregularly branched, sclerodermis present, central strand well-developed; rhizoids irregularly scattered, red, smooth. Leaves 1.5–2 mm long, erect to erect-incurved when dry, wide-spreading to squarrose from an erect, clasping base when wet, ovate-lanceolate, broadly concave above; apices broadly acuminate or acute, rounded or apiculate; margins unistratose, recurved in lower 3/4, plane to erect near apex, entire, not bordered, decurrent; costa thickened above, percurrent to stoutly short-excurrent, papillose at back, ventral superficial cells short-rectangular, guide cells and two stereid bands present, ventral and dorsal epidermal layers enlarged; upper cells at times bistratose near the costa, 6–12 x 6–8 μm, firm-walled, oblate, quadrate, or short-rectangular, pluripapillose with thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells 12–35 x 6–10 μm, long-rectangular, smooth, firm-walled, alar cells not differentiated. Obovoid propagula at times on rhizoids. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen in Central America. “Setae 7–8 mm; capsules 2.2–2.5 mm long, ellipsoidal; annuli of 1–2 rows of vesiculose cells, revoluble and fragmenting; operculum 0.5–0.9 mm long, short- to long-conic, with cells in straight rows; peristome none or rudimentary, the teeth only 25 μm long, erect, subulate, pale-yellow, spiculose, without a basal membrane. Spores 12–15 μm, weakly papillose” (Zander 1994a).

Ochrobryum gardneri (C. Mull.) Mitt. J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 108. 1869. Leucophanes gardneri C. Mull., bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 2: 741. 1844.

Plants 3–13(–20) mm high. Leaves 2–5 mm long, 0.3–0.8 mm, closely and densely erect-patent or somewhat spreading, narrowly ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, shortly acuminate, bluntly acute or rounded obtuse, at times cucullate, frequently apiculate; margins erect; costa with a single dorsal and a single ventral leucocyst layer throughout most of the leaf, apical ventral leucocysts multi-layered; leaf lamina narrow, of 2–4 rows of long-rectangular, variously porose cells at midleaf and 4–6 rows of rectangular, firm-walled cells at base. Asexual reproduction by brown, multicellular, globose propagula clustered on short stalks on the upper dorsal leaf surface. Setae smooth, 1.0–1.5 mm long; capsules immersed to emergent, 0.5–1.0 mm long; opercula 1.5 mm long. Calyptrae 4–5 mm long, ciliate or laciniate at base. Spores spherical, smooth or lightly roughened, 12–18 µm.

Macromitrium longifolium (Hook.) Brid., Bryol. Univ. 1: 309. 1826.

Orthotrichum longifolium Hook., Musci Exot. 1: 44. 1818. Protologue: Venezuela. Ad radices Bifariae glaucae altitudine 950 hexapod, regione temperata, in devexis montis Avilae prope Caraccas. Humboldt et Bonpland.

Macromitrium homalocron C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier. 5: 197. 1897. Protologue: Guatemala. Coban, 4300 ped. alt., Jan. 1886: H. v. Türckheim in Hb. Brotheri, 1891 (NY).

Macromitrium haitense Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 14: 15. 1944. Protologue: Haiti. Haïti: Massif de la Hotte, western group, Les Roseaux, pineland, on stones, 2.400 m. [Ekman]  n° 10.645 (FH, US).

Macromitrium perundulatum Bartr., Fieldiana, Bot. 25: 219. 1949. nom. nud. Based on: Guatemala, Quezaltenango: Volcán Santo Tomas, Steyermark 34880 (F, FH).

Plants robust, yellow‑green to reddish brown. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 6 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, flexuose to spirally contorted and frequently undulate above when dry, erect at base, flexuose spreading above when wet, 3–5 x 0.7 mm, narrowly lanceolate; apices slenderly acuminate; margins undulate, serrate to serrulate, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae percurrent; upper interior cells 7–15(–25) x 7–12 μm, rounded hexagonal to rhombic, occasionally porose, smooth, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 40–60 μm long, long‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, strongly tuberculate. Setae 5–12 mm long, papillose, frequently with a whitish collar representing the torn upper portion of the vaginula just below the capsule base. Capsules 1.5–2 mm long, oblong, furrowed; opercula rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth truncate, to 300 μm high, yellow‑brown, papillose, united and forming an erect membrane, endostome hyaline, lightly papillose, basal membrane short, 50–75 μm high, segments stout, to 150 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 17–25 μm, smooth, hyaline and 25–40 μm, papillose, yellow‑brown. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked or sparsely to densely hairy by stout, ascending hairs, 3.5 mm long.

Macromitrium oblongum (Tayl.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 211. 1869.

Schlotheimia oblongum Tayl., London. J. Bot. 5: 46. 1846. Protologue:  Ecuador. n. 322. Andes of Quito, Prof. William Jameson, 1845.

Plants medium to large-sized, yellowish to brownish green. Stems weakly creeping, branches 2–3 cm long, weakly tomentose below. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, flexuose to spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, erect‑patent when wet, 4–6 x 0.5–1.0 mm, lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins undulate, crenulate to serrulate, occasionally distantly and irregularly serrate to dentate near apex, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion present; costae percurrent; upper interior cells 6–10 μm, strongly thickened, isodiametric to quadrate, smooth to weakly bulging, upper marginal cells not forming a border, basal cells 30–50 long, narrowly rectangular, incrassate and porose, strongly tuberculate. Setae 10–15 mm long, smooth. Capsules 2–2.5 mm long, cylindric, furrowed; operculum not seen; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, 280–300 μm high, yellow‑orange, striate‑papillose, united forming an erect membrane, with age splitting into 8–16 teeth, recurved when dry, endostome hyaline, densely papillose, basal membrane 120 μm high, segments 120–150 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 14–20 μm, hyaline, smooth and 26–40 μm, yellow, densely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 4–5 mm long.

Plants medium-sized to large, 5–15 cm long, in usually flattened, pale green to yellowish green masses. Primary stems (stolons) creeping; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, not or irregularly branched, densely present on stolons and on secondary stems and branches when in contact with substrate; leaves erect, obovate to ovate-triangular, evenly foliate, 1–1.5 mm long. Secondary stems erect, hor-izontal or pendent, not stipitate, irregularly branched, complanate-foliate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–4 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, thick- to firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia present or absent, uniseriate, less than 0.5 mm long; pseudoparaphylliafoliose. Secondary stems and branches complanate-foliate; leaves erect-spreading, occasionally spreading, undulate, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 2.0–3.5 mm long, symmet-ric or asymmetric, acute, short-decurrent and subauriculate or rounded to the insertion; margins subentire to serrulate, broadly inflexed on one side below, plane or sometimes narrowly recurved on other side; costae faint, short and double with one fork usually longer than the other; cells smooth, apical cells rhomboidal or long fusiform, 26–42 # 4–6 µm, firm- to thick-walled; basal cells linear-fusiform, 50–80 # 4–8 µm, thick-walled, often porose; alar cells reddish yellow, of 6–10 subquadrate to subrectangular cells, cells across the insertions yellow. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves oblong-lanceolate, 2–3 mm long; costae short and double or absent. Setae 2–3 mm, smooth, yellow to yellow red. Plants medium-sized to robust, 3–10 cm high, stipitate-frondose, flattened, forming pale green or yellowish green, lax tufts. Stolons creeping; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, densely present on stolons and at the base of stipitate stems; leaves appressed, widely spaced, evenly foliate, triangular-lanceolate. Secondary stems erect, stipitate, irregularly bi- or tripinnate, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudopa-raphyllianarrowly foliose to filamentous. Stipe leaves erect-spreading from an appressed base, evenly foliate, triangular to oblong-triangular, 1.5–2.0 mm long, broadly acuminate; margins entire to suben-tire below, serrate above; costae single, ending above midleaf. Asexual reproduction by microphyllous branches. Dioicous. Sporophyte unknown in the Neotropics, description from Ninh (1984) and Enroth (1989). Perichaetia to 2 mm long; leaves ovate at base, ligulate to long lanceolate and spreading above, dentate at apex. Setae 1.5–4.5 mm long, smooth throughout or smooth below and mammillose above. Capsules ovoid-cylindrical, 1.5–3.0 mm long; exothecial cells near mouth subquadrate, thick-walled, short-rectangular, thick-walled below; stomata on neck; opercula conic, obliquely short-rostrate; annuli weakly differentiated; pe

Plants medium-sized to robust, 2–8 cm high, stipitate-frondose, flattened, forming pale green or yellowish green, lax tufts. Stolons creeping; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, densely present on stolons and at the base of stipitate stems; leaves appressed, widely spaced, evenly foliate, triangular-lanceolate. Secondary stems erect, stipitate, irregularly bi- or tripinnate, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudopa-raphyllia narrowly foliose to filamentous. Stipe leaves erect-appressed when dry, somewhat spread-ing from an appressed base when wet, evenly foliate, triangular to oblong-triangular, 1.0–1.5 mm long, acuminate to broadly acuminate; margins plane, entire to lightly serrulate; costae single or dou-ble, ending above midleaf. Stem leaves 1.0–1.5 mm long, branch leaves 0.5–1.0 mm long, both strongly flattened, spreading to wide-spreading, more or less plicate when dry, smooth when wet, oblong-ovate, asymmetric, short-acute to short-acuminate, narrowly decurrent, straight at the insertion; margins sub-entire, serrulate, or serrate, inflexed on one side below, otherwise plane; costae often spurred below, strong throughout, reaching 1/2–2/3 the leaf length; cells smooth, apical cells oval, rounded-rhomboid, or elliptic, 6–14 µm long, firm- to thick-walled, not porose, median cells long-oval to long-rhomboidal, 12–18 µm long, firm-walled, not porose; basal cells and median cells near the costa long-rectangular, 24–30 µm long, thick-walled, often porose; alar cells rectangular to oblong-rectangular, weakly dif-ferentiated, cells across the insertions porose. Asexual propagula not seen.

Pohlia chilensis (Mont.) Shaw, Mem. New York Bot. Garden 45: 684. 1987.

Plants slender to robust, shiny, yellow-green to brownish when dry, in loose tufts. Stems 3–6 mm, red, simple; rhizoids at base, reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Leaves crowded above, 0.5–1.0 mm long, erect to imbricate, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acute; margins narrowly and tightly recurved below, serrulate above; costae yellow throughout, ending below the apex to percurrent; upper cells narrowly rhomboidal, thin-walled, 60–100 x 6–10 μm, marginal cells longer and narrower, basal cells rectangular to subquadrate, narrowly rectangular to rhomboidal. Capsules erect to inclined, 2–3 mm long, cylindric, tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with straight walls; stomata superficial; opercula conic, apiculate, 0.5 mm long; annuli of 2–3 rows of cells exostome teeth yellow to light brown, narrowly triangular, densely papillose above, endostome hyaline, basal membrane _ the exostome length, segments keeled, not or narrowly perforate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Plants small, shiny, yellow-green to brownish when dry, in loose tufts. Stems 5–9 mm high, red, branched by subfloral innovations or forked; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose-roughened.
