Protologue: Costa Rica. Forêts du Barba, brins en mélange avec Leptodontium subgracile (Pitt. no 5557). – Bolivia. Bolivie: Sorata, 13,000 pieds (Rusby no 3137, a domina Britton benevole communicata).

Plants medium to large-sized, in dense or loose, glossy, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 10 cm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, hyalodermis and central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth or roughened. Leaves 3–5 mm long, well-spaced or occasionally closely spaced, wide-spreading to squarrose or deflexed from an erect, clasping, plicate base with to 3 pairs of sulci at junction of the sheath and limb, obovate-lanceolate; apices long, slenderly acuminate, apices not twisted when dry; margins plane or narrowly revolute, serrulate or serrate to sharply serrate above; costae short- or long-excurrent, scabrous at back; leaf cells papillose at lower ends, or from both ends, upper cells short- to long-rectangular  firm- and straight‑walled or porose, 12–50 x 3–8 μm, basal cells narrower and elongate, 25–75 x 5 μm, thin- or thick-walled, smooth or porose, alar region with 2–4 enlarged cells along the basal margin and 0–1(-2) marginal rows of enlarged rectangular cells, otherwise undifferentiated. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 0.5–2 cm long, faintly arcuate, capsules inclined to horizontal, furrowed when mature and dry, ovoid, 3–4 mm long x 1.5 mm wide, exostome teeth faintly papillose below, more coarsely papillose above, 375–825 μm long, endostome segments nearly equaling the teeth, yellowish, keeled, split above into 2–4 forks, coarsely papillose except at extreme base, cilia 2–3, rudimentary. Spores reniform, papillose areolate, 23–35 μm in diameter” (Griffin 1988).

Breutelia chrysea (C. Müll.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873-74: 98. 1875. Bartramia chrysea C. Müll., Linnaea 38: 598. 1874. Protologue: Colombia. Nova Granata, prov. Antioquia, Paramo de Sonson, 10-12,000 pedes alta: G. Wallis 1872.

Plants moderate to robust-sized, in dense, somewhat glossy, yellowish‑green or brownish green tufts to 13 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis and central strand present, moderately to densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose. Leaves 3–5 x 0.8–1.3 mm, ovate-lanceolate, closely spaced, erect-spreading to secund when wet, loosely appressed, erect-spreading, wide-spreading or subfalcate above when dry, base plicate, spreading or erect; apices slenderly acuminate, at times twisted when dry; margins recurved above midleaf, serrulate; costae shortly excurrent; leaf cells porose or smooth-walled, papillose at lower ends above, from either end below, upper cells linear-elongate, thick‑walled, 17–55 x 3–7 μm, basal cells linear-elongate, 40–84 x 3–5 μm, thick-walled, alar region with 4–9 rows of enlarged, firm-walled or inflated cells at basal angles, often extending up the basal margins, intra-alar cells enlarged, hyaline or orange, straight-walled. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 10–14 mm long, somewhat curved above, capsules subglobose, 3.5–4 mm long x 2.5–3 mm wide, longitudinally furrowed when dry, peristome inserted below the mouth, teeth lanceolate, reddish orange, 550–575 μm long, papillose, endostome pale yellow, nearly equally the exostome, faintly granulose to smooth, spores subreniform, areolate-tuberculate, 24–27 μm long x 18–22 μm wide” (Griffin 1984).

Macromitrium parvirete Bartr. in Grout, Bryologist: 47: 16. 1944.

Protologue: Costa Rica: Entre Rio Jesus y Calera de San Ramon, A. M. Brenes 17075 (F, FH, NY).

Plants small to medium-sized, greenish yellow. Stems moderately creeping to 2 cm, branches 5–10 mm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves moderately keeled, erect below, flexuose, crispate and undulate above when dry, erect‑spreading to spreading‑recurved when wet, 2–3 x 0.8 mm, oblong‑lanceolate to lingulate; apices obtuse, mucronate; margins undulate, crenulate, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent, 60–80 μm from apex; upper interior cells 6–8 μm, strongly rounded, hexagonal to rounded‑quadrate, bulging mammillose, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 60–80 μm long, long‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, tuberculate. Setae 5–12 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1–2 mm long, cupulate, smooth above, furrowed at neck; opercula erect‑rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth short, truncate, 80–140 μm high, yellow‑brown, papillose, united forming an erect membrane, endostome absent or present as a rudimentary membrane at base of exostome. Spores anisosporous, 14–18 μm, smooth, hyaline and 20–36 μm, papillose, yellowish brown. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 2–3 mm long.

Macromitrium richardii Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 2(2)1: 70. 1826.

Protologue: French Guiana (?). In arboribus Guianae lectum ded. beatus Claud. Richardus. Florschütz (1964, p. 234) considered the origin of the type material uncertain.

Macromitrium didymodon Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond. Suppl. 2(2)2: 138. 1827. Protologue: Brazil. Legit ad vicum Novo Friburgo Brasiliae capsulis maturis mense Decembri dilig. Beyrich.

Macromitrium rhabdocarpum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 199. 1869. Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, Antombos, Spruce.

            Plants small-sized, yellowish green above, brown below. Stems strongly creeping, branches 5–8 mm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves moderately keeled, erect below, crisped and inrolled above when dry, erect‑patent when wet, 1.5–2 x 0.3–0.5 mm, lanceolate to lingulate‑lanceolate; apices acute to obtuse or apiculate; margins crenulate, plane or reflexed below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae subpercurrent to percurrent; upper interior cells rounded hexagonal to rounded quadrate, 7–12 μm, pluripapillose by 2–3 low papillae in upper ½ to _, bulging mammillose below, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 15–30 μm long, rectangular, firm‑walled, weakly porose, not tuberculate. Autoicous. Setae 7–12 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1.5–2 mm long, obovoid, furrowed, puckered at mouth; opercula erect‑rostrate, 0.7–1 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome rudimentary, teeth lanceolate‑truncate, 120 μm high, hyaline, papillose, endostome absent. Spores isosporous, 22–30 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, laciniate, naked to sparsely hairy, 2–3 mm long.

Schizymenium gracilisetum (Hampe) Shaw, Bryologist 88: 29. 1985.

Leptoclaena graciliseta Hampe, Linnaea 32: 130. 1863. Mielichhoferia graciliseta (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 324. 1869.  Protologue: Colombia. Bogota, La Penna, 2800 metr. Julio, Lindig 2014. 

Plants slender to medium-sized, shiny, yellow-green to brownish when dry, in loose tufts. Stems to 10 mm high, red, simple or forked; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Lower leaves reduced, distant, erect-spreading, upper leaves crowded,  0.8–1.3 mm long, erect to imbricate, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane, serrulate to serrate above; costae ending near apex; upper cells narrowly linear-rhomboidal to linear-vermicular, thin- but firm-walled, 80–110 x 6–8 μm, marginal cells narrower, sometimes shorter, basal cells rhomboidal, rectangular or sub-quadrate. Paroicous. Setae 15–20 mm long, yellow to yellowish orange, flexuose. Capsules inclined, 2–3 mm long, oblong-cylindric to pyriform, tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with wavy walls; stomata superficial; opercula conic, apiculate, 0.5 mm long; annuli well-developed, of 2–3 rows of cells; peristome double, exostome narrowly triangular, 160–200 μm long, _ to ¾ as long as the endostome, yellow, smooth, endostome smooth below, papillose above, yellowish, basal membrane low, segments filiform, perforate, not keeled, cilia absent. Spores 14–18 μm, lightly papillose.

Schizymenium lindigii (Hampe) Shaw, Bryologist 88: 29. 1985. 

Mielichhoferia lindigii Hampe, Linnaea 31: 520. 1862. Protologue: Colombia. Bogota, Cipacon, 2600 metr., aug. 1861, et Rio Arzobispo 2800 metr., in umbrosis, mense junio leg. A. Lindig. 

Plants slender to medium-sized, shiny, yellow-green to brownish when dry, in loose tufts. Stems to 12 mm high, red, simple or forked; rhizoids, reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Lower leaves reduced, distant, erect-spreading, upper leaves crowded, 1.7–1.9 mm long, erect-spreading, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane, serrate above; costae ending below the apex; upper cells narrowly linear-rhomboidal to linear-vermicular, firm-walled, 100–140 x 6–8 μm, marginal cells narrower, basal cells rhomboidal to rectangular. Paroicous. Setae 15 mm long, reddish orange, flexuose. Capsules 2–4 mm long, oblong-cylindric tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with straight to wavy walls; stomata not seen; operculum not seen; annulus not seen; exostome absent, endostome hyaline to yellowish, basal membrane smooth, 40–60 μm above capsule mouth, segments filiform, papillose, cilia absent. Spores 14–16 μm, lightly papillose.

Plants medium-sized, in dull, yellowish green, thick, dense mats. Primary stems creeping; leaves
reduced, 0.6–0.7 mm long, ovate-triangular to triangular, long hair-pointed; cells pluripapillose; rhizoids
red brown, in clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or weakly and irregularly branched.
Secondary stems crowded, erect-ascending, 0.5–2 cm long, densely branched; cross section with
sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm- or thick-walled,
central strand well developed; paraphyllia and pseudoparaphyllia absent. Secondary stem and branch
leaves erect-imbricate when dry, erect when wet, ovate-lanceolate, to 1.3 mm long, acuminate, hyaline
hair-pointed, long-decurrent; margins broadly revolute above to near the apex, plane or revolute
at base, papillose-crenulate, denticulate at the base of the decurrencies; costae single, ending below
the apex, yellow, wavy, channeled on ventral surface, dorsal surface with elongate, seriate-papillose
cells, in cross section cells homogeneous, thick-walled; upper cells hexagonal, oblong, rhomboidal to
elongate, 10-24 x 3-4  μm, densely pluripapillose, papillae thick and branched, cells of the hair-point
smooth; basal cells along the margins and in the alar regions oblate to quadrate, 8–10 μm, densely
pluripapillose, inner basal cells near the costa elongate, thick-walled, often porose, to 40 μm long, basal
decurrency cells quadrate, weakly papillose. Dioicous. Perigonia and perichaetia gemmate, lateral on
secondary stems. Setae elongate, dark red, flexuose, 7–12 mm long. Capsules erect, oval-cylindrical
to elliptic, 1.0–1.5 mm long, smooth, light brown; exothecial cells small, oblate, thick-walled in 1–2
rows below the mouth, short-rectangular below; stomata at base of capsules; opercula obliquely
conic-rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, cells often clinging to capsule mouth or operculum;
exostome white when dry, narrowly triangular, dorsal (outer) surface horizontally papillose-striate in
lower half, papillose above, ventral (inner) trabeculae projecting; endostome papillose, to 3/4 the exostome
length, segments narrow, rudimentary, basal membranes low, cilia absent. Spores spherical,
smooth to lightly roughened, 10–15 μm. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2 mm long.

Breutelia inclinata (Hampe & Lor.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 93. 1875. Bartramia inclinata Hampe & Lor., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 27: 435. 1869. Protologue: Ecuador, in planitie summa Cordillerarum, 14,200' [H. Krause].

Breutelia deflexifolia Card., Rev. Bryol. 37: 4. 1910. Protologue: Mexico. District fédéral: vallée de mexico, 1907 (Pringle, n. 10429) [FH, MO, US]. Etat de Puebla: mt. Malintzi (A. Hecquet, 1904; herb I. Thériot).

Plants robust,  in loose, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 6–11 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis weakly developed, central strand present, spasely branched, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 5–7 mm long, closely spaced, spreading, deflexed or squarrose when dry, erect-spreading to spreading when wet,  lanceolate-acuminate from an ovate, erect, sheathing, smooth or plicate base; margins plane or weakly revolute above, broadly revolute at shoulders, singly or rarely doubly serrulate; costae excurrent and sharply toothed; leaf cells papillose at either end, upper cells rectangular to long-rectangular, firm‑walled, not porose, 17–38 x 4–5 μm, basal cells long-rectangular to sublinear, 25–108 x 5 μm, alar cells large, rectangular, thin-walled, hyaline in 5 or more rows that extend well up the basal margins. Dioicous. Setae 2 per perichaetium, straight, 6–7 mm long. Capsules pendent, 2 mm long, subglobose, rugose; opercula plano-convex, 0.5 mm long; peristome not seen. Spores not seen.

Breutelia jamaicensis (Mitt.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873-74: 96. 1875. Bartramia jamaicensis Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 265. 1869. Philonotis jamaicensis (Mitt.) Card., Rev. Bryol. 38: 102. 1911. Protologue: Jamaica. Ins. Jamaica, Wilson n. 815, Wilds, M’Fadyen, etiam ex Herb. Brown.

Breutelia sartorii Besch. in Fourn., Mexic. Pl. 1: 29. 1872. Protologue: Mexico. Mirador (Sartorius in herb. Schimper).

Philonotis schlumbergeri Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 203. 1872. Breutelia schlumbergeri (Schimp.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 656. 1904. Protologue: Mexico. Orizaba, F. Müller.

Philonotis haitensis Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 29(1): 177. 1890. Protologue: Haiti. Haïti, Port-au-Prince, Bertrand.

Plants small to medium-sized, in dense or loose, glossy, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 4 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis weakly developed, central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 2–3 mm long, moderately to well-spaced, appressed to erect or erect-spreading when dry, erect or erect-spreading when wet, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, straight or sometimes falcate, variably plicate at base; apices long, slenderly acuminate; margins plane or narrowly revolute, singly serrate; costae long-excurrent and sharply toothed or percurrent; cells papillose at upper ends, upper cells long-rectangular to sublinear, firm‑walled, 25–63 x 2.5–3.5 μm, basal cells quadrate to sub-rectangular, 10–40 x 10–15 μm, alar cells quadrate in 5 or more rows. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Setae straight or flexuose, 20–30 mm long. Capsules inclined to pendent, 2–3 mm long, ovoid to subglobose, furrowed when dry, striate when wet; exothecial cells thin-walled; stomata numerous at base; opercula plano-convex; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, finely papillose below, coarsely papillose near tips, to 500 μm high, dorsal trabeculae faint, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened, endostome nearly as long as the exostome, segments broad, yellowish, finely papillose, papillae in vertical rows, segments split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia, cilia 2–3, well-developed. Spores reniform, 17–23 μm, coarsely papillose, red-brown.

Macromitrium scoparium Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 206. 1869.

Protologue: Ins. Jamaica, Wilds; Trinidad, Crüger.

Macromitrium tonduzii Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 31(1): 155. 1892. Protologue: Costa Rica. Forêt du Rancho Florés, Pittiér n° 5545 (NY, US), syn. nov.

Macromitrium palmense Williams in Britt. & Williams, Torreya 4: 25. 1914. Protologue: Costa Rica. La Palma, Costa Rica, 480, Maxon, May 6, 1906 (F, FH, NY), syn. nov.

Macromitrium williamsii Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 84. 1928. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, La Hondura, Province of San Jose, Costa Rica, altitude 1,300 to 1,700 meters, Paul C. Standley, March 24, 1924, no. 36405 (FH, NY, US).

Plants medium-sized, reddish yellow to yellowish green. Stems moderately creeping, branches to 5 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, crispate, tightly spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, erect‑patent to spreading when wet, 4–6 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, lanceolate; apices acuminate to subulate; margins undulate, sharply serrate in upper half, recurved below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent into a sharp, serrate point; upper interior cells extremely variable in size and shape, (8–)15–36 x 10 μm, incrassate, variably porose, oval to rhomboidal, smooth to somewhat bulging, upper marginal cells linear, forming a more or less differentiated border, basal cells to 52 μm long, narrowly rectangular, incrassate and porose, smooth or sparsely to moderately tuberculate. Setae (7–)10–20 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1.5–2.5 mm long, subglobose, smooth, wrinkled at neck; opercula erect‑rostrate, 1–2 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth lanceolate, to 300 μm high, red, densely papillose, united forming an erect membrane, endostome firm, red, strongly papillose, basal membrane 100 μm high, segments stout, 200 μm high. Spores weakly anisosporous, 18–26 μm, smooth and 28–40 μm, lightly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, laciniate, naked, 3–4 mm long.

Husnotiella revoluta Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 71. 1909. 

Didymodon revolutus (Card.) Williams, Bryologist 16: 25. 1922. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Mexico: Lecheria, murs, 1908 ([Pringle] n. 10523); Amecameca, 1908 ([Pringle] n. 10610). Etat de Morelos: près de Cuernavaca, murs, 1908 ([Pringle] no. 10531, 10636 [MO]). Etat de Hidalgo: Tula, murs en terre, 1908 ([Pringle] n. 15214). Etat de Jalisco: Guadalajara, murs, 1908 ([Pringle] n. 10574, in parte, 15231 in parte, 15233). 

Plants small, dull, green to yellow-green above, brown below, in tufts,  5–10 mm high. Stems greenish yellow to yellow above, reddish yellow below, erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis of somewhat enlarged, thin-walled cells, central strand present; rhizoids sparse, at base of stems or scattered throughout. Axillary hairs 4–7 cells long, basal cell brown. Leaves 0.8–1.2 mm long, lingulate to elliptic or ovate, erect, imbricate-incurved when dry, wide-spreading when wet, broadly channeled on ventral surface; apices rounded-obtuse to cucullate; lamina unistratose or with bistratose areas along the margins; margins entire, recurved to revolute to near the apex; costa subpercurrent, broad, spurred above midleaf, upper surface ventral cells of costa quadrate, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band present, ventral surface cell layer of enlarged, bulging, papillose cells; upper and basal cells differentiated, upper cells rounded-quadrate to rhomboidal or oblate, 4–12 x 6–10 μm, firm-walled, with 1–2(–3) large papillae, interior basal cells short-rectangular, firm-walled, smooth, 10–20 x 6–8 μm, basal marginal cells quadrate to oblate, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal, perigonia gemmiform. Setae smooth, 4–8 mm long, red. Capsules elliptic to cylindrical, erect, 1 mm long, smooth; exothecial cells rectangular, firm-walled; stomata in neck; opercula erect, obliquely short-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli vesiculose; peristome absent to rudimentary, yellow to red-orange, basal membrane absent, teeth erect, papillose. Spores 8–11 μm, smooth. Calyptrae cucullate, 2 mm long.

Philonotis cernua (Wils.) Griffin & Buck, Bryologist 92: 376. 1989.

Gyphocarpa cernua Wils., J. Bot. (Hooker) 3: 383. 1841. Bartramidula cernua (Wils.) Lindb., Öfvers. Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 20: 389. 1863. Glyphocarpus cernuus Wils. ex Par., Index Bryol. 512. 1896. Protologue: Ireland and Wales. On Connor Hill in Ireland in the year 1829, and subsequently at Curn Bychan, near Harlech [Wales], by the Rev. Mr. Salwey, 38 .

Bartramidula wilsonii Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G., Bryol. Eur. 4: 57. 1846. Bartramia wilsonii (Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 479. 1848. Philonotis wilsonii (Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 7: 153. 1863. Glyphocarpus wilsonii (Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 59. 1875.  Protologue: Britain and Ireland. In montosis Britanniae et Irlandiae. Ad Cannor Hill Irlandiae, prope Corn Bychon Valesiae, in Alpibus scoticis ad Glen-Dole in Clova mountains copiose.

Bartramia patula Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 255. 1869. Glyphocarpus patulus (Mitt.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 60. 1875. Bartramidula patula (Mitt.) Par., Index. Bryol. 116. 1894. Philonotis patula (Mitt.) Griffin & Buck, Bryologist 92: 376. 1989. Protologue: Guatemala. Guatemala, Volcan de Agua (7000–12,000 ped.), inter caespites Tortulae aeneae, Godman et Salvin (FH).

Bartramidula mexicana Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 202. 1872. Glyphocarpus mexicanus (Schimp. ex Besch.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 60. 1875. Bartramia mexicana (Schimp. ex Besch.) C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 335. [1900] 1901. Philonotis mexicana (Schimp. ex Besch.) Griffin & Buck, Bryologist 92: 376. 1989. Protologue: Mexico. Orizaba, F. Müller.

Bartramidula carolinae Sharp ex Flow. in Grout, Moss Fl. N. Amer. 2(3): 163. 1935. Bartramia carolinae (Sharp ex Flow.) Grout, Moss Fl. N. Amer. 2(5): 275. 1940. Protologue: North Carolina. Bridal Veil Falls, Highlands, North Carolina, 3500 feet (Sharp). 

Plants small, in loose, yellowish green tufts, to10 mm high. Stems red; rhizoids at base, reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 0.6–1.4 mm long, erect when dry or erect-spreading when wet, straight, lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins plane, singly serrate; costae percurrent; cells papillose, papillae at lower cell ends on dorsal side of leaf and median/basal cells on ventral side of leaf, papillae at upper ends of apical cells on ventral surface, upper cells rectangular, firm‑walled, 12–30 x 5 μm, basal cells rectangular, to 40 x 10 μm, alar cells not or weakly differentiated. Synoicous. Setae 4–8 mm long, flexuose to cygneous, red. Capsules 1.5 mm long, brown, ovoid to globose, erect to inclined, irregularly rugose; exothecial cells thin-walled; opercula conic-convex, 0.2 mm long; peristome absent. Spores reniform, 40–42 μm, papillose.

Fissidens angustifolius Sull., Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts & Sci. 5: 275. 1861. Type. Cuba, Wright 18 (FH). 

     Fissidens bernoullii Schimp. in C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 173. 1897. Type. Guatemala, Bernoulli (NY).

     Fissidens svihlae Bartr., Bryologist 50: 202. 1947. Type. Guatemala, Svihla 2871 (FH).

     Plants (2–)3–5(–8) mm × to ca. 3 mm. Leaves 1.5–2.5 mm × 0.2–0.3 mm; apex acute to broadly acute; margins limbate, more or less entire, serrulate at apices; vaginant laminae more or less ½ the leaf length, equal, acute; costa (20–)23–30(–33) µm broad, percurrent to short-excurrent; cells (8–10–13(–15) µm in diameter, mammillose-papillose, irregularly hexagonal, those juxtacostally in parts of proximal vaginant laminae large, more or less oblong and pellucid. Sporophytes terminal.

Fissidens goyazensis Broth., Hedwigia 34: 120. 1895. Syntypes. Brazil, Ule 1510, 1519 (H).

Fissidens veracruzensis Pursell, Bryologist 69: 493. 1966 [1967]. Type. Mexico, Pursell & Reese 4939 (US).

Plants to 5 mm × ca. 1.5 mm. Leaves 1.3 mm × to 0.4 mm; apex acute; margins entire, slightly crenulate near apex, limbate; vaginant laminae mostly equal, more or less 2/3 the leaf length; costa percurrent to excurrent; cells 5.5–7 µm × 3.5–7 µm, bluntly unipapillose, irregularly shaped. Sporophytes not seen.

Fissidens intramarginatus (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 594. 1869. Conomitrium intramarginatum Hampe, Linnaea 31: 531. 1862. Type. Colombia, Lindig 2149 (NY).

Fissidens hancockianus Steere, Allan Hancock Found. Publ., Pacific Exp. 3: 2. 1936. Type. Colombia, Taylor 1081 (US).

Fissidens willisiae Bartr. in Willis, Bryologist 42: 152. 1939. Type. Panama, Willis 35 (FH).

Plants (3–5–)6–9(–14) mm × ca. 2 mm. Leaves (0.5–)0.9–1.5–(1.7) mm × ca. 0.3 mm; apex acute; margins crenulate-serrulate, limbate on all vaginant laminae, limbidia unistratose, extending onto lower part of ventral laminae; vaginant laminae more or less 1/3 the leaf length, equal, acute; costa percurrent to short excurrent; cells (4–)5–6–(7) µm, pluripapillose, rounded-hexagonal. Sporophytes terminal.

Breutelia rhythidioides Herz., Hedwigia 74: 108. 1934.

Protologue. Colombia. Columbia: páramo El Boqueron, 3500–3600 m ([Troll] 2152 und 2192).

Plants robust, in loose or dense, somewhat glossy, yellowish‑green to brownish yellow tufts, to 11 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis and central strand present, moderately to densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose. Leaves 3–5 x 1.2–1.9 mm, closely spaced, secund to subfalcate, rugose, at times twisted when dry, erect-spreading to secund when wet, curved-falcate, ovate to broadly lanceolate, strongly plicate at base, not decurrent; apices slenderly acuminate; margins recurved below, plane above midleaf, serrulate; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; leaf cells porose or straight-walled,  papillose at lower ends above, from either end below, upper cells linear-elongate, thick‑walled, 37.5–75 x 3.7–5 μm, basal cells linear-elongate, 50–125 x 5–7.5 μm, thick-walled, alar region with 4-9 rows of enlarged, firm-walled or inflated cells at basal angles, often extending up the basal margins, intra-alar cells reddish orange, porose, length to width ratio often more than 2:1. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 10–12 mm long, arcuate, capsules subglobose to ovoid, 4 mm long x 3 mm wide, irregularly rugulose when dry, peristome inserted below the mouth, exostome equaling the endostome or nearly so, pale yellow, smooth below, papillose above. Spores subreniform, areolate-tuberculate, 33–35 μm long x 25–26 μm wide” (Griffin 1984a).

Trematodon longicollis Michx., Fl. Bor. Amer. 2: 289. 1803. Type. U.S.A., North Carolina, in arenosis Carolinae, Michaux. 

Plants scattered, yellow-green, terricolous, 3–5 mm long. Leaves evenly spaced, flexuous spreading when wet, clasping, oblong to oblong-ovate at base, gradually long linear-subulate above, 2–3 mm long; margins weakly recurved above, entire below, weakly denticulate by blunt teeth above; costa percurrent; upper cells short-rectangular, walls firm and thickened; basal cells laxly oblong-rhomboidal to long rectangular, pale whitish yellow. Autoicous. Setae 10–15 mm long, smooth, yellow; capsules inclined, yellow, urn ellipsoidal 1.5–2.0 mm long, neck 3.0–4.0 mm long; annuli deciduous, revoluble; opercula rostrate, 1.0 mm long; stomata crytoporic and phaneroporic stomata; peristome teeth red, lanceolate, vertically striate. Spores densely papillose or minutely warty.

Plants small, 3–6(–10) mm tall, glossy, yellowish green to reddish yellow, in thin to dense mats. Stems erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, somewhat complanate-foliate, dark red; stems in cross section at times with enlarged, reddish hyalodermis cells, subepidermis of 1–2 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, 1–2 basal cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper 1–2 cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base of stems, around branch primordia, and on stems abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth or sometimes roughened, reddish brown, often pinnately branched. Leaves erect, curled-contorted when dry, lateral leaves wide-spreading when wet, ventral and dorsal leaves smaller than the lateral leaves, erect to erect-spreading when wet, ovate, obo-vate, oblong-ovate, oblong, or spathulate, 1–2 mm long, acute to broadly rounded, apiculate, or shortly cuspidate, apices at times twisted, decurrent; margins entire, bordered completely by 2–5 rows of elongate cells, plane; costae single, slender, ending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, in cross section cells homogeneously thick-walled; upper cells rounded, rhombic, or hexagonal, 8–15 µm, smooth, firm-walled, median cells similar but somewhat larger; basal cells enlarged, firm-walled, occasionally somewhat bulging, oblong, juxtacostal basal cells longer, but not much broader, cells across the in-sertions enlarged, irregularly rectangular to subquadrate, reddish brown. Asexual reproduction occa-sionally by rhizoidal propagula. Autoicous, synoicous, or dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 4–6 mm long, red, roughened above, smooth below. Capsules erect, ovoid to short-cylindric, constricted at the neck, symmetric, 0.4–0.8 mm long; exothecial cells at the mouth short-rectangular, in 2–3 rows, lower cells in upper 2/3 of the capsule larger, rounded-quadrate, col-lenchymatous, cells in lower 1/3 short-rectangular, not collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5–0.7 mm long; annuli rudimentary, persistent; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth pale yellow to white, erect-recurved when wet, erect-incurved when dry, narrowly triangular, dorsal surface more thickly papillose than ventral surface, dorsal trabeculae and median line thick, ventral trabeculae faint; endos

Plants small or medium-sized, 3–15(–25) mm tall, glossy, green to yellowish green, in tufts or thin to dense mats. Stems erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, somewhat complanate-foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with epidermis of 1–2 rows of small, thin-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs (3–)4–6 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper 3–5 cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base of stems, around branch primordia, and on stems abaxial to the leaf inser-tions, smooth, reddish brown, often pinnately branched. Leaves erect, curled-contorted to spirally twisted when dry, lateral leaves wide-spreading when wet, ventral and dorsal leaves smaller than the lateral leaves, erect to erect-spreading when wet, ovate, obovate, oblong, or spathulate, 1.0–2.5 mm long, acute to broadly rounded, apiculate, cuspidate, or piliferous, apices often twisted, decurrent; margins entire, bordered completely by 2–3 rows of elongate cells, plane; costae single, slender, end-ing 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, in cross section cells homogeneously thick-walled; upper cells rounded or hexagonal, 16–30 µm long, smooth, thin-walled, usually collenchymatous, median cells similar but somewhat larger; basal cells enlarged, thin-walled, occasionally somewhat bulging, oblong, juxta-costal basal cells longer and broader, cells across the insertions enlarged, irregularly rectangular to subquadrate, reddish brown. Asexual reproduction occasionally by rhizoidal propagula. Autoicous or synoicous. Perichaetia and perigonia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 3–6 mm long, red, smooth. Capsules erect, ovoid to short-cylindric, constricted at the neck, symmetric, 0.8–1.0 mm long; exothe-cial cells at the mouth red, short-rectangular, in 2–3 rows, lower cells subrectangular to rectangular, not or weakly collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.6–1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary, persistent; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth pale yellow to white, erect-recurved when wet, erect-incurved when dry, narrowly triangular, dorsal surface broader than ventral surface, papillose throughout, dorsal trabeculae and median line thin, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened and long-projecting; endostome as long or longer than the exostome teeth, yellowish to white, papillose, basal membranes low, segments broad, weakly keeled, not perforate, cilia rudimen-tary or absent. Spores rounded, 10–12 µm, lightly papillo

Bryomanginia saint-pierrei Thér., Trav. Cryptog. Déd. L. Mangin 8. 1931. Type. Mexic, Nevado de Toluca, Saint-Pierre 1780 (FH, NY).

Melophyllum radiculosum Herz., Feddes Repert. Spec. Nov. Regni Veg. 47: 100. 1939. Type. Peru, Cordillera Blanca, Cantuc Hirca, 31 May 1932, Lukas s.n.

Astomiopsis saint-pierrei Thér. ex Buck, Brittonia 31: 488. 1979, nom. illeg. incl. sp. prior. Type. Mexico, Nevado de Toluca, Saint-Pierre 1780 (NY).

Plants saxicolous; stems erect, to 1.5 cm long, fasciculate branched or branches arising below the vaginula. Leaves erect-spreading, oblong-lanceolate, concave, 1.5 mm long, apex obtuse; margins recurved from near the base to the apex, entire; costa percurrent, wide, filling the apex; upper laminal cells round to oval, 6–15 µm × 6–8 µm, incrassate, smooth to mammillose-bulging, bistratose at apex; basal cells rectangular, 75 µm × 15 µm, thin-walled, smooth; a few rows of cells extending upward along the margin as a short, hyaline border; alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setaeshort, 0.3–0.5 mm long; capsules 0.5–0.6 mm long, smooth, light to dark brown; annuli of 1–3 rows of cells; opercula bluntly conic. Spores rounded, 25 µm, distally rugose, brown.

Plants small to medium-sized, 1–2 cm long, pale green, reddish yellow, or yellowish, in mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, subepidermal sclerodermis sometimes pres-ent, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-spreading, at times lightly undulate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, monomorphic, oblong-lanceolate, 1.0– 1.6 X 0.2–0.4 mm, symmetric, abruptly constricted above to piliferous acumina, concave; margins entire throughout or subentire in upper 1/4, plane to erect, not bordered; costae double, thin, ending 1/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, usually unequal, smooth at back, not projecting at the apex; cells smooth, upper cells long-rhomboidal, 24–100 X 6–14 µm, thin-walled, lower cells oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular, bulging near insertions, cells across the insertions short-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 8–15 mm long, red, smooth throughout. Cap-sules horizontal to pendent, oblong-cylindric, 0.7–1.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells reddish, quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oval to oblong, collenchymatous; stomata rudi-mentary, 3–5-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.7 mm long; annuli of 3–5 rows of yellowish, thin-walled cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the opercu-lum; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellow, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments broad, strongly keeled, not or faintly perforate, cilia absent. Spores rounded, 8–12 µm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 1.5–2.0 mm long, yel-lowish, irregularly lobed at base, naked or sparsely hairy.

Plants slender to medium-sized, creeping or pendent, epiphytic. Primary stems to 15 cm long; stems in cross section with 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, central strand small. Secondary stems pendent, erect or becoming adnate to the substrate, identical to primary stems, irregularly or weakly pinnately branched, branches to 1.5 cm long, at times elongating into filiferous branches to 4 cm long. Leaves trimorphic: stolon leaves, primary stem leaves, and branch leaves. Stolon leaves 1.7–3.0 # 0.3–1.0 mm, ovate-lanceolate; upper margins dentate or with recurved teeth. Primary stem leaves erect-appressed, 1.5–3.0 # 1.0– 1.2 mm, orbicular to broadly ovate below, abruptly acuminate above, strongly decurrent; margins en-tire or weakly serrulate above; costae single, weak; median cells linear-flexuose, 90–130 # 4–5 µm, firm-walled, not porose; alar cells strongly differentiated, short-rectangular, quadrate or oblate, thick-walled. Branch leaves imbricate to julaceous, 0.6–2.0 # 0.4–1.0 mm, broadly ovate to elliptic-ovate, shortly acute to cuspidate, usually galeate; margins plane below, erect to incurved above, serrulate above or entire throughout. Dioicous. Setae yellow red to dark red, 1.5–2.0 mm long, smooth. Capsules exserted, erect, ellipsoid, 2.5–3.0 mm long; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate at the mouth, irregularly rectangular below, firm-walled; stomata on neck; opercula 1.0–1.5 mm long, shortly rostrate; annuli rudimentary, deciduous, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, papillose; en-dostome lightly papillose, basal membranes 0.08–0.09 mm high, segments linear, not perfo

Plants medium-sized to large, creeping or pendent, corticolous or saxicolous. Primary stems to 35 cm long; stems in cross section with 2–5 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, central strand small. Secondary stems pendent, erect or becoming adnate to the substrate, identical to primary stems, irregularly or weakly pinnately branched, branches 1.0–2.5 cm long, at times elongating into stoloniferous branches to 4.0 cm long. Stem and branch leaves weakly dimorphic. Stem leaves erect-appressed, 2–4 # 0.5–1.5 mm, well spaced, laxly appressed, ovate-lanceolate to oblong, cordate at base, abruptly constricted to long, crispate, hair-points, strongly decurrent; margins entire or weakly serrulate; costae single, weak; me-dian cells linear-flexuose, 62–125 # 4–6 µm, firm-walled, to incrassate; alar cells strongly differen-tiated, short-rectangular, thin-walled, inflated and bulging in excavate groups restricted to the region below and interior to the cordate bases, orange yellow, occasionally hyaline. Branch leaves spreading to erect-spreading, 1.5–4.5 mm long, broadly ovate to oblong from a cordate base, abruptly narrowed to long, crispate hair-points; margins entire below, inflexed and serrulate above; cells as in stem leaves. Dioicous. Setae yellow to yellow red, 1.0–1.2 mm long, smooth. Capsules immersed, erect, ellipsoid, 2.2–2.7 # 1.0–1.3 mm; exothecial cells at the mouth quadrate to oblate, irregularly rectan-gular below, firm-walled; stomata on neck; opercula 1.7–2.0 mm long, shortly rostrate; annuli rudimentary, deciduous, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, lightly papillose; endostome lightly papillose, basal membranes 0.10–0.17 mm high, segments linear, perforate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores round to oblong, 15–33 µm, lightly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2.0–2.5 mm long, densely hairy.

Plants small to medium-sized, creeping or pendent, corticolous. Primary stems to 15 cm long; stems in cross section with 2–5 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, central strand small (occasionally absent). Secondary stems pendent, erect or becoming adnate to the substrate, identical to primary stems. Primary branches 1.0–2.5 cm long, occurring singly or in well-separated, fasciculate groups of 2–4, at times elongating into filiferous branches. Filiferous branches nearly always present on stems, to 10 cm long. Leaves dimorphic: stem and filiferous branch leaves of one type, primary branch leaves of another. Stem leaves erect to erect-spreading when moist, appressed when dry, 1.5–3.5 # 0.9–1.8 mm, well spaced, broadly ovate to oblong, cordate at base, abruptly setaceous into long acumina, strongly decurrent; margins entire; costae single, weak; median cells linear-flexuose, 42–112 # 4–7 µm, firm-walled, not porose; alar cells strongly differentiated, short-rectangular, thin-walled, inflated and bulging in excavate groups restricted to the region below and interior to the cordate bases, reddish yellow to hya-line. Branch leaves 0.8–2.2 mm long, broadly ovate with acute to rounded acute apices; margins plane below, broadly inflexed above to just below the apex, then abruptly plane and forming a galeate apex, entire or minutely serrulate above; cells as in stem leaves. Dioicous. Setae red, 0.2 mm long, smooth. Capsules immersed, erect, ellipsoid, 2.5 # 1.5 mm; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate at the mouth, irregularly rectangular below, firm-walled; stomata on neck; opercula 1.2 mm long, shortly rostrate; annuli rudimentary, deciduous, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, smooth below, lightly papillose above; endostome smooth below, lightly papillose above, basal membranes 0.12–0.15 mm high, segments linear, perforate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores round, 17–23 µm, lightly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2.0 mm long, lightly hairy.

Plants medium-sized, creeping or pendent, epiphytic. Primary stems to 30 cm long; stems in cross section with 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, central strand small. Secondary stems pendent, erect or becoming adnate to the substrate, identical to primary stems, irregularly or densely branched, branches to 1.5 cm long, at times elongating into flagella. Leaves trimorphic: stolon leaves, primary stem leaves, and branch leaves. Stolon leaves 3–4 # 0.5–1.5 mm, erect to erect-patent, ovate-lanceolate, tortuose above; mar-gins dentate with recurved teeth from the shoulders to apex. Primary stem leaves erect-appressed, simi-lar in size to stolon leaves, broadly ovate below, abruptly acuminate above, strongly decurrent; mar-gins entire or weakly serrulate above; costae single, weak; median cells linear flexuose, 55–105 # 4–5 µm, firm-walled, occasionally porose; alar cells strongly differentiated, short- to long-rectangular, more or less bulging, at times firm-walled. Branch leaves erect to erect-spreading, at times loosely tumid, frequently in seriate rows, 1–2 # 0.5–1.0 mm, broadly ovate to elliptic, shortly acute to rounded-acute, galeate; margins entire and plane below, erect to incurved, serrulate above. Dioicous. Setae yellow red to dark red, 2–3 mm long, smooth. Capsules exserted, erect, ellipsoid, 2.0–2.7 mm long, exothecial cells quadrate to oblate at mouth, irregularly rectangular below, firm-walled; stom-ata on neck; opercula 1.0–1.5 mm long, shortly rostrate; annuli rudimentary, deciduous, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, papillose throughout or papillose above and smooth below; endostome lightly papillose, basal membranes 0.13–0.14 mm high, segments linear, not per-forate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores round, 17–32 µm, lightly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 3 mm long, densely hairy.

Plants very slender, soft, in yellowish green, filiform-flagelliform, festooning masses. Primary stems and branches elongate, irregularly branched, not stipitate, to 40 cm long; stems in cross section with 1–2 rows of somewhat enlarged, firm-walled epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow, firm-walled, central strand weakly developed; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; rhizoids sparse, in dense clusters, dark brown to blackish, smooth, not branched, from elongate clusters of ini-tials abaxial to the leaf insertions; axillary hairs with 1 short, reddish brown, basal cell and 1–2 elon-gate, hyaline, upper cells. Primary stem leaves ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate; branch leaves lanceo-late to narrowly lanceolate, 0.9–1.6 # 0.3–0.5 mm. Leaves distantly spaced, not or rarely touching the leaf above, usually spreading from insertions, erect-spreading when dry, long-acuminate, apices often twisted when wet or dry, inserted in a shallow U-shaped line; margins recurved at base, plane above, serrate to serrulate to near the leaf base; costae single, ending above midleaf, at times ending in a spine, in cross section cells homogeneous, thick-walled; cells smooth, median cells linear to lin-ear-fusiform, thick-walled, rarely porose, 60–90 # 4–5 µm; alar cells in small groups of short-rec-tangular to subquadrate, thick-walled, porose cells. Dioicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems and branches. Sporophytes unknown in Central America, description from Peru (Bryophyta Neotropica 2, MO). Setae short, straight, red, smooth, 3–4 mm long, twisted when dry. Capsules erect, oblong to short-cylindric, 2–3 mm long; exothecial cells at mouth subquadrate, red, lower cells rounded-rec-tangular, thick-walled, not collenchymatous; stomata phaneroporic, on neck; opercula obliquely short-rostrate, 1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary, persistent; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth reddish brown, narrowly triangular, cross-striate in lower half, papillose above; endostome yellowish, lightly papillose, basal membranes low to medium-high, segments linear, keeled, perforate, cilia ab-sent or rudimentary and reduced to low stubs. Spores round, lightly papillose, 20–32 µm. Calyptrae cucullate, naked, 1–2 mm long.

Orthotrichum anomalum Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 162. 1801.

Protologue: Germany. In saxis, muris, tetulis, in Germania vulgaris.

Plants small to medium-size, in dense tufts or cushions, red‑brown, yellowish brown or olive‑green. Stems erect, 10–20 mm high, moderately tomentose. Leaves stiffly erect‑imbricate to erect‑patent when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 2–3 mm long, lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate, not decurrent; apices acute to rounded‑acute; margins entire, irregularly recurved to near the apex or plane in upper _ and recurved below; costae ending below the apex; upper cells 10–15 μm wide, rounded, isodiametric or irregularly hexagonal, pluripapillose, incrassate, basal cells short to long rectangular, 25–45 μm long, thin‑ or thick‑walled, sometimes nodose, smooth. Gonioautoicous. Setae to 2–3 mm long, twisted when dry. Capsules exserted, cylindric or oblong‑cylindric 1.5–2.0 mm long, 8‑ribbed in upper _, smooth or lightly ribbed below, not contracted below mouth when dry; stomata immersed, in upper to middle regions of capsules, subsidiary cells projecting over the stomata; opercula conic to rostellate, beak erect, 0.5 mm long; peristome single, exostome teeth 16, sometimes united into eight teeth‑pairs, erect, horizontally striate below, vertically striate above. Spores 12–16 μm, roughly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2.5–3.0 mm long, with numerous, erect, papillose hairs.

3. Orthotrichum bartramii Williams, Bryologist 28: 76. 1925.

Protologue: Arizona. On bark of oaks, Whitehouse Canyon, Santa Rita Mts., Arizona, at 6000 ft. E. B. Bartram, no. 1465, Feb. 11, 1925 [MO], and no. 27, at 5000 ft., Dec. 1922.

Plants small, in low, dense tufts, brown below, olive‑green above. Stems erect, to 0.5 mm high, moderately tomentose. Leaves erect‑appressed when dry, wide‑spreading when wet, 2–2.5 mm long, oblong‑lanceolate to lanceolate, not decurrent; apices apex abruptly rounded into a channeled cuspid, acute or obtuse; margins serrate at apex, recurved or revolute to near the apex; costae ending near the apex; upper cells 8–13 μm wide, rounded‑hexagonal to elliptic, with 1–3 small, low papillae per cell, thick‑walled, basal cells long-rectangular, 45–90 μm long, thin‑walled, bulging, smooth, those along the margins nearly quadrate. Gonioautoicous. Setae 0.5–1 mm long. Capsules emergent, oblong to cylindric 1.5–2.0 mm long, 8‑ribbed, the ribs 4–5 cells wide, contracted below mouth when dry; stomata immersed, in central and basal regions of capsules, subsidiary cells projecting over the stomata; opercula rostellate, beak erect, 0.5 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth 8, reflexed when old, densely and evenly papillose, endostome segments 8, erect to incurved, hyaline, consisting of 1 row of cells above and 1–2 cells at base, finely papillose, more or less the length of the exostome teeth. Spores 16–18 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 1.5–2.0 mm long, with sparse, erect, papillose hairs.

Hymenostylium recurvirostrum (Hedw.) Dix., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 6: 96. 1934.

Gymnostomum recurvirostrum Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 33. 1801. Protologue: Poland and Germany. In rupibus gypsaceis prope Osterode et Niedersachswerfen dextexit Ehrhart. 

Plants small to medium-sized, tufted or forming mats, yellowish green to yellowish brown, saxicolous or terricolous. Stems erect, 2–45 mm high, smooth or papillose, sclerodermis present, central strand absent; rhizoids red-brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves distant and evenly spaced, lanceolate, oblong or ligulate, 1–3 mm long, appressed, somewhat contorted and incurved when dry, erect to wide-spreading when wet; apices acute to acuminate or obtuse, mucronate; margins generally plane above weakly recurved on one side or both sides at mid-leaf or below, entire to crenulate; costa ending just below the apex, narrow, dorsal surface smooth, ventral surface smooth, guide cells and two stereid bands present, ventral surface cells not enlarged; upper cells round quadrate to oblate above and becoming short-rectangular below mid-leaf, 8–20 x 8–14 μm, walls thickened to incrassate and frequently nodose, cells papillose with low papillae centered over lumina, basal cells rectangular to oblong, 20–40 x 12–18 μm, walls somewhat thickened and pitted, smooth, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae 4–10 mm long, reddish brown, smooth, sigmoid when dry. Capsules exserted, erect, short cylindrical, 0.8–1.2 mm long, smooth, systylius, reddish brown; stomata in neck; opercula obliquely rostrate, 1 mm long. peristome absent. Spores 12–18 μm, granulate, brown. Calyptrae 1.5–2 mm, cucullate, smooth.

Hyophila involuta (Hook.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1871–72: 354. 1873.

Gymnostomum involutum Hook., Musci. Exot. 2: 154. 1819. Protologue: Nepal. In Nepal. Hon. D. Gardner.

Gymnostomum tortula Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Suppl. 2(2): 78. 1826. Hyophila tortula (Schwaegr.) Hampe, Bot. Zeitung 4: 267. 1846. Protologue: Cuba. In insula Cuba legit cl. D. Poeppig.

Plants small to medium-sized, dark green to blackish green above, red to reddish brown below, in tufts to 15 mm high. Stems irregularly branched, hyalodermis not or weakly differentiated, central strand present; rhizoids sparse, red, smooth, greatly branched. Leaves 2–4 mm long, closely spaced, erect at base, tubulose, incurved or spreading when dry, erect-spreading when wet, spathulate, concave, grooved along the costa; apices rounded to rounded-obtuse; margins unistratose, plane or occasionally recurved below, entire to denticulate or dentate above, not bordered but occasionally the marginal cells lighter in color than the interior cells; costa covered on ventral surface by short, quadrate cells, subpercurrent, percurrent, or shortly excurrent into a reddish apiculus, guide cells and two stereid bands present, enlarged ventral surface layer present; upper cells 6–10 x 8–10 μm, mammillose-bulging on upper surface, plane to weakly convex, smooth on dorsal surface, rounded-quadrate to hexagonal, basal cells 12–40 x 8–18 μm, rectangular, with thin- or thick-walled. Propagula stellate to dentate-ellipsoidal often on branched, axillary stalks. Dioicous. Setae 5–12 mm long, yellow, becoming red with age. Capsules 1.0–3.2 mm long, cylindric; opercula 0.75–1.0 mm, conic-rostrate; annuli of 2–3 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome absent. Spores 8–10, smooth to lightly roughened. Calyptra cucullate, spirally twisted around the capsule, smooth, 2.0–2.5 μm long.

Zygodon ehrenbergii C. Müll., Linnaea 18: 672. 1844.

Protologue: Mexico: C. Ehrenberg legit Cl. de Schlechtendal inter muscos alios mexicanos intermixtum benevole communicavit (NY).

Zygodon oligodontus Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 107. 1909. Protologue: Mexico. District fédéral: Cima, sur troncs d’Arbutus, 1908 [Pringle] n. 10546 (MO).

Plants medium-sized, in cushions or mats, reddish brown below, dark-green above. Stems erect, to 30 mm high, sparsely or densely tomentose. Leaves irregularly twisted, erect-patent  when dry, erect‑spreading to spreading when wet, 1.0–2.0 mm long, oblong-lanceolate; apices slenderly acute, ending in hyaline apical cell; margins often undulate when dry, usually with a few irregular teeth near apex, otherwise entire, plane throughout or weakly reflexed below; costa subpercurrent or percurrent, covered in the upper ¼ to _ by short, papillose, quadrate cells; upper cells 6–12(–16) μm, irregularly rounded, pluripapillose, incrassate, basal cells near costa 16–30 μm long, oblong to rectangular, smooth. Brood bodies clavate to oblong with both transverse and vertical walls. Dioicous. Setae 5–7 mm long, smooth, yellow, at times plurisetous. Capsules 2–3 mm long, ovoid‑cylindrical to oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry; operculum not seen; peristome single, exostome absent, endostome rudimentary, of 8 short, hyaline segments extending just beyond the capsule mouth. Spores isosporous, 18–24 μm, papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants very slender, in dense cushions, reddish brown below, dark-green above. Stems erect to 5–10(–20) mm high, sparsely or densely tomentose. Leaves erect or imbricate, not contorted when dry, erect‑incurved to erect‑spreading when wet, 0.7–1.0 mm long, lingulate to ovate‑lingulate; apices broadly obtuse and rounded at the apex; margins crenulate by bulging, papillose leaf cells, plane or weakly recurved; costae stout, ending well below the apex, covered in the upper 1/2 to 2/3 by short, papillose, quadrate cells; upper cells 5–8 μm, rounded, bulging mammillose and densely pluripapillose, incrassate, basal cells near costa oblong, smooth. Brood bodies not seen. Autoicous. Setae 2–5 mm long, smooth, yellow when young, becoming red‑brown with age. Capsules 0.7–1 mm long, obovoid to oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry, constricted at neck; opercula conic‑rostrate, 0.3–0.5 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth 16 united into 8 teeth‑pairs, red, becoming white with age, densely papillose to horizontally striate, reflexed to recurved when dry, to 140–200 μm, endostome ¾ the length of the exostome teeth, red, basal membrane short, cilia absent, segments stout, vertically striate‑papillose, erect when dry. Spores isosporous, 10–14 μm, smooth. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 1 mm long.

Plants medium-size, in loose or dense tufts, brown below, olive‑green above. Stems erect, to 3 cm high, moderately tomentose. Leaves erect‑flexuose when dry, spreading to recurved when wet, 2.5–3.5 mm, lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate, undulate, not or very weakly decurrent; apices acute to long-acuminate or long‑cuspidate; margins entire, recurved to revolute in lower ½ to ¾, undulate near apex; costae ending below apex; upper cells 8–15 μm wide, irregularly rounded to elliptic, with 1–3 stout papillae per cell, thick‑walled, basal cells long-rectangular, 25–50 μm long, nodose or smooth, those along the margins shorter. Gonioautoicous. Setae 2–8 mm long. Capsules immersed, emergent or exserted, cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, smooth or 8‑ribbed in upper ½, not or slightly contracted below mouth when dry; stomata superficial, in central region of capsule; opercula rostellate, beak erect, 0.5 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth 16, reflexed when old, densely and evenly papillose, endostome segments 16, erect to incurved, consisting of 1–2 rows of cells, coarsely papillose, more or less the length of the exostome teeth. Spores 20–30 μm, densely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2.0–2.5 mm long, with sparse, erect, papillose hairs.

Plants small to medium-sized, in dense tufts, yellowish brown, 1.5–3 cm high. Stems red-brown, erect or laxly ascending, often covered above with unistratose enations, small hyalodermis present, sparsely radiculose below. Leaves widely spaced, erect-spreading, contorted to crispate when dry, spreading to patulous when wet, oblong-ovate to elliptic, 2.5–3 mm long, concave, erect-sheathing at base, decurrent; apices broadly acute; margins recurved in lower 1/2, coarsely serrate in upper 1/3; costa ending well below the apex; upper leaf cells quadrate to hexagonal, firm- to thick-walled with rounded corners, pluripapillose, papillae small, simple or c-shaped, 8–11 μm in diameter, outer basal cells narrowly long-rectangular, thick-walled, often porose, 32.5–75 x 5–10 μm, inner basal cells elongate, oblong to oblong-hexagonal, thin-walled, bulging, hyaline, 35–75 x 12.5–22.5 μm, sharply demarcated from upper cells and outer basal cells, alar cells not differentiated. Asexual reproduction by fusiform gemmae (with transverse and vertical walls) borne at the apex of stout, leafless branches, on upper part of main stem, gemmiferous branches densely covered with enations identical to those often found on the stems. Inflorescences and sporophytes unknown.

Plants small, dark-green to yellow-green above, brown below, in dense mats or tufts, 2.5–5 mm high. Stems red, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis weakly developed, central strand well-developed; rhizoids sparse, red, smooth to roughened. Leaves 1.3–2.3 mm long, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, ovate to oblong, weakly clasping to erect at base, crisped and spirally contorted above when dry, erect-flexuose to erect-spreading when wet; apices acuminate, mucronate; lamina unistratose, not fragile; margins entire, strongly involute above the base to the apex; costa stoutly excurrent, broad at base (40–80 μm), ventral surface cells quadrate, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer enlarged, papillose, green; upper cells rounded to quadrate, 6–11 μm long, thick-walled, bulging at the surface, with 4–6 bifid papillae, basal cells narrowly rectangular, thick- or thin-walled, yellow or hyaline, smooth, 20–50 x 6–10 μm, outer basal cells hyaline, thin-walled, not or somewhat running up the margins in a v-shaped pattern. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves somewhat larger and longer than vegetative leaves, otherwise not strongly differentiated. Sporophytes not known from Central America. Setae smooth, 4–8 mm long, yellow. Capsules ovoid to oblong, erect, 0.8–1.2 mm long, somewhat furrowed when dry; stomata in neck; opercula rostrate, 0.7–1.0 mm long; annuli of several rows of cells persistent cells; peristome teeth 16, short, narrowly triangular, erect, red, papillose, basal membrane absent, rudimentary or absent. Spores 18–22 μm, papillose. Calyptrae yellow, cucullate, smooth, 1.2 mm long.

Plants small to medium-sized, reddish green to reddish yellow, 5–25 mm high. Stems red, erect, irregularly branched, stems sclerodermis present, central strand well-developed; rhizoids red, smooth. Leaves 1.5–2.3 mm long, erect-sheathing at base, erect-twisted and incurved when dry, erect-spreading to spreading when wet, oblong-lanceolate; apices broadly acute, apiculate; margins unistratose, weakly reflexed below, plane above, distantly dentate above, sometimes entire, not bordered, weakly decurrent at base; costa percurrent to short-excurrent, papillose at back, ventral superficial cells short-rectangular, pluripapillose, guide cells present, ventral stereid band weakly developed, dorsal stereid band present, upper ventral epidermal layer enlarged, papillose; upper cells 4–8 x 4–8 μm, firm-walled, oblate to irregularly quadrate, densely pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells smooth, inner basal cells rectangular, enlarged, thin-walled and bulging, 30–40 x 18 μm, outer basal cells narrowly rectangular, firm-walled, not bulging and forming a distinct basal  border, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal; perichaetial leaves elongate, sheathing. Setae smooth, 12–18 mm long,  red. Capsules cylindric, curved, 1.5–2 mm long, suboral ring differentiated in 4–5 rows; exothecial cells long-rectangular, bulging mammillose; stomata in neck; opercula erect, long-conic, 1 mm long; annuli persistent, of 1–2 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome of 32 erect, red, filamentous, densely spiculose teeth, to 300 μm long, basal membrane absent. Spores 14–20 μm, smooth to slightly papillose. Calyptrae not seen.

Plants small, reddish green, to 8 mm high. Stems red, erect, not or irregularly branched,  sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids red, smooth. Leaves 0.8–1 mm long, erect, spirally incurved when dry, erect-spreading when wet, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, plane above, obtuse; margins unistratose, revolute to the apex, entire, not bordered, not to weakly decurrent at base; costa percurrent or ending 1–2 cells below the apex, smooth at back except near the apex, ventral superficial cells quadrate to short-rectangular, pluripapillose, guide cells present, ventral stereid band weakly developed, dorsal stereid band present, ventral epidermal layer enlarged, papillose; upper cells 6–16 x 6–10 μm, firm-walled, oblate to irregularly quadrate, rounded-hexagonal, or short-rectangular, pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells smooth, those near costa 14–30 x 10–22 μm, short-rectangular, outer basal cells oblate to irregularly quadrate 6–20 x 12–16 μm, firm-walled, alar cells not differentiated. Plants medium-sized, 2–5 cm long, yellow green, golden, or reddish yellow, in dense mats. Leaves homomallous to falcate-secund, undulate, erect-spreading when dry or wet, symmetric, concave, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, 2–3 mm long; margins serrulate above, subentire to entire below, plane, occasionally erect to slightly incurved above; costae double, slender, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, diverging throughout, and usu-ally ending on or very near the margins, smooth on back, weakly projecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells incrassate, porose, long-rectangular to sublinear, flexuose, 40–50 X 3–4 µm, cells across the base rectangular, strongly porose; alar cells shortly rectangular. Spores rounded, 14–19 µm, faintly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, irregularly lobed, reddish and lightly roughened, yellowish below, 2 mm long.

Dioicous. Setae elongate, 30–35 mm long, red, smooth throughout, or at times roughened on neck and below the cap-sules. Capsules horizontal to pendent, oblong-cylindric, 2.0–2.5 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4

Plants slender, 1–2 cm long, reddish to purple tinged, in thin mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly to subpinnately branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, subepidermal layer of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Plants large, caespitose, pale green to yellow above, fulvous brown below; stems tomentose, comal tufted, to 10 cm long. Barbula stillicidiorum Card., Rev. Bryol. 37: 126. 1910. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Vera Cruz: Xico, rochers suintants, en compagnie de Tortula mniifolia (Barnes et Land, 1906). 

Plants small to medium-sized, dull, dark-green to yellow-green above, brown below, in tufts, 15–46 mm high. Stems red, erect, not or sparsely branched, hyalodermis absent or weakly present, central strand well-developed;, rhizoids sparse. Axillary hairs five cells long, all cells hyaline. Leaves 1.2–2.0 mm long, triangular-lanceolate, lanceolate, oblong-lanceolate, ligulate, or lingulate, erect-incurved, twisted and catenulate or erect when dry, erect-spreading when wet; apices acute, broadly acute to obtuse, at times apiculate; lamina unistratose; margins entire throughout, entire below, serrulate above or with 1–3 teeth at apex, variously recurved to near the apex or plane; costa excurrent, percurrent or ending below the apex, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral and dorsal surface layer enlarged; upper cells in regular rows, short-rectangular, quadrate or oblate, 4–16 x 5–10 μm, firm-walled, smooth, basal cells short to long-rectangular, firm-walled, smooth, 10–28 x 6–7 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Dense clusters of fusiform, stalked, multicellular propagula occasionally present in leaf axils.  Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia terminal. Setae 1 per perichaetia, smooth, 10–15 mm long, red. Capsules cylindrical, erect, 1.2–2 mm long, smooth; exothecial cells short-rectangular, thin-walled; stomata in neck; opercula erect, long-rostrate, 1.5 mm long; annuli well-developed; peristome red-orange, well-developed, basal membrane high, teeth spirally twisted, 0.9–1.2 mm long. Spores 8–12 μm, smooth or lightly papillose. Calyptrae smooth, 1.5–2.5 mm long.

Plants small to large, 3–7 cm long, yellowish to green or light green, dull. Primary stems (stolons) creeping; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, densely present on stolons and on secondary stems and branches when in contact with substrate; leaves appressed to spreading, scarious. Secondary stems pendent, ascending or erect, variously stipitate, simple to irregularly pinnate, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, somewhat thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia narrowly foliose to subfilamentous, lanceolate, serrulate on margins. Stipe leaves evenly foliate, erect to erect-spreading. Secondary stems and branches complanate-foliate; leaves wide-spreading, smooth to crisped when dry, flat when wet, broadly oblong, 1.0–1.7 mm long, asymmetric, broadly rounded-obtuse to truncate, retuse to broadly apiculate, narrowly decurrent, rounded, not auriculate at base; margins crenulate-serrulate at apex, distantly serrulate below, inflexed on one side below; costae single, extending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, often forked or branched near tips; cells smooth, apical cells hexagonal to rhombic, to 8 µm long, median cells rhomboidal, 16–18 µm long, linear-fusiform near insertion, marginal cells on inflexed side of leaf elongate-linear, at times forming a more or less distinct border, thick- to firm-walled, not porose; alar cells weakly differenti-ated, of 2–5 short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions porose. Asexual propagula absent. Synoicous. Perichaetia ramentose, ramenta loriform to linear, 1.7–2.0 mm long; perichaetial leaves ovate to oblong-ovate. Sporophyte elevated at maturity by a pseudopodium. Setae red, smooth, 0.2–0.5 mm long. Capsules immersed, emergent to short-exserted, erect, symmetric, broad-cylindric, 1.0–1.5 mm long; exothecial cells oblate at mouth in 5–7 rows, those below short-rectangular, firm-walled; stomata absent; opercula short, obliquely rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli rudimentary, of small, thin-walled cells; peristome diplolepideous, inserted within the capsule mouth; exostome teeth pale yellow, linear, to 300 µm long, papillose throughout on both sides, trabeculae and median line weakly developed; endostome yellow, papillose throughout, basal membranes short, barely exceeding the capsule mouth, segments linear to 1300 µm long, weakly and narrowly perfo-rate,

Plants robust, 5–13 cm high, stipitate-frondose, forming dark green to yellowish green, lax tufts. Stolons creeping, evenly foliate; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely branched, in circu-lar clusters just below the leaf insertions, on stolons, and at the base of stipitate stems; leaves loosely imbricate, widely spaced, broadly triangular. Stems erect, stipitate, irregularly pinnate, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 5–7 rows of small, thick-walled cells, grading into somewhat larger, thick-walled cortical cells, central strand poorly developed; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Stipes evenly foliate; leaves appressed below, erect-spreading above, 2.0–2.5 mm long, ovate-triangular to triangular, acute to acuminate, de-current; margins entire to subserrulate; costae single and strong, ending 1/2–2/3 the leaf length. Stem leaves erect-spreading, flattened, plicate, 3–4 mm long, ovate-ligulate, more or less symmetric, broadly rounded to obtuse, sometimes apiculate or mucronate, shortly decurrent; margins serrate above, teeth unicellular, serrulate below, usually shortly incurved below on one side, or plane throughout; costae single, strong, ending near the apex, often sinuose and forked or spurred; cells smooth or prorate, upper cells isodiametric, irregularly rounded, rounded-hexagonal, subrhomboidal, subquadrate, or oblate, 8–20 X 4–10 µm, median cells rhomboidal-fusiform to fusiform-elongate, 26–50 X 4–6 µm, median marginal cells linear, in 2–3 rows; basal cells elongate-linear, 40–90 X 6 µm, porose; alar cells not or weakly differentiated as oblate, quadrate, or short-rectangular cells at the basal angles. Branch leaves similar to stem leaves except smaller and marginal teeth at apex better developed. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown in Central America, description from Buck (1998) and Sastre (1987). Setae elongate, 1.5–2.5 cm long, smooth, red brown. Capsules horizontal to pendent, cylindrical, 1.6–2.8 mm long; exothecial cells short-rectangular, firm- to thick-walled, not smaller at the mouth; stomata pres-ent; opercula obliquely conic-rostrate, 1.4 mm long; annuli rudimentary, of 2 rows of thick-walled cells; peristome diplolepideous</

Schizymenium schiedeanum (C. Müll.) Shaw, Bryologist 88: 30. 1985.

Mielichhoferia schiedeana C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 230. 1848.  Protologue: Mexico. In monte Orizaba vulcanico, sin. coll.

Meilichhoferia tolucensis Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 5: 100. 1932 [1933]. Protologue: Mexico. Nevado de Toluca, cratère, Saint-Pierre 1902. 

Plants slender to medium-sized, light-green, in loose tufts. Stems to 10 mm high, yellow, simple or forked; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose roughened. Lower leaves reduced, distant, erect to erect-spreading, upper leaves crowded,  0.8–1.2 mm long, erect, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane, serrulate to serrate above midleaf; costae ending near apex to percurrent; upper cells linear-rhomboidal to linear-vermicular, firm-walled, 60–130 x 6–8 μm, marginal cells narrower than the interior cells, basal cells rhomboidal, rectangular or subquadrate. Paroicous. Setae 15–20 mm long, reddish, flexuose. Capsules erect to inclined, 2 mm long, oblong-cylindric, tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with wavy walls; stomata superficial; operculum not seen; annuli well-developed, of 2–3 rows of cells; peristome absent, occasionally rudimentary and fugacious. Spores 14–16 μm, lightly papillose.

Schizymenium serratum (Card. & Herz.) Shaw, Bryologist 88: 29. 1985.

Mielichhoferia serrata Card. & Herz., Rev. Bryol. 38: 3. 1911. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Vera-Cruz: pic d’Orizaba, versant Sud (H. Ross, 1906: comm. Herzog).

Plants slender to medium-sized, shiny, yellow-green to brownish, in loose tufts. Stems 5–20 mm high, red, simple or forked; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Lower leaves reduced, distant, erect-spreading to spreading, upper leaves crowded, 1.0–1.5 mm long, erect to imbricate, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane, sinuolate, serrulate or serrate above middle; costae ending below apex to percurrent; upper cells narrowly linear-rhomboidal to linear-vermicular, firm-walled, 70–130 x 6–8 μm, marginal cells narrower than the interior cells, basal cells rhomboidal, rectangular or subquadrate. Paroicous. Setae 15–30 mm long, yellowish orange, flexuose. Capsules inclined, 2–4 mm long, oblong-cylindric, tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with wavy walls; stomata superficial to somewhat immersed; opercula conic, apiculate, 0.5 mm long;  annuli well-developed, of 2–3 rows of cells; exostome absent, endostome hyaline to yellowish, papillose, basal membrane low, segments filiform, cilia absent. Spores 14–20 μm, lightly papillose.

Streptopogon cavifolius Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 180. 1869.

Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, Baños ad pedem montis Tunguragua, in ramulis praecipue malvacearum suffruticosarum, etiam in monte Guayrapata (6000–10,000 ped.), Spruce n. 140 (G, NY). 

Plants small, scattered or gregarious, brownish to reddish green, corticolous. Stems 5–10 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand absent, cortical cells thin-walled, hyaline, uniform throughout; rhizoids densely clustered at base of stem. Leaves 2–2.5 mm long, oblong to narrowly spathulate, sheathing at base, concave, evenly spaced, appressed, contorted when dry, erect-spreading when wet; apices obtusely rounded, cucullate; margins entire, incurved above; costa narrow, subpercurrent to percurrent, ventral surface cells rectangular, smooth on both surfaces, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band well-developed, enlarged ventral epidermal cells absent, guide cells ventrally exposed; upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal, 24–48 x 10–20 μm, thin-walled, somewhat bulging, smooth on both sides, longer near the costa, shorter near the margin, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 34–80 x 8–20 μm, those near the margin shorter and firmer walled, alar cells not differentiated. Asexually reproducing by clavate or cylindrical, multicellular, smooth gemmae borne singly on apical leaf surface. Dioicous. Sporophytes rare, not known from Central America, description based on South American plants. Setae 2 mm long, yellow. Capsules cylindrical, erect, 3.3 mm long, smooth, yellowish brown; opercula rostrate; peristome teeth filamentous. Spores not seen. Calyptrae mitrate.

Streptopogon erythrodontus (Tayl.) Wils., Hooker’s J. Bot. Kew Garden Misc. 3: 51. 1851. 

Barbula erythrodonata Tayl., London J. Bot. 5: 50. 1846. Protologue: Ecuador. On Pichincha, near Quito, Prof. William Jameson, (Dr. Greville’s Herbarium).

Streptopogon rutenbergii C. Müll., Abh. Naturwiss. Vereine Bremen 7: 207. 1881. Streptopogon erythrodontus var. rutenbergii (C. Müll.) Salm., Ann. Bot. (London) 17: 113. 1903. Protologue. Madagascar. Wald von Ambatondrazaka, 6 Decbr. 1877, in wenigen Individuen.

Steptopogon matudianus Crum, Bryologist 55: 51. 1952. Protologue. Mexico. On the bark of an ash tree below El Puerto, above Acultzingo, Estadao de Veracruz, México, 7300 ft. elev., Aaron J. Sharp 689, September 13, 1944 (MICH), syn. nov. 

Plants small to medium-sized, scattered or gregarious, dark-green, reddish green to reddish yellow, corticolous. Stems 10–30 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand absent, cortical cells thin-walled, hyaline, uniform throughout; rhizoids in dense clusters on lower parts of stem, densely branched, branches often at right-angles. Leaves 4–7 mm long, lanceolate, erect at base, more or less keeled, evenly spaced, erect, crispate and contorted  when dry, wide-spreading when wet; apices acuminate, cuspidate to long-awned; margins sharply serrate, plane, bordered by several rows of long, narrow cells; costa excurrent as a toothed awn, ventral surface cells rectangular, smooth on both surfaces, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid or substereid cells present, dorsal surface cells enlarged, ventral surface cells absent the guide cells ventrally exposed; upper cells rectangular to rhomboidal 30–70 x 10–24 μm, thin-walled, somewhat bulging near costa, smooth on both sides, marginal cells long, narrow, thick-walled in 2–3 rows, basal cells long-rectangular, thin-walled, bulging, smooth, 44–100 x 14–24 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Asexually reproducing by long uniseriate, marginal propagula. Autoicous. Setae 2–4 mm long, reddish yellow. Capsules cylindrical, erect, 2–4 mm long, smooth, yellowish brown; exothecial cells rhomboidal, thin-walled; stomata at base of capsule; opercula conical, 1.5 mm long; annuli adherent, 1–2 rows of non-vesiculose, thick-walled cells, adherent to operculum on dehiscence; peristome teeth 1–1.4 mm long, dark red, teeth filamentous, spiculose, twisted several turns, basal membrane short, red above, hyaline at base. Spores granular, 18–22 μm. Calyptrae campanulate, 2 mm long, lobed at base, roughened to hispid.

Fissidens bourgaeanus Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 170. 1872. Type. Mexico, Veracruz, Vallée de Cordoba, Bourgeau 2136 (NY, isotype).

     Plants to 6.5 cm × 10 mm. Leaves 3.4–6.2 mm × 0.5–1.3 mm; apex acute to short-acuminate; margins elimbate, entire to irregularly dentate at apex, more or less entire to irregularly serrate on the vaginant laminae; vaginant laminae 0.5–0.6 the leaf length, equal to slightly unequal, acute; costa percurrent; cells (8–)10–12–15) µm long, occasionally irregularly bistratose, smooth to slightly bulging, rounded to irregularly hexagonal, 3–5 marginal rows thicker, forming a darker marginal band. Sporophytes unknown, male branches short, axillary.

Fissidens curvatus Hornsch., Linnaea 15: 148. 1841. Type. South Africa, Cape: Löwenrücken, Ecklon s.n. (H).

Conomitrium lindigii Hampe, Linnaea 31: 532. 1862. Fissidens lindigii (Hampe) Jaeg., Enum. Fissident. 12. 1869. Type. Colombia, Bogotá, Lindig 2149 (FH, lectotype; FH, NY, isolectotypes).

Plants with more or less dimorphic stems, the infertile stems to ca. 5 mm × ca. 1.5 mm, the fertile (perichaetial) stems 1.2–5 mm × 1–2 mm. Leaves with apex acuminate; margins more or less entire, limbate, the limbidia confluent; vaginant laminae acute, ½–⅔ the leaf length, more or less equal; costa percurrent to short excurrent; cells 8–14 µm × 4–6 µm, smooth, somewhat larger in the vaginant laminae; sporophyte terminal.

Fissidens intermedius C. Müll., Linnaea 21 : 181. 1848. Type. Suriname, Kegel 501 (GOET).

Plants to ca. 2.5 mm × ca. 1.2 mm. Leaves ca. 1 mm × ca. 0.35 mm; apex acute; margins serrulate-crenulate, entire to slightly denticulate on the vaginant laminae, limbate along the entire length of the vaginant laminae; vaginant laminae ca. 1/2 the leaf length, acute; costa percurrent to ending 2–3 cells below the apex; cells 5–7 µm, unipapillose, quadrate to hexagonal. Sporophytes terminal.

Didymodon crassicostatus (Bartr.) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Sci. 32: 162. 1993.
