Plants robust, dull, green above, brown below, in loose tufts, 30–40 mm high. Stems red erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids sparse, at base of stems or scattered throughout. Axillary hairs 4–5 cells long, basal cell brown. Leaves 4–6 mm long, linear-lanceolate to triangular-ovate, spreading at base, circinate-contorted above when dry, spreading to falcate-secund above when wet, plane along the costa on ventral surface; apices subulate; lamina unistratose, fragile; margins entire, recurved below, plane above; costa stout, 100–140 μm wide at base, filling the apex and percurrent to excurrent, ventral surface cells of costa quadrate, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral and dorsal surface cells enlarged; upper and basal cells weakly differentiated, upper cells in regular rows, rounded, 8–10 x 8 μm, firm-walled, smooth, basal cells quadrate, rounded or short-rectangular, firm-walled, smooth, 10–30 x 10 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Sporophytes not known.

Plants 1–6 mm high. Stems erect, strongly rosulate or with evenly spaced and sized leaves throughout, irregularly branched, sclerodermis and central strand present, rhizoids sparse, red, smooth. Leaves 1.5–2.5 mm long, erect at base, tubulose, incurved when dry, wide-spreading when wet, spathulate to oblong, concave; apices rounded to obtuse; margins unistratose, plane or incurved, entire to weakly denticulate, not bordered; costa covered on upper ventral surface by bulging, quadrate to oblong cells, subpercurrent, percurrent or excurrent, guide cells well-developed, ventral stereid band absent or present, at times present as 2-4 small, parenchymatous cells, dorsal stereid band well-developed, epidermal layer enlarged; upper cells 6–14 x 6–8 μm, mammillose-bulging on upper surface, plane to weakly convex, smooth or variously pluripapillose on dorsal surface, rounded-hexagonal, basal cells differentiated only juxtacostally at extreme base, 18–24 x 6–8 μm, short-rectangular to rectangular, with thin- or thick-walled. Leaves ca. 1 mm x 0.5.0.6 mm; apex rounded-obtuse to broadly acute; margins serrulate-crenulate, limbate on proximal 1/2 or les s of vaginant laminae of most leaves, limbidia unistratose; vaginant lamina e acute, more or less 2/3 the leaf length; costa ending 2.4 cells below ape x; cells 7.10 5m, smooth, guttulate, irregularly hexagonal. Sporophytes ter minal.

Fissidens allenianus Bruggeman-Nannenga & Pursell, Bryologist 93: 332. 1990. Type. U.S.A., Florida, Pursell 2915 (PAC, U).

Plants to 7.5 mm ×1.5–2.5 mm. Leaves 1.2–2.1 mm × 0.3–0.4 mm; apex abruptly narrowed, rounded-obtuse; margins crenulate; vaginant laminae ½–2/3 the leaf length, somewhat unequal; minor laminae acute-rounded; costa ending (4–)5–7(–10) cells below the apex, 2 stereid bands distally, 3 stereid bands proximally; cells smooth. Sporophytes terminal.

Plants small to medium-sized, 3–5 cm long, golden reddish, yellow green, or pale green, in glossy, dense mats. Stems prostrate, densely, irregularly, or subpinnately branched, dark red; stems in cross section with epidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, yellowish to hyaline, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; ax-illary hairs 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hya-line; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Stem leaves erect, widely spaced, ovate, broadly acute, 0.7–1.0 mm long, concave, rounded to the insertions, not decurrent; margins entire or with a few small, widely spaced serrations, erect to broadly incurved; costa none or occasionally double and short, less than 1/3 the leaf length; cells from leaves on single plants variably ornamented (entirely smooth, entirely pluripapillose, or a mix of smooth and pluripapillose), papillae simple or branched, more or less bi-seriately arranged over the lumina, upper cells linear-flexuose, 60–100 X 4–7 µm, usually thick- or firm-walled, often porose, occasionally thin-walled; basal cells across the insertions enlarged, rec-tangular, strongly porose, yellowish to reddish; alar cells undifferentiated. Branch leaves erect-spreading to weakly homomallous, dense, oblong-lanceolate, bluntly acute, 0.6–0.9 mm long. Asex-ual reproductive structures not seen. Autoicous. Perigonia and perichaetia sessile along stems and branches. Setae elongate, flexuose, 15–25 mm long, red to red brown, smooth below, papillose above. Capsules red, erect to inclined, ovoid-cylindrical, 1–2 mm long, neck well developed, strongly tuber-culate; exothecial cells at mouth reddish, quadrate to shortly oblate in 2–3 rows, red, rectangular, strongly collenchymatous below; stomata

Plants in thin, green mats, occasionally purple tinged, 2–3 cm long. Stems irregularly branched, red; stems in cross section with some enlarged epidermal cells forming a partial hyalodermis, other-wise cells small, thick-walled, red, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, yellowish to hyaline, central strand absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell quadrate, red brown, upper cells enlarged, oblong, hyaline; rhizoids not seen. Leaves flattened, erect when dry, spreading to wide-spreading when wet, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, gradually narrowed to long, slender, flex-uose acumina, 1.0–1.8 X 0.15–0.30 mm; margins weakly serrate below, strongly serrate at apex, teeth mostly single, occasionally double, teeth often papillose-tipped, cells somewhat wider and shorter than laminal cells; costae double, long, ending in 1–2-celled spines, serrate along the upper dorsal sur-face; cells thin-walled, with 1–4 scattered papillae, at times papillae in horizontal rows, upper cells rectangular to elongate-fusiform to vermicular, 12–53 X 6–8 µm; basal cells long-rectangular, 25–47 X 5–6 µm, cells across the insertions reddish or hyaline, rectangular, 30–40 X 6–8 µm. Sporophytes unknown.

Macrocoma gastonyi Norris & Vitt in Vitt, Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 39: 209. 1973.

Protologue: Dominican Republic. La Vega Prov. : On boulders near the summit of Pico Duarte, at elev. 3175 m., Norris, Gastony & Jones 5840 (NY).

Plants medium-sized, in stiff, yellowish red, radiculose mats. Primary stems creeping to 5 cm long, irregularly branched. Leaves erect‑imbricate, spreading at tips when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 1.2–2.0 mm long, weakly keeled, ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins entire to minutely crenulate, recurved below, plane above; costae ending below the apex, covered at back with short quadrate cells; apical cells elongate, upper and median cells, 11–20 μm, elliptic‑oblong, mammillose or stoutly and bluntly unipapillose, basal cells rounded to elliptic often stoutly mammillose, inner basal cells near costa elongate, incrassate. Gonioautoicous. Setae 8–12 mm long, smooth, yellow to red. Capsules 2–3 mm long, erect, oblong‑cylindrical, furrowed throughout when dry; opercula short‑rostrate, 1 mm long; peristome reduced to a short, hyaline, densely papillose membrane barely extending above the capsule mouth. Spores isosporous, 44–56 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, densely hairy, 3 mm long.

Orthotrichum malacophyllum Card., Rev. Bryol. 38: 2. 1911. Protologue: Mexico. Frontière des Etats de Morelos et de Mexico: La Cima, troncs d’arbres (Barnes et Land, 1908, n° 418).

Plants small to medium-size, in loose or dense tufts, olive‑green to brown below, green to yellow‑green above. Stems erect, 8–20 mm high, moderately to weakly tomentose. Leaves contorted, erect‑flexuose, tips incurved when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 2–3 mm long, oblong‑lanceolate to lanceolate, decurrent, sharply keeled near costa; apices acute to shortly acuminate; margins entire, plane in upper ½–_, recurved near base, undulate above; costae ending near the apex; upper cells 10–15 μm wide, rounded, oblate to angular‑hexagonal, with 2–4 small, low papillae per cell, thick‑walled, basal cells short- to long-rectangular, 25–65 μm long, thin‑ or thick‑walled, often nodose, smooth. Gonioautoicous. Setae to 0.5 mm long. Capsules emergent, cylindric or ovoid‑cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, 8-ribbed, contracted below mouth when dry; stomata immersed, in central and basal regions of capsules, subsidiary cells projecting over the stomata; opercula rostellate, beak erect, 0.5–1 mm long; exostome of eight teeth‑pairs, at times splitting to 16, erect when first exposed, reflexed or recurved when old, papillose, endostome segments 8, erect to incurved, more or less the length of the exostome teeth, hyaline, of one row of cells, finely papillose, the papillae at times in vertical rows. Spores 12–20 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2–2.5 mm long, with sparse, erect, smooth to weakly papillose hairs.

Plants small, dull, dark-green to yellow-green above, brown below, in tufts, 2–25 mm high. Stems red, erect, not or sparsely branched, sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids sparsely distributed at base of stems, smooth. Axillary hairs 4–5 cells long, all cells hyaline. Plants slender in loose yellow‑green tufts. Stem leaves arched-incurved and lightly plicate to smooth when dry, erect-spreading to spreading, somewhat flattened when wet, 2–3 mm long, ovate to ovate-lanceolate or oblong-ovate, more or less symmetric, broadly acute to short-acuminate, shortly decurrent; margins serrate above, teeth unicellular or multicellular, serrulate below, usually shortly incurved below on one side, or plane throughout; costae single, strong, ending near the apex, often sinuose and spurred; cells smooth, at times lightly porose, upper cells between the end of the costa and the apex rhomboidal to shortly fusiform, apical cells irregularly hexagonal, isodiametric, or subrectangular, 8–20 X 6–10 µm, me-dian cells rhomboidal-fusiform to fusiform-elongate, 20–40 X 6–10 µm; basal cells elongate-linear, 30–70 X 4–6 µm; alar cells not or weakly differentiated as oblate, quadrate, or short-rectangular cells at the basal angles. Branch leaves similar to stem leaves except smaller, more flattened, often obo-vate. Asexual reproduction by axillary, microphyllous, flagelliform branches. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown.

Pseudopohlia didymodontia (Mitt.) Andrews, Bryologist 53: 179. 1950.

Bryum didymodontium Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 289. 1869. Pohlia didymodontia (Mitt.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 552. 1903. Webera didymodontia (Mitt.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. (ed. 2) 10: 362. 1924. Protologue: Mexico, Beechey, in Herb. Hooker.

Pohlia tenuiseta Bartr., Bryologist 50: 206. 1947. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. Huehuetenango: most tailside [sic] bank, Puente Alto, between Santa Eulalia and Barillas, alt. 4700 ft., A.J. Sharp 4909. (TENN).

Plants small, dull, in erect, loose tufts. Stems simple or sparsely and irregularly branched, 10–15 mm high, red; rhizoids reddish orange to brownish, major rhizoids papillose, minor rhizoids smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves crowded, 0.8–2.0 mm long, erect to imbricate, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane, erect or narrowly recurved below, denticulate to serrate; costae ending below the apex to percurrent; upper cells narrowly rhomboidal, to elongate, firm-walled, 70–90 x 6–8 μm, marginal cells narrower, basal cells short-rectangular to sub-quadrate, 14–20 x 12 μm. Gemmae in leaf axils, obconic to obovate, reddish orange, with 3–6 leaf primordia at apex. Dioicous. Setae flexuose, 30–50 mm long, reddish brown. Capsules erect to inclined, 2.5–3.5 mm long, symmetric, oblong-cylindric with a short, tapered neck; annuli revoluble, of 2–3 rows of cells; opercula low-conic, apiculate; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with wavy walls; stomata superficial; exostome teeth whitish yellow, united in pairs ½ or more their length, broadly triangular, papillose below, vertically striate above, endostome irregular, whitish yellow, basal membrane low, segments flat, not or narrowly perforate, cilia broad. Spores 20–26 μm, coarsely papillose.

Bryum leptotorquescens C. Müll. ex Broth., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 24: 246. 1897.

Protologue: Cameroon. An Felsen in Bächen bei Buea Dusén 208.

Bryum subelimbatum Thér., Smithsonian Misc. Collect. 81: 13. 1928. Protologue: Mexico. Puebla: Fort Lorette, alt. 2,200 m. [Arsène] 657 (US). 

Plants medium- to robust-sized, shiny, green to yellowish green, in loose tufts, 13–40 (–70) mm high, weakly rosulate to evenly foliate; rhizoids papillose, forming brownish red tomentum at base. Lower leaves distant, upper leaves crowded, 2.5–4 mm long, spirally twisted to spreading flexuose when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, oblong to broadly spathulate, long-decurrent; apices acuminate; margins recurved in lower ½, indistinctly bordered by 2–4 rows of narrower, longer, somewhat thick‑walled cells, serrate above; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; upper cells rhomboidal‑hexagonal, thin‑walled, 30–50 μm long, basal cells broadly rectangular, thin‑walled, lax, 40–80 μm long. Sporophytes not known from Central America. Pseudautoicous; male plants 1–2 mm high, on the tomentum of female stems. Setae 2 cm long. Capsules pendulous, oblong‑pyriform, neck short and slender; opercula nearly hemispheric, apiculate; endostome with a low basal membrane, narrowly perforate segments, and well‑developed, appendiculate cilia. Spores to 20 μm, roughened (Ochi 1994).

Bryum microchaeton Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot. sér 5, 4: 342. 1865.

Protologue: Columbia. Bogota, Guadalupe 2900 metr., ad Barrancos, inter alia intermixturm, augusto 1863, A. Lindig. parce legit.

Pohlia peracuminata Bartr., Bryologist 50: 206. 1947. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. Huehuetenango: bank of trail, pass above Todos Santos, alt. 11000 ft., A.J. Sharp 4780a (TENN). 

Plants small to medium-sized, lustrous, yellowish green to reddish yellow, in loose tufts to 10 mm high; rhizoids papillose. Leaves 1–2 mm long, erect and well‑spaced below, erect‑imbricate and crowded at apex, ovate‑lanceolate; apices long, slenderly acuminate; margins revolute throughout, not bordered, minutely denticulate at apex; costae percurrent to somewhat excurrent; upper cells linear‑rhomboidal to fusiform, lax, thin‑walled, 50–90 μm long, basal cells laxer with bulging walls, short‑rectangular, 40–60 μm long. Dioicous. Setae 12–30 mm long, red. Capsules 3 mm long, brown, oblong‑cylindrical, inclined to pendent, neck weakly constricted and roughened; opercula 0.5 mm long, conic-apiculate; exostome teeth orange below, yellow above, densely papillose, endostome yellowish hyaline, lightly papillose, basal membrane to ½ of exostome teeth length, segments well-developed, broadly perforate, cilia 2, nodose. Spores 12–16 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptra not seen.

Epipterygium mexicanum (Besch.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3) : 555. 1903.

Webera mexicana Besch., Bull. Soc. Bot. France 20: LXIII. 1873. Bryum mexicanum (Besch.) C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 226. 1901 [1900], hom. illeg. non, (Mont.) C. Müll., 1848. Protologue: Mexico. (Gal., Bourgeau n° 1357 part., cum Anomobryo prostrato mixta, Hahn in herb. Winter).

Plants small, glossy, light-green to pinkish in loose tufts, 5–15 mm high; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose, sparsely developed. Lateral leaves in 2–3 rows, 1.5–2.5 mm long, evenly spaced throughout, complanate-foliate, somewhat contorted when dry, spreading when wet, obovate, oblanceolate or elliptic, decurrent; apices acute; margins not bordered but cells gradually longer and narrower from costa to margin, plane, entire below, obscurely serrulate above; costa ½ to _ the leaf length; upper cells rhomboidal to linear-rhomboidal, thin-walled, 55–100 x 7–15 μm, basal cells larger, rhomboidal to long‑rectangular, alar cells not differentiated. Dorsal leaves in 2–3 rows, smaller and narrower, to 1.2 mm long, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, the costa weaker but otherwise identical to lateral leaves. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen.

Bryum limbatum C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 573. 1851.

Protologue: Costa Rica. America centralis, Costa Rica, in reg. montosa inter 5000–8000 ped. elevationis, inter Bartram. sphaericarpam leg. A. S. Oersted mens Febr. 1848. 

Webera mnioides Schimp. ex Besch., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot. sér. 6, 3: 204. 1876. Bryum mnioides (Schimp.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 574. 1903, hom. illeg.,  non Gmel. ex With., 1801, nec Wils. 1844. Protologue: Guadeloupe. (L'Herminier, in herb Shimp. [sic.]). 

Plants small to medium-sized, pale green to blackish brown in loose tufts to 3 cm high; rhizoids moderately developed at base. Leaves 1.3–2 mm long, well‑spaced on stem, spreading and somewhat contorted to twisted when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, oval, ovate to oblong; apices rounded‑obtuse or acute; margins recurved below, plane above, bordered by 3–5 rows of long‑rectangular, thick‑walled cells, entire to serrulate; costae percurrent to short‑excurrent; upper cells rhomboidal, firm‑walled, 16–40 μm long, basal cells rectangular, thin‑walled, bulging 40–80 μm long. Dioicous. Setae to 15 mm long, red. Capsules 2.0–2.5 mm long, red, oblong‑cylindrical, suberect to horizontal (occasionally pendent), neck abruptly narrowed and gradually tapering to the seta; opercula 0.5–1.0 mm long, conic apiculate; exostome teeth brown to yellow‑brown, densely papillose, endostome yellowish hyaline, lightly papillose, basal membrane to ½ of exostome teeth length, segments well-developed, narrowly perforate, cilia 2–4, nodose or appendiculate. Spores 13–16 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptra not seen.

or rarely branched. Secondary stems erect, 2–4.5 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with

yellow to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia
subfoliose. Secondary stem and branch leaves ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.8 mm long, imbricate
when dry, spreading to wide-spreading when wet, acute to shortly acuminate, decurrent; margins narrowly <br />
recurved in lower 1/2 or less, serrulate at the apex; costae strong, 0.4–0.6 the leaf length, occasionally
spurred above; upper cells oval to elliptic, 10–20 μm long, very thick-walled, smooth or
prorate, median cells oval, 12–16 μm long; basal cells near the costa elongate to linear, to 60 μm long,
thick-walled, straight-walled or porose; alar cells quadrate, or oblate, thick-walled, smooth. Autoicous.
Perigonia gemmate, borne laterally, leaves ovate, concave, acuminate, ecostate; perichaetia
terminal, leaves erect, 2–3 mm long, oblong to obovate, gradually contracted to long, serrate awns,
margins recurved, costae long-excurrent, lower leaf cells linear, thin-walled. Setae short, to 0.5 μm
long, yellow to red, cells quadrate. Capsules immersed, ovoid to ellipsoid, 1.0–1.6 mm long, smooth,

Spores spherical, lightly papillose, 20–30 μm. Calyptrae conic-mitrate, prorate, basally split, 0.5–
0.7 mm long.

Leaves closely or somewhat distantly spaced, weakly to not dimorphic, erect-spreading to spreading and flattened when wet, contorted to crispate when dry, oval-oblong, oblong, obovate, or spathulate, 1.5–3.0 mm long, symmetric, acute to short-acuminate, apiculate, apices often twisted whether wet or dry; margins sharply serrate, serrulate, or subentire above, entire below, elimbate or obscurely bordered by a row of elongate cells, plane or re-curved below; costae double, 1/4–2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, at times projecting at the apices; cells smooth, median cells rhomboidal, fusiform, or oblong-hexagonal, 34–60 X 10–18 µm, thick-walled, sometimes porose, lower cells oblong-rectangular to elongate-fusiform, firm-walled, sometimes porose, cells across the base enlarged, subrectangular, yellow to reddish yellow; alar cells not differentiated. Plants slender, 2–6 cm long, light to dark green, in lax tufts. Primary stems prostrate and creep-ing. Secondary stems erect-ascending, or pendent, sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, 1–3 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and at base of secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves distantly spaced, not or weakly di-morphic, flattened, erect-spreading to spreading, crispate to flexuose when dry, falcate-spreading when wet, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate (dorsal leaves at times oblong-lanceolate), 2–3 mm long, asymmetric, short- or long-acuminate; margins serrate above, plane above, often broadly infolded on one side at base, elimbate; costae double, slender, 1/4–1/2 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells narrowly to broadly fusiform, 60–140 X 8–18 µm, thin-walled, not porose, becoming oblong-rectangular to oblong-fusiform below; alar cells not differentiated. Asexual propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae. Autoicous or synoicous. Plants medium-sized to robust, 4–8 cm long, light to dark green, greenish yellow, in lax tufts. Pri-mary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems erect or ascending, not or sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red to red brown with age, slightly complanate-foliate or evenly foliate; stems in cross section with small hyalodermis, 3–5 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids usually on primary stems and at base of secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Plants medium-sized to robust, 3–6 cm long, dark green, greenish yellow, or reddish yellow, in lax tufts. Primary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems erect or ascending, not or sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red to red brown with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, 1–3 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axil-lary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids usually on primary stems and at base of secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched.
