Plants small, tufted or caespitose, dull, glaucous ­green. Stems 4–8 mm high, branched near base, central strand present. Leaves 1.5–2.0 x 0.5–0.9 mm, crowded, clasping at base, erect spreading , irregularly incurved, crisped to tubulose when dry, short oblong–elliptic to narrowly lingulate; apices acute, muticous; margins plane; costa single, subpercurrent, with 2 rows of dorsal stereids; upper cells angular-quadrate­, 10–14 x 12.5–17.5 μm, pluripapillose on both surfaces by coronate, c–shaped papillae; basal cells smooth, rectangular, 29–46 x 12.5–19 μm, transverse walls thickened, red to orange, longitudinal walls hyaline or pale yellow, thin, basal marginal cells gradually differentiated in 4–5 rows of elongate cells, 43.8–87.5 x 5–7.5 μm. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves sheathing, smaller than vegetative leaves. Setae single, 2–3.5 mm long, yellow-orange to reddish orange, twisted, smooth. Capsules 1.3–2.3 mm long, longitudinally ridged and furrowed, contracted below a reddish orange, suboral band of 2–3 rows of  hexagonal, angular-quadrate cells; exothecial cells in irregular longitudinal rows, more or less rectangular; neck wrinkled and puckered; opercula convex-rostrate; peristome absent. Spores heteropolar, 30–40 μm, on one side with radial plicae, the other side with vermiform projections. Calyptrae shiny, yellowish or golden, gradually tapered into the yellowish or reddish–brown, slightly curved rostrum, finely prorulose at apex, at base sharply divided into blunt, somewhat triangular segments.

Orthotrichum pariatum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 186. 1869.

Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, in montibus Titaicum et Carguairazo (11,000 ped.), Spruce, n. 130, etiam in monte praealto Cayambe, Jameson. Lectotype (Lewinsky 1987) Spruce 130, NY.

Plants medium-size, in loose or dense tufts, brown below, olive‑green or yellowish green  above. Stems erect, to 2.5 cm high, weakly to moderately tomentose. Leaves erect‑flexuose when dry, spreading to recurved when wet, 2.4–3.6 mm, lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate, often with bulging decurrencies; apices acute to long-acuminate or long‑cuspidate; margins recurved to revolute in lower ½ to ¾, undulate near apex; costae ending below apex; upper cells 8–15 x 6–10 μm, irregularly rounded, elliptic, or elongate with 1–3 stout papillae per cell, thick‑walled, basal cells long-rectangular, 30–80 μm long, thick-walled, nodose or smooth, those along the margins shorter. Gonioautoicous. Setae 2–4 mm long. Capsules exserted, cylindric, 2.0–2.5 mm long,  8‑ribbed in upper ½ or more, not or slightly contracted below mouth when dry; stomata superficial, in central and lower region of capsule; opercula rostellate, beak erect, 0.5 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth 8, reflexed when dry, densely papillose, endostome segments 8, erect to incurved, consisting of 1–2 rows of cells, coarsely papillose, more or less the length of the exostome teeth. Spores 22–28 μm, densely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, 2.0–2.5 mm long, with sparse, erect, papillose hairs.

Macromitrium frustratum Allen, Novon 8: 115. 1998.

Protologue: Honduras. Lempira: Montana de Celaque. Summit of Cerro la Castilla, ca 12 km SW of Gracias, 14°33'N, 88°41'W. On trunk of Pinus, Allen 11542, (DUKE, H, MICH, MO, NY, TEFH, US).

Plants robust, greenish yellow to greenish brown. Stems strongly creeping, branches to 5 cm long, moderately tomentose. Leaves keeled, erect below, flexuose to spirally twisted and undulate above when dry, erect‑patent to erect-spreading when wet, 5–7 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, linear‑lanceolate; apices long-acuminate into a fragile apex to 3 mm long; margins plane to undulate, entire to serrulate below, serrate above with one to several large, multicellular teeth on the leaf acumen, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent; upper interior cells 6–12 x 6–8 μm, quadrate to rounded, incrassate, not porose, smooth to weakly bulging, in distinct longitudinal rows, upper marginal cells at times longer and narrower than interior cells forming a weakly differentiated border, basal cells 24–40 μm long, long-rectangular, incrassate and porose, weakly tuberculate. Dioicous. Setae 5–8 mm long, smooth; capsules 2–3 mm long, cylindrical, furrowed; opercula rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth truncate, 240 μm high, yellow, densely papillose, fused at base into an erect membrane, more or less free at tips, endostome hyaline, weakly papillose, basal membrane to 160 μm high, segments to 80 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 10–14 μm, smooth, hyaline and 18–30 μm, papillose, yellow‑brown. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 3 mm long.

Erpodium coronatum (Hook. f. & Wils.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 403. 1869.

Anictangium ? coronatum Hook. f. & Wils., London J. Bot. 3: 150. 1844.  Pilotrichum coronatum (Hook. f. & Wils.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 184. 1851. Protologue: Brazil. On stems of trees near Cachoeira, Province of Ceará. July, 1839 [Gardner] (lectotype, NY). 

Erpodium brasiliense C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 2: 726. 1844, nom. nud. Based on Brazil [Gardner] No. 32.

Erpodium brasiliense C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 3: 90. 1845. Protologue: Brazil. Habit. in cortice arborum Brasiliae pr. Cachoeira (prov. Ceará) [Gardner No. 32].

Plants more or less shiny, dark-green, usually tinged brown or red-brown. Stems and branches terete, turgid, tightly appressed to the substratum. Leaves imbricate when dry, spreading when moist, 0.7–1.0 mm long, not complanate, usually symmetric, concave, broadly ovate; apices abruptly short-acuminate; cells smooth, upper cells hexagonal, 18–35 μm long, basal cells oblate-hexagonal. Perichaetial leaves enlarged. Sporophytes immersed; setae nearly lacking. Capsules ovate-cylindric, 1.3–1.7 mm long; annuli persistent, compound, as many as 4 rows of cells; peristome rudimentary, a delicate, pale, papillose, irregular membrane exceeding the annulus or not. Spores 29–32 μm, finely papillose to nearly smooth. Calyptrae mitrate, smooth, plicate, plicae scabrous.

Entosthodon bonplandii (Hook.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 245. 1869.

Gymnostomum bonplandii Hook., Pl. Crypt. 1b. 1816. Physcomitrium bonplandii (Hook.) De Not., Syllab. Musc. 283. 1838. Amphoritheca bonplandii (Hook.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 219. 1874. Funaria bonplandii (Hook.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 524. 1903. Protologue: Colombia. In umbrosis humidis prope Suacha et Santa Fè de Bogota, altit. 1370 hexapod. (Regnum Novum-Granatense), Humboldt & Bonpland.

Entosthodon pellucidus C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 13: 747. 1855. Funaria pellucida (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 523. 1903. Protologue: Martinique. Martinique: Sieber.

Entosthodon husnotii Schimp. ex Besch., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. sér. 6, 3: 203. 1876. Funaria husnotii (Besch.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 525. 1903. Protologue: Martinique. Martinique, sur la terre humide de la montagne Pelée, 1250 mètr. (Husnot Exsicc., n°. 116); sur le bord des chemins (Hahn n° 798)

Entosthodon microcarpus C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 174. 1897. Funaria microcarpa (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 524. 1903. Protologue: Guatemala. Zatulum prope Coban, in terra, 4400 ped. altus, Decembri 1895: v. Türckheim, in Hb. Levier.

Entosthodon paucifolius C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 548. 1897; Funaria paucifolia (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 524. 1903. Protologue: Jamaica. Jamaica, prope plantationes Cinchonae, 4900 ped. altus, 11 Aprili 1896: W. Harris. Hb Jamaciense n° 10044.

Entosthodon antillarum Besch. ex C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 108. 1901 [1900], nom. nud. 

Plants yellow‑ to brown‑green, usually gregarious in lax to dense tufts. Stems erect, 2–4 mm tall, sparsely branching by subperigonial innovations, usually more or less naked at base (except for rhizoids), the leaves usually clustered toward stem apices, with a single‑layered sclerodermis, central strand well-developed. Leaves erect‑spreading when dry, contorted, wide‑spreading to squarrose when moist, obovate to spathulate, acute to short‑cuspidate, (1.5–)2–2.5(–3.5) mm long, concave, not decurrent; margins bluntly serrate above, subentire below, plane; costa ending 3/4 the leaf length to subpercurrent; upper cells subquadrate to hexagonal to short‑rectangular, thin‑walled, smooth, (34–)45–85 x (17–)20–28(– 40) μm, differentiated at the margins with 1–2(–3) rows of narrow, elongate, yellowish cells, more or less confluent in the apex, disappearing toward the insertion, basal cells long‑rectangular, (68–)85–129(–157) x 22–43(–51) μm, sometimes inflated, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae orange to reddish brown, straight to slightly flexuose, twisted to the right throughout, weakly hygroscopic, smooth, 0.5–1(–2) cm long. Capsules reddish brown, oblong‑pyriform with the neck somewhat less than 1/2 the capsule length, erect, symmetric, somewhat constricted below the flaring mouth when dry, wrinkled to sulcate in the neck, smooth above, 1–1.4(–2) mm long; exothecial cells fusiform‑hexagonal to rectangular, thick‑walled, shorter in the neck, becoming quadrate to oblate and thin‑walled in 5–6 rows at the mouth; stomata phaneroporous; opercula plano‑convex, with a slightly paler margin, cells subquadrate to short‑rectangular, thick‑walled, in more or less regular, straight vertical rows; annuli simple; peristome typically none, rarely single and exostomial, when present teeth rudimentary, deeply inserted, barely exceeding mouth. Spores subspherical to reniform, (24– )28–34 μm in diameter, verrucate‑lirate, appearing very finely but densely roughened, without trilete scars. Calyptrae cucullate‑rostrate, 2–2.6 mm long, naked, smooth.

Funaria calvescens Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 1(2): 77. 1816.

Funaria hygrometrica var. calvescens (Schwaegr.) Mont., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. ser. 2 12: 54. 1839. Funaria hygrometric ssp. calvescens (Schwaegr.) Kindb., Eur. N. Amer. Bryin. 2: 330. 1897. Protologue: Dominican Republic. In Domingo lectam communicarunt Desfontaines, Thouin. Australia (?). In novo Belgio carptam La Billardiere.

Funaria megapoda C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5:175. 1897. Protologue: Guatemala. Pansamalá, in rupibus, Decembri 1887, Türckheim (NY).

 

Plants small to medium-sized, light-green or yellowish green in loose tufts 5–25 mm high; stems nearly naked below, sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth, clustered at base of stems. Upper leaves 2–3 mm, lower leaves reduced, leaves crowded at apex, erect-contorted when dry, erect, concave when wet, soft and flaccid, deeply concave, obovate‑oblong, acute to short-acuminate, not or weakly decurrent at base; not bordered, margins plane to erect, often undulate when dry, entire to somewhat serrulate above; costa subpercurrent to shortly excurrent; upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, with thin, bulging walls, 37–62 x 12–30 μm, basal cells enlarged, rhomboidal-hexagonal, 90–112 x 70–87 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Paraphyses clavate with enlarged, subglobose to ellipsoid cells. Setae 15–70 mm long, brownish red, cygneous when wet, not or weakly twisted when dry. Capsules 3–4 mm long, pyriform, suberect but very oblique at mouth, gradually tapered from the neck, plicate when wet or dry; opercula 0.2–0.5 mm high, weakly conic, not or minutely apiculate; annuli compound and revoluble; peristome diplolepidous, exostome teeth from a short, yellow, densely papillose membrane, brownish yellow below with well-developed, dark-red trabeculae, hyaline at tips, densely striate-papillose, asymmetrically curved above and united at tips with a latticed central disk, endostome lacking basal membrane and cilia, segments opposite and united at base of exostome teeth, broad below, abruptly narrowed above, pale-yellow, densely papillose, 2/3 the length of the exostome. Spores 10–14 μm, yellowish, verrucate. Calyptrae 3 mm long, cucullate, inflated, long-rostrate.

Plants medium-sized to robust, 2.0–2.5 cm long, glossy, light green to yellowish green, in dense mats. Primary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems prostrate or weakly ascending, not or sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red to red brown with age, strongly complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, 3–5 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyl-lia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves closely spaced, strongly flattened, weakly dimorphic. Lateral leaves erect-spreading to spreading when wet, spreading, undulate to crispate when dry, ovate-oblong to ob-long-lingulate, 1.8–3.0 mm long, symmetric or weakly asymmetric, obtuse to broadly acuminate, apiculate; margins entire below, sharply serrate above, elimbate, plane above, broadly infolded on one side at base; costae double, weak, 1/4–1/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, not projecting at the apex; cells smooth, median cells linear-fusiform to long-fusiform, 60–140 X 6–10 µm, thin-walled, not porose, lower cells elongate-rectangular, thin-walled, not porose, cells across the base enlarged, subrectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Dorsal leaves erect when wet, ovate-oblong to lingulate, 2 mm long, symmetric; margins entire below, sharply serrate above, elimbate, plane. Asexual propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, arising from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae. Dioicous. Setae elongate, (6–)8–12 mm long, red to reddish orange, densely spiculose-papillose. Capsules erect, ovoid to oblong-cylindrical, 1.0–1.7 mm long, neck well developed and thickly tuberculate; exothecial cells reddish, oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below rounded, oblong, to rectangular, thick-walled, somewhat collenchymatous; stomata rudi-mentary, 3–6-celled, on neck; opercula high-conic, 1.0 mm long; annuli of 10–20 rows of thin-walled cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peri-stome diplolepideous, exostome very narrowly triangular, med

Plants medium-sized, 2–3 cm long, glossy, green, yellowish green, or reddish yellow. Primary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems prostrate or ascending, not or sparsely branched, hya-line to yellowish when young, becoming red to red brown with age, often attenuate-foliate at tips; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, 2–3 layers of small, thick-walled subepi-dermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves closely spaced, strongly complanate, weakly dimorphic. Lateral leaves erect-spreading to spreading when wet, spreading, plane or lightly crispate when dry, oblong to oblong-ovate, 2–3 mm long, weakly asymmetric, obtuse to broadly acuminate, apiculate; margins entire below, serrulate above, elimbate, plane above, broadly infolded on one side at base; costae double, weak, 1/3–1/2 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, median cells linear-fusiform to long-fusiform, 100–180 X 8–18 µm, thin-walled, not porose, lower cells elongate-rectangular, thin-walled, not porose, cells across the base enlarged, subrectangular; alar cells not dif-ferentiated. Dorsal leaves erect to appressed when wet, oblong to obovate, symmetric; margins entire below, serrulate above, elimbate, plane. Asexual propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, arising from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen, description from Churchill (1988). Setae elongate, 6–9 mm long, yellowish red, papillose and spinose throughout. Capsules suberect, ovoid-cylindrical, to 1.6 mm long; opercula conic rostrate. Calyptrae campanulate-mitrate, 2.2–2.4 mm long, with multicellular ramenta.

Ditrichum ambiguum Best, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 20: 117. 1893. Type. U.S.A., Washington, Mason County, Piper s.n.

Plants small, 3–15 mm high, dull green to yellowish. Leaves 2.0–2.5 mm long, erect to erect-flexuous, with spreading points, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, subulate-acuminate; margins narrowly recurved, entire below, serrulate at apex; costa percurrent; cells firm-walled to incrassate; lower cells long-rectangular, 25–27 µm long; upper cells short-rectangular, 15–17 µm long. Dioicous. Setae 8–9 mm long, red; capsules erect, cylindric, 1.8–2.0 mm long; opercula high-conic, blunt; peristome teeth 500–800 µm, split nearly to the base into 2 terete, filiform, red, densely spiculose, obliquely twisted divisions. Spores 12–13 µm, smooth.

Ditrichum gracile (Mitt.) O. Kuntze, Rev. Gen. Pl. 2: 835. 1891. Leptotrichum gracile Mitt., Kew J. Bot. 3: 355. 1851. Type. Ecuador, Andes Quitenses, Jameson s.n.

Leptotrichum crispatissimum C. Müll., Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital., n. ser. 3: 97. 1896.

Ditrichum crispatissimum (C. Müll.) Par., Ind. Bryol. Suppl. 131. 1900. Type. China, Schen-si, in monte Si-ku-tzui-san, Giraldi (Müll. sub. no. 871).

Ditrichum giganteum Williams, Bull. New York Bot. Gard. 2: 113. 1901. Lectotype. U.S.A., Montana, Columbia Falls, Williams 568 (NY), syn. nov.

Ditrichum longicaule Bartr., Bryologist 49: 109. 1946. Type. Guatemala, San Marcos, between San Sebastián and summit of Volcán Tajumulco, Steyermark 35514 (F, FH).

Plants slender, in tall or short tufts, yellowish green to reddish yellow, 2–10 cm tall, sparsely to densely radiculose below. Leaves erect, sub-erect or laxly spreading with points often spirally twisted when dry, 4–8 mm long, abruptly or gradually linear-subulate from a clasping base; costa long excurrent, variously thickened, 50–80 µm wide, toothed at apex; cells thickened with pellucid walls; basal cells extremely variable in shape, linear to rectangular, 17–55 µm long, interior cells pitted or smooth, marginal cells at extreme base thin-walled, hyaline, forming an indistinct border, cells at the apex of the sheathing base irregularly oval to quadrate. Sporophyte not known in Central America.

Ephemerum spinulosum Bruch & Schimp. ex Schimp., Syn. Musc. Eur., ed. 1, 1: 6. 1860.

Protologue: U.S.A. Ph. serratum β angustifolium H. et W. in Drum. Musci amer. II. [ Louisiana, without locality, Drummond, Musci Americani (Southern States) No. 2 (NY, DUKE)].

Plants pale green, with abundant protonemata. Leaves to 1.4 mm long x 0.4 mm wide, linear-lanceolate, acuminate; margins spinose-dentate; costae more or less percurrent, sometimes lacking in the lower parts of the leaves, dorsally roughened; upper leaf cells oblong-rhomboidal, 4-6:1, scindulose to almost smooth. Rhizautoicous or dioicous. Capsules ovoid, obliquely apiculate, 0.5–0.6 mm long. Spores bluntly papillose, 56–90 x 48–56 μm.

Plants small to medium-sized, 2–4 cm long, green, reddish, yellowish, or yellow brown, in mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly to subpinnately branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-spreading, at times lightly undulate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, monomorphic, oblong-lanceolate, 1.2–2.0 X 0.3–0.5 mm, symmetric, abruptly constricted above to piliferous acumina, concave; margins entire throughout or subentire in upper 1/4, plane to erect, not bordered; costae double, thin, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging through-out, usually unequal, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells linear-elongate, sinuate, 40–80 X 3–6 µm, firm-walled, at times porose, lower cells oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular, bulging near insertions, cells across the insertions short-rectangular, reddish; alar cells not differentiated. Asexual propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, arising abaxial to the leaf insertions opposite the costae on specialized brood branches. Autoicous or paroicous. Setae elon-gate, 35–50 mm long, red, smooth throughout, at times somewhat roughened below the capsules. Capsules horizontal to pendent, oblong-cylindric, 2–3 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells reddish, quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, walls evenly thickened to slightly collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–5-celled, on neck; operculum and annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabecu-lae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments

Plants robust, pale green to yellowish green, in loose mats. Stems creeping to shortly ascending, 3–10 cm long, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyaline to pale green when young, red when old, epidermal cells long-rectangular to elongate, densely and often complanate-foliate; stems in cross section stems with cells weakly differentiated, outer cells smaller and more thick-walled than the inner cortical cells, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent, scale leaves present; axillary hairs fragile, 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves flattened or erect-spreading, 3–6 mm long, dorsal leaves narrower than lateral leaves, otherwise leaves similar, ovate-lanceolate, symmetric or asymmetric, apices flexuose-piliferous to long, narrowly acuminate; margins serrulate to subentire above, plane or inflexed on one side below, elimbate, absolutely ecostate; cells smooth, pellucid, lax, thin-walled, upper and median cells long-hexagonal to linear, 100–290 X 10–27 µm; basal cells enlarged, broadly long-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 15–40 mm long, red to red brown, smooth. Capsules inclined, asymmetric, cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells rectangular to long-rectangular, lateral walls very thick, horizontal walls thin; stomata on neck, variable in form: perfect, 2-celled and irregularly formed, 2–3-celled; opercula long-rostrate, 1.5 mm long; annuli well developed, of 7–8 rows of thin-walled, quadrate cells, persistent at the base of the opercula; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, dorsal (outer) surface dark red, median furrows present, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, ventral (inner) surface yellowish, smooth to lightly papillose, trabeculae weakly projecting; endo-stome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose, basal membranes high, segments well developed, keeled, weakly perforate, cilia 1–2, nodose. Spores rounded, 12–18 µm, smooth to finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, 2.0 mm long, smooth, naked.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in green, yellowish or golden brown, often blackish tinged, dense, pendent masses. Primary stems creeping, secondary stems pendent, irregularly branched, not stipitate, to 40 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm-walled, central strand weakly developed; para-phyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; rhizoids in dense clusters, dark brown to blackish, smooth, not branched, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions; axillary hairs 4–5 cells long, with 1–2 short, reddish brown, basal cells and 3 elongate, hyaline, upper cells. Stem and branch leaves dif-fering only in shape, stem leaves ovate-triangular, abruptly long-acuminate to nearly piliferous, branch leaves ovate to lanceolate. Leaves 1–2 mm long, spreading from insertions (occasionally erect), somewhat contorted when dry, erect-spreading when wet, long-acuminate, apices nearly al-ways twisted when wet or dry, inserted in a U-shaped line, cordate to reniform at base; margins plane, serrate to serrulate to near the leaf base, rarely entire; costae single, ending at midleaf, at times end-ing in a spine, in cross section cells homogeneous, thick-walled; cells smooth, upper and median cells linear to linear-fusiform, thick-walled, rarely porose, 50–90 # 5–7 µm; basal cells broader, usually porose; alar cells short-rectangular, thick-walled, porose, in small excavate groups. Asexual repro-duction at times by deciduous flagelliform branches. Dioicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems and branches. Setae short, erect, red, smooth, 2–3 mm long. Capsules erect, oblong to short-cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exothecial cells short-rectangular, thick-walled, not collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula obliquely short-rostrate, 1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth reddish brown, narrowly triangular, cross-striate in lower half, papillose above; en-dostome yellowish, lightly papillose, basal membranes short, segments linear, keeled, perforate, cilia absent. Spores round, lightly papillose, 17–28 µm. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2 mm long.

Leptodontium exasperatum Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 74. 1909.

Leptodontium viticulosoides (P. Beauv.) Wijk & Marg. var. exasperatum (Card.) Zand., Bryologist 75: 254. 1972. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Vera-Cruz: Orizaba (F. Müller). Sans indication de localité (Diguet, in herb. Mus. Paris). Lectotype (Zander 1972): Müller, s.n. (NY). 

Plants medium to robust, in loose tufts, yellow-green to light green, to 9 cm high. Stems red, erect or laxly ascending, sclerodermis present, moderately to densely radiculose. Leaves moderately spaced, erect at base, spirally twisted to contorted above when dry, squarrose to squarrose-recurved when wet, ovate-lanceolate to long-lanceolate, 3–5 mm long, keeled above, sheathing at base, decurrent; apices acute; margins recurved in lower 1/2–2/3, dentate in upper 1/3, teeth pluripapillose; costa subpercurrent, usually with high papillae on upper dorsal surface; upper leaf cells quadrate to hexagonal, thick-walled, collenchymatous, 7.5–12.5 μm, with long, single, columnar, simple to bifid papillae, 4–10 μm high, centered over the lumina, inner basal cells long-rectangular to elongate, 30–100 x 5–8 μm, pluripapillose, thick-walled, porose, outer basal leaf cells similar to upper leaf cells, alar cells subrectangular to quadrate, thick-walled, porose, yellow-red. Sporophytes not seen from Central America, description based on Peruvian plants (Allen 4327, MO). Dioicous (?). Setae straight to flexuose, 1 per perichaetium, 10–15 mm long, yellow, becoming brownish with age. Capsules erect, narrowly cylindrical, 3–4 mm long, smooth when dry; exothecial cells short-rectangular, firm-walled; stomata at base of urn; opercula erect, conic-rostrate, 1.5 mm long; peristome teeth linear, divided to the base, red-brown, obliquely striate to slightly papillose on outer surface. Spores heterosporous, 5–10 μm and 12.5–15 μm, slightly papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 5–6 mm long.

Leptodontium excelsum (Sull.) Britt., Bryologist 11: 66. 1908.

Syrrhopodon excelsus Sull., Musci Allegh. 41. 1846. Zygodon excelsus (Sull.) Britt., Mem. Torrey Bot. Club 4: 180. 1893. Protologue: U.S.A. Hab. summo in cacumine montis Grandfather, Carolinae Septentrionalis, arboreus, Musci Alleghanienses No. 170 (MO).

Zygodon sullivantii C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 679. 1849. Amphoridium sullivantii (C. Müll.) Lesq. & James. Protologue: U.S.A. In summo cacumine montis Grandfather Carolinae septentrionalis, arboreus, Sullivant (MO). 

Plants small to medium-sized in loose tufts, yellow-green to light green, to 4 (-10) cm long. Stems red, erect or laxly ascending or pendent, sclerodermis present, moderately radiculose. Leaves well-spaced, erect at base, spirally twisted above when dry, squarrose to squarrose-recurved, smooth or undulate at margins when wet, ovate-lanceolate to long-lanceolate, 2–3 mm long, keeled above, sheathing at base, decurrent; apices acute; margins recurved in lower 1/2–2/3, dentate in upper 1/3, teeth usually pluripapillose; costa subpercurrent; upper leaf cells quadrate to hexagonal or shortly elongate, thick-walled, not or occasionally collenchymatous, 6–10 μm, pluripapillose, papillae low, scattered over the lumina, leaf apex with 1 to several enlarged, hyaline, smooth nematogen cells often giving rise to rhizoids, inner basal cells long-rectangular to elongate, smooth, thick- or thin-walled, straight-walled or porose, 32–100 x 3–8 μm, outer basal leaf cells quadrate, alar cells differentiated, short-rectangular to quadrate. Plants often with long, slender, flagellate branchlets along the stems, branchlet leaves spreading to recurved when wet, lanceolate, not deciduous, costa subpercurrent. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves elongate, to 6 mm long, sheathing the seta and nearly overtopping the capsule. Setae straight, 1 per perichaetium, 5–10 mm long, yellow. Capsules erect to somewhat curved, cylindrical, 2.5–3.5 mm long, smooth; exothecial cells short-rectangular, firm-walled; stomata at base of urn; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5–1 mm long; peristome teeth deeply inserted within the capsule mouth, short, linear, irregularly divided, red-brown below, hyaline above, striate, 300 μm long. Spores 17–25 μm, slightly papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 5 mm long.

Mniomalia viridis (Mitt.) C. Müll., J. Mus. Godeffroy 3: 61. 1874.

Drepanophyllum viride Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 318. 1869. Protologue. Fl. Amazon, Pará, Spruce, n. 553; fl. Guamá (v. potius Guainia?), in lapidibus rivuli exsiccati, Spruce, n. 554; fl. Negro, San Gabriel, Spruce, n. 555; San Carlos, Spruce, n. 556; Andes Quitenses, fl. Bombonasa (1300 ped. ), Spruce, n. 557. Lectotype, designated here. Brazil, Pará, Spruce 553 (NY).

Drepanophyllum ramulinum Spruce, Cat. Musc. 9. 1867, nom. nud.

Mniomalia bernoullii C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 176. 1897. Protologue. Inter Casnajá et Rascachi, cum Calymperi Carionis C. Müll. associata, [Bernoulli & Cario] Coll. N° 91. Synonymized by Bartram (1949). 

Plants olive-green, dull. Stems to 1 cm long x 2.5 mm wide, ascending, branching often initiated just below perichaetium; axillary hairs to 7 cells long. Leaves often shrunken and crispate when dry, usually appressed to stem, to 1.5 mm long, oblong-ovate; apices acute to apiculate; perichaetial leaves more or less equilateral, spirally arranged, lanceolate, cuspidate, longer than stem leaves, to 2.5 mm long; margins elimbate, recurved, serrulate distally, otherwise mostly entire; costae percurrent in stem leaves, ending in cusps of perichaetial leaves; leaf cells rounded-quadrate, 10–14 x 8–10 μm, unipapillose. Propagula olive-green to reddish brown, in terminal clusters on infertile stems or infrequently axillary, to 9-celled (exclusive of stalks); leaves subtending propagula clusters smaller, somewhat spirally arranged, less inequilateral than vegetative leaves. Sporophytes unknown in Central America, description based on Reese 16511 (NY). Setae orange-red, to 1.2 cm long. Capsules orange-red, to 1.4 mm long, erect and radially symmetric or slightly obliquely oriented, more or less bilaterally symmetric. Spores and calyptra not seen.

Streptopogon calymperes C. Müll. in Geh., Abh. Naturwiss. Verein Bremen 7: 207. 1882.

Protologue: Madagascar. Spärlich mit voriger Art [S. rutenbergii C. Müll., Wald von Ambatondrazaka, 6. Decbr. 1877, in wenigen Individuen].

Calymperes lindigii Hampe, Ann. Sci Nat. Bot. sér. 5, 3: 342. 1865. Streptopogon hampeanus Besch., Ann. Sci Nat. Bot. sér. 8, 1: 290. 1895, nom. nov. Protologue: Colombia. Bogota, Pacho, ad rad. arb., inter Fabroniam, sterile, leg. A. Lindig.

Streptopogon rigidus Mitt. ex Salm., Ann. Bot. (London) 17: 125. 1903. Protologue: Ecuador. Musci Amazonici et Andini. Andes Quitensis, Legit Ric. Spruce 139 (BM, NY). 

Plants small, in tufts, dark-green, reddish green to reddish yellow, corticolous. Stems 10–18 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand absent, cortical cells thin-walled, hyaline,  uniform throughout, densely tomentose; rhizoids smooth, densely branched, branches often at right-angles. Leaves 3–4 mm long, spathulate to obovate, erect at base, concave, evenly spaced, erect-crispate, contorted or stiffly erect-incurved when dry, spreading when wet; apices acute, cuspidate, apex usually elongated into a stout proboscis; margins entire, recurved below, plane to inflexed above; costa narrow, percurrent into a stout proboscis, ventral surface cells rectangular, smooth on both surfaces, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band well-developed, ventral and dorsal surface cells enlarged, smooth; upper cells subquadrate, hexagonal, rhomboidal or short-rectangular, those near the costa enlarged and bulging, those near the margins short, subquadrate, median leaf cells 24–50 x 16–30 μm, thin- or firm-walled, at times porose, somewhat bulging near costa, smooth, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 18–90 x 15–30 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Asexually reproducing by clavate or cylindrical, multicellular, smooth propagula in tufts on leaf apices. Dioicous. Setae smooth, 6 mm long, reddish yellow. Capsules cylindrical, erect, 3–4 mm long, smooth, yellowish brown; exothecial cells short-rectangular, thick-walled; stomata at base of capsule; opercula conical, 1.5 mm long, annuli 2–3 rows of vesiculose cells, adherent to capsule mouth on dehiscence; peristome 1.2 mm long, teeth red, filamentous, spiculose, twisted 1/2 turn, basal membrane short, red above, hyaline at base. Spores granular, 12–22 μm. Calyptra not seen.

Leptodontium wallisii (C. Müll.) Kindb., Enum. Bryin. Exot. 63: 1888.

Trichostomum wallisii C. Müll., Linnaea 38: 603. 1874.  Protologue: Colombia. Nova Granata, prov. Antioquia, Paramo de Ruiz 13,000 ped. altum in locis paludosis sphagnosis: G. Wallis 1872.

Didymodon wallisi C. Müll. in Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1871-1872: 362. 1873. Based on. Colombia. Patria: Amerika austral., Nova Granata, prov. Antioquia, Paramo de Ruiz 13000' (G. Wallis Nr. 186), nom. nud. 

Plants medium-sized in loose tufts, yellowish brown, 2.5–6 cm high. Stems red, erect or laxly ascending, hyalodermis present, sparsely radiculose. Leaves spreading,  flexuose to crispate and twisted when dry, wide-spreading to squarrose when wet, lanceolate from an high, oblong sheathing base, 3–4 mm long, keeled above, strongly erect-sheathing at base, moderately decurrent; apices acuminate; margins recurved in lower 1/2–2/3, dentate to minutely crenulate in upper 1/3; costa subpercurrent to percurrent; upper leaf cells irregularly quadrate, subrectangular or triangular, firm-walled with rounded corners, pluripapillose, papillae crowded,  simple to multifid, 7.5–15 x 10–12 μm, median leaf cells longer, with thicker, often porose cell walls, inner basal cells long, narrowly rectangular, with thick, often sinuose-porose cell walls, 37–87 x 7.5–10 μm, papillae scattered, outer 1–3 rows of basal cells wide, short-rectangular, smooth, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Sporophytes not known in Central America, description based on South American plants. Setae straight, 10–17 mm long, yellow-brown (sometimes reddish). Capsules erect, cylindrical, 1.5–2 mm long, smooth when dry; exothecial cells subquadrate to short-rectangular; stomata at base of urn; operculum not seen; peristome teeth linear, irregularly divided nearly to the base, yellow-brown, smooth to indistinctly striate and papillose. Spores 20–40 μm, papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Gymnostomiella vernicosa (Harv. in Hook.) Fleisch., Musci Buitenzorg 1: 310. 1904.

Gymnostomum vernicosum Harv. in Hook, Icon. Pl. 1: tab. 17, f. 4. 1836. Pottia vernicosa (Harv. in Hook.) Hampe in C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 557. 1849. Hymenostylium vernicosum (Harv. in Hook.) Mitt., J. Proc. Linn. Soc., Bot. Suppl. 1: 33. 1859. Protologue: Burma. Prome, leg. N. Wallich s.n. (isotype E, Arts 1998).

Gymnostomum vernicosum Hook. in Wallich. Numer. List 7549. 1832. nom. nud.

Gymnostomiella orcuttii Bartr.,  Jamaica Naturalist 1: 15. 1928. Protologue: Jamaica. Sherwood Forest, St. Thomas Parish, Jamaica, September 1927, C. R. Orcutt, No 2786, on concrete walls of reservoir near the “Great House.” 

Plants very small, delicate, light-green, in tufts or mats, 1–3 mm high. Stems simple or forked, reddish, surface cells rectangular, central strand absent; rhizoids sparse only at base. Axillary hairs 2-3 cells long, upper 1–2 cells globose, basal cells quadrate, light-brown. Leaves 0.3–0.6 mm long, spathulate, oblong-obovate or elliptic, erect to spreading at base, more or less rosulate, erect and somewhat shriveled when dry, erect-spreading when wet; apices broadly rounded to obtuse; lamina unistratose; margins papillose-crenulate, plane; costa slender, ending well below the apex, often spurred above, upper ventral surface cells elongate, stereid cells absent, cells homogeneous; upper cells irregularly hexagonal, subquadrate to short-rectangular, 10–28 x 10–14 μm, thin-walled, translucent, with 2-4 simple papillae, basal cells  long-rectangular, hyaline, smooth, 20–46 x 12–18 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Brood bodies brown, ellipsoid to cylindric, multicellular, on rhizoids, in leaf axils, or terminal cups. Setae smooth, 3–6 mm long, yellow, becoming reddish with age. Capsules ovoid, erect, 0.5–0.8 mm long, smooth; exothecial cells hexagonal, thin-walled; stomata in neck; opercula obliquely rostrate, 0.5–0.8 mm long; annuli rudimentary, of several rows of quadrate cells, often adhering to the capsule mouth after dehiscence; peristome absent. Spores 10–12 μm, smooth to lightly roughened. Calyptrae yellow, cucullate, smooth, 1.0–1.3 mm long.

Erpodium beccarii C. Müll. in Vent., Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital. 4: 18. 1872.

Aulacopilum beccarii (C. Müll. in Vent.) Mitt. ex Par., Index Bryol. (ed. 2) 2: 156. 1904. Protologue: Ethiopia. In truncis Doberae glabarae Kessareth secus viam a massauah ad Keren, in regiones Bogos Abyssiniae septentr. [Beccari] (lectotype NY).

Erpodium paraguense Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 21: 265. 1877. Protologue:  Paraguay.  Assomption, sur les troncs d’arbres, mai 1877, [Balansa] 1214.

Erpodium lorentzianum C. Müll., Linnaea 42: 384. 1879. Protologue: Argentina. Argentinia subtropica, in sylvis ad Orán, (Urundey ?), 15 Septbr. 1873d, [Lorentz].

Erpodium opuntiae Card., Rev. Bryol. 37: 6. 1910. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Oaxaca: environs de Oaxaca, sur Opuntia, 1894, Pringle 31a (FH, MICH, MO, NY).

Plants dark-green, somewhat hoary, usually in dense mats. Leaves appressed when dry, wide-spreading to more or less complanate when wet, 0.8–1.5 mm long (including subulae), usually asymmetric, ovate; apices ending in a serrulate, hyaline subula; median leaf cells hexagonal, thin-walled, 11–20 μm long, pluripapillose, lower cells oblate-hexagonal in numerous rows at margin. Perichaetial leaves enlarged. Setae 0.2–0.3 mm long. Capsules immersed, oblong-cylindric, 1.0–1.3 mm long; opercula conic-rostrate; annuli persistent, compound, consisting of 5–6 rows of pale cells; peristome absent. Spores 29–40 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, papillose, plicate, plicae scabrous.

Erpodium domingense (Spreng.) Brid. ex C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 1: 774. 1843.

Anoectangium domingense Spreng., Neue Entdeck. Pflanzenk. 3: 3. 1822. Anoectangium Erpodium domingense (Spreng.) Brid., Bryol. Univ. 2: 167. 1827. Pilotrichum domingense (Spreng.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 184. 1851. Protologue: Dominican Republic. Ad corticem Guaiaci verticalis Orteg. in Hispaniola. Bertero (lectotype NY; isolectotype FH).

Pilotrichum diversifolium C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 20: 392. 1862. Erpodium diversifolium (C. Müll.) Ångstr. ex Kindb., Enum. Bryin. Exot. 14. 1888.  Protologue: Mexico, ad Laguna di Terminos in Mangifera indica: Dr. S. Hógberg  (lectotype NY; isolectotype FH). 

Plants green, or yellow to brown, usually in dense mats. Stems and branches subjulaceous. Leaves loosely appressed when dry, spreading and usually complanate when moist, 0.5–0.9 mm long, asymmetric, ovate to elliptic; apicesrounded to obtuse; cells pluripapillose, upper cells rounded-hexagonal, 14–19 μm long, basal cells more or less oblate-hexagonal in numerous rows at the margins. Perichaetial leaves sheathing, not enlarged. Sporophytes shortly exserted; setae to 0.5 mm long, usually slightly curved. Capsules to 1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome absent. Spores 26–32 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, papillose, slightly plicate, plicae not scabrous.

Mironia crassicuspis (Robins.) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Hist. 32: 112. 1993.

Barbula crassicuspis Robins., Bryologist 67: 446. 1964 [1965]. Morinia crassicuspis (Robins.) Zand., Bryologist 81: 557. 1978 [1979]. Protologue: Mexico. Park like area at edge of grassland, Llano de las Flores in Sierra Juarez, Oaxaca, Sharp, Dec. 21, 1962 (F, MO isotypes). 

Plants small to medium-sized, reddish green above, reddish brown below, to 25  mm high. Stems red, erect, irregularly branched, sclerodermis present, central strand well-developed, rhizoids red, smooth, at base of and scattered on stems. Leaves 2–3 mm long, sheathing at base, erect-incurved, twisted when dry, spreading-recurved when wet, oblong-lanceolate, leaf tips enlarged, thickened, caducous; apices acuminate; margins bistratose, recurved to base of caducous tips, entire, not bordered, somewhat decurrent at base; costa subpercurrent, smooth at back, ventral surface cells rectangular, pluripapillose, guide cells, small ventral substereid band, and dorsal substereid to stereid bands present, upper ventral surface layer somewhat enlarged, papillose; upper cells 4–12 x 4–10 μm, firm-walled, oblate, irregularly quadrate, to short-rectangular, densely pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells smooth to lightly pluripapillose, rectangular thin, but firm-walled, not especially bulging, 40–60 x 6–14 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal, perichaetial leaves sheathing with an exceptionally long, caducous apex. Sporophytes unknown.

Mironia ehrenbergiana (C. Müll.) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Hist. 32: 112. 1993.

Barbula ehrenbergiana C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 636. 1849. Morinia ehrenbergiana (C. Müll.) Thér., Smithsonian Misc. Collect. 85(4): 22. 1931. Protologue: Mexico. C. Ehrenberg. 

Barbula trichostomoides Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 182. 1872. Morinia trichostomoides (Besch.) Card., Rev. Bryol. 37: 124. 1910. Protologue: Mexico. In valle Mexicensi, silva della Desierta Vieja (Bourg.[eau] n° 1335) (NY). 

Plants medium- to large-sized, red to reddish green above, red below, to 50 mm high. Stems red to reddish yellow, erect, irregularly branched, sclerodermis and central strand present; rhizoids matted at base, red, smooth, of two forms, small, highly branched ones and large, unbranched, solitary ones. Leaves 3–4 mm long, erect-sheathing at base, erect-twisted and incurved when dry, erect-spreading when wet, oblong to oblong-lanceolate; apices broadly acute; margins bistratose, narrowly recurved or revolute in lower 3/4, variously dentate in upper 1/5 to 1/2 entire, not bordered, somewhat decurrent at base; costa short-excurrent, into a short, stout mucro, smooth at back, ventral surface cells short-rectangular, pluripapillose, guide cells and two stereid bands present, upper ventral surface layer somewhat enlarged, papillose; upper cells 6–10 x 4–8 μm, firm-walled, oblate, irregularly quadrate, rhombic or short-rectangular, densely pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells smooth, rectangular,  thin-walled, not or weakly bulging, 30–80 x 8–16 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal; perichaetial leaves convolute. Setae 1–2 per perichaetium, smooth, 10–15 mm long, red to orange. Capsules cylindric, curved above when dry, 3.5–5.0 mm long, smooth; exothecial cells rectangular; stomata in neck; opercula erect, long-conic, 1.5–2.0 mm long; annuli of 1–2 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome to 1 mm long, with 32, red, filamentous, densely spiculose, spirally twisted teeth, basal membrane low. Spores 9–11 μm, lightly papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 6.0 mm long.

Gymnostomum aeruginosum Sm., Fl. Brit. 3: 1163. 1804.

Trichostomum aeruginosum (Sm.) Lindb., Öfvers. Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 21: 229. 1864. Mollia aeruginosa (Sm.) Lindb., Musci Scand. 106. 1879. Eucladium aeruginosum (Sm.) C. Jens., Danmarks Mosser 2: 313. 1923. Protologue: Wales. Gathered in North Wales by J. W. Griffith Esq.

Anoectangium arizonicum Bartr., Moss Fl. N. Amer. 1(3): 192. 1938. Protologue: U.S.A. Arizona: ledges back of Daly’s mine, White House Canyon, Santa Cruz Co. Alt. about 6,500 ft. [E. B. Bartram 919] (FH). 

Plants small and slender to medium-sized, forming tufts or caespitose, yellowish green to pale-green, saxicolous or terricolous. Stems 2–20 mm long, smooth, branching irregularly, sclerodermis and central strand usually present; rhizoids dimorphic: slender, red, smooth, branched ones scattered on the stem and massive, red, roughened, sparsely branched ones originating in leaf axils. Leaves somewhat distant and evenly spaced, wide‑spreading when wet, appressed when dry, apex contorted, ligulate to linear-lanceolate, 0.6–1.0 mm long; apices acute to obtuse or sometimes rounded; margins plane, entire to crenulate; costa ending just below apex, narrow, dorsal and ventral surfaces papillose, guide cells present, ventral stereid band not present in Central American material but weakly developed in robust collections outside the region, dorsal stereid band present, ventral surface cells enlarged, dorsal surface cells smaller than laminal cells and strongly thickened; upper leaf cells somewhat heterogeneous, rounded to quadrate sometimes transversely rectangular, 8–10 μm long, 1:1–2 (length:width), walls weakly thickened, papillose on both surfaces by scattered, low papillae, basal cells homogeneous, short-rectangular, 2–3:1 (length:width), thin-walled, smooth, marginal cells not differentiated, alar cells not differentiated. Gemmae in leaf axils. Dioicous. Perigonia terminal, geminate. Perichaetia terminal. Setae 4–6 mm long, yellow, smooth. Capsules exserted, erect, short-cylindrical, 0.5–0.8 mm long, smooth, brown; stomata in neck; opercula rostrate, beak erect, 0.5 mm long; peristome absent. Spores 9–12 μm, round, granulate, brown. Calyptrae cucullate, 0.7–1.0 mm long, smooth.

Pseudosymblepharis schimperiana (Par.) Crum, Bryologist 55: 139. 1952.

Syrrhopodon circinatus Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 172. 1872, hom. illeg.  Syrrhopodon schimperianus Par., Index Bryol. 1254. 1898, nom. nov.  Symblepharis schimperiana (Par.) Card., Rev. Bryol. 38: 99. 1911. Pseudosymblepharis circinata (Schimp.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. (ed. 2) 10: 261. 1924, illeg. type of earlier name included.  Protologue: Mexico. Orizaba, Cordova (F. Müller, 1853).

Tortella mollissima Broth. ex Bartr., Bryologist 50: 203. 1947. Trichostomum mollissimum (Broth. ex Bartr.) Crum, Bryologist 72: 245. 1969.  Protologue: Mexico, Zacuapán, Vera Cruz, on rocks, Dec., 1918, C.A. Purpus 9361. 

Plants medium-sized or robust, dull yellow-green to dark-green, in dense tufts or cushions, to 80 mm high. Stems red, erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis present, central strand weakly developed or absent; rhizoids moderately developed below, reddish brown, smooth. Leaves 5–8 mm long, erect, linear-lanceolate from a broadly ovate, clasping, sheathing base, incurved, spirally twisted and contorted, tubulose above when dry, spreading when wet; apices acute to acuminate, sharply mucronate; laminae fragile and often broken or eroded above; margins entire and plane; costa short excurrent, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer enlarged; upper cells sub-quadrate to short rectangular, 16–10 x 8–10 μm,  firm-walled, pluripapillose, basal cells near costa and junction of the sheath and limb rectangular, thick-walled and porose, outer and lower basal cells enlarged, 85–30 m x 10–25 μm, rectangular, thin-walled, bulging, hyaline, smooth, outer cells extending up the margins in a v-shaped pattern less than 1/4 the leaf length. Setae 1–2 per perichaetium, elongate, smooth, spirally twisted, 10–15 mm long, yellow, becoming red with age. Capsules narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–2 mm long, smooth to lightly wrinkled when dry; stomata in neck; opercula erect-rostrate, 1 mm long; annuli well-developed; peristome teeth 16, short, erect to weakly twisted, papillose. Spores 13–15 μm. Calyptrae smooth, 4 mm long.

Entosthodon lindigii (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 243. 1869.

Amphoritheca lindigii Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. sér. 5, 3: 341. 1865. Protologue: Colombia. Bogota, Pancho, alt 3200 metr., ad Barrancas, julio. leg. A. Lindig. Lectotype (Fife, 1987): Colombia (Nova Granata). Bogotá, Pacho, Jul 1863, A. Lindig s.n. (lectotype, BM; isolectotypes BM, NY). 

Plants yellow‑brown. Stems erect, to 4 mm high, simple or branching by subperigonial innovation, usually naked at base, leaves clustered above, with a single‑layered sclerodermis over 2–3 rows of small reddish thick‑walled cells, central strand present. Leaves erect when dry, slightly contorted, oblong to ovate-lanceolate, gradually tapered to a long, slender acumen, usually long-aristate, to 2 mm long, concave; margins entire; costa ending in acumen, sometimes fused with arista; apical cells 150–330 μm long, upper cells oblong-hexagonal, thin‑walled, smooth, 37–65 x 14–25 μm, not differentiated at the margins, toward the insertion longer more oblong, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae reddish brown, lightly twisted when dry, weakly hygroscopic, smooth at base, coarsely papillose in upper _, to 7 mm long. Capsules erect, reddish brown, narrowly pyriform to pyriform, neck 1/2 the capsule length, symmetric, mouth transverse, constricted below the mouth when dry, wrinkled to sulcate in the neck, smooth above, 1.2–1.5 mm long; exothecial cells elongate, thick-walled, shorter in the neck, becoming oblate and thick‑walled in more or less 6 rows at the mouth; stomata phaneroporous, numerous in neck; opercula plano‑convex; annuli simple; peristome double and rudimentary or absent. Spores 25–35 μm in diameter, coarsely bullate. Calyptrae cucullate‑rostrate, naked, smooth.

Plants small to large, creeping, to 15 cm long, or erect and dendroid, 2–5 cm tall, 1–2 cm wide, yellowish, light green to brownish green, glossy. Stems creeping to erect from stolons, stipitate, reg-ular to irregularly pinnate to bipinnate, loosely foliate, usually ending in a broad or rarely cuspidate tip; flagellate branchlets sometimes present. Pseudoparaphyllia foliose, narrowly to broadly ovate, margins serrulate. Stipe leaves appressed, scarious, tips recurved. Stem leaves erect to somewhat spreading, variously striate, slightly concave, oblong-lanceolate, 1.5–2.0 X 0.5–0.8 mm, often cusp-idate; margins serrate to serrulate above, serrulate to entire below, incurved in upper half or below; costae extending 1/2–2/3 the leaf length; cells smooth, rhombic near apex, 10–20 X 4–6 µm, linear-fusiform below, 16–36 X 4–6 µm, thick-walled throughout, porose toward the insertion; alar cells weakly differentiated, quadrate to rectangular, hyaline to yellowish, adjacent cells yellowish across base. Branch leaves erect to erect-spreading, often finely striate, concave, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 1.0–1.4 X 0.3–0.4 mm, gradually acute; margins serrate to serrulate at apex, weakly serrulate to en-tire below, slightly incurved above; costae extending 1/2–2/3 the leaf length; cells smooth, rhombic near apex, 14–20 X 4–5 µm, linear-fusiform below, 22–44 X 3–4 µm wide, thick-walled throughout; alar cells weakly developed, rectangular to quadrate or nearly rounded, hyaline to yellowish, adjacent cells yellowish across leaf insertion. Setae flexuose, 1.5–2.5 cm long. Capsules erect to inclined, cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long; opercula to 2 mm long.

Plants medium-sized to large, 3–20 cm long, yellowish to green or light green, glossy to dull. Stolons creeping; stems creeping to ascending and erect, stipitate, irregularly pinnate to bipinnate, complanate to terete-foliate, narrowed at tips, sometimes cuspidate; flagellate branchlets sometimes present. Pseudoparaphyllia foliose, broadly ovate, variable, ovate to lanceolate, rarely linear, serrate to serrulate on margins. Stipe leaves appressed to spreading, scarious. Stem leaves erect-spreading, complanate to somewhat concave, occasionally undulate, 1.5–3.0 X 0.6–1.5 mm, broadly acute to somewhat obtuse, often abruptly apiculate, rounded to slightly auriculate at base; margins irregularly serrate with unicellular or multicellular teeth near apex, serrate to serrulate in upper half, sometimes nearly entire, plane to incurved above; costae single, extending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, sometimes ending in a small spine on the dorsal surface; cells smooth, rhombic near apex, 10–22 X 4–6 µm, linear-fusiform below, 20–50 X 3–5 µm, thin- to thick-walled below, thick-walled above, porose through-out; alar cells weakly differentiated, of 2–5 short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions strongly porose, orange. Branch leaves erect-spreading, smooth, concave, oblong-lanceolate to oblong-ovate, 0.8–1.5 X 0.3–0.8 mm, abruptly acute, often apiculate, sometimes reddish or orange across insertions; margins irregularly serrate to serrulate above, sometimes incurved above, serrulate to entire below; costae single, extending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, sometimes weak and nearly lacking; cells smooth, rhombic above, 12–28 X 2–6 µm, linear-fusiform below, 18–42 X 2–4 µm; alar cells weakly differentiated, of 2–5 short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions strongly porose, orange to slightly reddish. Dioicous. Setae red, smooth, flexuose, 3.0–3.5 cm long. Capsules long-exserted, erect to inclined, ovoid, 1.5–3.0 mm long; exothecial cells short-rectangular to subquadrate, at times oblate, firm- to thick-walled; stomata superficial to somewhat immersed on capsule neck; opercula long-rostrate, 2–3 mm long; annuli large, compound, persistent on capsule mouth; peristome diplolepideous, inserted within the capsule mouth; exo

Groutiella chimborazensis (Spruce ex Mitt.) Florsch., Fl. Suriname 4: 215. 1964.

Macromitrium chimborazense Spruce ex Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 218. 1869. Micromitrium chimborazense (Spruce ex Mitt.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–72: 157. 1874. Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, ad radices occidentalis montis Chimborazo (3500 ped.), Spruce, n. 110 (NY).

Macromitrium durandi Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 31(1): 159. 1892. Protologue: Costa Rica. Forêts du Barba, Pitt. n° 5538 (NY).

Macromitrium undosum Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 108. 1909. Micromitrium undosum (Card.) Grout, Bryologist 47: 4. 1944. Craspedophyllum undosum (Card.) Grout, N. Amer. Fl. 15A: 41. 1946. Groutiella undosa (Card.) Crum & Steere, Bryologist 53: 147. 1950. Protologue: Mexico, Etat de Jalisco: Rio Blanco, rochers, 1908, [Pringle] n.10560 (FH, MO).

Plants small to medium-sized, greenish yellow to reddish yellow above, brown below. Stems creeping, branches to 5 mm long, densely tomentose. Leaves erect below, crispate to spirally contorted, at times undulate on upper margins when dry, erect‑spreading to erect‑recurved when wet, 2.0–2.5 mm long, lanceolate; apices gradually narrowed to the apex, acute to shortly acuminate; margins entire, plane or weakly recurved below, plane above, bordered in the lower _ to ½ by 3–4 rows of elongate, thick‑walled cells, basal marginal cells inflated, at times with rhizoids; costae percurrent, rarely excurrent; upper cells 6–8 μm, rounded, flat, basal cells to 24 μm long, rectangular, those near the costa somewhat enlarged and thin‑walled. Dioicous. Setae 5–15 mm long, smooth. Capsules 2–4 mm long, oblong‑cylindrical, smooth to weakly furrowed, wrinkled at neck; opercula erect-rostrate, 1.5–2 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; peristome rudimentary, reduced to a short whitish membrane to 96 μm high. Spores isosporous, 26–44 μm, papillose, firm‑walled. Calyptrae to just below the capsule mouth, plicate above, naked or occasionally sparsely hairy, 2 mm long.

Syntrichia amphidiacea (C. Müll.) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Sci. 32: 267. 1993.

Barbula amphidiacea C. Müll., Linnaea 38: 639. 1874. Tortula amphidiacea (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 434. 1902. Protologue: Mexico, monte Orizaba: Freder. Müller inter alios muscos legit. Hb. Lorentz sub Zygodon..

Tortula caroliniana Andr., Bryologist 23: 72. 1920. Protologue: U.S.A. Bank of Swannanoa River at Swannanoa, Buncombe Co., July 9; North Fork, some 5 miles above its confluence with Swannanoa River, July 10; Grandmother Gap, Avery Co., Aug. 13; all in North Carolina, 1919. 

Plants small, scattered or in loose tufts, yellowish green to reddish green, corticolous. Stems 5–15 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand present, sclerodermis present; rhizoids smooth, densely branched clustered at base of stem. Leaves spathulate, oblong or oblong-ovate, erect at base, twisted and irregularly contorted when dry, erect-spreading when wet; apices acute, apiculate; laminae unistratose; margins entire to crenulate, at times bordered by thick-walled, colored cells, plane above, recurved below; costa narrow, subpercurrent to percurrent, ventral surface cells quadrate, smooth, guide cells and single (dorsal stereid band) present, ventral surface layer of enlarged cells present; upper cells irregularly rounded-quadrate, hexagonal, short-rectangular, oblate, or triangular, 8–22 x 8–20 μm, firm-walled, irregularly thickened to collenchymatous, lightly pluripapillose, the papillae low, o-shaped, scattered over the lumina, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 36–100 x 12–22 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Asexually reproducing by gemmae on leaf laminae near apex, usually on ventral, but sometimes on dorsal surface, gemmae multicellular with both vertical and horizontal cell walls. Dioicous. Setae smooth, 6–8 mm long, red. Capsules exserted, cylindrical, erect, 2–3 mm long, smooth, red; stomata not seen; opercula rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; peristome teeth 0.5–1.0 mm long, irregularly twisted, basal membrane short. Spores 18–22 μm, granulate. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2.5 mm long.

Syntrichia bogotensis (Hampe) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Sci. 32: 267. 1993.

Barbula bogotensis Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. sér. 5, 3: 349. 1865. Tortula bogotensis (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 171. 1869. Protologue: Colombia. Bogota, Guadalupe, altit. 2900 metr., in nemorib., August. 1863 leg. Lindig.

Tortula guatemalensis Bartr., Bryologist 49: 114. 1946. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. San Marcos: between San Sebastián and summit of Volcán Tajumulco, alt. 3800–4600 m., Steyermark 35564 (F). 

Plants large, green to brownish green, in tufts, corticolous. Stems 10–50 mm high,  irregularly branched, central strand weakly developed, hyalodermis present; rhizoids dense at base of stems, smooth, red, densely branched. Axillary hairs 10–13 cells long, all cells hyaline. Leaves evenly spaced, 3–6 mm long, lingulate to ovate-lanceolate, clasping at base, twisted and crisped when dry, squarrose-recurved when wet; apices acute to acuminate, tapered to a long, reddish, sparsely spinulose awn; lamina unistratose, often fragile above; margins irregularly wavy, entire, plane or occasionally recurved near middle; costa long-excurrent, ventral surface cells quadrate, papillose, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band present, ventral surface layer of enlarged cells present; upper cells round, quadrate, hexagonal, to short-rectangular, 10–24 x 12–16 μm, firm-walled, irregularly thickened, collenchymatous, densely pluripapillose, papillae at times branched, inner basal cells abruptly enlarged, hyaline, rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 34–90 x 16–20 μm, outer basal cells, yellow, longer and narrower, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae smooth, 10 mm long, brown. Capsules exserted, cylindrical, erect, 3–4 mm long, brown, smooth; stomata not seen; opercula rostrate, 1–2 mm long; peristome teeth 1.0 mm long, twisted 1/2 turn, basal membrane short. Spores 12–16 μm, granulate. Calyptra not seen.

Plants robust, in green, yellow green, occasionally reddish yellow, lax tufts. Primary stems creep-ing; leaves reduced, scale-like; rhizoids red, smooth to lightly roughened, irregularly branched, from circular clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions. Secondary stems erect, dendroid, often reg-ularly pinnately branched, also simple or irregularly branched, 8–50 cm long; cross section with scle-rodermis of 3–6 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hya-line, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent, scale leaves present; rhizoids present at base of secondary stems. Secondary stem and branch leaves differing pri-marily in size, leaves long, narrowly lanceolate from an ovate base, plicate, apices intact or fragile, 3–6 mm long, erect to wide-spreading when dry, wide-spreading to subsquarrose when wet, decur-rent, acuminate; margins plane, sometimes narrowly recurved below, coarsely serrate above, teeth uni- or multicellular, marginal cells at times obscurely to distinctly differentiated; costae single, per-current to subpercurrent, at times wavy above, in cross section at base with two rows of guide cells, dorsal and ventral stereid cells in multiple rows; cells unipapillose, upper cells rhombic to elliptic, porose, 10–20 # 4–6 µm; basal cells near costa fusiform to linear, porose, 20–60 # 4–8 µm; alar cells confined to the basal angles, quadrate to oblate. Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia gemmate, lateral along the secondary stems; inner perichaetial leaves aristate. Setae short, 1.0–1.5 mm long, red, smooth. Capsules shortly exserted, ovoid, red, 2–3 mm long; exothecial cells short-rectangular to sub-quadrate, firm-walled; stomata phaneroporic, on capsule neck; opercula rostrate, 1 mm long; annuli complex, deciduous; peristome diplolepideous, yellowish white; exostome teeth linear, smooth to weakly papillose at very base, densely papillose above; endostome reduced, smooth to weakly papil-lose at very base, densely papillose above, 0.8 mm long, basal membranes low, segments linear, not keeled, united at the tips, cilia absent. Spores lightly papillose, 14–20 µm. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, naked, 2.5–3 mm long.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in yellow green, loose or dense mats. Primary stems creeping, with small, imbricate-appressed, distantly spaced, ecostate, lanceolate leaves, 0.4–0.8 mm long; rhi-zoids red brown, smooth, not or irregularly branched, from clusters of initials at abaxial side of pri-mary stem leaf insertions, and at base of stipes. Secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect and stipi-tate, with evenly foliate stipe leaves or pendent, irregularly pinnate-branched, branches at times becoming flagellate, 4–10 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 4–8 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellowish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous. Secondary stem leaves tumid to laxly imbricate, at times loosely spreading, 2.0–3.5 mm long, ovate, shortly acute, concave, rounded at base, strongly decurrent; margins entire below, serrulate to denticulate above, plane; costae single, slender, ending at or somewhat above midleaf, in cross section cells homogeneously thick-walled; cells linear-flexuose, smooth, porose and firm-walled throughout, apical cells 14–48 # 4–10 r m, me-dian cells 28–64 # 4–10 r m; basal cells 40–90 # 6 r m, cells across the insertions yellowish red; alar cells very well developed, quadrate to oblate in 10–30 rows, incrassate, 9–24 # 9–22 r m. Branch leaves somewhat smaller (1.5–3.0 mm long) than the secondary stem leaves, but otherwise similar. Asexual gemmae common, from circular clusters of initials in leaf axils, cylindrical, uniseriate, but occasionally biseriate at the tips, 3–12 cells long, gemmae becoming secondarily elongate, cells smaller and papillose-roughened. Sporophyte unknown.

Plants small to medium-sized, in green to yellow green, lax tufts or masses on trees. Primary stems creeping, with small, erect to imbricate, distantly spaced leaves; rhizoids red brown, smooth to roughened, not or irregularly branched, from clusters of initials at abaxial side of primary stem leaf insertions and at base of secondary stems. Secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect, not stipitate, not or rarely branched, stem tips at times becoming flagellate, 1–4 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow-ish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia fil-amentous; leaves wide-spreading to squarrose, 1–3 mm long, broadly ovate to ovate-lanceolate, acute to broadly acuminate, concave, cordate at base, not or very shortly decurrent; margins entire to lightly serrulate below, serrulate above, plane; costae variable, short, faint and either single or double or sin-gle, slender and reaching just beyond midleaf; cells linear-flexuose, smooth, porose and firm-walled throughout, apical cells 32–50 # 4–6 µm, median cells 40–60 # 4–6 µm; basal cells to 70 µm long; alar cells weakly developed, of a few irregularly subquadrate, incrassate cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions yellow. Asexual reproduction by smooth, hyaline, uniseriate, septate gemmae arising from large, circular clusters of initials in leaf axils, germinating from both ends, new filaments coarsely papillose. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves sheathing the lower 1/3 of the setae, 2–3 mm long. Setae smooth to lightly roughened below, reddish brown, 4–6 mm long. Capsules erect, symmetric, short-cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exothecial cells at mouth red, quadrate to oblate, thick-walled, in 6–8 rows, lower exothecial cells short-rectangular, firm-walled; stomata absent; opercula conic-rostrate, 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, of firm-walled cells; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth pale yellow, rudimentary, truncate-triangular, to 100 µm long, smooth to finely roughened, weakly trabeculate, prostome present; endostome absent. Spores round, smooth to lightly papillose, 22–28 µm. Calyptra not seen (“cucullate, naked, slightly roughened,” Buck 1998).

Ptychomitrium lepidomitrium (C. Müll.) Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 185. 1872. 

Brachysteleum lepidomitrium C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 767. 1849. Glyphomitrium lepidomitrium (C. Müll.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 106. 1869. Protologue: Mexico, M. Orizaba: Liebmann.

Brachysteleum cylindrothecium C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 199. 1897. Ptychomitriuim cylindrothecium (C. Müll.) Par., Index Bryol. 1056. 1897. Protologue: Guatemala. Cuesta de Argueta. [Bernoulli & Cario] N° 95. 

Plants medium-sized to robust in loose tufts, dark‑green. Stems erect, to 4 cm high; rhizoids sparse. Leaves erect at base, crisped and contorted, sometimes lightly rugose above when dry, erect‑incurved to erect‑spreading when wet, 5–6 mm long, ovate‑lanceolate; apex acuminate; margins narrowly recurved below, bistratose, coarsely dentate above; costa stout, percurrent, with two stereid bands; lamina unistratose; upper cells 6–8 μm, irregularly quadrate to short‑rectangular, thick‑walled, basal cells 28–40 μm long, linear, porose, thick‑walled, alar cells more or less bulging, rectangular. Setae 1–7 per perichaetium, yellow, 4–7 mm long. Capsules 2–3 mm long, narrowly cylindric, erect; stomata at base of capsule; opercula erect, long‑rostrate, 1.0–1.3 mm long; annuli compound, revoluble; peristome teeth linear, red, densely papillose, deeply divided nearly to the base, 0.7–1.0 mm long. Spores 8–10 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae , 2.5–3 mm long, yellow, mitrate, lobed, scabrous above, occasionally with thick, erect hairs.

Rhabdoweisia fugax (Hedw.) B.S.G., Bryol. Eur. 1: 98. 1846. Weissia fugax Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 64. 1801. Type. Germany, Sudeten, Ludwig. Neotype. Germany, Sudeten, Musci frondosi 260, Breutel (designated by Lawton 1961).

Rhabdoweisia fugax var. tenerrima Bartr., Bryologist 50: 203. 1947. Syntypes. Guatemala, San Marcos, Sharp 5413a; Quezaltenango, Sharp 5035 (FH, US).

 Plants small, loosely tufted; stems 2–3 mm high. Leaves to 2 mm long, linear-lanceolate, acuminate; margins plane or weakly recurved below, entire to minutely crenulate above; costa ending below the apex; upper leaf cells rounded quadrate; basal cells elongate, hyaline. Setae 2–3 mm long; capsules 0.5–0.8 mm long, ribbed when dry; opercula as long as the capsule; peristome teeth very fragile, smooth, filiform or subulate.

Trichostomum tenuirostre (Hook. & Tayl.) Lindb., Öfvers. Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 21: 225. 1864. Weisia tenuirostris Hook. & Tayl., Muscol. Brit. (ed. 2) 83. 1827. Oxystegus tenuirostris (Hook. & Tayl.) A. Smith, J. Bryol. 9: 393. 1977. Protologue: Scotland and Ireland. Moist rocks, in fructification at Campsie, near Glasgow, Scotland.–About Powerscourt Waterfall, near Dublin. 

Weissia cylindrica Bruch ex Brid., Bryol. Univ. Vol. 1. 806. 1827. Trichostomum cylindricum (Bruch ex Brid.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 586. 1849. Oxystegus cylindricus (Brid. ex Brid.) Hilp., Bot. Centralbl. 50(2): 620. 1933. Protologue: Germany. In saxis ad aggeres umbrosos viarum sylvaticarum prope Bipontium clar. Bruchius detexit et communicavit. 

Plants small to medium-sized, green, dark-green, or yellow-green above, yellow to brown often shiny at base, in tufts, 5–15 (–30) mm high. Stems red, erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis present, central strand weakly developed; rhizoids weakly developed below, reddish brown, lightly roughened. Leaves 3–5 mm long, lanceolate, erect and appressed to stem at base, incurved-contorted, curled, concave above when dry, erect-spreading to flexuose when wet; apices acute, mucronate; lamina unistratose, at times fragile and broken or eroded above; margins entire, plane or erect, often undulate; costa shortly excurrent, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer enlarged, papillose; upper cells rounded-quadrate, oblate, to short-rectangular, 7–12 μm long, firm-walled, pluripapillose, basal cells long rectangular to oblong,  firm- or thin-walled, hyaline, smooth, shorter and thicker-walled in upper part of base, 20–40 x 12 μm, outer basal cells running up the margins in a weak v-shaped pattern. Dioicous. Sporophytes not known from Central America. Setae 10–15 mm long, Capsules 1.5–3.0 mm long, cylindrical; opercula obliquely long-conic to rostrate; annuli of 1–2 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome teeth erect, 160–240 μm high, weakly to strongly papillose, or striolate. Spores 13–20 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, naked (Allen 2000a).

Plants medium-sized, in green to yellow green, loose mats, often pendent. Primary stems creep-ing, with erect to imbricate, distantly spaced leaves; rhizoids red brown, smooth, not or irregularly branched, from clusters of initials at abaxial side of primary stem leaf insertions and at base of stipes.

Secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect, stipitate, irregularly pinnate-branched, 3–8 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 2–4 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellowish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous. Primary stem leaves erect to imbricate, ovate, abruptly narrowed to long flexuose apices, to 1.0 mm long, not decurrent; ecostate. Secondary stem and branch leaves closely spaced, erect-spreading when dry, 2.5–4.2 mm long, ovate to obovate, deeply concave, rarely somewhat rugose, with long, narrow flexuose acumina, auriculate and clasping at base, not decurrent; margins entire below, weakly serrulate above; costa none; cells linear-flexuose, thick-walled and porose throughout, smooth, 35–85 X 6–10 mm, cells of the acumen and auriculate base somewhat shorter; alar cells orange red, weakly developed, in a small, bulging-excavate group, somewhat en-larged, rhombic to short-rectangular cells across the leaf base orange red, thick-walled. Dioicous (?). Perigonia, perichaetia, and sporophytes unknown.

Sphagnum gomezii Crum, Cryptogamie, Bryol. Lichénol. 5: 295. 1984.

Sphagnum subdivisum Crum, Bryologist 92: 98. 1989, syn. nov.

Plants slender, pale, pinkish or pinkish violet, especially in the capitulum; stems and branches red; cortical cells in 3 layers, rectangular, rarely uniporose; wood cylinder red. Stem leaves 1.6–2 mm long, oblong-ovate, broadly acute, concave toward the apex, sometimes more or less pinched at the tip, bordered all around but not wide-bordered at base; hyaline cells divided into 2–4 compartments, on the outer surface more or less fibrillose toward the leaf tip, with 1–4 large, round or oval membrane gaps or occasionally membrane pleats, on the inner surface largely resorbed or some cells with 1 or more large, round or oval gaps and some few vestiges of fibrils and some cells with pleats but no fibrils. Branches in fascicles of 3 (2 spreading); cortical retort cells differentiated. Branch leaves 1.4–1.6 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, bordered by 2–3 rows of linear cells; hyaline cells strongly bulging on the outer surface, nearly plane on the inner, on the outer surface with numerous ringed, narrowly elliptic commissural pores, those at adjacent cell corners noticeably in 3's, on the inner surface with pores lacking or with 1(–2) large, round, unringed pores, at side regions with 1–3 round gaps about as wide as the cells, at the basal margins with as many as 5 gaps; green cells in section triangular to trapezoidal, with exclusive or broader exposure on the inner surface.

Plants medium-sized, in glaucous green, greenish yellow, or reddish yellow mats. Primary stems
inconspicuous, creeping, sympodially branched, leaves reduced; rhizoids rare, densely clustered at
base of sympodial branches, red, smooth, more or less unbranched. Secondary stems prominent, prostrate
or erect, irregularly branched from all sides of the stems; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–5
rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow, thick-walled, central
strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, upper cell oblong
yellowish hyaline, lower cell subquadrate, red. Secondary stem and branch leaves oblong to broadly
elliptic, often panduriform, 1–2 mm long, erect to erect-spreading when dry, erect-spreading when
wet, ending in a long, yellow, red, or hyaline hair-point, decurrent; margins narrowly recurved at base,
broadly incurved above, serrulate; costa absent; cells linear-flexuose, 40–50 x 6 μm, thick-walled,
porose, densely covered by a finely papillose reticulum; marginal cells longer, narrower, smooth,
forming a distinct border; cells at the insertions smooth, linear, strongly porose, yellow to red; alar
cells extensively developed, oblong to subquadrate, extremely thick-walled, porose, smooth. Dioicous.
Perigonia gemmate, lateral on secondary stems and branches, 1–2 mm long. Perichaetia terminal,
red, 3–5 mm long; leaves erect, elongate, very long hair-pointed, cells elongate-flexuose, strongly
porose, smooth to prorate from both ends, yellow red; alar cells not differentiated. Sporophytes not
seen in Central America, description based on plants from Mexico and Colombia. Setae elongate,
dark red, 8–25 mm long, smooth below, lightly papillose below the capsule. Capsules erect, ovoid,
3 mm long, irregularly furrowed, wide-mouthed, constricted at neck; exothecial cells small, red, thickwalled
in several rows below the mouth, enlarged, irregularly long-rectangular below, moderately
firm-walled throughout; cells in neck isodiametric, extremely thick-walled, mammillose-bulging;
stomata deeply immersed on neck; opercula obliquely long-rostrate, to 2 mm long; annuli rudimentary,
reduced to a single-cell abscission layer; peristome absent. Spores tetrahedral, finely papillose
on one side, with trilete scar on opposite side, 20–28 μm. Calyptrae cucullate, reddish brown, smooth,
3–4 mm long.

Pyrrhobryum spiniforme (Hedw.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 10: 174. 1868.

Hypnum spiniforme Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 236. 1801. Rhizogonium spiniforme (Hedw.) Bruch in Kraus, Flora 29: 134. 1846. Mnium spiniforme (Hedw.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 175. 1848. Protologue. Jamaica. Habitat in Jamaica, primo inventum a Sloanio. 

Plants medium- to robust-sized in loose, dark‑green to reddish‑brown tufts. Stems erect, to 7 cm high, simple or forked, sparsely or densely tomentose below; rhizoids branched red. Leaves distant, erect-contorted to incurved when dry, spreading when wet, (3.5–)5.0–8.0 mm long, linear‑setaceous to linear‑lanceolate not or scarcely decurrent; apices long acuminate; margins bistratose, coarsely doubly serrate from near base; costae stout, spinose at back, dorsal surface covered with quadrate to rectangular cells, percurrent or shortly excurrent; upper cells 10–20 μm long, irregular in size and shape, mostly rounded to rounded‑quadrate, occasionally rectangular to elongate, thick‑walled, not porose, smooth, basal cells similar to upper cells except more sharply angled. Synoicous or autoicous. Inflorescences small and bud‑like, arising from tomentum at base of stems. Setae 3.5–7.0 cm long, erect‑flexuose, smooth, red. Capsules 2–3 mm long, oblong‑cylindrical and curved or long‑cupulate and more or less erect, constricted at base; opercula short and stoutly or long and slenderly obliquely rostrate, 2–4 mm long; exostome lanceolate, brownish‑red, cross‑striate below, yellow to hyaline, papillose above, endostome yellowish, basal membrane high, segments stout, narrowly perforate, cilia 2–3, well‑developed, nodose. Spores 16–18 μm, faintly roughened. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, to 4 mm long.
