mouth, becoming short-rectangular below; stomata present; opercula high-conic, to 1 mm long; annuli
of 1–2 rows of enlarged, thick-walled cells; exostome white to yellow, narrowly triangular, dorsal
(outer) surface weakly cross-striate at base, papillose above; endostome papillose, to 1/2 the exostome
length, segments narrow, perforate, basal membrane 0.05–0.15 mm high, cilia absent. Spores
papillose, 11–22 μm. Calyptrae cucullate, naked, smooth.

Ceuthotheca cryptocarpa (Bartr.) Lewinsky‑Haapasaari, Lindbergia 19: 18. 1994.

Pleurorthotrichum cryptocarpum Bartr., Ann. Bryol. 11: 25. 1938. Protologue: Costa Rica. General, 950 m, Cespedez 183 (Holotype FH).

Plants medium-sized, olive‑green to yellow‑green above, brown below. Stems creeping to 4 cm long, branches erect, simple or forked, to 25 mm long, reddish tomentose below. Leaves erect at base, flexuose‑crispate, at times undulate and spirally contorted above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, to 3 mm long, ovate‑lanceolate, moderately keeled; apices acuminate; margins denticulate throughout, plane or erect, not tuberculate at basal margins; costae percurrent; upper cells 8–14 μm, rounded, strongly bulging to mammillose, thick‑walled, marginal cells rhomboidal forming a more or less distinct border, basal cells not tuberculate, 30–50 μm long, elongate‑rectangular, incrassate and porose. Phyllodioicous. Male plants to 200 μm high; perichaetial leaves 5–6 mm long, oblong‑lanceolate, abruptly long‑aristate; margins denticulate above; costae long-excurrent; cells elongate, sharply prorate. Setae 0.24–0.5 mm long. Capsules immersed, 2–3 mm long, ovoid, smooth; stomata superficial, at capsule base; operculum not seen; exostome red, united into low, papillose membrane, 100 μm long, endostome white to hyaline, coarsely papillose, basal membrane low, segments stout, to 500 μm high. Spores anisosporous: 20–25 μm and papillose or to 50 μm and smooth to lightly papillose. Calyptrae deeply laciniate, hairy, 2 mm long.

Hymenostylium jacksharpii (Crum) Allen, comb. nov.

Barbula jacksharpii Crum, Bryologist 87: 204. 1984. Gymnostomum jacksharpii (Crum) Allen, Bryologist 93: 207. 1990. Protologue: Guatemala. Guatemala, Huehuetenango, above San Juan Ixcoy, “on bank of calcareous creek, 7500 ft alt., A. J. Sharp 4982, Jan. 5, 1946.”

Dicranoweisia calcarea Bartr., Bryologist 49: 111. 1946. Dicranella calcarea (Bartr.) Crum, Bryologist 87: 204. 1984. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. Huehuetenango: above San Juan Ixcoy, Sierra de los Cuchumatanes, alt. 2400 m., Steyermark 50001. 

Plants medium-sized to robust, in tufts, lime-encrusted, yellow-green, terricolous. Stems erect, 2–6 cm high, smooth, forked, sclerodermis present, central strand absent; rhizoids red-brown, smooth. Leaves ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm long, spreading when wet, loosely spreading with incurved, contorted tips when dry, decurrent; apices long, gradually acuminate to a slender, blunt tip; margins erect to recurved below, entire; costa ending just below the apex to percurrent, dorsal surface smooth, ventral surface smooth, guide cells and two stereid bands present, ventral surface cells not enlarged; upper cells quadrate to subquadrate at the margins, short-rectangular near costa, 10–28 x 8–10 μm, thick-walled, smooth, basal cells short-rectangular at margins, otherwise elongate-rectangular, 36–80 x 4–10 μm, thick-walled, nodose-pitted to straight-walled, smooth, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous (?); perichaetia terminal, not strongly differentiated. Setae 8–10 mm long, reddish brown, smooth. Capsules exserted, inclined to erect, short cylindrical, 1.5 mm long, smooth, brown; annuli persistent at mouth; peristome absent. Operculum, calyptra, and spores not seen.

Plants small, in green, yellow green, or reddish green mats. Primary stems creeping. Secondary
stems horizontal or erect, pinnately branched, to 5 cm long; cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6
rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm-walled,
central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose and with scale leaves; rhizoids
red, smooth, not or weakly branched, from circular clusters of initials at abaxial side of leaf insertions
and extending onto the costae at the leaf bases. Leaves dimorphic; secondary stem leaves lanceolate,
1.6–2.2 mm long, erect-patent when dry, erect when wet, gradually and broadly acuminate, shortly
decurrent; margins lightly recurved in lower 1/2, at times plane, entire to serrulate above; costae
strong, 0.6–0.9 the leaf length; cells smooth and thick-walled, basal, median, and apical cells linear,
18–28 μm long, median cells 25–45 μm long; basal cells near costae to 95 μm long; alar cells rounded
to subquadrate, 8–14 μm; branch leaves ovate, costae 0.3–0.6 the leaf length, margins nearly always
plane. Autoicous. Perichaetia lateral, leaves oblong to oblong-lanceolate, inner ones abruptly narrowed
to long, smooth to papillose aristae, more or less equal to leaf length, costae discontinuous,
stoutly filling the apex, ending at midleaf. Setae short, 0.7–0.1 μm long, cells quadrate. Capsules
immersed, ellipsoid, 1.7–2.0 mm long, smooth, light brown, narrowed at the mouth, abruptly
rounded-indented to the setae; exothecial cells small, red, in 2–3 rows below the mouth, irregularly
short-rectangular below; stomata immersed, at very base of capsule near seta; opercula conic, 0.4–
0.6 mm long, smooth; annuli compound; peristome diplolepideous, deeply inserted within the mouth; 
exostome teeth narrowly triangular, hyaline to white, papillose, to 0.36 mm long; endostome segments
linear, papillose, cilia absent, basal membranes very low. Spores spherical, papillose, 33–
37 μm. Calyptrae mitrate, 0.4–0.6 mm long.

Sphagnum strictum Sull., Musci Appal. 201. 1845.

Sphagnum mexicanum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 624. 1869.

Plants pale brown or yellowish, generally in low, dense, small tufts; cortical cells in 1–3 layers, without pores; wood cylinder yellow-green. Stem leaves very small, bluntly deltoid, scarcely bordered; hyaline cells not divided, without fibrils or pores, sometimes with membrane pleats in a few apical cells, on the inner surface with an irregular membrane gap in each cell near the leaf apex occupying nearly the entire cell. Branches usually in fascicles of 5 (2 spreading); cortical cells in 1 layer, each ending in a pore. Branch leaves squarrose-spreading, ovate, involute-concave above and ending in a broad, truncate apex, more or less denticulate along a resorption furrow toward the apex; hyaline cells convex on the inner surface, on the outer surface toward the leaf apex with 2–6 large, round or round-elliptic, non-ringed pores at the commissures, becoming more numerous and more or less ringed below, on the inner surface with 2–4 elliptic, ringed pores especially in corners and often in 2's or 3's at adjacent corners; green cells in section narrowly triangular, often enclosed on the inner surface.

Plants medium-sized to robust, brownish green, in dense, pendent masses. Primary stems creep-ing, with erect to imbricate leaves; rhizoids red brown, smooth, not or irregularly branched, from clus-ters of initials at abaxial side of primary stem leaf insertions, but also on abaxial side of leaves on transformed secondary stem and branch tips; leaves not spirally arranged, erect, oblong-ovate, 1.0–1.5 mm long, hair-pointed, concave, decurrent; margins serrulate throughout, plane to lightly in-curved; costae variable, at times absent or short and double, but usually single and ending above mid-leaf; leaf cells linear to linear-flexuose, smooth, firm- or thick-walled, porose, reddish yellow across the base; alar cells weakly differentiated, of a few subrectangular, very thick-walled and porose cells. Secondary stems more or less turgid, to 20 cm long, irregularly branched, stems and branches often transformed to stoloniferous stems at the tips; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 4–6 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellowish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous; leaves erect to erect-spreading, little altered when dry, not seriately arranged, broadly oblong to broadly oblong-ovate, abruptly long-cuspidate to hair-pointed, 1.6–2.0 mm long, cusp 0.4–0.7 mm long, deeply con-cave, rounded to more or less cordate at base; margins plane below, broadly incurved above at base of cusp, entire to subentire below, subentire to serrulate above; costae single, slender, mostly reaching 3/4 the leaf length, in cross section with 2 layers of thick-walled cells, ventral layer enlarged; leaf cells smooth, very thick-walled, porose, linear-fusiform, 35–55 # 3 r m, toward base 6–8 r m wide; cells across the leaf base red to red yellow in a broad band; alar cells weakly differentiated, thick-walled, porose, in 2–3 rows along the basal margin, extending inward 4–6 cells, subquadrate at the margins, short-rectangular intramarginally. Branch leaves erect-spreading, in distinct seriate rows, broadly oblong to oblong-ovate, abruptly long-cuspidate to hair-pointed, 1.2–1.5 mm long, cusp 0.4 mm long, concave, rounded to the insertion; margins plane below, incurved above, serrulate in the cusp, serrulate to subentire below; costae

Plants medium-sized to large, frondose, from creeping stolons, 3.5–8.0 cm high. Stolon leaves short, ovate-acuminate, 0.4 X 0.25 mm, appressed, abruptly narrowed to the acumen; costa absent. Stems stipitate, densely and regularly, bipinnately branched. Stipes 7–18 mm long; lower leaves broadly ovate-acuminate, 1.2–1.6 X 0.65–0.75 mm, abruptly narrowed and recurved to squarrose acumina; base rounded to weakly auriculate; costa absent; upper leaves long ovate-acuminate, 2.9–3.85  X 1.4–1.6 mm, clasping at base, recurved to squarrose, gradually narrowed to long acumina; margins denticulate above; base strongly auriculate; upper cells 16–48 X 3.5 mm, strongly prorate, walls moderately thickened, porose; alar cells numerous, linear and contorted, filling auricles; costae reaching above midleaf. Stem leaves ovate-acuminate, 3.2–4.7 X 1.1–1.4 mm, erect, slightly con-cave; cells in concave region 18–35 X 5 mm, strongly prorate; upper margins strongly denticulate near apex; costae reaching 2/3 the leaf length. Branch leaves in five weak spiraling rows, lanceolate, falcate, 1.5–2.1 X 0.4–0.5 mm, weakly concave, slightly auriculate; margins erect, flattening out above to form short apical blades, denticulate above; alar cells contorted, filling auricles; cells in con-cave region 21–30 X 5 r m, strongly prorate, walls thickened, porose below; costa reaching 2/3 the leaf length. Axillary gemmae not seen, asexual reproduction by means of deciduous branch leaves. Dioicous, only female plants known. Perichaetial leaves narrow, ovate-acuminate, 1.2–3.7 X 3–8 mm, abruptly narrowed to acumina, often notched at the shoulders; cells 14–46 X 5 mm, strongly porose, not prorate; costae of inner leaves vanishing in apices; margins of acumina denticulate. Setae elon-gate, 6.5 mm long, scabrous throughout, with low, warty papillae. Capsules exserted, spheroid, 1.8 X 1.5 mm, mouth small, 0.5 mm; opercula rostrate; peristome obscured, (upper portion missing). Ca-lyptra and spores not seen.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in green to yellow green, loose or dense mats. Primary stems creeping, with erect to imbricate, distantly spaced leaves; rhizoids red brown, roughened, not or ir-regularly branched, from clusters of initials at abaxial side of primary stem leaf insertions and at base of stipes. Secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect, stipitate, irregularly pinnate-branched, branches at times becoming flagellate, or transformed to stoloniferous stems, 4–15 cm long; stems in cross sec-tion with sclerodermis of 4–6 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellowish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudopara-phyllia filamentous; leaves loosely erect-spreading in more or less spiral rows when dry, erect to imbricate in distinct spiral rows when wet, 1.5–3.0 mm long, oblong-ovate, acute to short-acuminate, at times more or less cuspidate, concave, cordate to subauriculate at base, shortly decurrent; margins entire throughout or lightly serrulate at the apex, broadly incurved above; costae absent or short, faint, and double; cells linear-flexuose, porose and firm-walled throughout, apical cells 20–40 # 6–8 r m, median cells 40–70 # 3–5 r m; basal cells 50–98 # 3–6 r m; alar cells red to reddish yellow, weakly developed, rhombic to short-rectangular in 2–5 rows, cells across the leaf insertions red. Branch leaves smaller and less cordate at base than secondary stem leaves, otherwise similar to secondary stem leaves. Asexual reproduction by smooth, hyaline to yellowish, uniseriate, septate, often clavate gemmae arising from large, circular cluster of initials in leaf axils; gemmae becoming secondarily elongate, cells smaller and papillose-roughened. Dioicous. Setae short, smooth, 0.5–1.0 mm long. Cap-sules immersed, erect, symmetric, oblong-oval, 2–3 mm long; exothecial cells oblate in 8–10 rows at mouth, short-rectangular to subquadrate, firm-walled below; stomata absent; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.4–0.5 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome diplolepideous, prostome well developed; exostome teeth pale

Plants medium-sized to large, 2–15 cm long, flattened, pale green to yellowish green, at times yellowish red, glossy. Primary stems (stolons) creeping, occasionally pendent; rhizoids smooth, red-dish brown, densely present on stolons and on secondary stems and branches when in contact with sub-strate; leaves appressed to spreading, sigmoid-oblong, evenly foliate, 0.8–1.5 mm long. Secondary stems erect, horizontal or pendent, not stipitate, irregularly branched, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia fo-liose. Secondary stem and branch complanate-foliate; leaves spreading to wide-spreading, smooth when dry or wet, cultriform to sigmoid-oblong, 1.5–2.5 mm long, asymmetric, short-acuminate, not decurrent, rounded to the insertion; margins serrulate above, subentire below, inflexed on one side below; costae usually faint, very short and double; cells smooth, apical cells long-hexagonal to long fusiform, 30–60 # 4–6 µm, firm- to thick-walled, porose; basal cells linear-fusiform, 60–80 # 4–6 µm, thick-walled, porose; alar cells not or very weakly differentiated, cells across the insertions yellow. Asexual reproduction occasionally by deciduous leaves or filiform, axillary branchlets. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves oblong, sheathing at base, long-acuminate. Setae elongate, 2.5–4.0 cm, smooth, red. Capsules suberect to inclined, short-cylindric, symmetric, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exothecial cells not strongly differentiated at mouth, those below rounded, subquadrate to short-rectangular, firm- or thick-walled; stomata on neck; opercula obliquely long-rostrate, 0.8–1.2 mm long; annuli well developed, of

Plagiobryum zieri (Hedw.) Lindb., Öfvers. Förh. Kongl. Svenska Vetensk.-Akad. 19: 606. 1862 [1863]. Bryum zierii Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 182. 1801. Protologue: Scotland. Ad aggeres humidos in alpibus Scotiae.

Plants small, tufted, simple or sparsely branched, often with slender innovations; stems to 3 mm high, red; rhizoids reddish orange to brownish, roughened. Leaves crowded, 1–2 mm long, erect to imbricate, turgid to julaceous, soft, ovate to broadly ovate-lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acute; margins plane to irregularly and loosely recurved, entire to serrulate above; costae ending in the apex to percurrent; cells lax, thin-walled, upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal 50–80 x 20–30 μm, marginal cells longer and narrower, basal cells short-rectangular, 40–60 x 12–24 μm. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves lanceolate, upper cells linear-rhomboidal to elongate, firm-walled. Setae short, stout, curved, 6 mm long, reddish brown. Capsules horizontal to pendent, 4 mm long, strongly asymmetric, narrowly clavate, with a long, well-developed neck as long or longer than urn; stomata superficial; opercula low-conic, apiculate, 0.8 μm long; annuli revoluble, of 2–3 rows of cells; exostome teeth slender, reddish brown, striate-papillose below, whitish hyaline, smooth above, endostome reduced, whitish yellow, basal membrane _ the height of the exostome, segments slender, narrowly perforate, cilia rudimentary. Spores 30–36 μm, ellipsoid, coarsely papillose.

Bryum chryseum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 304. 1869.

Protologue: Guatemala. Volcan de Fuego, Godman & Salvin 304 (NY).  

Bryum guatemalense Hampe ex C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boiss. 5: 182. 1897. Protologue: Guatemala: Bernoulli sine loco speciali in Hb. Hmp.(BM, Ochi 1980).

Plants small, golden‑yellow, lustrous, in loose tufts, 3–5 mm high; rhizoids sparse. Leaves 0.7–1.0 mm long, imbricate with long, recurved apices when dry, imbricate when wet, concave, broadly ovate to deltoid; apices filiform‑acuminate; margins recurved below, plane or narrowly recurved above, not bordered, entire or lightly crenulate above, somewhat decurrent; costae  long-excurrent, denticulate at apex; upper cells narrowly rhomboidal, firm‑walled, 44–90 μm long, basal cells quadrate to short‑rectangular, thick‑walled, 12–18 μm long. Dioicous. Setae 15–25 mm long, red. Capsules 2.5–4 mm long, narrowly clavate, neck slender and constricted, horizontal to inclined, light-brown becoming red with age; opercula 0.5 mm long, conic‑mammillate; annuli compound and revoluble; exostome teeth papillose, light-brown 350 μm high, endostome 320 μm high, yellowish to hyaline, basal membrane high, segments broad, widely perforate below, abruptly narrowing above, lightly papillose, cilia short to rudimentary, nodose. Spores 10–13 μm, faintly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants small and slender, in dark green or yellow green, loose mats. Primary stems creeping,
freely and irregularly branched; leaves reduced, 0.26–0.4 mm long, well spaced, triangular to slenderly
acuminate from an ovate-deltoid base; cells smooth to weakly papillose; rhizoids red brown, in
clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or weakly and irregularly branched. Secondary stems
weakly differentiated, often transformed to stolons at the tips, erect and loosely spreading, 0.5–2.5 cm
long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical
cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia and pseudoparaphyllia
absent. Secondary stem and branch leaves erect-imbricate when dry, spreading to squarrose
when wet, ovate at base, abruptly narrowed to a lanceolate or lingulate acumen, 0.5–0.9 mm
long, acute to rounded, often apiculate, shortly decurrent, extremely fragile, most leaves with lamina
broken and apices detached; margins plane or erect, papillose-crenulate, at times serrulate near the
apex; costae single, ending at or below midleaf, yellow, ventral surface somewhat channeled, covered
by quadrate, papillose cells above, in cross section cells homogeneous, thick-walled; upper cells
rounded-quadrate, subquadrate, or irregularly hexagonal, 8–11 μm, bulging-mammillose and pluripapillose,
juxtacostal cells near the insertions yellow, long-rectangular, 15–36 μm long, weakly papillose
to smooth. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen; known only from Asia. “Setae 3–5 mm long, more
or less curved. Capsules oblong 0.8–1.2 x 0.40–0.55 mm. Operculum 0.4–0.6 mm long. Exostome
teeth 0.25–0.30 mm long. Spores 20–25 μm, densely papillose. Calyptra 1.2–1.5 mm long.” (Noguchi
1991).

Leiomela bartramioides (Hook.) Par., Index Bryol. ed. 2, 3: 132. 1905.

Leucodon bartramioides Hook., Icones Pl. Rar. 1: pl. 71. 1836. Protologue: Ecuador. Surucucho, near Cuenca, Prof. W. Jameson.

Plants small and slender to medium-sized, in dense or loose, glaucous-green, dark-green to glossy yellow tufts, to 10–50 mm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, not or sparsely branched below, at times with highly branched portions having deciduous leaves, hyalodermis absent, central strand weakly developed, moderately to strongly tomentose; rhizoids reddish brown, densely papillose; pseudoparaphyllia orbicular. Leaves 3–9 mm long, well-spaced, erect-flexuose when wet or dry, linear throughout or narrowly lanceolate below linear above, shiny at base, erect-spreading from the insertion or more or less clasping at base; apex setaceous to long, narrowly acuminate; margins spiculose, narrowly recurved below at shoulders or recurved throughout; costae excurrent, spiculose at back; upper cells short-rectangular, firm- and straight-walled, densely papillose by projecting end-walls, 17–57 x 7.5 μm, basal cells long- rectangular, firm- and straight-walled, smooth, 45–125 x 5–10 μm, alar cells shorter, otherwise undifferentiated. Deciduous leaves 0.6–0.9 mm long, lanceolate, erect to erect-spreading, obtuse, margins plane and entire, costa ending well below the apex, cells smooth. Dioicous or synoicous. Perigonia terminal, gemmiform; outer perigonial leaves ovate-lanceolate, basal cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline to orange, inner perigonial leaves ovate-linear, to 15 mm long, basal cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline to orange. Setae 1–2 mm long, red or yellow. Capsules erect, 2–5 mm long, oval-oblong, red; stomata in neck; opercula plano-convex to nearly plane; peristome rudimentary, exostome of 16, narrowly triangular, irregularly perforate, orange-red teeth, 250–280 μm long, weakly trabeculate, lamellae smooth, endostome rudimentary, reduced to an irregular, hyaline membrane. Spores red, round, reticulate-roughened, 22–33 μm. Calyptrae conic, 1 mm long.

Leiomela deciduifolia Herz., Biblioth. Bot. 87: 90. 1916.

Protologue. Bolivia. An faulen Baumstümpfen an der Waldgrenze über Tablas, ca. 3400 m,  No. 2800; auf faulem Holz an der Waldrenze des Rio Saujana, ca. 3400 m,  No. 3283; an Baumwurzeln im Bergwald des Rio Tocorani, ca. 2200 m, No. 4011, 4056 u. 4109; im oberen Coranital, ca. 2600 m, No. 5070 [all Herzog].

Plants small and slender, in loose, green to glossy yellow tufts, to 20 mm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, not or sparsely branched below but at times highly branched above, hyalodermis absent, central strand weakly developed; moderately tomentose; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose; pseudoparaphyllia orbicular. Leaves fragile and deciduous, 1.5–2.4 mm long, well-spaced, erect-flexuose when wet or dry, lanceolate, spreading from the insertion; apices acute; margins dentate, plane; costae percurrent, sub-percurrent or ending well below the apex, weakly serrate at back; upper cells prorate, short-rectangular, firm- and straight-walled, 17–32 x 7.5 μm, basal cells long-rectangular, firm- and straight-walled, smooth, to 63 x 7.5 μm, alar cells shorter, otherwise undifferentiated. Dioicous. Perigonia terminal, gemmiform; outer perigonial leaves ovate-lanceolate, basal cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline to orange, inner perigonial leaves ovate-linear, to 15 mm long, basal cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline to orange. Perichaetia and sporophytes not seen.

Plants medium-sized, in green or yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched,
leaves reduced; rhizoids red brown, from sparse clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, not
or rarely branched. Secondary stems erect, to 4 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis
of 3–5 rows of small, orange to red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow
to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia
subfoliose. Secondary stem leaves ovate, branch leaves ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.2–1.7 mm long,
imbricate with erect-spreading apices when dry, spreading to wide-spreading when wet, abruptly
long- or short-acuminate, decurrent; margins narrowly recurved in upper 1/4, serrulate above; costae
strong, 0.4–0.8 the length of the leaves; apical cells linear, upper cells elliptic to oblong, 11–20 μm
long, very thick-walled, smooth or prorate, median cells oblong, 11–18 μm long; basal cells near the
costae elongate to linear, to 60 μm long, thick-walled, straight-walled or porose, radiating outward
from the costae in a broad band; alar cells quadrate, or oblate, thick-walled, smooth. Autoicous.
Perigonia gemmate, borne laterally, leaves ovate, concave, acuminate, ecostate; perichaetia terminal,
leaves erect, oblong to obovate, 2.5–3.5 mm long, abruptly rounded or truncate to long, serrate
awns, margins recurved, costae long-excurrent, lower leaf cells linear, thin-walled. Setae short, to
0.5 μm long, cells quadrate. Capsules immersed, ovoid to ellipsoid, 1.0–1.8 mm long, smooth, light
brown, narrowed at the mouth, abruptly rounded-indented to the setae; exothecial cells small, red, in
2–3 rows below the mouth, irregularly quadrate to rectangular below; stomata superficial at junction
of seta and capsule; operculum not seen; annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, intact peristome not seen;
exostome teeth deeply inserted within the mouth, linear, whitish, densely and thickly papillose;
endostome absent. Spores spherical, lightly papillose, 20–25 μm. Calyptra not seen.

Brachymenium exile (Dozy & Molk.) Bosch & Lac., Bryol. Jav. 1: 139. 1860.

Bryum exile Dozy & Molk., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. sér. 3, 2: 300. 1844. Protologue: Java, Sumatra. 

Plants minute, yellow-green, gregarious or in tufts. Stems slender, 2–7 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, sparsely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose. Leaves 0.5–0.8 mm long, erect-appressed to imbricate, spreading when wet, concave, ovate; apices short acuminate; margins weakly bordered by short-rectangular cells, entire, erect above, slightly reflexed below; costa stoutly short-excurrent, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled throughout, upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, 30–50 x 10 μm, basal cells quadrate to short-rectangular, 10–20 x 10 μm. Bulbous axillary gemmae sometimes present. Dioicous. Setae 15–30 mm long, red. Capsules 1.5–2.0 mm long, claviform to obovate-oblong, constricted at neck, erect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth whitish red, thickly papillose, endostome yellowish, papillose, basal membrane to ¾–_ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores 10–14 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptrae 1 mm long, cucullate, hyaline-yellow below, reddish above.

Brachymenium klotzschii (Schwaegr.) Par., Index Bryol. 123. 1894.

Didymodon klotzschii Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 4: 310a. 1842. Protologue: Brazil. In muscorum Brasiliensium variorum magnis caespitibus legi specimina pauca anno 1830.

Brachymenium macrocarpum Card., Rev. Bryol. 38: 6. 1911. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Vera-Cruz: Zacuapan, rochers dan les bois de chênes (Purpus, 1907 n° 9). 

Plants medium-sized, dark-green, in dense tufts. Stems 4–10 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 1.5–2.5 mm long, erect-appressed and spirally contorted when dry, erect to erect-spreading when wet, concave, ovate to broadly oblong; apices acuminate to obtuse, ending in a smooth or toothed, reddish yellow awn; margins bordered below by 1–2 rows of narrow rectangular cells with more or less right-angled end-walls, crenulate to serrulate (at times teeth double) above, narrowly reflexed in lower _, sometimes to near the apex; costa reddish, stoutly long-excurrent and filling the awn, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled throughout, sometimes weakly porose, upper cells oblong-hexagonal to oblong-rhomboidal, 26–40 x 16–20 μm, basal cells quadrate to short-rectangular, 30–50 x 30 μm. Dioicous. Setae 10–20 mm long, yellow-red. Capsules 2–4 mm long, oblong to oblong-clavate, constricted at neck, erect, smooth or irregularly wrinkled when dry; opercula 0.7 mm long, conic, short-beaked; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth linear, whitish above, red-brown below, densely papillose, well-separated from each other at base; endostome whitish yellow, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments absent or rudimentary, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores 10–14 μm, spherical, lightly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Sphagnum subsecundum Nees ex Sturm var. rufescens (Nees, Hornsch. & Sturm), Hüb., Musc. Germ. 26. 1833. S. contortum var. rufescens Nees & Hornsch., Bryol. Germ. 15. 1823.

Sphagnum flavicans Warnst., Allg. Bot. Z. Syst. 1: 205. 1895.

Plants of medium size, green or, more commonly, yellow-brown to orange; stems brown; cortical cells in 1 layer, without pores; wood cylinder yellow-green to brown. Stem leaves 1.3–2.5 mm long, oblong-ovate to lingulate, rounded at the apex, the border not much expanded at base; hyaline cells commonly divided and often with membrane pleats, fibrillose in the upper 1/3–1/2 or nearly throughout, with many elliptic commissural pores on the outer surface, few to numerous on the inner. Branches often curved, in fascicles of 4 (2 spreading); cortical retort cells differentiated. Branch leaves appressed or more or less secund, 1.5–2.5 mm long, rather narrowly to broadly oblong-ovate; pores more or less contiguous and commissural on the outer surface, few or none on the inner; green cells in section more or less truncately elliptic, exposed equally or somewhat more broadly on the outer surface.

Sphagnum trinitense C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 102. 1848.

Sphagnum laxifolium var. serrulatum Schlieph., Verh. Zool.-Bot. Ges. Wien 15: 397. 1865. Sphagnum cuspidatum var. serrulatum (Schlieph.) Schlieph., Irmischia 2: 67. 1882.

Plants relatively robust (to 12, rarely 45 cm long), pale yellow-green to yellowish, in lax, floating mats; cortical cells long, narrow, poorly differentiated in 1–3 layers; wood cylinder yellowish. Stem leaves concave, oblong to ovate, acute to blunt or rounded-obtuse, often erose at the apex, not or somewhat broad-bordered at base; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout or sometimes only above, few to many (usually) 1-divided, on the outer surface without pores or gaps, on the inner surface with fibrils and 2–5 small, round pores or with fibrils vestigial to lacking and 2–4 median gaps, or the membrane largely resorbed, both surfaces largely resorbed near the leaf apex. Branches in fascicles of 4 (rarely 5) (with 2 deflexed), sometimes cuspidate-tipped but more often ending in a loose tuft of long-tapered leaves that are flexuous-contorted when dry; retort cells differentiated. Branch leaves when young (in the capitulum) often rather short and broadly truncate or rounded at the apex, the others narrowly lanceolate and long-tapered (longer and narrower toward the branch tips), involute-concave when moist, flatter and wavy-margined when dry, with bordered margins serrulate in the upper third, half, or nearly throughout (more distinctly so at tips of long upper leaves), hyaline cells slightly convex on the inner surface; on the outer surface with pores 1–2 (rarely 3) very small, inconspicuous, and round, at ends and corners, sometimes lacking, on the inner surface with 3–6 (rarely 8) small, indistinct, unringed, round pores at ends and corners, sometimes also at commissures.

Plants small, in green to pale green, glossy mats, becoming yellow green to reddish with age. Stems yellow, becoming red with age, closely adnate to substrate, to 30 mm long; stems in cross sec-tion with 2–3 rows of small, firm-walled epidermal cells, cortical cells hyaline, thin-walled, central strand absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; paraphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell quadrate, brown, upper cell elongate, clavate, hyaline. Branches identical to stems, but frequently ending in a terminal mass of gemmae. Leaves 1–2 mm long, concave, uniform, erect to erect-spreading, branch leaves with terminal gemmae stiffly erect-appressed, lanceolate to elongate-triangular, gradually long-acuminate, rounded to the insertion, strongly plicate when wet or dry; margins entire (occa-sionally weakly serrulate at apex), elimbate, plane; costae double, weak, to 2/3 the leaf length, one side often longer than the other, frequently difficult to distinguish from the leaf plicae; cells smooth, firm- to thick-walled, not or weakly porose, upper and median cells narrowly linear, 20–60 # 3–4 µm, basal margins shortly rectangular to more or less quadrate, usually with a band of orange red cells across the leaf insertions. Asexual reproduction by large, greenish to hyaline masses of gemmae at ends of branches; gemmae uniseriate, filiform, 5–14 cells long, cells rectangular to quadrate, firm-walled. Dioicous. Setae elongate, to 12 mm long, red, smooth. Capsules horizontal, oblong-cylindric, to 1.8 mm long, wrinkled at neck; exothecial cells broadly rectangular, collenchymatous; stomata 4–8-celled, on neck; opercula long-rostrate, to 1.8 mm long; annulus not seen; peristome diplolepi-deous; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, yellowish to red, with median furrows, densely and closely striate below, papillose above, median line present throughout, ventral surface yellowish hyaline, smooth, trabeculae well developed and projecting; endostome as long as the exostome, yel-lowish white, smooth below, lightly papillose above, basal membranes high, segments broad, keeled, weakly or not perforate, cilia absent. Spores rounded, 12–18 µm, faintly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, yellowish white, lobed at base, naked, with a few short hairs at base, to 2 mm long.

Plants small and slender, 1–3 cm long, pale greenish, green, or yellowish red, in dense or loose mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age; stems in cross section with moderate-sized hyalodermis, subepidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia absent, foliose scale leaves present; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect-flexuose when dry, erect-spreading when wet; dorsal and lateral leaves oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate, 0.6–1.2 mm long, symmetric, gradually acute to short-acuminate; margins serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth slightly swollen, often bifid, entire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, serrate on back, projecting at the apices by one or more swollen cells; cells smooth, upper cells variable, isodiametric, hexagonal to long-rhomboidal, 18–36 X 10–20 µm, thin-walled, eporose, lower cells elongate-rhomboidal to long-rectangular; basal cells near the insertion enlarged, oblong-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated; ventral leaves erect, lanceolate, 0.6–1.0 mm long, symmetric, short-acuminate; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, smooth on back, not projecting at the apex; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 4–10 mm long, red, flexuose, scabrose in Central America, smooth to somewhat roughened in Colombia. Capsules horizontal to erect, ovoid to short-cylindric, 0.5– 1.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls somewhat collenchy-matous; stomata rudimentary, on

Plants small and slender, 1–4 cm long, pale greenish, green, or reddish, in dense or loose mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age; stems in cross section with moderate-sized hyalodermis, subepidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia absent, but with foliose scaly leaves; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Lat-eral and dorsal leaves erect-flexuose to crispate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 0.9–1.2 mm long, acute to short-acuminate; margins serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth slightly swollen, often bifid, entire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, often serrate on back, projecting at the apex; cells smooth, upper cells oval-hexagonal to long-rhomboidal, 14–32 X 5–10 µm, firm-walled, usually eporose but occasionally slightly porose, lower cells elongate-rhomboidal to long-rectangular; basal cells near the insertions enlarged, oblong-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Ventral leaves erect, ovate-lanceolate, 1.2 mm long, symmetric, short-acuminate; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, un-equal, smooth on back, not projecting at the apex; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 10–15 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth. Capsules horizontal, short-cylindric, 1.0–1.5 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimen-tary, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.7 mm long; annuli of 7–9 rows of cells, lower cells trans-versely rectangular, upper cells quadrate, all cells thin-walled with irregular nodose thickenings, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae project-ing laterally, secondary

Plants small and slender, 1–3 cm long, pale green, green, rarely yellowish red, in dense mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, yellowish when young, red with age; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, cen-tral strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia subfoliose, thin-walled; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect at base, falcate-secund above when dry, erect-spreading, flexuose when wet. Dorsal and lateral leaves lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.5 mm long, grad-ually long-acuminate, at times somewhat undulate; margins coarsely serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth swollen, often bifid, serrate to subentire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, weakly diverging throughout or parallel, serrate on back, projecting at the apices; cells smooth or prorate in upper 2/3, upper and median cells linear-flexuose, firm-walled, eporose or porose, 50–60 X 4–6 µm, lower cells between the costae 60–80 X 4–6 µm; basal cells enlarged, oblong-rectangular; alar cells short-rectangular, otherwise undifferentiated. Ventral leaves erect, lanceolate, symmetric; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, smooth on back, not pro-jecting at the apices; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 8–14 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth below, somewhat roughened below capsules. Capsules erect, horizontal or inclined, short-cylindric, 1.0–1.5 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls somewhat collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5– 0.7 mm long; annuli of 2–3 rows of quadrate cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular,

Bryohumbertia filifolia (Hornsch.) Frahm var. filifolia Cryptogamie, Bryol. Lichénol. 3: 366. 1982. Dicranum filifolium Hornsch., Fl. Bras. 1(2): 12. 1840. Thysanomitrion filifolium (Hornsch.) Hampe, Linnaea 25: 361. 1853. Campylopus filifolius (Hornsch.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 76. 1869. Type. Brazil, prope Novo-Friburgum, Beyrich (lectotype, Frahm 1991a).

Plants yellow-green; stems to 6 cm long, branching from the terminal comal tufts. Leaves when dry erect to appressed below, spreading above, concave at base, leaves of comal tufts linear-lanceolate, those between the comal tufts ovate-lanceolate, 10–16 mm long; margins serrulate above; costa long excurrent, dorsal surface strongly toothed above; upper laminal cells irregularly elongate, 20–30 µm long, walls incrassate, not pitted; basal cells rectangular, narrower towards margin, 30–75 µm long, walls thickened, not pitted; alar cells forming distinct groups of red-brown, thin-walled, bulging cells. Setae 15–17 mm long, yellow, smooth; capsules inclined, cylindrical, 1.5 mm long, ribbed when dry, yellow to red, neck weakly strumose; peristome teeth hyaline above, red below, teeth narrowly triangular below, abruptly filiform above, split 2/3 their lengths, dorsal lamellae vertically striate below, densely papillose above, ventral lamellae smooth, ventral trabeculae weakly papillose to smooth; opercula 1.5 mm long. Calyptrae 2.5 mm long. Spores 12–19 µm.

Microcampylopus leucogaster (C. Müll.) Allen, comb. nov. Dicranum leucogaster C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 387. 1848. Campylopus leucogaster (C. Müll.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 75. 1869. Type. Mexico, prope Xalapa, Deppe & Schiede s.n.

Aongstroemia curviseta Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 3: 355. 1865. Dicranella curviseta (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 38. 1869. Campylopodium curvisetum (Hampe) Par., Index Bryol. 237. 1894. Microcampylopus curvisetus (Hampe) Giese & Frahm, Lindbergia 11: 116. 1985. Type. Colombia, Bogotá, Tequendama, Lindig s.n.

Campylopus pusillus Schimp. in Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 165. 1872. Campylopodium pusillum (Schimp.) Williams, N. Amer. Fl. 15: 94. 1913. Type. Mexico, Orizaba, F. Mueller s.n. (NY).

Plants, gregarious, yellowish green, terricolous; stems dimorphic, male plants slender, to 8 mm high, female plants 5–10 mm long; central strand small. Leaves evenly spaced, spreading, flexuosus, leaves on male plants and the lower leaves on female plants lanceolate from an oblong, clasping base gradually narrowed and subulate above; upper leaves on female plants 2.5–4.0 mm long, from a short, broadly ovate, sheathing base, abruptly narrowed into a long subula; margins plane above, entire; costa in cross section with a median row of guide cells, ventral and dorsal stereid bands; upper cells rectangular to rhomboidal thick-walled, basal cells of leaves on male plants and lower leaves of female plants quadrate, rectangular on upper leaves thick- to firm-walled. Dioicous. Setae 3–7 mm long, yellowish to brown, smooth; capsules exserted, ovoid to cylindrical, 1.0–1.5 mm long, sometimes ribbed when dry; annuli present; stomata absent; peristome red below, yellowish white above, teeth lanceolate, vertically striate below, papillose above; opercula 1 mm long. Calyptrae 1.0–1.5 mm long.

Plants medium-sized, 3–6 cm high, stipitate-frondose, forming yellow green to green, lax tufts. Stolons creeping, evenly foliate; rhizoids smooth to lightly roughened, reddish brown, not or sparsely branched, in circular clusters just below the leaf insertions, on stolons, and at the base of stipitate stems; leaves loosely imbricate, widely spaced, triangular. Stems erect, stipitate, irregularly pinnate, complanate-foliate, at times flagellate-attenuate; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, grading into larger, firm-walled cortical cells, central strand well devel-oped; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Stipes evenly foliate; leaves erect-spreading to spreading, ovate-triangular to triangular, acute to acuminate; margins entire to subserrulate. Stem leaves 2–3 mm long, flattened, oblong-cultriform, asymmetric, broadly acute, broadly apiculate; mar-gins serrate or dentate at apex, teeth sometimes of 2–3 cells, serrulate to midleaf; costae very short and double or single and reaching 1/3 the leaf length; cells smooth, upper cells long-rhomboidal, 30–60 X 7–10 µm, median and basal cells linear-fusiform to vermicular, 50–90 X 6–10 µm; alar cells shorter, often porose, cells across the insertions yellow. Branch leaves similar to stem leaves except smaller and sometimes oval or spathulate. Gonioautoicous. Setae 15–20 mm long, reddish yellow. Capsules erect to suberect, ovoid-cylindrical, somewhat constricted at base, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exo-thecial cells small and thick-walled at mouth, rounded-rectangular, firm-walled below; stomata at base of capsules; opercula conic-rostrate, 1.5 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome diplolepideous; ex-ostome teeth linear, 0.6–0.8 mm long, dorsal surface cross-striate and papillose below, vermiculate-papillose at middle, lightly papillose above, trabeculae and median line thin below, thickened above, ventral surface with projecting trabeculae, lightly papillose; endostome lightly papillose, basal mem-branes 0.2 mm high, segments 0.4–0.5 mm long, broadly perforate, cilia 1–3, nodose, 0.30–0.35 mm long. Spores spherical, lightly papillose, 14–20 µm. Calyptrae tubular-cucullate, 2–3 mm long.

Mielichhoferia paroica Shaw & Allen in Shaw, Allen & Buck, Bryologist 101: 600. 1998 [1999].

Protologue: Costa Rica. San José. Summit of Volcán Irazu, alt. 3400 m elev., on the ground, 14 February 1966, Crosby 3638 (F, MO).

Plants slender, highly branched, to 5 mm high. Stems forking or with subfloral innovations. Leaves erect to erect‑spreading, lanceolate, 0.4–0.75 x 0.2–0.4 mm; apices acute; margins plain, sharply serrate in the upper _, serrulate or crenulate to midleaf; costa weak, ending in the upper ¼ of the leaf or rarely subpercurrent; upper cells rhomboidal to linear‑rhomboidal, vermicular, firm-walled, 60–90(–115) x 7–11 μm, not or weakly differentiated at the base. Paroicous. Inflorescence bracts long, narrowly lanceolate to narrowly triangular, 1.5–2.8 mm long; margins sharply serrate near the apex, serrulate or crenulate to midleaf. Setae 1–2 per perichaetium, erect, to 20 mm long, orange‑yellow. Capsules inclined, yellow‑tan, 2.5–4.0 mm long, neck shorter (_) than the urn; stomata superficial; opercula blunt‑conic; annuli separating irregularly; peristome double, exostome teeth uncolored to pale orange‑yellow, narrowly triangular or irregular, irregularly perforate and/or divided, 275–350 μm long, coarsely papillose, papillae sometimes in rows; endostome rudimentary, short, hyaline membrane barely extending beyond the capsule mouth, segments absent. Spores finely roughened, 16–22 μm. Calyptra not seen.

Schizymenium linearifolium Allen, sp. nov.

Type: Costa Rica. San José: Along Inter American Highway. About 10 km NW of summit at La Ascensión. 9°37'N, 83°48W, Crosby & Crosby 6107 (holotype MO, isotype DUKE). 

Species haec a S. campylocarpo foliis longioribus, cellulis basalibus anguste rectangularibus saepe incrassatus et porosis setis longioribus differt. 

Plants medium-sized, shiny, yellow-green, in loose tufts. Stems to 10 mm high, red, simple or forked; rhizoids, reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Lower leaves reduced, distant, spreading, upper leaves widely spaced, 1.6–2.2 mm long, spreading to slightly erect-spreading, soft, lightly twisted when dry, linear-lanceolate, not or weakly decurrent; apices acuminate; margins plane below, plane, erect, or narrowly recurved above, serrulate above; costae ending near apex; upper cells narrowly linear-vermicular, firm-walled, 90–140 x 4–6 μm, marginal cells longer and narrower than the interior cells, basal cells long, narrowly rectangular to linear-vermicular. Paroicous. Setae to 35 mm long, orange-red, flexuose. Capsules erect, 3–4 mm long, oblong-cylindric, tapered at neck; exothecial cells elongate-rectangular, smooth, with wavy walls; stomata superficial; opercula conic, apiculate, 0.5 mm long; annuli well-developed, of 2–3 rows of cells; exostome absent, endostome smooth, reddish orange, basal membrane to 80 μm high, segments filiform, firm, cilia rudimentary. Spores 14–20 μm, papillose.

Brachymenium mexicanum Mont., Ann. Sci. Nat., Bot. sér. 2, 9: 54. 1838.

Protologue: Mexico. Hab. ad terram in provinciâ Oaxaca Regni Mexicani à D. Andrieux lectum (FH). 

Plants-medium sized, bright-green to yellowish green, shiny, in dense tufts or mats. Stems 3–10 mm long, epidermal cells rectangular, densely tomentose at base; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose. Leaves crowded in rosulate tufts, 1.4–2.3 mm long, erect-appressed when dry, spreading when wet, concave, ovate, to oblong-lanceolate; apices short acuminate, ending in a stout, reddish brown mucro; margins not bordered, upper marginal cells short-rectangular, entire or weakly crenulate, plane; costa short excurrent, filling the mucro, ventral superficial cells at base quadrate to rectangular; cells firm-walled throughout, upper cells hexagonal to rhomboidal-hexagonal, 40–60 x 10 μm, basal cells quadrate to short-rectangular, 16–30 x 18–20 μm. Dioicous. Setae 15–25 mm long, yellowish red. Capsules 3–4 mm long, cylindrical, constricted at neck, erect to suberect; opercula 0.3–0.5 mm long, conic-apiculate; annuli compound, revoluble; exostome teeth reddish yellow, lightly papillose, endostome yellowish, papillose, basal membrane to ½ the exostome teeth length, segments rudimentary, cilia rudimentary to absent. Spores 14–18 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptra not seen.

Bartramia strumosa (Hampe) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 270. 1869.

Glyphocarpa strumosa Hampe, Linnaea 32: 139. 1863. Protologue: Colombia. Bogota Rio Arzebabo, 2800 metr. Jul. [Lindig] 2003.

Plants small, in loose, glaucous-green or yellowish green tufts, 2–5 (–9) mm high. Stems red, erect, hyalodermis and central strand well-developed, lightly tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown. Leaves 2.5–3.8 mm long, closely spaced, erect and sheathing but not strongly clasping at base, leaf limb usually firm, occasionally broken, erect-flexuose to erect-patent when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 2–3 mm long, sheathing base 0.5–0.8 mm long, not plicate; apices subulate to long, slenderly acuminate; limb margins unistratose, multistratose elsewhere, narrowly recurved, doubly serrate; costae excurrent, sharply toothed to spinose at back and above; limb cells stoutly papillose to mammillose, short-rectangular to rectangular, 12–30 x 5 μm, cells at leaf shoulder lax, thin-walled, not fragile, yellow or hyaline, rhomboidal to rectangular, 25–50 x 17–20 μm, sheath cells rectangular to linear, lax and thin-walled throughout, 50–100 x 10–15 μm, alar cells reddish yellow, rectangular to subquadrate, thin-walled, bulging. Synoicous. Perigonial and perichaetial leaves shorter than vegetative leaves. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae straight, yellowish brown to reddish brown, 6–20 mm long, 120–160 μm diameter. Mature capsules greenish brown to brown, ovoid to globose, erect, symmetric, 1.2–1.9 mm long; diameter of mouth 400–520 μm; exothecial cells nearly isodiametric to irregularly quadrate to rectangular, 22–37 μm. Peristome lacking. Spores brown, coarsely papillose, 26–40 μm long” (Fransén 1995).

Breutelia austro-auriculata (C. Müll.) Par., Index Bryol. 151. 1894.

Bartramia austro-auriculata C. Müll., Linnaea 43: 406. 1882. Protologue: Argentina. Argentinia subtropica, Cuesta de Pinos in descensu ab alta Puna in covallem Tarija Boliviae, 27 Majo 1873, copiosa sed sterilis in rupibus cum Bartramia cuspidatissima [Lorentz].

Plants medium-sized, in dense or loose, glossy, yellowish green or green tufts, to 12 cm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, hyalodermis and central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth or roughened. Leaves 3–5 mm long, well-spaced, squarrose to deflexed from an erect, clasping, plicate base often with 1 pair of sulci at junction of sheath and limb, obovate-lanceolate; apices long, slenderly acuminate with non-twisted apices; margins plane or narrowly revolute, serrulate to serrate or sharply serrate above; costae short- or long-excurrent, scabrous at back; leaf cells papillose at lower ends, or from both ends, upper cells short- to long-rectangular firm- and straight‑walled, 15–42 x 5 μm, basal cells narrower and elongate, 27–82 x 3–5 μm, thick-walled, smooth or porose, alar region with 4–6 rows of enlarged, lax, hyaline cells extending well up the leaf margin. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Setae flexuose, 5–6 mm long, red. Capsules inclined, 2.5–3 mm long, subglobose to globose, furrowed when dry, striate when wet; exothecial cells firm-walled; immersed stomata at base; opercula plano-convex, 0.5 mm; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, finely papillose below, more coarsely papillose near tips, 400–500 μm high, dorsal trabeculae faint, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened, endostome segments broad, _ as long as the exostome, yellowish, finely papillose, papillae in vertical rows, segments split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia, cilia rudimentary. Spores reniform, 25–36 μm, coarsely papillose, red-brown.

Breutelia squarrosa Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1873–74: 98. 1875, nom. nov. Bartramia squarrosa Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 265. 1869, hom. illeg., non  Turner, 1805. Protologue. Colombia. Andes Bogotenses, Bogota, Holton, n. 15.

Plants medium-sized to robust-sized, in loose or dense, somewhat glossy, yellowish‑green or brownish yellow tufts, to 6 cm high. Stems red, hyalodermis and central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, lightly papillose. Leaves 3–4 x 1–1.5 mm, closely spaced, erect, plicate at base, squarrose to squarrose-recurved or erect-spreading above, irregularly wrinkled, squarrose to erect-spreading when wet, ovate to broadly lanceolate, not decurrent; apices slenderly acuminate; margins recurved below, plane above midleaf, serrulate; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; leaf cells smooth-walled, papillose at lower ends, upper cells linear-elongate, thick‑walled, 22–58 x 3.7–5 μm, basal cells linear-elongate, 37–68 x 2.5–3.7 μm, thick-walled, alar cells weakly differentiated, 1–3 inflated cells at extreme basal angles and a few enlarged supra-alar cells, otherwise undifferentiated. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Sporophytes not seen. “Setae 7–9 mm long, arcuate, capsules subglobose, 3 mm long x 2 mm wide, irregularly rugulose when dry. Peristome inserted below the mouth, exostome of 16 lanceolate teeth, 150 μm long, finely granulose, endostome adherent to and nearly equaling exostome in length. Spores subreniform, areolate-tuberculate, 33–38 μm long x 25–27 μm wide” (Griffin 1984a).

Plants small to medium-sized, in dense or loose, glossy, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 70(–120) mm high. Stems red, laxly ascending, hyalodermis and central strand present, densely tomentose below; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth or roughened. Leaves 1.4–3 mm long, stem leaves usually with erect and laxly clasping leaf bases, branch leaves usually well-spaced, and erect- or wide-spreading from the insertion, straight or somewhat secund, ovate-lanceolate, plicate at base; apices long, slenderly acuminate, twisted when dry; margins plane below narrowly revolute above, serrulate; costae long-excurrent and sharply toothed or percurrent; cells papillose mostly at lower ends, occasionally from both ends, upper cells long-rectangular to sublinear, firm- and straight‑walled or porose, 17–45 x 4–6 μm, basal cells 25–65 x 3.7–6 μm, alar region with 1–3 enlarged, inflated alar cells at extreme basal angle and 1–6 enlarged quadrate supra-alar cells. Dioicous. Perigonia discoid. Setae straight or flexuose, 15–27 mm long. Capsules erect, inclined to horizontal, 1.5–3.5 mm long, ovoid, furrowed when dry, striate when wet; exothecial cells firm-walled; stomata numerous at base; opercula plano-convex, mammillate; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, reddish orange, finely papillose below, coarsely papillose near tips, dorsal trabeculae faint, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened, endostome segments broad, nearly as long as the exostome, yellow to reddish yellow, lightly papillose below, densely papillose above, segments split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia, cilia 2–3, rudimentary, often fused. Spores reniform, 25–35 μm, warty, red-brown.

Plants medium-sized, in dense or loose, glaucous-green, yellowish‑green or gray-green tufts, to 3 cm high. Stems red, erect, lightly tomentose below, hyalodermis and central strand well-developed; rhizoids reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 3–5 mm long, moderately spaced, erect and sheathing but not strongly clasping at base, leaf limb usually firm, occasionally deciduous, erect-flexuose to erect-patent when dry when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 2.2–4 mm long, sheathing base 0.8–1 mm long, not plicate; apices subulate to long, slenderly acuminate; limb margins unistratose, multistratose elsewhere, margins narrowly recurved, single or doubly serrate; costae excurrent, sharply toothed to spinose at back; limb cells papillose or mammillose, subquadrate, short-rectangular to rectangular, 12–33 x 7.5 μm, cells at leaf shoulder firm, thick-walled, not fragile, yellow or hyaline, rhomboidal to rectangular 25–42 x 10–15 μm, sheathing base cells linear, firm to thick-walled near costa and in median area, lax and thin-walled near margin, 75–150 x 10–15 μm, alar cells reddish yellow, rectangular to subquadrate, thin-walled, bulging. Synoicous (rarely dioicous). Perigonial and perichaetial leaves shorter than vegetative leaves. Setae 1 per perichaetium, straight to flexuose, red, 7–10 mm long. Capsules reddish brown, suberect, inclined or horizontal, 1.5–2 mm long, globose to oblong, asymmetric, furrowed when dry, striate when wet; exothecial cells firm-walled; stomata at base; opercula plano-conic, mammillate; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, reddish orange, finely papillose below, upper half vertically striate-papillose, dorsal trabeculae faint, ventral trabeculae strongly thickened, endostome rudimentary, consisting of a low basal membrane. Spores oblong to subreniform, 25–32 μm long, coarsely papillose, red-brown.

Plants medium-sized, in yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched; leaves
well spaced, reduced, ovate, abruptly long-acuminate, erect below, squarrose-recurved above, 0.6–0.8
mm long; rhizoids red brown, in sparse clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or rarely
branched. Secondary stems horizontal and often with lateral stolons, or erect and loosely spreading,
3–10 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, red brown,
thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand
absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent. Secondary stem and branch leaves erect at base,
spreading to squarrose above when dry, spreading to wide-spreading when wet, oblong-ovate,
strongly plicate, 2–3 mm long, ending in a slender, hyaline hair-point, shortly decurrent; margins
narrowly recurved in the lower 1/2 or less, plane above; apices erose; costa absent; upper cells shortrectangular
to rectangular, 8–20 μm long, thick-walled, strongly sinuose, pluripapillose; basal median
cells long-rectangular, 98 x 4 μm, thick-walled, porose, pluripapillose; alar cells short-rectangular,
quadrate, or oblate, 6–12 μm long, thick-walled, smooth. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves erect, elongate.
Setae elongate, yellow, 3–5 mm long. Capsules erect, globose to subglobose, 1.3–1.7 mm long,
somewhat wrinkled when dry, yellowish brown when young, becoming red brown with age, narrowed
at the mouth, variously constricted at neck; exothecial cells small, reddish brown, in 5–15 rows below
the mouth, becoming larger, oblate, irregularly quadrate to short-rectangular below; neck cells small,
irregularly subquadrate to short-rectangular; stomata in neck; opercula obliquely conic-rostrate, to 1
mm long; annuli rudimentary, cells often clinging to capsule mouth or operculum; peristome absent,
mouth closed by a membrane; anisosporous. Spores massive, thin-walled, vermicular-papillose, more
or less spherical, 60–90 μm, and small, smooth, spherical, 8–10 μm. Massive spores undergoing endosporic
germination and becoming multicelluar before dispersal. Calyptrae mitrate-cucullate, sparsely
hairy, 3.5–4.5 mm long.

Plants medium-size, in loose or dense tufts, reddish brown below, olive‑green above. Stems slender, erect, to 13 cm high, densely tomentose. Leaves erect‑flexuose to erect-patent when dry, squarrose‑recurved when wet, 1–3 mm long, lanceolate to linear‑lanceolate; apices acute, apex brittle, often broken; margins entire and recurved below, irregularly notched to toothed and plane above; costae stout, percurrent to subpercurrent, covered in the upper ½ by short, quadrate cells; upper cells 7–8 μm, irregularly hexagonal with rounded lumina, smooth or papillose, incrassate, basal cells rectangular, 16–30 μm, smooth. Brood bodies not seen. Dioicous. Setae 3–5 long, smooth, yellow. Capsules 2.0–2.5 mm long, oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry; opercula obliquely short‑rostrate, to 1 mm long; peristome double, exostome teeth 16 united into 8 teeth‑pairs, yellowish, densely papillose, to 240 μm high, endostome extending ¾ the length of the exostome teeth, yellowish, basal membrane not seen, cilia absent, segments stout, densely papillose. Spores isosporous, 12–16 μm, papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2–3 mm long.

Plants slender, sparsely clustered, light-green above, brown below. Stems erect to 10 mm high, sparsely tomentose. Leaves erect‑patent to lightly spirally twisted when dry, patent to squarrose‑recurved when wet, 0.6–1.4 mm long, lanceolate; apices broadly acute to rounded‑obtuse, apiculate; margins entire above, extreme basal margins dentate, plane or slightly recurved below; costae stout, ending at or near the apex, short, papillose, quadrate cells on upper 1/3 or less of dorsal surface; upper cells 4–8 μm, irregularly rounded, occasionally oblate, incrassate, pluripapillose, basal cells 12–20 μm long, enlarged, thin‑walled, bulging, rectangular, smooth. Brood bodies ovoid to oblong‑ellipsoidal, 3–6-celled, mostly only with transverse walls, occasionally with oblique walls. Dioicous. Setae to 4 mm long, smooth, yellow. Capsules to 1 mm long, obovoid to oblong, 8‑ribbed when dry, constricted at neck; operculum not seen; peristome double, exostome teeth 16 united into 8 teeth‑pairs, red to brown, densely papillose, recurved when dry, erect when wet, to 240 μm long, endostome 2/3 to 3/4 the length of the exostome teeth, rudimentary, basal membrane short, cilia absent, segments narrow, smooth, erect when dry. Spores isosporous, 16–18 μm, papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants small to medium-sized, in loose mats, reddish brown below, dark-green above. Stems erect 4–25 mm high, moderately tomentose. Leaves erect‑patent, irregularly twisted, to contorted and loosely spiraled around the stems, more or less undulate when dry, spreading or sub‑squarrose when wet, 1.8–2.3 mm long, oblong‑lanceolate; apices sharply acute, often apiculate; margins entire below, sharply dentate‑serrate near apex, plane or weakly recurved below, undulate; costae stout, percurrent or ending just below apex, dorsal surface near apex with short, papillose, quadrate cells; upper cells 8–12 μm, rounded, irregularly hexagonal to oblate, densely pluripapillose, incrassate, basal cells near costa elongate‑rectangular, smooth, 16–50 μm long. Brood bodies not seen. Mostly synoicous, occasionally autoicous with perigonia just below the perichaetial, rarely perigonia on separate branches. Setae 10–21 mm long, smooth, yellow. Capsules 2–3 mm long, oblong to cylindric, 8‑ribbed when dry, constricted at base and more or less puckered at mouth; opercula conic‑rostrate, to 1 mm long; peristome single, exostome absent, endostome of 16 (or 8?) short, slender, hyaline, fragile segments. Spores isosporous, 24–30 μm, papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2–3 mm long.

Plants small, dark-green to yellow-green above, brown below, in dense mats or tufts, 2.5–5 mm high. Stems red, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis weakly developed, central strand well-developed; rhizoids sparse red, smooth to roughened. Leaves 1.2–2.0 mm long, linear-lanceolate to lanceolate, ovate to oblong and weakly clasping at base, erect at base, crisped and spirally contorted above when dry, erect-flexuose to erect-spreading when wet; apices acuminate, mucronate; lamina unistratose, firm or occasionally fragile; margins entire, strongly involute above the base to the apex; costa stoutly excurrent, broad at base (50–60 μm), cells on ventral surface quadrate, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer enlarged, bulging-mammillose or papillose; upper cells rounded to quadrate, 6–11 μm long, thick-walled, dorsal surface, plane to weakly bulging, smooth, ventral surface bulging-mammillose or pluripapillose with 4–6 bifid papillae, basal cells narrowly rectangular, thick- or thin-walled, yellow or hyaline, smooth, 20–50 x 6–10 μm, outer basal cells hyaline, thin-walled, not noticeably running up the margins in a v-shaped pattern. Autoicous (?). Intact sporophytes not seen in Central America. Setae long, straight, slender, yellow. Capsules symmetric, erect or somewhat inclined, ovate to ellipsoid; opercula long-rostrate; annuli lacking; peristome lacking, narrow mouth of capsule usually covered by fugacious membrane developed from columella. Calyptra cucullate, reaching middle of capsule (Crum & Steere 1957).

Secondary stems erect-ascending, or pendent, not or sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, 1–3 lay-ers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, red-dish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and at base of secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves distantly spaced, not or weakly dimorphic, flattened, erect to erect-spreading, crispate to flexuose when dry, erect-spreading when wet, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate (dorsal leaves at times oblong-lanceolate), 2–3 mm long, asymmetric, long-acuminate; margins serrate above, plane above, often broadly infolded on one side at base, elimbate to obscurely limbate; costae double, slender, 1/2 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, not project-ing at the apex; cells smooth, upper cells narrowly to broadly fusiform, 50–120 X 8–18 µm, thin-walled, not porose, becoming oblong-rectangular to oblong-fusiform below; alar cells not differentiated. Asexual propagula not seen. Autoicous. Setae short, 1.5–3.0 mm long, red to reddish orange, densely scabrose to spinose throughout. Capsules erect, oblong-cylindrical, 1.0 mm long, neck well devel-oped; exothecial cells reddish, oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, firm-walled, vertica

Plants medium-sized, 2–7 cm long, pale, glaucous green, greenish yellow, or reddish, in lax tufts. Primary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems prostrate, erect, ascending, or pendent, at times attenuate, not or sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red to red brown with age, complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, 1–2 lay-ers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, red-dish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and on secondary stems when in contact with substrate, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Asex-ual propagula usually present, especially abundant on attenuate branch tips, propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, arising from clusters of initials abaxial

Plants medium-sized, caespitose, dull yellowish to ­olive green. Stems 8–12 mm, branched near base, central strand absent. Leaves crowded above, lingulate to narrowly oblong-elliptic, 2.5–5 x 0.8–1.2 mm, slightly clasping at base, erect-spreading, irregularly undulate above, crisped, folded when dry; apices cucullate, apiculate; margins crenulate, irregularly and narrowly recurved in lower 2/3; costa single, excurrent, with 2–3 rows of small dorsal stereids; upper cells angular-quadrate, 12.5–18.5 x 12.5–18.8 μm, thick-walled, pluripapillose on both sides by digitate c–shaped papillae; basal cells smooth, rectangular, 32.5–87.5 x 12.5–25.0 μm, transverse walls thickened, red to orange, longitudinal walls thin, hyaline or pale yellowish, basal marginal cells differentiated in 5–10 rows of narrow, elongate cells (5–9:1). Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves sheathing, ovate-elliptic, shorter than vegetative leaves, tubulose above. Setae single, 6–8 mm long, yellow, becoming reddish orange with age, twisted, smooth. Capsules cylindric, 2–5.4 mm long, orange-red or golden-brown, smooth or finely striolate, contracted below a reddish, suboral band of 6–7 rows of quadrate cells; exothecial cells rectangular to fusiform, thin-walled; stomata superficial; neck wrinkled; opercula narrowly rostrate from a plane-convex, reddish base; peristome single, of 16 brownish orange, triangular, slightly inserted teeth. Spores orange-brown, 35–44 μm wide, heteropolar, one side with a triculpate scar in a slight surface depression, the opposite side with a central rim and 4–5 radial plicae. Calyptrae 3–6 mm long, cylindric to elliptic-cylindric, shiny, yellowish brown or golden, tapering abruptly into a yellowish brown, straight or slightly curved rostrum, smooth, fringed at base with triangular segments, lacerate at their tips.

Plants medium-sized, in dark‑green to yellowish‑green mats. Stems creeping to 4–5 cm long, irregularly and commonly branched. Leaves dimorphic: lateral leaves in two rows, strongly incurled when dry, 1.5–2.0 mm long, lingulate; apices rounded to obtuse; margins entire, recurved,  bordered to near the apex by linear, hyaline cells; costae strong, ending below the apex; upper cells 6–10 μm, rounded hexagonal to irregularly subquadrate, mammillose to stoutly unipapillose, basal cells similar to upper cells, 8–16 μm long, dorsal leaves nearly ½ the size of the lateral leaves but otherwise similar; ventral leaves to 1.0 mm long, lanceolate to triangular‑acuminate, cells short‑rectangular, thin‑walled, pellucid, unipapillose, costae percurrent to shortly excurrent. Perigonia to 1 mm long, perigonial leaves 0.7  mm long, upper cells 8–22 μm, lower cells 24–48 μm, paraphyses present. Perichaetia strongly differentiated, perichaetial leaves 1.5–1.8 mm long, cells 50–80 μm long, paraphyses absent. Setae 0.3–0.4 mm long. Capsules cupulate to oblong, dark red, incurved and greatly thickened at mouth, 1 mm long, columella thick, not systylius. Spores 26–36 μm, densely papillose. Caylptra absent (?).

Plants small, yellow-green above, brown below, in dense mats or tufts, 2–3 mm high. Stems reddish yellow, irregularly branched, hyalodermis and central strand present;; rhizoids sparse red, smooth to roughened. Leaves 1.3–1.8 mm long, ovate-lanceolate, weakly clasping at base, erect at base, incurved to somewhat spirally contorted above when dry, erect-flexuose to erect-spreading when wet; apices acute, mucronate; lamina unistratose, not fragile; margins entire, strongly involute above the base to the apex; costa excurrent, 40–50 μm at base, ventral surface cells quadrate, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer enlarged, papillose, green; upper cells rounded to quadrate, 7–9 μm long, thick-walled, bulging at the surface, with 4–6 bifid papillae on both surfaces, basal cells narrowly rectangular, thick- or thin-walled, yellow or hyaline, smooth, 14–46 x 8–12 μm, outer basal cells hyaline, thin-walled, not noticeably running up the margins in a v-shaped pattern. Capsules ovoid, erect, 0.8–1.0 mm long, smooth to lightly furrowed when dry; stomata in neck; opercula oblique-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli of several rows of cells persistent cells; peristome none. Plants small, dull, green to yellow-green above, brown below, at times reddish yellow, in tufts 5–15 mm high. Plants medium-sized in loose tufts, dark‑green. Stems erect, to 3 cm high, often with densely tomentose throughout; plagiotropic stolons common, to10 cm long; macronemata and micronemata present, often dense reddish. Leaves crisped and contorted when dry, spreading when wet, 4–8 mm long at stem tips, oblong‑elliptic, decurrent; apices rounded obtuse to emarginate; margins uniserrate (teeth 1–2(–3) cells long) nearly to base (occasionally subentire), border of unistratose, linear cells; costae stout, smooth at back, subpercurrent to percurrent and confluent with border, or shortly excurrent into a mucro; upper cells 25–50 μm, isodiametric, hexagonal, quadrate or short‑rectangular, firm‑walled, juxtacostal cells conspicuously enlarged. Leaves of stolons often larger and remote, less decurrent, often subentire. Synoicous. Setae mulitple, yellow to red, 15–30 mm long. Capsules 2.5–3.0 mm long, oblong‑cylindric, horizontal to pendulous; stomata scattered over the capsule; opercula obliquely short- or long-rostrate, 1.0–1.5 mm long; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, yellow to yellow‑brown, dorsal surface finely papillose, endostome yellow, papillose, basal membrane high, segments stout and broadly perforate, cilia 2–4, nodose. Plants small to medium-sized, greenish yellow to reddish yellow above, brown below. Stems creeping, branches to 10 mm long, strongly tomentose. Leaves circinate‑crispate, at times spirally twisted when dry, erect‑spreading to erect-incurved with undulate margins when wet, 2–3 mm long, keeled, linear‑lanceolate; apices gradually rounded to a stout apiculus; margins entire, plane or weakly recurved at middle, bordered from _ the leaf length to near the apex by 3–4 rows of elongate, thick‑walled cells, basal marginal cells inflated, frequently with rhizoids, often with swollen teeth near leaf insertions; costae stoutly excurrent into an apiculus to 200 μm long; upper cells 6–8 μm, rounded, bulging mammillose, at times collenchymatous, extreme basal cells to 16 μm long, rounded‑rectangular, those near the costa neither enlarged nor thin‑walled. Dioicous. Setae 5–9 mm long, smooth. Capsules dark‑red, 2–3 mm long, oblong‑cylindric, weakly furrowed, wrinkled at neck and strongly contracted below mouth when dry; opercula erect rostrate, 1.5–2 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; peristome rudimentary, reduced to a short, densely papillose membrane projecting 80–160 μm above the capsule mouth.  Spores isosporous, 22–36 μm, papillose. Calyptrae ½ the capsule length, laciniate, plicate above, naked, 2–3 mm long.

Plants medium-sized to large, to 7 cm long, dull, yellowish to green or light green, at times with an intense blackish tinge. Secondary stems pendent, as-cending or erect, variously stipitate, simple to irregularly pinnate, complanate-foliate; secondary stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia broadly foliose. Stipe leaves evenly foliate, erect to erect-spreading. Secondary stems and branches complanate-foliate; leaves wide-spreading, strongly undulate when wet or dry, oblong-ligulate, 1.4–2.5 mm long, asym-metric, broadly rounded to truncate, not decurrent, clasping at base, rounded, cordate to auriculate at base; margins crenulate-serrulate at apex, distantly serrulate below, inflexed on one or both sides below; costae single, extending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, occasionally forked; cells smooth, apical cells horizontally rectangular, irregularly rectangular to rhombic, 8–18 µm long, median cells irregularly rhomboidal, 15–30 µm long, linear-fusiform toward insertion; alar cells weakly differentiated, of 2–5 short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions yellowish, porose. Plants small, yellowish green in tufts to 5 mm high; rhizoids moderately developed at base. Stem central strand absent. Plants medium-sized, grayish green, caespitose. Stems erect, branched at base, 15–30 mm, yellowish green, brittle when dry, central strand present, radiculose with dense, reddish brown tomentum; rhizoids branched, dimorphic, smooth; axillary hairs with 1–3, short-cylindric, red, basal cells, apical cell elongate-cylindric, becoming glutinous in age. Spores olive-brown, elliptical, 8–13 μm, minutely papillose or smooth. Calyptrae conic, smooth, greenish yellow.
