Asexual reproduction by frag-ile leaf apices. Dioicous. Male plants smaller, more slender than female plants. Perigonia and perichaetia sessile along stems and branches. Setae elongate, 10–18 mm long, yellow when young, becoming red to red brown when old, spinose to hispid. Capsules suberect to inclined, ovoid, neck mod-erately developed, 1.0–1.5 mm long; exothecial cells at mouth reddish, quadrate to shortly oblate in 2–3 rows, yellowish,

Andreaea alpestris (Thed.) Schimp. in B.S.G., Bryol. Eur. 6: 146. 1855. A. petrophila Ehrh. var. alpestris Thed., Bot. Not. 5: 79. 1849. A. rupestris Hedw. var. alpestris (Thed.) Sharp in Grout, Moss Fl. N. Amer. 1: 2. 1936. Type. Sweden, Thedenius.

Plants small, 1–2 cm high. Leaves without a whitish bloom, imbricate-appressed, lanceolate, concave, weakly cucullate above, somewhat constricted above the base, weakly panduriform, 0.5–1.0 mm long, apices straight, obtuse; margins erect somewhat incurved above; lamina unistratose or bistratose in streaks; ecostate; upper leaf cells irregularly short rectangular to quadrate or oval, 7–10 µm ×5 µm, firm-walled to incrassate, not pitted; lower leaf cells 12–30 µm × 7 µm, yellowish, long-rectangular, incrassate, pitted and sinuous; cells smooth or with low, weak dorsal papillae. Perichaetial leaves differentiated, sheathing, convolute. Sporophytes as in the genus. Spores not seen.

Campylopus surinamensis C. Müll., Linnaea 21: 186. 1848. Type. Suriname, Kegel 516.

Campylopus gracilicaulis Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 83. 1869. Syntypes. Brazil, Fl. Negro, Spruce 60 (NY); Fl. Amazon, Santarém, Spruce 60b (NY).

Campylopus costaricensis Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 62. 1928. Type. Costa Rica, Limón, Finca Montecristo, on Río Renventazon below Cario, Standley & Valerio 48579 (FH, US).

 

Plants medium sized, forming loose tufts, yellowish to bright green; stems variously tomentose, to 3.5 cm long. Leaves typically spreading at base, becoming abruptly appressed to the stem, then crowded and spreading in apical comal tufts, exceedingly variable in shape: basal leaves oblong-ovate, acute, to 3 mm long, concave; margins inflexed, serrate at apex, not bordered by elongate cells; upper leaves linear-lanceolate, concave, acute, to 2–4 mm long, serrate or entire, not bordered by elongate cells; costa percurrent in basal leaves, excurrent in others, at times more or less hyaline, ridged on back and dorsally serrate above, frequently spurred, in cross section with ventral hyalocysts equal to or smaller than the guide cells, dorsal stereids well developed; upper cells short to long rhomboidal, firm-walled not pitted, median cells rhomboidal to rectangular, firm-walled, basal cells above the alar cells quadrate to rectangular, thin walled; alar cells of basal leaves inflated, brown, well-developed, alar cells of other leaves poorly developed, hyaline. Perichaetial leaves frequently hyaline hair-tipped. Sporophytes unknown in Central America.

Campylopus weberbaueri Broth., Bot. Jahrb. Syst. 56: 5. 1920. Type. Peru, Dept. Loreto, Weberbauer 4718.

Campylopus wurdackii Robins., Bryologist 70: 319. 1967. Type. Peru, Dept. Amazonas, Prov. Chachapoyas, Wurdack 1524 (US).

Plants large, laxly caespitose, pale green to yellow; stems moderately red-tomentose, with comal tufts, 2–6 cm long. Leaves 8–13 mm long, circinate above, stem leaves erect, comal leaves patent, narrowly lanceolate, oblong below, long-subulate above; margins serrate; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent, 1/3–1/2 the leaf width at base, sharply serrate above at back, in cross section guide cells well-developed, ventral hyalocysts absent, dorsal and ventral stereid bands well-developed; upper cells quadrate, firm-walled, not porose; basal cells long rectangular, incrassate and porose, those at the margin narrower, forming an indistinct, non-hyaline border; alar cells reddish brown, in excavate groups. Setae clustered in comal tufts, 7–8 mm long, yellow; capsules oval, inclined, plicate when dry, 1.5–2.0 mm long, strumose at base. Calyptrae ciliate at base.

Aongstroemia julacea (Hook.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 27. 1869. Gymnostomum julaceum Hook., Musci Exot. 1:42. 1818. Type. Ecuador, Humboldt & Bonpland.

Plants minute, delicate, scattered to gregarious, green to yellowish green; stems slender, 2–3–10) mm long, irregularly and simply branched. Leaves minute, shortly-oval, 0.4–0.8 mm long; apex rounded-apiculate to obtuse; margins plane to weakly erect, erose-denticulate (frequently by double projecting cells in the upper two-thirds); costa ending below apex, smooth; upper cells oval-rhomboidal, incrassate, basal cells larger, quadrate to shortly rectangular. Sporophytes not seen from Central America, reported by Mitten (1869) as setae elongate, capsule oblong, annuli large, peristome absent.

Holomitrium pulchellum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 60. 1869. Type. Ecuador, Spruce 26 (NY).

 

Breedlovea chiapensis Crum, Bryologist 89: 23. 1986. Type. Mexico, Chiapas, Breedlove 15087 (MO).

Plants slender, forming compact cushions; stems 5–20 mm long. Leaves crowded, erect-spreading to flexuous when wet, crisped and contorted with the apex more or less spirally twisted when dry, keeled to canaliculate above, linear-lanceolate, 3–7 mm long, acuminate, weakly clasping at base; margins erect, entire or weakly crenulate to toothed at the extreme apex, unistratose; costa smooth at back; upper leaf cells quadrate to rounded, incrassate with straight or wavy walls; basal cells linear, strongly differentiated, incrassate and pitted; alar cells weakly differentiated, fugacious and remaining on stem when leaves are removed, hyaline.Perichaetial leaves reaching mid-capsule. Setae 5–10 mm long, yellow; capsules oblong, 1.5 mm long; peristome reddish, lanceolate, undivided or irregularly fenestrate, papillose throughout or the papillae arranged in weak vertical rows; opercula 1 mm long.

Tetraplodon mnioides (Hedw.) Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G., Bryol. Eur. 3: 215 (fasc. 23–24). 1844. Splachnum mnioides Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 51. 1801. Protologue: Czechoslovakia and Austria. Alpestribus locis provenit, (in Sudetibus, Krug, in Austria, Host.)

Plants densely caespitose, yellowish green above, brownish below. Stems erect, 30–45 mm high, branched at base, central strand present, tomentose; rhizoids red-brown or brown, smooth, dimorphic; axillary hairs of 1–2 red basal cells and a hyaline, elongate terminal cell. Leaves erect and somewhat concave when moist, clasping below, variously twisted, folded and undulate when dry, oblong-¬obovate, abruptly subulate to a  filiform apex; margins erect or somewhat inrolled in the upper ¾ of the leaf, plane below, entire; costa single, yellowish green, percurrent, narrow above; upper cells rhombic, 47–70 x18–23 μm, thin-¬walled, lower leaf cells rectangular, 91–150 x 25–34 μm, thin-walled, upper marginal cells more or less rectangular. Autoicous. Setae single, 3–7 mm long, erect or slightly curved, bright red when young, becoming dark brownish red in age, cells mammillose. Capsules 2.5–4.2 mm long, erect or suberect, red when young becoming dark reddish brown in age, subcylindric, contracted slightly below the mouth, neck comprising _ of the capsule length, irregularly longitudinally wrinkled, not wider than the urn, smoothly tapered to the seta; exothecial cells below the mouth oblate in 10–16 rows, lower urn exothecial cells rectangular, 40–81 x12–31 μm, neck cells rectangular, 37–75 x 18–44 μm; stomata in neck, phaneroporic, long-pored; opercula convex-discoid, blackish red; peristome of  8 exostome teeth, sometimes splitting into 16 with age, red or reddish brown, deeply inserted within the capsule, strongly reflexed when dry, papillose, outer surface with 4 columns of cell remnants, inner surface hyaline, thin, with 2 columns of cell remnants. Spores subspherical, 10–14 μm, tan in mass, smooth. Calyptra conic, 2.5–3 mm long, reddish to golden and somewhat verrucose above, pale golden and smooth below, slit on one side.

Philonotis longiseta (Michx.) Britt., Bryologist 14: 44. 1911.

Bartramia longiseta Michx., Fl. Bor.-Amer. 2: 301. 1803. Protologue: Carolina and Virginia. In Carolina, ex herbario D. Bosc, et in Virginia ex D. Beauvois.

Philonotis graminicola C. Müll., Linnaea 38: 632. 1874. Protologue: Mexico. Orizaba? Satorius in Hb. C. Mohr. Ex Hb. Hmp. a Freder. Müller in monte Orizaba lectam habeo.

Plants small to medium-sized, in loose, yellowish‑green or green tufts, to 15 mm high. Stems red; rhizoids at base, reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 1–2.5 mm long, erect to erect-spreading when dry or erect-spreading when wet, straight or secund, lanceolate to triangular-lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins narrowly revolute, singly or doubly serrate; costa long-excurrent; cells papillose, papillae at upper cell ends, upper cells rectangular, firm‑walled, 25–47 x 6–8 μm, basal cells rectangular, to 50 x 12 μm, alar cells short-rectangular or with 2-3 quadrate cells at extreme base. Autoicous. Perigonia gemmiform, axillary, below the perichaetia. Setae 10–33 mm long, red. Capsules 2–3 mm long, brown, ovoid to subglobose, inclined to pendent, abruptly constricted at neck; exothecial cells thick-walled; opercula 0.5 mm long, conic‑mammillate; peristome double, exostome teeth red, outer surface densely and thickly papillose above, finely and evenly papillose below, trabeculae thin, inner surface smooth, trabeculae thick, endostome yellow, evenly papillose throughout, basal membrane short, each segment split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia, cilia 1–3, short, stout. Spores reniform, 20–27 μm, papillose.

Campylopus cavifolius Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 87. 1869. Syntypes. Ecuador, Andes Quitenses, in montibus Chimborazo Cordovasto, Titaicun, Spruce 50, Jameson.

Plants large, compactly tufted, greenish yellow, frequently dark reddish yellow, more or less glossy; stems moderately tomentose, to 8 cm long, hyalodermis present, of 1–2 layers of enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline cells. Leaves 10–12 mm long, stiffly erect, linear-lanceolate, apex setaceous; margins entire below, weakly toothed at the extreme apex; costa excurrent, at times subhyaline at tip, 3/4 the leaf width at base, dorsal surface smooth, in cross section ventral hyalocysts large and well developed, guide cells well developed, stereid cells present in the middle of leaf but not extending to costa margins, the edges of costa therefore composed of 2–3 layers of enlarged, thin-walled cells; upper cells narrowly oblong to linear, 20–50 µm long, incrassate, not porose, more or less flexuous; basal cells incrassate, not porose, long rectangular, near the costa 40–65 µm, becoming narrow and elongate toward the margins and forming a distinct border to 10 cells wide; alar cells reddish, weakly developed, frequently remaining on stem when leaves are dissected away. Sporophytes not seen.

Leucoloma cruegerianum (C. Müll.). Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1870–71: 412. 1872. Dicranum cruegerianum C. Müll.., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 588. 1851. Poecilophyllum cruegerianum (C. Müll.). Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 92. 1869. Type. Trinidad, Crüger.

Dicranum subimmarginatum C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 589. 1851. Poecilophyllum subimmarginatum (C. Müll.). Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 94. 1869. Leucoloma subimmarginatum (C. Müll.). Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges., 1870–71: 413. 1872. Type. Costa Rica, Oersted.

Plants small, whitish to glaucous green; stems fragile, 0.5–2.0 cm long. Leaves crowded, evenly spaced, flexuous to wide-spreading, lanceolate-subulate, 2.5–5 mm long, apex setaceous; margins tubulose above subtubulose to incurved below; entire throughout except for the sharply denticulate apex, limbidia at midleaf well developed, 6–10 cells, ending in the acumen, distinct at leaf base; costa percurrent, smooth to papillose above at back; upper leaf cells irregularly sub-quadrate, densely pluripapillose, walls thickened; basal cells elongate-rectangular, walls at times pitted, smooth to weakly papillose, grading into the upper leaf cells; alar cells enlarged and firm-walled, yellow-red. Setae 10–12 mm long, red; capsules erect, cylindrical, 2–3 mm long, smooth above, scabrose at base, red; stomata absent; peristome teeth red, lanceolate, striate below; opercula 1.5 mm long. Calyptrae 2.0 mm long, smooth. Spores rounded, smooth.

Plants medium-sized, glossy, pale green, yellowish green, or reddish brown, in loose mats. Stems prostrate, simple or irregularly branched, 2–4 cm long, hyaline to pale green when young, becoming red with age, complanate-foliate; young stems in cross section with outer cells smaller than the inner cells, otherwise cells thin-walled and undifferentiated, old stems in cross section with epidermis of 1–2 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; pa-raphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves flattened, lateral leaves spread-ing, dorsal and ventral leaves erect to erect-spreading, laxly crispate when dry, flaccid when wet, somewhat distantly spaced, ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm long, asymmetric, gradually narrowed to long or piliferous, flexuose or undulate apices; margins entire or subentire, at times with distantly serru-late apices, plane, not decurrent; costae very short and double or absent; cells smooth, thin-walled, linear-flexuose to fusiform, 80–140 X 10–14 µm; basal cells enlarged, broadly long-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Synoicous. Setae elongate, red, flexuose, 1–3 cm long, smooth, at times some-what roughened below capsules. Capsules inclined to arcuate, asymmetric, short-cylindric, 1.5–2.5 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells rounded to short-rectangular, incrassate, collenchyma-tous; stomata rudimentary, 3–5-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 1.0 mm long; annuli well de-veloped, of 7–8 rows of thin-walled, quadrate cells, persistent at the base of the opercula; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular, dorsal (outer) surface yellow, with broad median fur-rows, densely and closely cross-striate and papillose below, coarsely papillose above, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, smooth to lightly papillose, trabeculae weakly projecting; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments broad, keeled, weakly perforate, cilia absent or rudimentary.

Andreaea subulata Harv. in Hook., Icon. Pl. Rar. 3: 201. 1840.

Type. South Africa, Cape of Good Hope, Harvey.

Plants small, 1–2 cm high. Plants medium sized, reddish green; stems 1–2 cm long. Leaves evenly spaced, curved-secund, lanceolate-subulate, 3–5 mm long, subulate; margins incurved to subtubulose, entire, denticulate at the extreme apex, limbidia narrow and poorly defined above, 2–3 rows of cells at midleaf, merging with the basal cells below; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent, smooth to weakly papillose above at back; all leaf cells elongate and firm-walled, weakly pluripapillose above, smooth below; basal cells pitted; alar cells in bulging groups, reddish brown, firm-walled. Plants medium sized, pale greenish or reddish yellow; stems to 8 cm long. Leaves evenly spaced, wide-spreading to patent, often nearly straight or somewhat curved, secund at stem apex, linear-lanceolate, 4–7 mm long, narrowly subulate-acuminate to setaceous; margins incurved, sharply serrulate above, limbidia not reaching the apex, 2–3 cells wide in upper 1/3, increasing rapidly to 10–16 cells wide at midleaf and contrasting sharply with the smaller interior cells; costa excurrent, papillose at back; upper leaf cells oblong, incrassate, short oblong along the costa in a broad band nearly to the leaf base; alar cells in bulging reddish groups of thin-walled, rectangular cells, commonly remaining on the stem when the leaves are removed. Plants in rather small, dense, rounded clumps, soft, pale orange-brown or green tinged with red or pink; capitulum rounded in profile; cortical cells in 3–4 layers, those of the epidermis with 1–3 (rarely 6–8) pores and fibrils few and delicate or none; wood cylinder brown to dark purplish red. Stem leaves lingulate, rounded at the apex, finely fringed all around, generally approaching branch leaves in fibrils, pores, and membrane gaps. Branches in fascicles of 4-5 (2 spreading); cortical cells porose at their upper ends, with fibrils very delicate or, more often, lacking. Branch leaves ovate, broadly pointed, and concave-cucullate, roughened at back of the apex and denticulate along a marginal resorption furrow; hyaline cells convex on both surfaces, on the outer surface with few inconspicuous pseudopores in 2's and 3's at adjacent corners, passing into irregular membrane gaps above, on the inner surface with few large, unringed pores at corners and commissures; green cells in section narrowly rectangular or lenticular, equally exposed on both surfaces.

Plants robust, dark, greasy green above and brown below or yellow-brown throughout, in wide carpets; cortical cells in 3–4 layers, the outermost fibrillose, with 1–6 irregularly rounded pores; wood cylinder brown. Stem leaves lingulate, broadly rounded at the apex, with a broad, finely fringed mesh at the margins; hyaline cells often 1–2-divided, on the outer surface almost completely resorbed, on the inner surface with small pores and traces of fibrils, especially near the leaf apex. Branches in fascicles of 4–5 (2 spreading), stoutly club-shaped; cortical cells nested together by funnel-shaped bases porose at the bottom, fibrillose, the inner wall densely cross-fibrillose, the outer surface lacking pores. Branch leaves imbricate, dimorphous: those at the base of branches cucullate-concave, broadly ovate, hyaline-fringed, the hyaline cells on the outer surface strongly convex, almost entirely resorbed toward the leaf tip, with 7–10 large, elliptic commissural pores below, on the inner surface with about 4 small, elliptic corner pores in the upper part of the leaf but more numerous larger, round pores in side regions; leaves of the upper part of branches much larger, denticulate along a marginal resorption furrow, with hyaline cells resorbed on the outer surface only in a few apical cells; green cells in section equilateral-triangular and exposed on the inner surface (or rarely more or less trapezoidal with narrow exposure on the outer surface), the walls of adjacent hyaline cells usually beset with fringe fibrils (sometimes evident only near leaf bases).

Leaves erect, appressed, with flexuose apex when dry, spreading to nearly spreading when moist, 2–3 mm long, lanceolate, gradually tapering into an acuminate apex, canaliculate, muticous; margins broadly recurved to 1/2 the leaf length on one side and flat on the other side, occasionally only shortly and narrowly recurved in the middle of one side, entire; costa percurrent, reniform, broad and not prominent on the dorsal surface; laminae 2-stratose in the distal half, mainly towards the margins; cells smooth, upper cells 5–16 μm, irregularly quadrate to rectangular, incrassate, sinuose when rectangular, basal cells near costa 25–80 x 6–12 μm, rectangular to narrowly rectangular, with thin, smooth or weakly sinuose walls, basal marginal cells 10–30 x 10–16 μm, isodiametric to rectangular, with transverse walls thicker than longitudinal walls. Perichaetial leaves 4.0–5.5 mm, muticous. Dioicous. Setae straight, 1.5–2.0 mm long. Capsules immersed, ellipsoid to ovoid, erect, symmetric, smooth; stomata superficial in neck; opercula rostellate to rostrate; annuli of 1–3 rows of cells; peristome teeth 16, narrowly triangular, red to yellowish, outer surface nearly smooth below, papillose above, inner surface papillose throughout. Spores 10–16 μm, granulose. Calyptrae mitrate.

Plants medium-sized, in green or yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched,
leaves reduced; rhizoids red brown, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, not or rarely
branched. Secondary stems erect, 2–4.5 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis
of 3–5 rows of small, orange to red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to
hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia subfoliose.
Secondary stem and branch leaves ovate to broadly ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.7 mm long, imbricate
when dry, spreading to wide-spreading when wet, acute to shortly acuminate, decurrent; margins
plane, serrulate at the apex; costae strong, 0.4–0.6 the leaf length; upper cells oval to elliptic, 12–16 μm
long, very thick-walled, smooth or prorate, median cells oval, 12–18 μm long; basal cells near the
costae short-rectangular, thick-walled, to 35 μm long, with straight or occasionally porose cell walls;
alar cells quadrate, or oblate, thick-walled, smooth. Autoicous. Perigonia gemmate, borne laterally,
leaves ovate, concave, acuminate, ecostate; perichaetia terminal, leaves erect, oblong to obovate, 2–3 mm
long, gradually contracted to long, serrate awns, margins recurved, costae long-excurrent, lower leaf
cells linear, thin-walled. Setae short, to 0.5 μm long, yellow to red, cells quadrate. Capsules immersed,
ovoid to ellipsoid, 1.3–1.8 mm long, smooth, light brown, narrowed at the mouth, abruptly
rounded-indented to the setae; exothecial cells small, red, in 2–3 rows below the mouth, irregularly
quadrate to rectangular below; stomata superficial, at junction of seta and capsule; opercula highconic
to short rostrate, smooth, 0.5 mm long; annuli compound, revoluble; peristome diplolepideous;
exostome teeth deeply inserted within the mouth, linear, whitish yellow, densely and thickly papillose
with papillae often branched, to 0.5 mm long; endostome absent. Spores spherical, lightly papillose,
20–30 μm. Calyptrae conic-mitrate, prorate, basally split, 0.5–0.7 mm long.

Fissidens papillosus Lac., Natuurk. Verh. K. Akad. Wet. Amsterdam 13: 1. 1872. Type. Java, de Vriese (L).

Fissidens donnellii Aust., Bot. Gaz. (Crawfordsville) 4: 151. 1879. Type. Florida, Smith & Austin (NY).

Fissidens crenatoserrulatus Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 70. 1909. Type. Mexico, Pringle 15167(PC).

Plants to ca. 3 mm × ca. 2 mm. Leaves to 1.6 mm × ca. 0.3 mm; apex obtuse to acute; margins serrulate-dentate, often coarsely so on vaginant laminae, elimbate; vaginant laminae unequal, ca. 1/2 the leaf length; costa ending 2–4 cells below the apex; cells 7–11 µm, mammillose (unipapillose), hexagonal. Sporophytes terminal.

Fissidens platyphyllus Broth., Akad. Wiss. Wien, Math.-Naturwiss. Kl. Denkschr. 83: 275. 1926. Type. Brazil, Ule, Bryotheca brasiliensis 122 p.p. (BM, H).

Fissidens tamaulipasensis Pursell, Cryptogamie, Bryol. Lichénol. 7: 41. 1986. Type. Mexico, Sharp 3512 (PAC, TENN).

Plants 1.5–5 mm × ca. 2 mm. Leaves to ca. 3 mm × ca. 0.4 mm; apex acute to rounded; margins serrate, often coarsely so on the vaginant laminae, elimbate; vaginant laminae slightly unequal, acute, ca. 1/2 the leaf length; costa percurrent to ending 2–4 cells below the apex; cells 7.5–13 µm, slightly bulging to smooth, irregularly hexagonal, lower juxtacostal cells of the vaginant laminae enlarged and pellucid. Sporophytes terminal.

Plants medium-sized to robust, 3–8 cm long, pale green or yellowish green, lustrous, in thin mats. Stems prostrate, simple or sparsely and irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, be-coming reddish with age, complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with epidermis and cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand rudimentary to weakly developed; paraphyllia absent; pseudopa-raphyllia foliose; axillary hairs fugacious, 2–3 cells long, basal cell quadrate, hyaline, median cell (when present) subrectangular, hyaline, upper cell oblong, reddish brown; rhizoids from initials ab-axial to the leaf insertions, reddish brown, papillose-roughened, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves not or slightly contorted when dry. Lateral leaves flattened, wide-spreading when wet, slightly asymmetric, ovate to oblong-ovate, 3–6 mm long, gradually acute to bluntly acute, sometimes rounded; margins entire, plane, not or obscurely bordered by a single row of somewhat elongate and broader cells; costa absent, or leaves with bistratose region at the very base; cells smooth, elongate-hexagonal to rhomboidal, 102–205 # 41–62 µm, laxly bulging; alar cells undif-ferentiated. Dorsal leaves erect, symmetric; margins plane. Asexual reproduction by reddish brown, papillose-roughened, rhizoid-like propagula, usually with straight cross-walls originating from ne-matogen cells at leaf apices and along or near leaf margins. Autoicous. Perigonia and perichaetia sessile along stems and branches. Setae elongate, 8–20 mm long, reddish to orange, smooth, flexu-ose. Capsules inclined to pendent, ovoid to short-cylindric, neck moderately developed, 1–2 mm long; exothecial cells at mouth reddish, quadrate to shortly oblate in 5–8 rows, short-rectangular below, collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic to conic-rostrate, 0.7–1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary, deciduous; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, dark red, not furrowed, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, median line and trabec-ulae weakly developed, ventral surface smooth, trabeculae well developed and projecting; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish white, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, seg-ments broad, strongly keeled, faintly perforate, cilia absent. Spores rounded, 12–16 µm, faintly pa-pillose. Calyptrae mitrate, yellowish white, irregularly lobed at base, naked, fleshy, 3–5 cells thick, inner 2 layers small, thick-walled,

Plants small and slender, in dull green or yellow green, pendent masses. Stems irregularly to pin-nately branched, not stipitate, to 10 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 2–4 rows of small, yellow or red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm-walled, central strand weakly developed; paraphyllia and pseudoparaphyllia absent, scale leaves present; rhi-zoids sparsely developed, when present reddish brown, smooth, not or rarely branched, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions; axillary hairs with 1–2 short, subquadrate, basal cells and 3–4 short, rounded, hyaline upper cells. Stem and branch leaves widely spaced, erect-spreading to spread-ing and twisted when dry, erect-spreading when wet, lanceolate with a somewhat ovate, strongly clasping base, 1.6–2.0 mm long, gradually tapered to long, slender hair-points, plane, smooth, cor-date at base, slightly decurrent; margins plane, serrulate to serrate above, crenulate by projecting papillae below; costae single, ending at or a little above midleaf, in cross section consisting of ho-mogeneous, thick-walled cells; cells seriate-papillose with 3–5 papillae over the cell lumina and/or cell walls, upper and median cells linear, firm-walled, 40–80 # 3–4 µm; basal cells oblong to rectan-gular, 20–50 # 5–10 µm, smooth and porose; alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen.

Macromitrium dubium Schimp. ex C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 723. 1849.

Protologue: St. Kitts. In truncis arborum montium insulae, s. coll. & n. (NY).

Plants medium-sized, reddish yellow. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 2 cm long, weakly tomentose below. Leaves weakly keeled at base, erect below, flexuose above when dry, erect to erect‑spreading when wet, 6–9 mm long, 0.5–0.7 mm wide, linear‑lanceolate; apices long acuminate; margins plane, entire to obscurely serrulate, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae subpercurrent; upper leaf cells 36–52 μm long, 10 μm wide, linear‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 60–72 x 10 μm, linear‑rectangular, incrassate, porose, not tuberculate. Setae (12–)15–20 mm long, smooth. Capsules 2–2.5 mm long, cylindrical, smooth; opercula rostrate, to 2 mm long; peristome absent. Spores isosporous, 24–40 μm, papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, entire, naked, 2.5–3.0 mm long.

Macromitrium flavopilosum Williams, Bull. Torrey Bot. Club 38: 38: 34. 1911.

Protologue: Panama. Cana, Prov. Darien, Panama. Williams 1063 (F, FH, NY).

Plants medium-sized to large-sized, reddish green to reddish yellow. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 4 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves keeled, erect below, flexuose to spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, erect to erect‑patent when wet, 5.5–7.0 mm long, 1 mm wide, lanceolate; apices acute to somewhat rounded into a long, setaceous, excurrent costa; margins undulate or plane, obscurely serrulate by projecting cell end‑walls below, serrate near apex, recurved below, recurved to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae long-excurrent into a naked awn 1–2 mm long; upper interior cells 12–16 μm long, long‑rhomboidal to fusiform, incrassate and porose, upper marginal cells linear, forming a distinct border, basal cells 46–54 μm long, narrowly long-rectangular, incrassate and porose, not tuberculate. Setae 10–15 mm long, smooth. Capsules to 2 mm long, obovoid, smooth; opercula rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; peristome not seen, "double, papillose, reddish brown, the outer a low cylinder with irregular margin, the inner a little higher than the outer with margin more deeply incised" (Williams 1911). Spores anisosporous, 12–16 μm, hyaline, smooth and 30–32 μm, reddish‑brown, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 3 mm long.

Macromitrium greenmanii Grout, Bryologist 47: 11. 1944.

Protologue: Costa Rica, Greenman [sic], 5574 in Herb. Bartram (FH, MO).

Plants robust-sized, reddish yellow. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 3 cm long, moderately tomentose at base of branches. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, flexuose to spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, erect‑patent when wet, 3–5 x 0.5–1 mm, lanceolate to linear-lanceolate; apices shortly acuminate; margins entire to serrulate, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae percurrent; upper interior cells 10–12 x 6–8 μm, strongly rounded, shortly rectangular to nearly quadrate, smooth to bulging mammillose, upper marginal cells not forming a border, basal cells 24–40 μm long, rectangular, incrassate and porose, strongly tuberculate. Setae 10–15 mm long, papillose. Capsules 2–3 mm long, cylindrical, furrowed; opercula rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth 16, narrowly triangular, 480 μm high, free, yellow to hyaline, papillose, endostome hyaline, smooth, basal membrane 140 μm high, segments 80 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 18–22 μm, smooth, hyaline and 32–48 μm, papillose, yellowish‑brown. Calyptrae mitrate, laciniate, naked, 3–4 mm long.

Macromitrium podocarpi C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 6: 96. 1898.

Protologue: Brazil. Brasilia, Minas Geraës, Serra Itabira do Campo, ad truncos arborum, Aprili 1892, E. Ule, Coll. N° 1066 (NY, as Bryotheca brasiliensis 222).

Macromitrium portoricense Williams, Bryologist 32: 69. 1929. Protologue: Puerto Rico. On road between Maricao and Monte Alegrillo, Porto Rico, at 500–900 meters, on exposed rock. No. 2638. Elizabeth G. Britton, April 13, 1913 (NY), syn. nov.

Plants slender, yellow‑green to dark green. Stems strongly creeping, branches 1.0–1.5(–3.0) cm long, densely red‑tomentose at base. Leaves moderately keeled, erect below, crispate to flexuose‑contorted above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 1.5–2.2 x 0.5 mm, lanceolate; apices broadly acute to obtusely‑apiculate; margins entire or crenulate, recurved or plane below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion present; costae percurrent or excurrent into a short apiculus; upper interior cells 6–12 μm, rounded to hexagonal‑rounded, bulging mammillose, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells to 40 μm long, long‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, tuberculate. Setae 4–5 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1–1.5 mm long, cylindrical to oblong‑ovate, weakly or strongly furrowed, at times only wrinkled; opercula rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth lanceolate, 160–180 μm high, whitish, densely papillose, united forming an erect membrane, endostome hyaline, weakly papillose, basal membrane 80 μm high, segments 100 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 10–14 μm, smooth, thin‑walled and 16–28 μm, weakly papillose, thick‑walled. Calyptrae mitrate, laciniate, naked, to 2.5 mm long.

Plants small, green to yellowish green, occasionally yellowish red, in loose, glossy mats. Primary stems creeping, to 6.5 cm long, secondary stems erect to 1 cm long, sparsely and irregularly branched, yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with epidermis of 2–4 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2–3 cells long, basal 1–2 cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from dense clusters of initials abaxial to the primary stem leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irreg-ularly branched. Leaves somewhat erect, flattened, not undulate when wet or dry, primary stem leaves triangular-lanceolate to broadly ovate-lanceolate, 0.9–1.2 mm long; secondary stem leaves ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1.0–1.3 mm long, broadly acuminate; margins serrulate above, subentire below, broadly incurved on one side below, plane to erect above, rounded at base; costae double, thin, ending 3/4 the leaf length, more or less parallel above the base, one branch often longer than the other, smooth on back, not or weakly projecting at the tips; cells smooth, firm- to thick-walled, upper cells long-rectangular to linear, at times flexuose, usually porose, 18–40 # 3–4 µm, median cells and basal cells linear-flexuose, porose, to 60 µm long; basal cells near the insertions oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular; alar cells undifferentiated. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 1.5–2.0 cm long, red, smooth. Cap-sules inclined, symmetric and cylindric, neck well developed, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exothecial cells oblong to rounded-rectangular, incrassate, more or less collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 4–6-celled, on neck; operculum and annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, densely and closely striate below, coarsely papillose above, ventral surface hyaline to yellowish, smooth to lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments broad, strongly keeled, cilia absent or rudimentary. Spores rounded, 12–18 µm, papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants slender, 1–4 cm long. Leaves pale green to yellowish green, in thin mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly to subpinnately branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming red with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, subepidermal layer of 1–2 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-patent, flexuose-contorted when dry, erect-spreading when wet, monomorphic, oblong-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.5 mm long, symmetric, abruptly constricted at base of acumina, concave; margins serrate to serrulate in upper 2/3, subentire below, plane to erect, not bordered; costae double, thin, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, usually unequal, smooth at back, often projecting at the apex; upper and median cells spiculose-papillose, papillae to 10 µm high, upper cells flexuose-elongate, 30–40 X 3–4 µm, firm-walled, not porose, lower cells enlarged, oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular, thin-walled, bulging near insertions, cells across the insertions short-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 20–25 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth below, papillose to scabrose below the capsules. Capsules inclined to pendent, short-cylindric, 1–2 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below ob-long to rectangular, collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 4–6-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 1.0 mm long; annuli of 7–9 rows of quadrate cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangu-lar with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface orange, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellowish hyaline, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose throughout, basal mem-branes high, segments broad,

Plants medium-sized to robust, 3–6 cm long, greenish, yellowish green, to golden, in dense mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly subpinnately branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, subepidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves monomorphic, erect-spreading, somewhat crispate to lightly undulate when dry, erect to erect-spreading when wet, ovate-to oblong-lanceolate, 1.4–1.8 mm long, symmetric, gradually to abruptly acuminate, occasionally blunt at the apex, flat to concave; margins sharply serrate in upper 2/3 by greatly enlarged, swollen, bifid teeth, serrulate at base, plane or erect, not bordered; costae double, diverging throughout, on lateral and dorsal leaves ending 1/2–2/3 the leaf length, variously spinose at back by swollen, bifid teeth, strongly projecting at tips, on ventral leaves ending 1/4 the leaf length, smooth at back, not pro-jecting at the tips; cells smooth, thin-walled, not porose, linear-flexuose throughout, upper cells 90–100 X 6–10 µm, median and basal cells 100–180 X 6–10 µm, enlarged, more or less bulging, often porose, oblong-rectangular near the insertions; alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 15–20 mm long, red, smooth throughout, or at times roughened on neck and below the cap-sules. Capsules horizontal to pendent, oblong-cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; opercula long conic-rostrate, 0.75 mm long; annuli of 2–3 rows of thin-walled, quadrate to short-rectangular cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base, and persistent on the operculum; peri-stome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-stri-ate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowi

Plants medium-sized, 2–6 cm long, green, yellowish, or yellow brown, in mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly to subpinnately branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with hyalodermis, subepidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-patent, flexuose-contorted, at times lightly undulate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, monomor-phic, oblong- to ovate-lanceolate, 2–3 mm long, symmetric, abruptly constricted at base of acumina, concave; margins serrulate to serrate in upper 2/3, subentire below, plane to erect, not bordered; costae double, thin, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, usually unequal, smooth at back, oc-casionally projecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells linear-elongate, 40–90 X 3–5 µm, firm-walled, porose, lower cells oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular, porose, bulging near insertions, cells across the insertions short-rectangular, porose; alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 25–40 mm long, red, smooth throughout, or at times somewhat roughened below the cap-sules. Capsules horizontal to pendent, oblong-cylindric, 1.5–2.5 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; opercula long conic-rostrate, 1.0–1.5 mm long; annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly tri-angular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish,

Plants slender to medium-sized, dull, light green, yellow green, reddish yellow, or brownish green, in loose mats often with pendent strands. Stolons yellow to red, creeping; rhizoids on stolons, at base of stipitate stems, or on flagelliform branch tips, red, not or irregularly branched, from clus-ters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions; leaves widely spaced, reduced, erect, ovate-triangular, abruptly acuminate, ecostate, 1.0–1.4 mm long. Stems stipitate or nonstipitate, horizontal, erect or pendent, frequently and irregularly branched, branches at times with flagelliform tips, 4–10(–40) cm long, yellowish green, becoming dark red with age; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 small, thick-walled, yellowish to reddish orange cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, pale yel-low, red with age, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent, pseudoparaphyllia absent, scale leaves present; axillary hairs 2–3 cells long, basal cell quadrate to subquadrate, reddish brown, upper 1–2 cells broadly cylindrical, red. Stipe leaves ovate, cordate, rounded to the insertions. Stem and branch apices turgid; stem and branch leaves differentiated only in size, stem leaves not or obscurely ranked when dry, branch leaves often distinctly seriately ranked when dry or wet, leaves obovate to oblong-obovate, erect to erect-spreading, variously clasping below, 1.0–1.2 mm long, auriculate, apex cusp-idate; margins broadly incurved and sharply serrulate above, plane or broadly incurved, serrulate or entire below; costae mostly absent, occasionally short double or short single; leaf cells long-flexuose, smooth, upper cells 20–40 X 4–6 µm, median cells 30–60 X 3–4 µm, outer basal cells shorter and broader, inner basal cells near insertion elongate, often porose; alar cells red to red yellow, sub-quadrate to short-rectangular, not reaching the outer margins or extending up the margins, cells across the insertions yellow. Asexual reproduction by deciduous leaves. Dioicous. Perigonia gemmiform, lateral on secondary stems and branches, 0.8–1.2 mm long; leaves ovate, acuminate. Perichaetia lat-eral, 1.4–2.0 mm long; leaves lanceolate, vaginulae moderately hairy. Setae short, wavy, 3–5 mm long, smooth below, roughened above, yellow, becomi

Plants slender, dull, yellow green, reddish yellow, or brownish red, in dense mats. Stolons red, creeping; rhizoids only on stolons, red, not or irregularly branched, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions; leaves widely spaced, reduced, erect, broadly ovate, abruptly long-pointed, ecostate or costa short and double, 0.6–0-8 mm long. Stems occasionally stipitate, horizontal or erect, frequently and irregularly branched, at times with flagelliform tips, to 5 cm long, yellowish green, becoming dark red with age; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 small, thick-walled, reddish orange cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, pale yellow, red with age, central strand absent; paraphyllia ab-sent, pseudoparaphyllia absent, scale leaves present; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, basal cell quadrate to subquadrate, reddish brown, upper 2–3 cells broadly cylindrical, hyaline or reddish. Stem and branch apices turgid; stem and branch leaves differentiated only in size, obscurely seriately ranked when dry, distinctly so when wet; leaves panduriform, broadly oblong, appressed and clasping below, broadly obovate, abruptly flexed and spreading above, stem leaves 1.0–1.5 mm long, strongly auric-ulate; apex abruptly acuminate, long-cuspidate, cusp 80–140 µm long; margins broadly incurved, sharply serrulate above, plane or broadly incurved, serrulate below, weakly toothed on basal auricles; costae short-double, short-single, or absent; leaf cells long flexuose, smooth to slightly porose, 18– 40 X 3–5 µm, outer basal cells shorter and broader, inner basal cells elongate, porose; alar cells subquadrate to short-rectangular, extending up the margins in 2–4 rows and across the insertion in 2– 4 rows, yellow across the insertion. Dioicous. Setae short, wavy, 2–3 mm long, smooth below, rough-ened above, yellow. Capsules exserted, erect to somewhat inclined, ovoid to short-cylindrical, 1.0– 1.5 mm long, neck

Plants medium-sized, 2–4 cm long, green, yellowish, or yellow red, in mats. Stems prostrate, ir-regularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, subepidermal layer of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia small, foliose; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-patent, flexuose-contorted when dry, erect-spreading when wet, monomorphic, ovate to oval, 2.0–2.5 X 0.7–1.0 mm, symmetric, abruptly constricted above to long, slender acumina, concave; margins entire throughout or obscurely sinuate on the acumina, plane to erect, not bordered; costae double, thin, ending 1/3–2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, usually unequal, smooth at back, not pro-jecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells linear-elongate, 45–100 X 4–6 µm, firm-walled, porose, lower cells oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular, porose, bulging near insertions, cells across the insertions reddish, short-rectangular, porose; alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Setae elon-gate, 25–30 mm long, red, smooth throughout, at times somewhat roughened below the capsules. Capsules horizontal to suberect, oblong-cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate in 2–4 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; operculum and annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellow-ish, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments broad, strongly keeled, not or faintly perforate, cilia absent. Spores rounded, 12–20 µm, smooth to faintly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Plants small to medium-sized, 1.5–5.5 cm long, yellowish to light green, glossy. Stems ascend-ing to erect from the stolons, stipitate, stems and branches ending in broad to cuspidate tips, regularly to irregularly pinnate or bipinnate; flagellate branchlets sometimes present. Pseudoparaphyllia fo-liose, narrowly to broadly ovate, margins serrulate. Stipe leaves scarious, appressed to stems. Stem leaves erect, somewhat spreading, concave, broadly ovate, 2.0–2.5 X 1.0–1.5 mm, shortly cuspidate, rounded to the insertions; margins serrulate to nearly entire near apex, entire or sometimes minutely serrulate below, incurved throughout; costae reaching 2/3 the leaf length; cells smooth, thick-walled throughout, porose toward the insertion, apical cells rhombic, 10–16 X 5–8 µm, lower cells long to shortly linear-fusiform, 20–36 X 4–6 µm; alar cells weakly differentiated, of 2–5 short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions strongly porose, orange. Branch leaves erect-spreading, smooth, strongly concave, ovate to somewhat oblong-ovate, 0.8–1.3 X 0.3–0.6 mm, cus-pidate, cusp erect to slightly recurved, weakly rounded to the insertions; margins serrate to serrulate at apex, serrulate to entire below, incurved throughout; costae extending 1/2–2/3 the leaf length, rarely short and double; cells smooth, thick-walled throughout, apical cells rhombic, 8–14 X 4–8 µm, lower cells linear-fusiform, 18–30 X 3–4 µm; alar cells weakly differentiated, of a few short-rectangular cells at the basal angles, cells across the insertions strongly porose, orange. Perigonia, perichaetia, and sporophytes not seen.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in green, yellow green, or golden brown, soft, pendent masses. Primary stems creeping; secondary stems pendent, to 20 cm long, irregularly branched, complanate-foliate, secondary stem and branch tips often transformed to stoloniferous stems; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, hyaline, thin-walled, central strand small; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose; rhizoids red brown, smooth, not branched or sparsely branched, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf inser-tions, developed only when stems and branches touch the substrate. Primary stem and stoloniferous leaves appressed, lanceolate, auriculate, 2.5–4.0 mm long, flexuose hair-pointed, convolute-concave, decurrent; margins plane, serrulate throughout or serrate to irregularly dentate near the leaf base; costa none or shortly and inconspicuously single or double; cells linear, 100–134 # 4–6 µm, thin-walled, smooth or inconspicuously unipapillose; alar cells short-rectangular to subquadrate, thin-walled. Sec-ondary stems and branches complanate-foliate, leaves wide-spreading, lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, rounded to weakly auriculate, 2–3 mm long, gradually acuminate, not hair-pointed, shortly decurrent; margins plane, serrulate throughout or serrate to irregularly dentate near the leaf base; costa absent or short and double; cells linear, 80–120 # 4–6 µm, smooth or unipapillose over the cell lumina, thin-walled; alar cells subquadrate to short-rectangular, thick-walled, porose. Dioicous. Perichaetia lateral, gemmate, 1 mm long, paraphyses absent. Sporophytes unknown from Central America.

Groutiella maracaibensis (Broth.) Allen & Goffinet, comb. nov.

Micromitrium maracaibense Broth., Mitt. Inst. Allg. Bot. Hamburg 8: 403. 1931. Protologue: Venezuela. Venezuela: Maracaibo, E. von Jess (H).

Plants medium-sized, greenish yellow to reddish yellow above, brown below. Stems creeping, branches to 8 mm long, densely tomentose. Leaves erect below, crispate and spirally contorted, often wavy to undulate on upper margins when dry, erect‑spreading to erect‑recurved when wet, 2–3 mm long, lanceolate; apices gradually narrowed, acute to shortly acuminate, cuspidate or apiculate; margins entire to crenulate, plane or weakly recurved below, plane above, bordered in the lower _ to ½ by 3–4 rows of elongate, thick‑walled cells, basal marginal cells inflated, at times with rhizoids; costae stoutly excurrent, filling the apiculus or cuspid; upper cells 4–8 μm, rounded, flat or somewhat bulging, extreme basal cells to 26 μm long, rectangular, more or less porose. Dioicous. Setae 7–12 mm long, smooth, red. Capsules 2.5–3.5 mm long, oblong‑cylindrical, smooth to weakly furrowed, wrinkled at neck; opercula erect-rostrate, 1–1.5 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; peristome rudimentary, reduced to a short whitish membrane to 100 μm high. Spores isosporous, 20–30 μm, lightly roughened-papillose. Calyptrae to just below the capsule mouth, plicate above, naked, 2 mm long.

Syntrichia percarnosa (C. Müll.) Zand.,  Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Sci. 32: 269. 1993.

Barbula percarnosa C. Müll., Linnaea 42: 347. 1879. Tortula percarnosa (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 432. 1902. Protologue: Argentina. Argentina subtropica, Cuesta de Pinos. – Monte Nevado prope Salta, 11,000 ped alta cum Brachystelio emerso. [Lorentz]. 

Tortula kingii Robins., Bryologist 70: 24. 1967. Protologue: Colombia. Colombia, Eastern Cordellera, Dept. Cundinamarca, Municipality of Calera, Hacienda La Sibera, Páramo de Palacio, 3,520 m, King, Jamamillo-Mejia & Guevara C-990. 

Plants medium-sized, matted, reddish green above, brown below, saxicolous. Stems to 10 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand weakly developed, hyalodermis present; rhizoids scattered on stem, smooth. Axillary hairs 6–8 cells long, all hyaline. Leaves 2–2.5 mm long, rigid, ligulate-spathulate, erect to spreading at base, erect-incurved when dry, spreading when wet; apices obtuse, cucullate; lamina mostly unistratose, occasionally bistratose at the margins and in streaks on lamina; margins entire or lightly crenulate, plane above, weakly recurved at base; costa narrow, subpercurrent, ventral surface cells quadrate, papillose, guide cells present, ventral substereid cells occasionally present, dorsal substereids present, ventral surface layer enlarged, papillose; upper cells irregularly quadrate, oblate, or short-rectangular, 6–15 x 6–15 μm, firm-walled, densely and thickly pluripapillose with branched or c-shaped papilla, marginal cells not differentiated, inner basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, hyaline, smooth, 30–40 x 20 μm, outer basal cells short-rectangular, firm- to thick-walled, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal. Sporophytes not seen.

Mironia elongata (Wils. in Mitt.) Allen, comb. nov. 

Barbula elongata Wils. in Mitt., Hooker’s J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 51. 1851. Tortula elongata (Wils. in Mitt.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 164. 1869, hom. illeg. Morinia ehrenbergiana var. elongata (Wils. in Mitt.) Zand., Bryologist 81: 557. 1978. Mironia ehrenbergiana var. elongata (Wils. in Mitt.) Zand., Bull. Buffalo Soc. Nat. Hist. 32: 112. 1993. Protologue: Ecuador. Locality not given, Jameson 7.

Morinia ecuadorensis Bartr., Bull. Brit. Mus. (Nat. Hist.), Bot. 2(2): 55. 1955. Protologue: Ecuador. San Juan, Paramo, on rock by stream, 3,505 m., 25th April, 1951; [Bell] 727. 

Plants medium- to large-sized, reddish green above to reddish brown below to 25 mm high. Stems red to reddish yellow, irregularly branched, sclerodermis and central strand present, rhizoids red, smooth, at base and scattered on stems. Intact leaves 4–5 mm long, leaves without caducous apices 3.0–3.5 mm long, erect-sheathing at base, stiffly erect to erect-incurved, twisted when dry, spreading-recurved when wet, oblong-lanceolate; lamina unistratose or irregularly bistratose above; apices acuminate, leaf tips enlarged, thickened, caducous; margins bistratose, recurved to base of caducous tips, entire or sinuate, not bordered, somewhat decurrent at base; costa subpercurrent, smooth at back, ventral surface cells rectangular, pluripapillose, guide cells, small ventral substereid, and dorsal substereid to stereid bands present, upper ventral surface layer somewhat enlarged, papillose; upper cells 4–12 x 6–12 μm, firm-walled, oblate, irregularly quadrate hexagonal or short-rectangular, densely pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells smooth to lightly pluripapillose, rectangular, with thin, firm to bulging walls, 44–120 x 8–14 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown.

Pseudosymblepharis guatemalensis (Bartr.) Allen, comb. nov.

Tortella guatemalensis Bartr., Bryologist 49: 113. 1946. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. Retalhuleu: Standley 88397 (F). 

Plants small to medium-sized, dull yellow-green to dark-green, in tufts or cushions, 5–15 mm high. Stems red, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyalodermis present, central strand weakly developed; rhizoids moderately developed below, reddish brown, smooth. Leaves 5–7 mm long, linear-lanceolate, erect to erect-appressed at base, incurved, spirally twisted and contorted, tubulose above when dry, spreading when wet; apices acute to obtuse, sharply mucronate; laminae fragile and often broken or eroded above; margins entire and plane; costa short and stoutly excurrent, with guide cells and two well-developed stereid bands, ventral surface layer enlarged; upper cells subquadrate to short-rectangular, 5–10 μm long, firm-walled, pluripapillose, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, enlarged, bulging, hyaline, smooth, 25–50 m x 12–20 μm, outer basal cells running up the margins somewhat, forming a weak v-shaped pattern. Setae 1 per perichaetium, elongate, smooth, spirally twisted, 7 mm long, yellow, becoming red with age. Capsules narrowly cylindrical, 1.5–2 mm long, smooth to lightly wrinkled when dry; stomata in neck; opercula erect-rostrate, 1 mm long; annuli well-developed; peristome teeth 16, short, erect to weakly twisted, papillose. Spores 10–15 μm, lightly roughened. Calyptrae smooth, 4 mm long.

Macromitrium subcirrosum C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 20: 373. 1862.

Protologue: Costa Rica, in trachytaceis montis vulcanicis de Barba: Dr. Carl Hoffmann  26 Apr. 1855 cum fructibus maturis pulcherrime legit. 

Plants robust, reddish yellow to yellowish green. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 7 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves strongly keeled, erect below, flexuose‑spreading to somewhat spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 6–8 x 1 mm, broadly lanceolate from an oblong base; apices subulate‑acuminate; margins undulate to plane, serrate above, recurved below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent into a long, stout point to 1 mm long; upper interior cells (10–)20–48 μm, long-rhomboidal, smooth to weakly bulging, incrassate and porose, upper marginal cells somewhat narrower, otherwise not differentiated, elimbate, basal cells to 70 μm long, narrowly rectangular, incrassate and porose, densely or sparsely tuberculate. Setae 16–30 mm long, smooth. Capsules 2–2.5 mm long, obovoid to subcylindrical, smooth; opercula erct-rostrate, to 2 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth lanceolate, to 320 μm high, red, densely papillose, united forming an erect membrane, endostome light red, lightly papillose, basal membrane to 80 μm high, segments to 100 μm high. Spores anisosporous, 18–20 μm, papillose and 24–36 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, lacinate, naked, 2–3 mm long.

Scopelophila ligulata (Spruce) Spruce, J. Bot. 10: 14. 1881.

Encalypta ligulata Spruce, Musc. Pyren. 331. 1847. Zygodon ligulatus (Spruce) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 636. 1851. Merceya ligulata (Spruce) Schimp., Syn. Musc. Eur. (ed. 2), 852. 1876. Protologue: France. Hab. in rupibus humidis praesertim ophiticis. Labassère. Superbagnères. Gorge de Cauterets, Spruce.

Weissia agoyanensis Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 135. 1869.  Hyophila agoyanensis (Mitt.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1871–72: 358. 1873. Scopelophila agoyanensis (Mitt.) Spruce, J. Bot. 10: 12. 1881. Merceya agoyanensis (Mitt.) C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 383. 1901 [1900]. Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, in scopulis humidas supra cataractam Agoyan fluv. Pastasae (5000 ped.) Spruce, n. 45 a (lectotype Zander 1967) et b.

Plants small to medium-sized, caespitose, green to brownish green below, brownish black below, saxicolous or terricolous. Stems 5–30 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand absent, cortical cells thin-walled, hyaline, uniform throughout; rhizoids scattered on stem, smooth or verucose. Axillary hairs 2–3 cells long, lower 1–2 cells brown. Leaves 1.2–5.0 mm long, ligulate, lingulate, oblong or spathulate, erect to spreading at base, keeled, flexuose when dry, erect-spreading when wet, weakly decurrent; apices rounded-obtuse, at times acute; margins entire or lightly crenulate, plane above, recurved at base, often with a border of thicker-walled, yellowish cells; costa narrow, subpercurrent, surface cells oblong, smooth on both surfaces, guide cells and a single (dorsal) stereid band well-developed, ventral surface layer of enlarged cells absent, the guide cells exposed on the ventral surface; upper cells rounded-quadrate, oblate, or hexagonal, 6–16 x 8–16 μm, firm-walled, somewhat bulging and smooth on both sides, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 26–120 x 12–30 μm, bulging the walls at times deep red to black, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia terminal. Setae smooth, 4–6 mm long, yellowish brown. Capsules short-cylindrical, erect, 1.5–2.0 mm long, smooth, yellowish brown; exothecial cells quadrate to rectangular, thin-walled; stomata in neck; opercula rostrate, beak erect, 0.6–1.0 mm long; annuli persistent 2–3 rows of cells, clinging to the capsule mouth or operculum after dehiscence; peristome absent. Spores 10–14 μm, granulate. Calyptra not seen.

Sphagnum lankesteri Crum, Cryptogamie, Bryol. Lichénol. 5: 293. 1984.

Slender plants in soft, pale yellowish tufts; cortical cells differentiated in 2–3 layers. Stem leaves 1.8–2 mm long, oblong or oblong-ovate, concave-acute, narrowly bordered throughout; hyaline cells fibrillose throughout, not divided, on the outer surface with unringed apical window pores and a few small, somewhat ringed pores scattered along the commissures, on the inner surface with round, thin-margined pores along the commissures (5–11 in the upper median region); green cells broadly exposed on both surfaces but more so on the outer. Branches in fascicles of 4 (2 spreading), noticeably tapered, the young pendent branches in the capitulum not seeming paired; cortical retort cells differentiated. Branch leaves somewhat flattened and wavy-margined with spreading to recurved tips when dry, 2–2.2 mm long, oblong-lanceolate, long-acuminate, entire, bordered by 2–3 rows of linear cells; hyaline cells bulging on the inner surface, plane or slightly convex on the outer, with somewhat enlarged, round, thin-margined, apical window pores and a few small, rounded-elliptic, more or less ringed pores at corners or along commissures, on the inner surface with numerous round, thin-margined pores along the commissures (8–13 in the upper median region); green cells as seen in section triangular to slightly trapezoidal, broadly exposed on the outer surface, reaching the inner surface and sometimes narrowly exposed.

Sphagnum magellanicum Brid., Musc. Recent. 2(1): 24. 1798.

Sphagnum aureum McQueen, Bryologist 92: 405. 1989.

Plants stout, in dense, pink, red, or purplish (green if shaded) cushions or hummocks; cortical cells in 3–4 layers, the outermost cells delicately spiral-fibrillose, with 1 (or occasionally 2–4) large, round to elliptic pores; wood cylinder red. Stem leaves more or less flat, oblong-lingulate, rounded at the apex and finely fringed at the margins; hyaline cells not divided, fibrillose near the leaf apex or not at all, largely resorbed on the outer surface, sometimes on both surfaces. Branches stout and tumid, in fascicles of 4–5 (2 spreading); cortical cells fibrillose, sometimes with 1 large, round pore near the upper ends. Branch leaves imbricate or rarely somewhat spreading at the tips, ca. 2 mm long, broadly ovate, deeply cucullate-concave, rough at back of the apex and denticulate along a marginal resorption furrow; hyaline cells plane or nearly so on both surfaces, on the outer surface with 2–10 large, elliptic, ringed pores at ends, corners, and commissures, usually in 3's at adjacent cell angles, on the inner surface with 0–5 round to elliptic pores or pseudopores at corners and commissures in upper and side regions; green cells in section small, elliptic, central and entirely included.

Pohlia richardsii Shaw, Contr. Univ. Michigan Herb. 15: 253. 1982.

Protologue: Costa Rica. Volcán Poas, on banks of volcanic ash near edge of water, c 2,500 m, 20 Feb. 1965, Richards R 6010. 

Plants slender to medium-sized, dull, green to yellowish green in loose or dense tufts. Stems 4–20 mm high, dark red, simple or irregularly forked; rhizoids reddish brown, papillose-roughened. Leaves distant or crowded above, 0.7–1.4 mm long, erect to erect-spreading, stiff, not contorted when dry, lanceolate, long decurrent; apices acute; margins plane, entire below, serrulate above; costae yellow above, reddish at base, percurrent; upper cells rhomboidal, thin- or firm-walled, 30–60 x 6 μm, basal cells longer, broader and laxer, narrowly rectangular to rhomboidal. Gemmae in upper leaf axils, spheroid to ovoid, red to orange-red. Dioicous. Perigonia terminal, gemmiform. Setae 10–25 mm long, red. Capsules horizontal to pendent, 1.5–2 mm long, ovoid and constricted at neck; exothecial cells isodiametric to short rectangular, strongly bulging mammillose, with straight walls; stomata superficial or slightly immersed; opercula conic, apiculate, 0.5 mm long; annuli separating irregularly; exostome teeth whitish to light yellow, fused at base, narrowly triangular, densely papillose, endostome whitish to pale-yellow, basal membrane to _ the exostome length, segments narrow, linear, not or scarcely keeled, papillose, cilia absent. Spores 10–20 μm, lightly papillose.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in green to yellow green, loose or dense mats, often pendent. Pri-mary stems creeping with erect to imbricate distantly spaced leaves; secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect or pendent, stipitate, irregularly pinnately branched, branches often becoming flagel-late, or transformed to stoloniferous stems, stipe leaves evenly foliate, 4–40 cm long; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 4–7 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells en-larged, yellowish to hyaline, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous; rhizoids red brown, roughened, not or irregularly branched, from clusters of initials at abaxial side of primary stem leaf insertions, on leaves of attenuate branch tips, and at base of stipes. Secondary stem variously complanate-foliate, leaves spreading, 2.5–3.5 mm long, oblong-ovate, rugose, gradually acute, concave, cordate-auriculate to subauriculate at base, not decurrent; margins entire throughout or lightly serrulate at the apex, plane; costae variable: either short, faint, and single or double, or slender, reaching midleaf, and single; cells linear to linear-flex-uose, porose and firm-walled throughout, apical cells 40–60 # 6–8 µm, median cells 50–85 # 5–6 µm; basal cells 40–90 # 6 µm; alar cells weakly developed, rhombic to short-rectangular in 2–5 rows.Branches weakly complanate-foliate to turgid; leaves imbricate, oblong-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 2.0–2.5 mm long, rounded to cordate at base, otherwise similar to stem leaves. Asexual reproduction by hyaline, smooth, uniseriate, septate gemmae arising from large, circular clusters of initials in leaf axils. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen, description from Buck (1998) and Wagner (1951). Setae short, smooth, to 0.85 mm long. Capsules erect, symmetric, short-cylindric to ovoid, to 2 mm long; exothe-cial cells short-rectangular, firm-walled; opercula conic-rostrate; annuli rudimentary; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth yellow, narrowly triangular, smooth to finely roughened, weakly tra-beculate, often with a well-developed prostome; endostome not seen. Spores round, lightly papillose, to 21 µm.

Sphagnum cuspidatum Ehrh. ex Hoffm., Deutschl. Fl. 2: 22. 1796.

Plants normally submerged, slender, flaccid, especially when wet, bright green to yellow; wood cylinder yellow-green; cortical cells more or less distinctly differentiated in 2 layers, long, more or less thick-walled, not inflated, without pores. Stem leaves concave, ovate to ovate-deltoid, blunt or acute, broadly bordered below; hyaline cells not divided, with or without fibrils above, on the outer surface with small end pores, on the inner surface largely resorbed near the leaf apex, the gaps decreasing in size below and at the leaf sides. Branches normally in fascicles of 4 (2 spreading), slenderly tapered; cortical cells with retort cells differentiated. Branch leaves slightly wavy when dry, long-lanceolate, involute-concave, bordered by 2–4 rows of linear cells; hyaline cells slightly convex on the inner surface, on both surfaces with few, small, inconspicuous end and corner pores; green cells in section broadly trapezoidal, more broadly exposed on the outer surface.

Plants slender to medium-sized, green to yellow green, often in dense, creeping or pendent, epi-phytic masses. Primary stems to 25 cm long; stems in cross section with 4–6 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, central strand small; irregularly branched, branches generally short, usually less than 1 cm long; rhizoids in dense groups, dark brown to blackish, smooth, not branched, from circular clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions. Leaves trimorphic: stolon/primary stem leaves, secondary stem leaves, and branch leaves. Stolon/primary stem leaves erect, strongly clasping, ovate-lanceolate, 1.8–2.8 mm long; apices long-acuminate to piliferous, sometimes twisted; margins generally plane, subentire to serrulate; costae single, slender, tapering to the apex, commonly ending above midleaf, at times ending in a small spine; median cells linear-flexuose, 45–80 # 5–8 µm, firm-walled, not porose; alar cells weakly differentiated in excavate groups, somewhat porose. Secondary stem leaves erect-appressed, broadly ovate-lanceolate, to 2.0 mm long, otherwise similar to primary stem leaves. Branch leaves closely spaced, wide-spreading, squarrose, to squarrose-recurved, not clasping, ovate-lanceolate to ovate-acuminate, 0.7–1.8 mm long, short- to long-acuminate, cordate at base; margins plane or narrowly re-curved below, subentire to serrulate above; costae single, slender, tapering to the apices, ending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, at times ending in a small spine; median cells fusiform to linear-flexuose, 45–80 µm long, firm-walled; alar cells weakly differentiated, cells subquadrate, firm- to thick-walled, at times porose. Asexual reproduction occasionally by filiform branches from branch leaf axils. Dioicous. Setae red to dark red, twisted when dry, 1.5–3.5 mm long, smooth to somewhat roughened below capsules. Capsules exserted, erect, ellipsoid to cylindric, constricted at neck, 1.5–2.5 mm long; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate at the mouth, irregularly rectangular, below with thick vertical walls and thin horizontal walls; stomata superficial on neck; opercula 0.7–1.3 mm long, shortly ros-trate; annuli rudimentary, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, yellow, papil-lose; endostome hyaline to light yellowish, smooth to lightly

Plants small to medium-sized, 1.0–1.5 cm tall, glossy, green to yellowish green. Stems erect, sparsely and irregularly branched, evenly foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with somewhat en-larged epidermis of 1–2 rows of firm-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, basal 1–2 cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base and along stems, smooth, reddish brown, from initials at base of costae on abaxial side and from scattered initials, at times pinnately branched. Leaves isophyllous, spirally contorted when dry, erect-flexuose when wet, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–3.2 mm long, often deeply keeled in lower 1/2, sharply acuminate, decurrent; margins plane throughout, or at times broadly reflexed on one side, bor-dered by elongate, thick-walled, sometimes porose cells, 6–10 cells wide at base, entire throughout or minutely denticulate near the apices; costae single, strong, often flexuose, ending 7/8 the leaf length, in cross section cells homogeneously thick-walled; upper cells rhombic, 10–14 X 6–10 µm, smooth, median cells similar, at times in oblique rows, basal leaf cells oblong to rectangular, enlarged and bulging, 30–60 X 8–12 µm; alar cells enlarged, irregularly rectangular to subquadrate, reddish brown, porose, cells across the insertions enlarged, reddish, porose. Asexual reproduction occasion-ally by multicellular, uniseriate, clavate to fusiform propagula, abaxial at the base of the costa. Auto-icous. Perichaetia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 5–8 mm long, red, scabrose above, smooth below. Capsules erect, ovoid, more or less constricted at the neck, symmetric, 1.0–1.5 mm long; exothecial cells at the mouth oblate in 3–4 rows, lower cells larger, oblate, rounded-quadrate, or subrectangular, collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.3–0.5 mm long; annulus not seen; peri-stome diplolepideous; exostome teeth yellow, recurved when wet, incurved when dry, narrowly triangular, both surfaces papillose throughout, dorsal trabeculae and median line thick, ventral tra-beculae faint; endostome yellowish white, papillose throughout, basal membranes low, segments lin-ear, not keeled, not or faintly perforate, cilia absent. Plants small, 0.3–1.0 cm tall, glossy, green to yellowish green. Stems erect, sparsely and irregu-larly branched, evenly foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with 1–2 rows of enlarged, reddish, often perforate hyalodermis cells, subepidermis of 1 row of small, firm- to thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axil-lary hairs 2–4 cells long, basal 1–2 cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper 1–2 cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base of stems, around branch primordia, and along the stems, smooth, reddish brown, from scattered initials, weakly branched, branches with transverse cross walls. Setae elongate, to 10 mm long, red, smooth throughout or lightly roughened below the capsule. Capsules erect, oval, to 1.5 mm long; opercula rostrate, erect, 0.75 mm long. Spores roughened, 12–16 µm in diameter. Calyptrae smooth above.

Plants small to medium sized, 1–3 cm high. Sporophytes not seen in Central America.

Plants small, 1–3 cm long, green, yellowish green, rarely yellowish red, in thin or dense glossy mats. Setae elongate, 20–30 mm long, red, smooth below, papillose-roughened to tubular-roughened on neck and upper part of setae. Plants dull yellow-green to green, in dense or loose tufts to 15 mm high. Stems red, erect,  sparsely and irregularly branched, rosulate-foliate; hyalodermis present, central strand well-developed; rhizoids moderately developed below, reddish brown, smooth. Lower leaves reduced, erect-appressed below, upper leaves 4–5 mm long, erect at base, incurved, spirally twisted and contorted, tubular above when dry, erect-spreading when wet, lanceolate; apices acute; margins denticulate above, serrulate to serrate below, plane below and variously incurved above; costa percurrent to short excurrent, guide cells and two stereid bands well-developed, ventral surface layer of short, bulging-mammillose cells; upper cells rounded-quadrate, firm-walled, bistratose except at margins, bulging-mammillose ventrally, plane dorsally, 7.5–10 x 7.5 μm, basal interior cells oblong, thin-walled, bulging, hyaline, smooth, to 87.5 x 17.5 μm, basal marginal cells narrowly rectangular to elongate, firm and straight-walled, smooth. Autoicous. Perigonia lateral, perichaetia terminal, perichaetial leaves weakly differentiated. Setae 15–25 mm long, red, smooth, spirally twisted. Plants delicate, medium-sized, in loose, yellowish green or green, often glossy tufts or mats, laxly ascending to prostrate, to 30 mm high. Spores reniform, 20–25 μm, papillose.

Plants small, glaucous green, 3–5 mm high. Leaves 2–3 mm long, erect at base, weakly flexuous above, lanceolate to narrowly ovate-lanceolate, gradually narrowed from base to apex; apex broadly acute to obtuse and apiculate; margins erect to incurved, entire; costa in cross section throughout the leaf with a single layer of dorsal leucocysts, a median layer of chlorocysts and a single layer of ventral leucocysts, in surface view the dorsal leucocysts enlarged, rectangular, not subdivided; upper chlorocysts subdivided and forming chains of rounded to quadrate cells; leaf lamina poorly developed, 1–2 rows of linear cells above, 2–4 rows of rectangular cells at base, basal cells not subdivided. Plants minute, delicate, scattered to gregarious, yellowish; stems slender, erect to arcuate, 2–10 mm long, simple or with a few branches.
