Plants small to robust, yellow-green, glossy, gregarious or in loose tufts. Stems slender, simple or with subperichaetial branches, 10–80 mm high; rhizoids sparse at base. Leaves 1–1.3 mm long, imbricate, wrinkled to plicate dry, concave, oblong to oblong-ovate; apices obtuse to broadly rounded; margins plane, not bordered, entire or obscurely denticulate; costa subpercurrent; upper cells rhomboidal hexagonal to linear-rhomboidal, thin- or thick-walled, 14–80 x 6–10 μm, basal cells rectangular to quadrate, abruptly broader, thin-walled, 40–60 x 10–20 μm, basal marginal cells quadrate. Dioicous. Perichaetia leaves longer than vegetative leaves, narrowly acuminate. Setae 10–25 mm long, red. Capsules 1.5–2.5 mm long,  red-brown, oblong-pyriform, strongly constricted and wrinkled at neck, pendent, horizontal or suberect; opercula conic-apiculate, 0.5 mm long; annuli compound and revoluble; exostome teeth yellow-brown, densely papillose, endostome hyaline, papillose, basal membrane to ½ of exostome teeth length, segments well-developed, broadly perforate, cilia 2–3, appendiculate. Spores 10–14 μm, smooth. Calyptra not seen.

Holomitrium arboreum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 58. 1869. Syntypes. Peru, Spruce 22 (F, NY); Ecuador, Spruce 22b (NY).

Holomitrium standleyi Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 66. 1928. Type. Costa Rica, Guanacaste, Standley & Valerio 46271 (FH, NY, US). Paratypes. Standley & Valerio 459332, 46260 (FH, NY, US).

 

Plants medium; stems 2–4 cm long. Leaves crowded, spreading when wet, strongly crisped when dry, keeled above, clasping at base, long linear-lanceolate from an erect, ovate base, 2–6 mm long, acuminate; margins plane, strongly dentate in the upper 2/3; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent, frequently toothed above on dorsal surface; cells occasionally bistratose above or on the upper margins, upper cells quadrate to subquadrate, walls thickened and straight, extending downward along the margins into the basal region; basal cells linear, strongly differentiated, incrassate, pitted, basal marginal cells short rectangular, not or weakly porose, wider than the inner basal cells; alar cells forming distinct groups of enlarged, red-brown thin-walled cells. Perichaetial leaves frequently reaching the base of the capsules. Setae 1–2 cm long; capsules 4–5 mm long; peristome teeth linear-lanceolate, 0.4–0.5 mm high.

Holomitrium longifolium Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 5, 3: 364. 1865. Type. Colombia, Lindig 2116.

Plants medium to large; stems to 8 cm long. Leaves crowded, erect-spreading when wet, erect at base and crisped above when dry, gradually narrowed from an oblong, clasping base into a long, linear-lanceolate, commonly keeled upper leaf, 10–12 mm long, apex setaceous and fragile, frequently broken; margins plane, sharply serrate to dentate in upper 1/2; costa excurrent, toothed at back above; upper leaf cells quadrate, homogeneous, walls evenly thickened, the outer walls straight; basal cells linear, yellow, incrassate and pitted, those at the margins narrower than the interior cells, thick-walled and pitted; alar cells persistent, forming distinct groups, rectangular, thin-walled, reddish yellow. Sporophytes not seen.

Holomitrium sinuosum Allen, Trop. Bryol. 3: 65. 1990. Type. Panama, Bocas del Toro, Allen 5648 (MO, PMA).

 

Plants medium to large; stems to 5–7 cm long. Leaves crowded, erect at base, spreading above when wet, twisted and crispate above when dry, variably undulate on the margins, strongly concave to keeled, abruptly narrowed from an ovate base, broadly acuminate above, 8–10 mm long, acuminate; margins erect to incurved, crenulate below, serrate at extreme apex, unistratose throughout; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent, smooth or weakly toothed at back; upper leaf cells rectangular, incrassate, the outer and inner walls strongly sinuose, not pitted, grading imperceivably into basal cells; basal cells linear-rectangular, incrassate, pitted and sinuose; alar cells quadrate to rectangular, usually forming distinct, persistent groups of red-brown cells (occasionally the alar cells hyaline and more or less fugacious), cell walls usually firm. Perichaetial leaves reaching the capsule middle. Setae 10–15 mm long, yellow; capsules cylindrical, 2.5–3.0 mm long, brown; peristome reddish orange, teeth linear-lanceolate, densely papillose, 0.6–0.7 mm high; opercula 2.5 mm long. Calyptrae 4.5 mm long.

Campylopodiella flagellacea (C. Müll.) Frahm & Isoviita, Taxon 37: 968. 1988. Dicranum flagellaceum C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 597. 1851. Campylopus flagellaceus (C. Müll.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 77. 1869. Dicranodontium flagellaceum (C. Müll.) Williams, N. Amer. Fl. 15: 153. 1913. Metzlerella flagellacea (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam., ed. 2, 10: 191. 1924. Type. Mexico, prov. Michoacán, Cerro San Andrés, Chrismar. Campylopus malagensis Herz., Biblioth. Bot. 87: 23. 1916. Campylopodiella malagensis(Herz.) Frahm, Bryologist 87: 250. 1984. Type. Bolivia, auf Torfboden der Cerros de Malaga, Herzog 4367 (NY).

Plants tufted, yellowish green; stems erect, 3–15 mm long. Leaves evenly spaced, erect-patent to appressed, concave, lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 mm long, oblong below, narrowly acuminate above; margins entire and erect below, incurved above, minutely serrulate at extreme apex; costa ½–⅔the leaf width at base, excurrent; upper cells short rectangular to quadrate, firm-walled, basal cells rectangular to subquadrate, hyaline, firm-walled, those at margins somewhat longer and narrower but not forming a distict border; alar cells in small, weakly auriculate groups, slightly inflated and at times poorly developed. Asexual reproduction by deciduous flagella at the stem tips, the flagella becoming black and necrotic in the area of separation from the stem, the stem remaining black-tipped after the flagella are lost; flagellate leaves short, with broader costa, leaf cells quadrate and more firm-walled and the leaf apices narrowly obtuse. Dioicous. Perichaetial leaves suddenly contracted from a broadly ovate base. Setae 10–13 mm long; capsules 2 mm long; peristome yellow, teeth lanceolate, papillose, cleft to the base, 0.3–0.4 mm high; opercula 1.0–1.2 mm long. Calyptrae 2.5–3.0 mm long, smooth. Spores 12 µm, rounded, smooth to lightly papillose, yellow.

Plants medium-sized, in dull, dark green or yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping; leaves
reduced, 0.3–0.5 mm long, well spaced, scale-like to triangular, cells variously papillose to nearly
smooth; rhizoids red brown, in clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or weakly and irregularly
branched. Secondary stems horizontal or erect and loosely spreading, to 5 cm long, irregularly
branched, secondary stems and branches often stoloniform-attenuate at the tips; cross section with
sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to
hyaline, firm- or thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia and pseudoparaphyllia absent;
branches usually recurved when dry. Secondary stem leaves oblong-lanceolate, to 2 mm long. Branch
leaves erect and homomallous when dry, erect-spreading when wet, ovate-lanceolate from an ovate
base, to 1.5 mm long, acute, apiculate, long and broadly decurrent; margins plane or erect at base, papillose-
crenulate, at times sparsely serrulate at the apex, denticulate at the base of the decurrencies;
costae single, ending well below the apex, yellow, wavy above, channeled on ventral surface, with
quadrate, densely papillose cells on upper dorsal surface, in cross section cells homogeneous, thickwalled;
upper cells quadrate, oblate, or irregularly hexagonal, 5–9 μm, densely pluripapillose by
thick, branched, or C-shaped papillae, cells near the apex lightly papillose to nearly smooth, juxtacostal
cells near the insertions long-rectangular, to 30 x 12 μm, porose, weakly papillose to smooth,
cells in basal decurrencies enlarged, smooth to weakly papillose. Dioicous. Perigonia and perichaetia
gemmate, lateral on secondary stems. Setae elongate, red to orange, flexuose, to 20 mm long. Capsules
erect, 2–3 mm long, smooth, light brown; exothecial cells small, oblate, thick-walled in 3–5
rows below the mouth, becoming subquadrate and short-rectangular below; stomata at junction of
urns and setae; opercula obliquely or straight conic-rostrate, to 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, cells
often clinging to capsule mouth or operculum; exostomes white to yellow above, reddish orange at
base, narrowly triangular to linear, dorsal (outer) surface papillose-striate in lower half, papillose
above, trabeculae laterally projecting; endostome papillose, to 3/4 the exostome length, segments narrow
and perforate, basal membranes low, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores spherical, subspherical,
or oblong, lightly papillose, 9–16 μm. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2–2.5 mm long.

Physcomitrium cupuliferum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 242. 1869.

Protologue: Cuba. Ins. Cuba, Wright, n. 6.

Physcomitrium ekmanii Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 14: 16. 1944. Protologue: Dominican Republic. Santo-Domingo: Cordillera Central, prov. de Azua, valle del Yaque, most place, 1.500 m. (n°137010 [Ekman]) 

Plants small to medium‑sized, pale‑green, laxly gregarious. Stems simple or sometimes irregularly and weakly branched, (1–)2–3 mm long. Leaves spreading to wide‑spreading, crispate when dry, spathulate to oblong‑obovate, 2.5–4.3 mm long, gradually or more often abruptly short‑acuminate; margins bluntly serrulate above, entire below, plane throughout or more often narrowly recurved below; costa slender, subpercurrent (ending 2–4 cells below the apex) to percurrent or rarely short‑excurrent; cells subquadrate to short‑rectangular, 28–85 x 20–35 μm, thin‑walled, smooth, toward the margins becoming more elongate in 1–3(–4) rows, at leaf apex the border 1–2 cells wide, near midleaf 2–3(–4) cells wide, toward the insertion differing only by narrower cells, basal cells becoming larger, laxer and thinner‑walled, 63–137 x 28–52 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous; antheridia and paraphyses naked in subapical leaf axils; paraphyses with 3–4 rectangular stalk cells and a single globose to inflated oblong apical cell. Setae (3–)5–7 mm long, straight or somewhat curved, orange to red, rarely yellow, smooth, the foot tapering. Capsules exserted, broadly short‑oblong when operculate, urceolate to pyriform or turbinate when empty, 1 mm long, usually without a well-developed neck; exothecial cells rounded subquadrate, 22–35 μm in diameter, evenly thick‑walled or slightly collenchymatous, becoming oblate in 9–12 rows at the mouth; stomata restricted to base of capsule, superficial; columella slender, initially attached to operculum and capsules thus systylius, but soon breaking near the middle, the upper portion remaining attached to the operculum and falling with it, the basal portion remaining attached to base of urn; opercula low‑convex, bluntly short‑rostrate, the rostrum 0.4 mm long, cells broadly oblate, in poorly defined straight rows, evenly thick‑walled to weakly collenchymatous; annuli of a 1(–2) rows of broadly oblate to short‑rectangular, firm‑walled cells, fragmenting. Spores spherical, brown, 28–35 μm in diameter, spiculose to coarsely spiculose, the spiculae 1.5–2 μm tall, straight. Calyptrae mitrate, long‑rostrate, only covering rostrum and flaring out over operculum, lobed at base, smooth, 1.5–2 mm long.

Plants medium-sized, dull, light green, yellow green, or golden brown, in stiff mats, sometimes with pendent strands. Secondary stems arising irregularly from the primary stems, creeping or pendent, to 25 cm long, irregularly branched; axillary hairs 4–5 cells long; cells reddish, basal cells 1–2, short, quadrate to subquadrate, upper cells 2–3, long-cylindrical; rhizoids present. Secondary stem and branch apices short and swollen; leaves broadly ovate to oblong-ovate, not ranked, wide-spreading to erect-spreading from the base with margins incurved when dry, erect-spreading when wet, 1–2 mm long, concave, clasping at base, rounded to the insertion or weakly au-riculate, acuminate, long- or short-cuspidate, leaf tips straight not reflexed; margins broadly incurved above, entire below, serrulate directly below the apex; costa absent; leaf cells linear-flexuose, porose throughout, median cells 16–50 X 3–4 µm; basal cells shorter and broader; alar cells in bulging, ex-cavate groups, subquadrate to short-rectangular, 14–20 X 2–12 µm, yellow red, reddish orange, or red. Asexual reproduction often by slender branches with microphyllous leaves, flagelliform branch tips, or deciduous leaves. Dioicous. Perigonia gemmate, lateral on secondary stems and branches, 1.0–1.3 mm long; perichaetia terminal on short lateral branches, unfertilized perichaetial leaves to 2.5 mm long. Setae elongate, 5–15 mm long, red, smooth to lightly roughened below, papillose above. Capsules exserted, erect, ovoid to short-cylindrical, 1.5–2.0 mm long; exothecial cells subquadrate to irregularly subrectangular, firm-walled; stomata superficial on neck; opercula long-rostrate, 1.0– 1.5 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome yellowish white, exostome to 0.5 mm long, dorsal (outer) surface lightly horizontally striate at ba

Dicranella harrisii (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 309. 1901. Aongstroemia harrisii C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 554. 1897. Microdus harrisii (C. Müll.) Par., Index Bryol. Suppl. 244. 1900. Type. Jamaica, Blue Mountains Peak, Harris 10068 (NY).

Plants yellowish green to green; stems 5–10 mm high. Leaves erect-flexuous, leaves triangular-lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, gradually narrowed to a sharply acute or acuminate apex, upper leaves occasionally weakly clasping at base; margins entire below, denticulate at apex, plane or narrowly recurved; costa excurrent, nearly filling the apex; leaf cells narrowly rectangular below, shortly rectangular above, the marginal cells frequently thin-walled and bulging. Setae yellow when young, red at maturity, 7–12 mm long; capsules oval, 1.0 mm erect, symmetrical; annuli compound, revoluble; peristome teeth well developed, striate-papillose and red below, densely papillose and hyaline above, divided to one half their length. Spores 16–20 µm, densely papillose.

Dicranella heteromalla (Hedw.) Schimp., Coroll. Bryol. Eur. 13. 1856. Dicranum heteromallum Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 128. 1801. Type. Europe.

Dicranella heteromalla var. pittieri Ren. & Card., Bull. Soc. Roy. Bot. Belgique 31(1): 145. 1893. Syntypes. Costa Rica, Potrero del Alto, massif du volcán du Poás, Pittier 5504, (NY, US); Barba et la Carrizal, Pittier 5505 (US), syn. nov.

Plants dark green; stems 10–20 mm high. Leaves 2–3 mm long, erect-flexuous to curved-secund, lanceolate to narrowly ovate-lanceolate, gradually narrowed to the apex; margins plane, entire below, serrulate above; costa excurrent, filling most of the upper leaf blade; cells rectangular to elongate-rectangular, firm-walled. Setae yellow, 5–15 mm long; capsules suberect or asymmetric and curved, 1.0–2.0 mm long, ovoid to cylindric; stomata absent; opercula 1.0 mm long, conic at base, long-rostrate above; annuli imperfect, of a single row of small thick-walled cells adhering to the capsule mouth after dehiscence; peristome teeth 400–500 µm long, divided halfway to the base into two hyaline, papillose forks, in lower 1/2 red and strongly striate-papillose, occasionally arising from a very low basal membrane. Spores 14–18 µm, lightly roughened.

Plants medium-sized, green to yellow green, in dense, creeping or pendent, epiphytic masses. Pri-mary stems to 15 cm long; stems in cross section with 3–4 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, yellow to hyaline, central strand small; irregu-larly branched, branches generally short, 0.5–2.0 cm long; rhizoids sparse, when present in small groups, reddish brown, smooth, not branched, from circular clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf in-sertions. Leaves dimorphic: stem leaves and branch leaves. Stem leaves erect, strongly clasping, ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.7 mm long; apices long-acuminate to piliferous; margins plane above, revo-lute below, subentire to serrulate; costae single, slender, tapering to the apex, commonly ending at or slightly above midleaf; median cells linear-flexuose, 35–60 # 5–8 µm, firm-walled, often porose; alar cells moderately differentiated in bulging, excavate groups. Branch leaves closely spaced, erect to some-what spreading, weakly clasping at base, ovate to broadly ovate, 0.6–1.2 mm long, short-acuminate; margins plane, revolute below, serrulate to serrate throughout; costae single, slender, tapering to the apex, ending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length; median cells fusiform to linear-flexuose, 35–75 µm long, firm-walled; alar cells moderately differentiated in bulging excavate groups, cells subquadrate to subrectangular, firm- to thick-walled, porose. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen, description from Manuel (1977a). Capsules erect, emergent, elliptic to ovate, 1.3–1.8 # 0.9–0.95 mm; exothecial cells quadrate to rectangular, thick-walled, with oblique end-walls; opercula 1.0 mm long, shortly rostrate; exostome teeth linear, 440–630 µm long, papillose; endostome papillose, basal membranes low, seg-ments 360–440 µm long, cilia absent. Spores 22.5–27.5 µm. Calyptrae mitrate, pilose, 1.8–1.9 mm long.

Plants slender to medium-sized, green to yellow green, often in dense, creeping or pendent, epi-phytic masses. Primary stems to 30 cm long, irregularly branched, branches short to medium-sized, to 2 cm long; stems in cross section with 4–6 rows of small, thick-walled, yellow to red epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, hyaline to yellowish, central strand small; rhizoids in dense groups, dark brown to blackish, smooth, not branched, from circular clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions. Leaves trimorphic: stolon/primary stem leaves, secondary stem leaves, and branch leaves. Stolon/primary stem leaves erect, strongly clasping, ovate-lanceolate, 1.5–2.5 mm long; apices long-acuminate to piliferous, sometimes twisted; margins generally plane, subentire; costae single, slender, tapering to the apex, commonly ending above midleaf; median cells linear-flexuose, 45–80 # 5–7 µm, firm-walled, often porose; alar cells weakly differentiated. Secondary stem leaves erect-appressed, broadly ovate-lanceolate, to 2.0 mm long, otherwise similar to primary stem leaves. Branch leaves closely spaced, squarrose to squarrose-recurved, not clasping, broadly ovate to orbic-ular, 0.8–1.5 mm long, short-acuminate to apiculate; margins plane, serrulate; costae single, slender, tapering to the apex, ending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length; median cells fusiform to linear-flexuose, 35– 70 µm long, firm-walled, not porose; alar cells weakly differentiated, subquadrate, firm- to thick-walled, at times porose. Dioicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems and branches. Setae red to dark red, twisted when dry, 1.5–2.5 mm long, smooth to somewhat roughened below capsules. Capsules exserted, erect, cylindric, constricted at neck, 1.5–2.3 mm long; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate at the mouth, ir-regularly rectangular, below with thick vertical walls and thin horizontal walls; stomata superficial on neck; opercula 1.0 mm long, shortly rostrate; annuli rudimentary, of several rows of thick-walled cells; exostome teeth linear, yellow, papillose; endostome hyaline to light yellowish, lightly papillose, 2/3 the exostome length, basal membranes low, segments linear, perforate below, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores round, 14–24<

Brachymitrion cochabambae (C. Müll.) A. Kop., Ann. Bot. Fenn. 14: 196. 1977. 

Tayloria cochabambae C. Müll., Nuovo Giorn. Bot. Ital. 4: 11. 1897. Protologue: Bolivia. Bolivia, Prov. Cochabamba prope Choquecamata, VI. 1889, Germain. 

Plants, crowded, caespitose, pale-green. Stems erect,  forked at base, angled, 15–20 mm, yellowish green, central strand present; rhizoidal tomentum dense, branched, dark-red, covering the lower _ of the stem, rhizoids dimorphic, papillose; axillary hairs with 2–3 red, cylindrical basal cells, terminal cell hyaline, clavate, becoming glutinous in age. Leaves erect-spreading when moist, irregularly inrolled, undulate, folded with the apex typically recurved when dry, somewhat clasping, long-decurrent, spathulate, 5 x 2–3 mm; apices short apiculate, apiculus occasionally multicellular; margins bluntly serrulate or crenulate above, bordered by 2–3 rows of hyaline cells at base; costa single, subpercurrent ending 4–10 cells below the apex; cells lax, thin-walled, upper cells 69–112 x 32–47 μm, irregularly hexagonal-fusiform, radiating from the costa, basal cells 40–70 x 10–14 μm, rectangular, upper marginal cells 30–65 x 7–2 μm; lower marginal cells 50–95 x  5–10 μm. Autoicous. Setae 2–3 mm long, yellow, twisted. Capsules 3.5–4.0 mm long, emergent to shortly exserted, subcylindric, tapered toward and slightly contracted below the suboral band, abruptly differentiated from the seta, yellowish brown or olive, suboral band orange-brown, neck short, undifferentiated or slightly wrinkled; exothecial cells arranged in longitudinal files, 59–100 x 24–35 μm, rectangular, longitudinal walls slightly thicker than the cross walls, yellowish, suboral cells short-rectangular 19¬–24 x 14–16 μm; stomata in capsule neck, phaneroporic; opercula short-rostrate; peristome of 16 exostome teeth, narrowly triangular, incurved, fused laterally above, outer surface papillose, inner surface with irregular ridges, endostome absent. Spores spherical-subspherical, 15–19 x 10–18 μm, brown in mass, finely papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, 4–lobed.

Brachymitrion moritzianum (C. Müll.) A. Kop., Ann. Bot. Fenn. 14: 195. 1977.

Tayloria moritziana C. Müll., Linnaea 19: 201. 1846. Protologue: Venezuela. Habit. inter Hypopterygium tamariscinum in montibus nivosis Meridae, Moritz. 

Plants crowded, caespitose, bright green to yellowish. Stems erect, forked below, 9–20 mm, central strand present; rhizoidal tomentum red, prominent on the lower _ of the stem, rhizoids branched, dimorphic, finely papillose; axillary hairs with 1–3 short-cylindric, reddish, thin-walled basal cells, terminal cell elongate, hyaline, becoming glutinous in age. Leaves clustered, larger above, erect when moist, imbricate with the upper portion recurved, infolded, tip reflexed and twisted when dry, decurrent, spathulate, 3–6 x 1.8–3 mm; apex awned, awn multicellular at base, terminal cell long-attenuate; margins undulate more or less incurved, spinose-toothed above; costa subpercurrent, ending 5–10 cells below the apex, sometimes forked, thin; upper cells 125–155 x 32–47 μm, irregularly hexagonal-fusiform, basal cells 130–157 x 40–47 μm, elongate-hexagonal. Capsules exserted, erect or suberect, 1.0–1.8 mm long, smooth, cylindric, pale brownish orange (becoming red or reddish brown), suboral rim shiny and slightly darker than the urn, neck undifferentiated or slightly wrinkled; exothecial cells in longitudinal files, irregularly rectangular, walls more or less evenly thickened; stomata phaneroporic; opercula short-rostrate, 1 mm long; peristome of 16 exostome teeth, brownish red, incurved when dry, laterally attached at apex, vertically striolate on upper dorsal surface, ventral surface with horizontal and swirled ridges. Spores light brown in mass, spherical to subspherical, 11–12 x 8–12 μm, finely papillose. Calyptrae campanulate, hairy, lobed at base.

Plants medium-sized, 1–5 cm tall, glossy, green to yellowish green. Stems erect, sparsely and ir-regularly branched, evenly foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with hyalodermis of enlarged, red-dish, at times pored cells, subepidermis of 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells en-larged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphylliaabsent; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, basal 1–2 cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, at times pinnately branched, at base of stems, around branch primor-dia, and along the stems abaxial to the leaf insertions. Asexual reproduction occasionally by multicellular, uniseriate, clavate to fusiform propagula, abaxial at the base of the costa. Autoicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 5–12 mm long, red, scabrose above, smooth or roughened below. Capsules erect, ovoid to oblong, more or less constricted at the neck, symmetric, 1.0–1.25 mm long; exothecial cells at the mouth oblate in 3–4 rows, lower cells larger, oblate, rounded-quadrate, or subrectangular, collenchy-matous;

Plants medium-sized, 1–3 cm tall, glossy, green to yellowish green. Stems erect, sparsely and ir-regularly branched, evenly foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with hyalodermis of enlarged, red-dish cells, subepidermis of 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, basal 1–2 cells short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cells oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base of stems, around branch primordia, and at times along the stems, smooth, reddish brown, ini-tials abaxial to the leaf insertions and from scattered initials, at times pinnately branched. Asexual propagula not seen. Autoicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 5–12 mm long, red, scabrose above, smooth below. Cap-sules erect, ovoid to oblong, more or less constricted at the neck, symmetric, 1–2 mm long; exothecial cells at the mouth oblate in 3–4 rows, lower cells larger, oblate, rounded-quadrate, or subrectangular, collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 1.0 mm long; annuli rudimentary, per-sistent; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth reddish yellow at base, recurved

Plants medium-sized to robust, 2–10 cm long, light green, yellowish red, golden, or brown. Stems procumbent below, pendent or projecting horizontally above, sparsely and irregularly branched, com-planate-foliate; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, very thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudo-paraphyllia filamentous to subfoliose; axillary hairs 5–12 cells long, basal 1–2 short-rectangular, upper cells short and bulging, all cells hyaline; rhizoids densely felting underside of stems, smooth, reddish brown, from scattered initials on stems and around branch primordia, intricately pinnately branched. Leaves dimorphic: lateral leaves wide-spreading, asymmetric, broadly ovate to obovate, 2.5–3.5 mm long, ventral leaves erect, symmetric, ovate to obovate, 1.5–3.0 mm long, mucronate to cuspidate, decurrent; margins plane, denticulate-crenulate throughout; costae single, strong, usually dark red, percurrent or ending in the acumen, sometimes spurred, cells above the costal tip elongate, in cross section cells very thick-walled, those in guide positions somewhat enlarged; cells in oblique rows from the costae, smooth, rarely papillose, upper and median cells isodiametric, oval, oblong, or short-rectangular, 10–22 µm long, strongly thick-walled, collenchymatous, porose; basal cells elon-gate, 30–90 µm, thick-walled, very porose; alar cells short rounded-rectangular to quadrate, reddish brown, porose, cells across the insertions reddish, porose. Stems and branches often ending in slen-der, tapering, microphyllous points with gemmaphore-bearing branches in leaf axils; propagula fusiform, ellipsoid, or cylindrical, sometimes stalked, usually paired, sometimes single, uniseriate, 2–5 cells long, 40–70 µm long. Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia on short lateral branches on stems; perichaetia to 2 mm long; leaves lanceolate, paraphyses not seen; perigonia to 1 mm long, leaves ovate-lanceolate; vaginulae densely hairy. Setae short, flexuose, 1.5–2.0 mm, smooth or some-what roughened. Capsules exserted, erect, ovoid to oblong, at times constricted at the neck, symmet-ric, 1–2 mm long; exothecial cells rounded to subquadrate, somewhat collenchymatous; stomata immersed on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5–0.7 mm long; annuli rudimentary; peristome diplo-lepideous; exostome teeth reddish yellow, narrowly triangular, dorsal surface densely cross-striate below, papillose above, not or variably furrowed, trabeculae and median

Tayloria scabriseta (Hook.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 250. 1869.

Splachnum scabrisetum Hook., Musci Exot. 1: 32. 1818. Protologue: Ecuador. In umbrosis temperatis Gonzanamam inter et Lucarque (Prov. Jaen de Bracamoros), altitudine 1060 hexapod. Humboldt et Bonpland.

Plants green to yellowish green above, brownish below. Stems erect, branched at base, 6–10 mm high, fragile, central strand present, cortex thin-walled, tomentose; rhizoids red-brown or brown, smooth, dimorphic; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell red, rectangular, to 50 μm long, terminal cell hyaline, cylindric, to 190 μm. Leaves erect when moist, erect below, variously twisted, contorted above when dry, ob¬ovate; apices rounded-obtuse; margins plane, entire; costa single, yellowish green, subpercurrent; leaf cells thin-walled, bulging, upper cells oblate, rectangular, rhombic, pentagonal, hexagonal, 40–100 x 32–60 um, basal¬ cells elongate-rectangular, 100-200 x 28–40 μm. Autoicous. Setae single, 5–7 mm long, erect or slightly curved, red to brownish red, cells bulging-mammillose. Capsules 2.0–2.5 mm long, erect, red to reddish brown, cylindric, neck 1.0–1.5 mm long, irregularly longitudinally wrinkled, narrower than the urn, tapered to the seta; urn exothecial cells isodiametric to oblate, thick-walled, neck exothecial cells rectangular; stomata in neck near junction with urn, phaneroporic, round-pored; opercula conic, brown to blackish red, 0.5 mm long; columella projecting when dry; peristome of 8 exostome teeth, forked above, united at base into a long basal membrane, red or reddish brown, papillose, the teeth reflexed when dry, incurved when wet. Spores spherical to subspherical, 18–12 μm, smooth to lightly roughened. Calyptra mitrate, 1.5 mm long, yellowish to golden, lobed at base.

Philonotis capillaris Lindb. ex Hartm., Handb. Skand. Fl. (ed. 10), 2: 46. 1871.

Protologue. Sweden. Stockh. vid Nacka, Petersberg, Drottningholm och Huddinge, vid jernvägen: Lindb.

Philonotis capillaris Lindb., Hedwigia 6: 40. 1867, nom. nud.

? Bartramia bernoullii C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 187. 1897. Philonotis bernoullii (C. Müll.) Par. Index Bryol. Suppl. 265. 1900. Protologue: Guatemala. In rep. Guatemala s. loco speciali. No 61[Türckheim].

Philonotis macounii Lesq. & James, Man. Mosses N. America 208. 1884. Protologue: Canada. Vancouver Island. Lectotype (Zales 1973): Canadian Musci 152. On wet shaded rocks, Nanaimo, Vancouver Island, Macoun (isolectotype MO).

Plants small, in loose, yellowish green or green tufts, to 5 mm high. Stems red; rhizoids at base, reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 0.7–1.0 mm long, erect when dry, or erect to erect-spreading when wet, straight or secund, lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins narrowly revolute, doubly or singly serrate; costa long-excurrent; upper cells papillose at upper ends, rectangular to elongate, firm‑walled, 15–35 x 2.5–7 μm, basal cells weakly and faintly papillose, papillae from lower cell ends, upper cell ends or midway between contiguous cells, rectangular, to 45 x 7μm, alar cells quadrate. Dioicous. Perigonia and sporophytes not known in Central America. "... perigonia discoid. Setae 13–20 mm long; capsules 1.3–2 mm long. Spores 17–24 μm" (Crum & Anderson 1981).

Dicranella longirostris (Schwaegr.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 30. 1869. Trematodon longirostris Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Suppl. 1(2): 343. 1816. Cosinodon longirostris (Schwaegr.) Brid., Musco. Recent. Suppl. 4: 51. 1819. Weissia longirostris (Schwaegr.) Schwaegr., Spec. Musc. Suppl. 2(1): 54. 1823. Seligeria longirostris (Schwaegr.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 421. 1848. Dicranella pseudolongirostris Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 68. 1909. Type. Mexico, Morelos, near Cuernavaca, Pringle 10661 (MO).

Plants greenish brown to yellow; stems 5–10 mm high. Leaves erect-spreading, to 1 mm long; lower leaves lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, gradually narrowed to the apex, upper leaves oblong to ovate-lanceolate, abruptly narrowed to the apex, frequently lanceolate-subulate, at times loosely clasping the stem; apex sharply acute; margins entire, plane or somewhat recurved above; costa excurrent; leaf cells rectangular below, narrow above, firm-walled throughout. Setae 5–7 mm long, yellowish to yellow-red; capsules 1.0–1.5 mm long, oblong, erect; annuli compound, revoluble; opercula obliquely long-rostrate; peristome teeth red, papillose, 120–200 µm high, irregularly divided, becoming red with age. Spores 16–20 µm, thickly papillose or warty.

Dicranodontium meridionale Bartr., Contr. U. S. Natl. Herb. 26: 65. 1928. Type. Costa Rica, Prov. Heredia, Cerro de las Caricias, north of San Isidro, Standley & Valerio 52296 (NY, US). Paratypes. Costa Rica, Heredia, Cerro de las Lajas, Standley & Valerio 51647 (NY, US); Cerro de Zurqui, Standley & Valerio 50492 (NY, US), 50284 (US), 50491a (FH); Cerro de las Caricias, Standley & Valerio 52234 (US).

Plants slender, forming deep silky turfs, yellow-green above, brownish below, moderately to densely red tomentose; stems 2–10 cm long. Leaves distantly spaced, erect-spreading to curved-secund, strongly concave, long and narrowly setaceous from a shortly ovate base, 8–10 mm long; margins incurved, densely spinose at apex, becoming denticulate in the upper one-third, entire below, bordered at base by several rows of narrow, elongate cells; upper cells long elongate-rhomboidal to linear, firm-walled, incrassate, pitted; basal cells near the costa forming a distinct group, short rectangular, enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline, outer basal cells narrow, elongate, firm-walled and pitted; alar cells well developed, reddish brown, at times fugacious. Dioicous (?). Sporophytes unknown.

Plants medium-sized, in green or yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly
branched; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, red, smooth, unbranched or rarely
irregularly branched. Secondary stems horizontal or erect and loosely spreading, to 5 cm long,
irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled
cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, very thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia
absent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous or subfoliose and with scale leaves. Secondary stem and
branch leaves ovate to elliptic, 1.5–2 mm long, imbricate when dry, spreading when wet, acute to
somewhat acuminate, decurrent; margins revolute in lower 3/4 or less, entire or crenulate above;
costae strong, 0.6–0.8 the length of the leaves; cells smooth and thick-walled, upper cells oval to
elliptic, 15–24 μm long, median cells round to elliptic, 10–20 μm long; basal cells near costa in lower
1/6 of leaf elongate to linear, to 50 μm long; alar cells short-rectangular, subquadrate, or oblate, 6–
16 μm. Autoicous. Perichaetia and perigonia lateral. Perigonial leaves ovate; perichaetial leaves oblong
to oblong-lanceolate, inner ones abruptly narrowed to a long, smooth awn, generally shorter than
the leaf lamina, costae stoutly filling the apex, weakly developed or absent at base. Setae short,
0.1–0.2 μm long, cells quadrate. Capsules immersed, ellipsoid, 1.0–1.5 mm long, smooth, light
brown, narrowed at the mouth, abruptly rounded-indented to the setae; exothecial cells small, red, in
2–3 rows below the mouth, irregularly short-rectangular below; stomata not seen; opercula conicrostrate,
smooth, to 0.5 mm long; annuli compound; peristome diplolepideous, inserted within the
mouth; exostome teeth narrowly triangular to linear, whitish yellow, dorsal (outer) surface smooth
below, papillose above, to 0.40 mm long; endostome segments linear, papillose, shorter than the exostome,
cilia absent, basal membranes very low. Spores massive, spherical or irregularly oblong,
lightly papillose, 44–65 μm. Spores endosporically germinated within the capsule, to 75 μm long. Calyptrae
mitrate, smooth, 0.4–0.6 mm long.

Ceratodon purpureus (Hedw.) Brid. subsp. stenocarpus (B.S.G.) Dix., New Zealand Inst. Bull. 3(2): 50. 1914. Ceratodon stenocarpus B.S G., Bryol. Eur. 2: 146. 1846. Type. Mexico, Chinanthe, Liebmann 84.

Plants greenish yellow; secondary stems 2 cm long, branches sparse and irregularly spaced. Leaves crowded, curved and contorted when dry, ovate-lanceolate to lanceolate, 1.5–2 mm long; apex acute to acuminate; margins recurved nearly to the apex, coarsely and irregularly toothed; upper cells subquadrate to quadrate, 7–9 µm long; basal cells short-rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Setae 2 cm long, pale yellow to reddish, smooth; capsules suberect to inclined, ovoid-cylindrical, 2 mm long, yellow; urns sulcate when dry; stomata phaneroporic; opercula conic; peristome teeth reddish yellow, lanceolate, lightly papillose, split nearly to the base. Spores rounded, 11–15 µm, finely papillose.

Fissidens steerei Grout, N. Amer. Fl. 15(3): 191. 1943. Type. Mexico, Steere 1539 (DUKE, MICH).

Plants to 7–8 mm × ca. 1 mm. Leaves 0.5–0.95 mm × ca. 0.25 mm; apex obtuse to broadly acute; margins crenulate, elimbate; vaginant laminae unequal, acute, ½–⅔ the leaf length; costa ending several cells below the apex; cells 8–11 µm, mammillose, rarely bulging, hexagonal. Sporophytes unknown.

Fissidens subulatus Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 589. 1869. Type. Brazil, Spruce

 Plants to 3 mm × ca. 1.25 mm. Leaves ca. 1.5 mm × ca. 0.2 mm; apex acute; margins more or less crenulate, elimbate; vaginant laminae 1/3 the leaf length, narrowed to the costa; costa mostly long excurrent; cells 12–32 µm × 7–18 µm, marginal ones smaller, smooth, oblong, oblong-hexagonal to rhombic. Sporophytes terminal.

Fissidens zollingeri Mont., Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot., sér. 3, 4: 114. 1845. Type. Java, Zollinger 1604 (not found).

Fissidens kegelianus C. Müll., Linnaea 21: 181. 1848. Type. Suriname, Kegel 1226 (GOET).

Fissidens clavipes Sull., Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts & Sci. 5: 275. 1861. Type. Cuba, Wright 20 (FH).

Fissidens monandrus Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 598. 1869. Type. Cuba, Wright 11 (FH).

Plants to 5.5 mm × 3 mm. Leaves to 2.5 mm × to 0.5 mm; apex acute to irregularly acute and apiculate; margins more or less entire, limbate on all laminae; vaginant laminae equal, acute, 1/2 the leaf length; costa percurrent to short-excurrent; cells 10–13(–18) µm, greatly enlarged, more or less pellucid, smooth to somewhat bulging, mostly irregularly hexagonal, more or less oblong in lower parts of vaginant laminae. Sporophytes terminal.

Fissidens reticulosus (C. Müll.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 603. 1869. Conomitrium reticulosum C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 525. 1851. Type. Mexico, Liebmann (NY).

Plants to 8 mm × ca. 2.5 mm. Leaves ca. 2.5 mm × ca. 0.3 mm; apex acute to somewhat obtuse and apiculate; margins more or less entire, limbate on all laminae, limbidia 2-stratose; vaginant laminae equal, acute, ca. 1/2 the leaf length; costa ending 8–15 cells below the apex; cells 16–48 µm × 7–20 µm, smooth, bulging, mostly oblong-hexagonal. Sporophytes terminal.

Plants medium-sized to robust, 3–15 cm long, yellow green, golden reddish, in glossy, lax mats or pendent masses. Stems prostrate, sparsely to irregularly pinnately branched, red; stems in cross section with epidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, yellowish to hyaline, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; ax-illary hairs 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hya-line; rhizoids not commonly encountered, on branches or stems in contact with substrate, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregu-larly branched. Leaves erect to erect-spreading when dry, little changed when wet, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 0.9–1.4 mm long, acute to rounded-acute, apices often recurved, concave, rounded to the insertions, not decurrent; margins entire at base, papillose-roughened to serrulate above, plane, erect or incurved; costae double, strong, diverging throughout, 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, at times ending in a projecting spine; cells pluripapillose with 2–6 simple or branched papillae, more or less seriately arranged over the lumina, linear-flexuose, 34–50 X 3 µm, thick-walled, usually porose, lower cells somewhat longer; basal cells across the insertions enlarged, rectangular, strongly porose, yellowish to reddish; alar cells undifferentiated. Plants medium-sized, 1–5 cm long, green, pale green, or yellowish green, in dull mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, dark red; stems in cross section with a single row of enlarged hyaloder-mis cells, epidermis of 2–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, yellowish to hyaline, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect and more or less crispate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, elliptic to oblong-lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, 1.5–2.0 mm long, concave, rounded at the apex and abruptly subulate, rounded to the insertions, not decurrent; margins serrulate below by projecting end walls, serrate to dentate above by serrulate projecting end walls and lateral projecting papillae, plane or erect; costae double, strong, 3/4 the leaf length, usually projecting at tips by 1–3-celled dorsal crests or spines; upper and median cells pluripapillose with 2–6 more or less seriately arranged, often high and curved papillae, oblong to linear-flexuose, 20–40 X 3–4 µm, firm-walled; basal cells en-larged, smooth, long-rectangular to elongate-hexagonal, cells across the insertions enlarged, rectan-gular, smooth or weakly porose, reddish, basal marginal cells narrow and elongate forming a more or less distinct border; alar cells undifferentiated. Asexual reproductive structures not seen. Autoicous. Perigonia and perichaetia sessile along stems and branches. Setae elongate, flexuose, 15–35 mm long, red to red brown, smooth below, weakly papillose above. Capsules red, inclined to pendent, ovoid-cylindrical to cylindrical, 2–3 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells at mouth quadrate to shortly oblate in 2–3 rows, reddish, yellowish red, rectangular to oblong, collenchymatous below; sto-mata rudimentary, on neck; opercula co

Plants small to medium-sized, pale green to yellowish green, in loose or dense mats. Stems creep-ing to shortly ascending, 1–4 cm long, sparsely and irregularly branched, hyaline to pale green when young, red when old, epidermal cells short, broadly rectangular, densely foliate or at times com-planate-foliate; stems in cross section with outer cells somewhat smaller than the inner cortical cells, otherwise cells undifferentiated, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs fragile, 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, not or sparsely and ir-regularly branched. Lateral and dorsal leaves flexuose-contorted when dry, flattened, spreading, erect-spreading, or falcate to falcate-secund, lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, 1–2 mm long, symmetric or asymmetric, apices long-acuminate; margins sharply serrate to serrulate above, plane or inflexed on one side below, marginal cells enlarged and bulging, sometimes forming a distinct border; costa ab-sent; cells smooth, pellucid, lax, thin-walled, upper and median cells long-hexagonal to linear, 90–150 X 8–20 µm; basal cells enlarged, broadly long-rectangular, extreme basal cells at middle of insertion line often greatly enlarged; alar cells not differentiated. Ventral leaves lanceolate; margins smooth to weakly serrulate, marginal cells not bulgingly inflated; upper cells linear, narrow, firm-walled, other-wise similar to those of dorsal and lateral leaves. Asexual reproduction from gemmae in loose clusters on stems abaxial to the leaf insertions; gemmae green to hyaline, uniseriate, borne terminally on loose filaments. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 10–25 mm long, red to dark red, smooth. Capsules inclined, cylin-dric, 1–2 mm long; exothecial cells rectangular to long-rectangular, lateral walls very thick, horizon-tal walls thin; stomata on neck, variable in form:

Meesia longiseta Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 173. 1801.

Protologue. In turfosis paludosis Sueciae, Berolini, Erlangae, in monte pinifero Franconiae. 

Plants small to medium-sized in yellow‑green tufts. Stems to 1 cm high, tomentose below. Leaves somewhat 3-ranked, spreading or wide‑spreading from an erect base, not much altered when dry, 2–3 mm long, ovate‑lanceolate, moderately keeled above, decurrent; apices acute or rounded‑obtuse; margins entire or obscurely and bluntly serrulate, plane or weakly revolute at base; costae subpercurrent; upper leaf cells short-rectangular to narrowly long‑rectangular, 24–50 μm long, thin to firm‑walled, smooth, basal cells laxly rectangular, enlarged, bulging, thin‑walled, to 60 μm long. Synoicous. Perichaetial leaves 4–7 mm long. Setae 6–10 cm long. Capsules 2.0–3.5 mm long, pyriform, curved and asymmetric from an erect neck; opercula bluntly conic, 0.5 mm long; exostome teeth short, blunt or truncate, outer (dorsal) surface lightly thickened and faintly horizontally striate, inner (ventral) surface more strongly thickened than the outer surface, inner trabeculae thickened and projecting, endostome 2–4 times as long as the exostome teeth, basal membrane low, segments narrow, keeled, slightly perforate, outer (dorsal) surface smooth, often with yellow, irregular, often discontinuously thickenings, inner (ventral) surface hyaline, lightly thickened, cilia 2–4, rudimentary. Spores 36–44 μm, brown, lightly papillose.

Cardotiella quinquefaria (Hornsch.) Vitt, J. Hattori Bot. Lab. 49: 102. 1981.

Macromitrium quinquefarium Hornsch., Fl. Bras. 1(2): 26. 1840. Protologue: Brazil. Habitat in montibus ad Lages, Sincora et al Rio de Contas, rel. in mediterraneis prov. Bahiensis: M[artius].

Anomodon scaberrimus Broth., Bih. Kongl. Svensk. Vetensk.‑Akad. Förh. 21, 3(3): 65. 1895. Coleochaetium scaberrimum (Broth.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. (ed. 2) 11: 26. 1925. Minas Geraës, Caldas prope amnem Rio Verde ad arbores (Mosén n. 365).

Coleochaetium standleyi Bartr. in Grout, Bryologist 47: 21. 1944. Leiomitrium standleyi (Bartr. in Grout) Grout, N. Amer. Fl. 15A: 62. 1946. Protologue: Guatemala. Dept. Huehuetenango: Rio Pucal, about 14 km. south of Huehuetenango, alt. about 1780 m., Jan. 4, 1941, Paul C. Standley, 82293 (F, MO).

Plants small to medium-sized, wiry, dull, light‑green above, yellow to brownish below in loose, radiculose mats. Primary stems creeping to 5 cm long, irregularly branched. Leaves 5‑ranked, smooth, erect‑imbricate to contorted when dry, patent to squarrose spreading when wet, 1–2 mm long, keeled, ovate‑lanceolate to ovate, abruptly narrowed to a lanceolate‑lingulate, acute or apiculate, fragile point, strongly decurrent; margins recurved below, plane above, papillose-serrate above; costa percurrent; upper and basal cells similar, 6–10 μm, rounded-quadrate, unipapillose with high conic papillae on both surfaces, basal decurrency cells enlarged, rectangular (to 20 μm long), pellucid, smooth or papillose, the marginal cells tuberculate. Sporophytes unknown.

Macrocoma tenuis (Hook. & Grev.) Vitt ssp. sullivantii (C. Müll.) Vitt, Bryologist 83: 413. 1980. Macromitrium sullivantii C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 20: 361. 1862. Macrocoma sullivantii (C. Müll.) Grout, Bryologist 47: 5. 1944. Protologue: U.S.A. In summitate mont. Jonah Georgiae americanae ad corticem pinorum vetust. Lesquereux (MO).

Macromitrium mexicanum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 198. 1869. Protologue: Mexico. Oaxaca, Herb. Van den Bosch. 

Macromitrium leiboldtii Hampe, Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 28: 50. 1870. Protologue: Mexico. Hab. pr. Veracrucem leg. Strebel, prius ab Leiboldtio sub no. 5 collectum et ab amico Gottsche statu vetusto communicatum.

Macromitrium ghiesbreghtii Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 188. 1872. Protologue: Mexico. Mejico, 1845 (Ghiesbreght in herb. Mus. Par.).

Macromitrium braunioides Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 108. 1909. Protologue: Mexico. Maltrata, W. Trelease, 1905 (MO). 

Plants slender, stiff, olive‑green to yellowish red, in radiculose mats. Primary stems erect to 3–5 cm long, irregularly branched. Leaves erect to erect‑appressed, spreading at tips when dry, erect‑spreading to wide‑spreading when wet, 1.0–1.4(–1.6) mm long, keeled, ovate‑lanceolate to lanceolate; apices sharply acute to short-acuminate; margins entire or minutely crenulate, recurved below, plane above; costae ending below the apex, covered at back with short quadrate cells; upper and median cells 6–10 μm, rounded‑quadrate, thick‑walled, smooth to mammillose, apical cells rounded to shortly elliptic, basal cells rounded to elliptic, often stoutly papillose, inner basal cells near costa elongate, incrassate, to 20 μm long. Gonioautoicous. Setae 4–8 mm long, smooth, yellow to red. Capsules 1.5–2.0 mm long, erect, oblong cylindrical, furrowed in upper _ when dry, smooth below, often puckered at mouth; opercula short‑rostrate, 0.7–1.0 mm long; peristome reduced to two short, hyaline membranes barely extending above the capsule mouth, the inner one smooth, the outer one densely papillose. Spores isosporous, 36–48 μm, papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, densely hairy, 3 mm long.

Macromitrium fuscoaureum Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 83. 1928.

Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, Cerros de Zurqui, northeast of San Isidro, Province of  Heredia, Costa Rica, altitude 2,000–2,400 meters, Paul C. Standley and Juvenal Valerio, March 3, 1926, no. 50403 (FH, NY, US).

Plants robust-sized, reddish yellow. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 4 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves strongly keeled, erect‑clasping at base, flexuose to spirally contorted and undulate above when dry, abruptly squarrose‑spreading from an erect clasping base when wet, 6–9 mm long, 0.5 mm wide, linear‑lanceolate; apices long-subulate, acuminate; margins often undulate, serrulate, recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent; upper interior cells 30–40 x 12 μm, fusiform to long-rhomboidal, smooth, incrassate and porose, upper marginal cells longer and narrower, forming a more or less distinct border, basal cells 40–70 μm, long‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, not tuberculate. Perichaetial leaves similar to vegetative leaves. Setae 17–20(–30) mm long, smooth. Capsules 1–2 mm long, cylindric, smooth to very weakly furrowed; annulus, operculum, peristome and spores not seen. Calyptrae mitrate, laciniate, naked, 2–3 mm long.

Macromitrium microstomum (Hook. & Grev.) Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 2(2): 130. 1827. Orthotrichum microstomum Hook. & Grev., Edinburgh J. Sci. 1: 114. 1824. Protologue: Australia. Van Dieman's Land; Dr. Spence.

Macromitrium stratosum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 199. 1869. Protologue: Jamaica, Maxwell (NY).

Macromitrium stolonigernum C. Müll., Linnaea 42: 489. 1879. Protologue: Venezuela.  [Fendler] 61 (NY), syn. nov.

Macromitrium acunae Thér., Mem. Soc. Cub. Hist. Nat. "Felipe Poey" 14: 353. 1940. Protologue: Cuba. Pico Turquino (Acuña 407).

Plants slender, yellow‑green above, brown below. Stems strongly creeping to 7 cm long, branches to 2 cm long, weakly tomentose. Leaves moderately keeled, erect below, incurved to inrolled above, spirally curved around the stem when dry, erect‑patent to erect‑inflexed when wet, 1.5–2.0 x 0.5 mm, lanceolate; apices narrowly acute to acuminate; margins entire, recurved below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae percurrent to shortly excurrent; upper interior cells 5–8 μm, strongly rounded to short-oblong, smooth, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 40–60 μm long, linear‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, not tuberculate. Autoicous. Setae 7–15 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1.5 mm long, obovoid, smooth below, distinctly puckered and dark-red at mouth; opercula obliquely rostrate, 0.5–1 mm long; annuli non‑revoluble, with fragments adhering to capsule mouth; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, 180 μm high, white to light brown, densely papillose, endostome absent. Spores isosporous, 30–60 μm, papillose. Calyptrae cucullate/mitrate, weakly laciniate, plicate above, naked, 3 mm long.

Macromitrium standleyi Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 85. 1928.

Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, Cerro de las Caricias, north of San Isidro, Province of Heredia, Costa Rica, altitude 2,000 to 2,400 meters, Paul C. Standley and Juvenal Valerio, March 11, 1926, no. 52147 (FH, NY, US).

Macromitrium standleyi var. subundulatum Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 86. 1928. Protologue: Costa Rica. On tree, Cerro de las Caricias, north of San Isidro, Province of Heredia, Costa Rica, altitude 2,000 to 2,400 meters, Paul C. Standley and Juvenal Valerio, March 11, 1926, no. 52096 (FH, NY, US), syn. nov.

Plants robust, yellowish red to yellow‑green. Stems strongly creeping to 15 cm long, branches widely spaced along the primary stems, to 4 cm long, moderately tomentose. Leaves keeled, erect below, crispate‑flexuose and undulate above when dry, flexuose-spreading when wet, to 18 x 1 mm, linear‑lanceolate; apices long-filiform acuminate; margins undulate, ciliate‑dentate from just above the leaf base, sharply spinose‑denticulate at apex, recurved at the extreme base below, otherwise plane, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae excurrent; upper interior cells variable, 18–40 x 8 μm, more or less rhomboidal, smooth or bulging mammillose, thick‑walled at times porose, upper marginal cells frequently longer and narrower forming a distinct border, basal cells to 55 μm long, narrowly rectangular, incrassate and porose, tuberculate. Setae to 20 mm long, smooth. Capsules 1.5–2 mm long, globose‑pyriform, smooth above, wrinkled at neck; annulus not seen; opercula-erect rostrate, 1 mm long; intact peristome not seen, exostome densely papillose. Spores anisosporous, 18–24 μm, smooth, thin‑walled and 45–50 μm, lightly papillose, thick‑walled. Calyptrae mitrate, deeply laciniate, naked, 2.5–3 mm long.

Macromitrium trichophyllum Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 207. 1869.

Protologue: Ecuador. Andes Quitense, in Cordillera occidentali, Chimborazo (3000 ped.),  Spruce, n. 92 (NY).

Plants large, reddish yellow to yellowish green. Stems weakly creeping, branches to 3 cm long. Leaves strongly keeled, erect‑clasping below, wide‑spreading to squarrose‑recurved above, upper leaf blade flexuose to spirally contorted when dry, erect at base, squarrose above when wet, 10–15 mm long; apices linear to setaceous, long, finely acuminate; margins serrate above, broadly recurved below, erect to plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae long- excurrent, sharply toothed at apex; upper interior cells 24–40(–54) x 10 μm, long‑rectangular to rhomboidal, incrassate and porose, smooth, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells 40–60 μm long, linear‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, not tuberculate. Sporophyte not seen. "Theca in pedunculo rubro, pyriformis, laevis, collo plicato, operculo subulato, peristomii dentibus adglutinatis; calyptra nuda" (Mitten 1869).

Pyrrhobryum mnioides (Hook.) Manuel, Cryptog. Bryol. Lichénol. 1: 70. 1980.

Hypnum mnioides Hook., Musci Exot. 1: 77. 1818. Rhizogonium mnioides (Hook.) Wils. in Hook., Fl. Nov.‑Zel. 2: 116. 1854. Rhizogonium mnioides Schimp ex C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 140. 1901 [1900], hom. illeg. Protologue. Argentina, Staten Island near Cape Horn, Menzies.

Plants robust in loose dark‑green to yellow‑green tufts. Stems erect, to 10 cm high, simple or forked, densely tomentose below; rhizoids branched, red. Leaves erect-contorted to incurved or crisped when dry, spreading when wet, 5–7 mm long, linear‑lanceolate, long and broadly decurrent; apices long acuminate; margins bistratose, coarsely doubly serrate from near the base; costae stout, spinose at back, dorsal surface covered with quadrate to rectangular cells, percurrent or shortly excurrent; upper cells 8–18 μm long, irregular in size and shape, mostly rounded to rounded‑quadrate, occasionally rectangular to elongate, thick‑walled, not porose, basal cells 12–22 μm long irregularly quadrate to rectangular, basal juxtacostal cells enlarged‑rectangular, thin‑walled and bulging, to 40 μm long. Dioicous. Inflorescences small and bud‑like, borne laterally along the stems, perichaetial leaves long-setaceous. Setae to 6 cm long, erect‑flexuose, smooth, red. Capsules 2–3 mm long, oblong‑cylindrical, curved or long‑cupulate, more or less erect, constricted at base; opercula short, stoutly and obliquely rostrate, 1–2 mm long; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, brownish‑red, papillose throughout, endostome yellowish, basal membrane high, segments stout, narrowly perforate, cilia 2–3, well‑developed, nodose. Spores 14–24 μm, faintly roughened. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, to 4 mm long.

Rhizogonium sublimbatum Crum, Bryologist 84: 390. 1981. 

Protologue. Costa Rica. Cerro Daser area, 6 km along road which turns off westward from national road no.4, 5 km south of Asseri, 10 km SSE of city center of San José, 9°50'N, 84°07'W, Crosby & Crosby 6226 (MO, isotype). 

Plants slender in loose yellow‑green tufts. Stems erect, to 3.0 cm high, simple or forked, naked below or with small, reduced, and remote leaves, densely radiculose at base or occasionally sparsely from axils of leaves. Upper leaves bifarious, flexuose tapered toward the tips, incurved when dry, wide‑spreading when wet, 1–2 mm long, ovate, oblong‑ovate to elliptic, not decurrent; apices broadly acute, abruptly cuspidate; margins coarsely and irregularly serrate in upper _, teeth uni‑ or multicellular, irregularly bi‑ and tristratose in places; costae stout, smooth at back, percurrent or excurrent; cells smooth, upper interior cells 12–18 μm long, irregular in size and shape, mostly hexagonal, with firm, thick‑walls, clearly thickened at the corners, upper marginal cells extremely variable, from quadrate to hexagonal to elongate, basal interior cells somewhat larger, irregularly quadrate to rectangular, basal marginal cells usually elongate, but occasionally short and quadrate enlarged‑rectangular. Brood‑bodies uniseriate, papillose at times clustered in leaf axils or on rhizoids. Dioicous. Inflorescences small and bud‑like at base of stems, perichaetial leaves long and narrowly acuminate. Setae to 3.5 cm long, erect‑flexuose, smooth, red or yellow. Capsules 2.0 mm long, oblong to long‑cupulate, narrowed to a distinct neck, suberect; exothecial cells thick‑walled, straight-walled; stomata phaneroporic, in capsule neck; operculum not seen; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, yellowish‑white, papillose throughout, endostome hyaline, basal membrane high, lightly papillose, segments narrow, not perforate, densely papillose, cilia stout, 2–3, nodose, papillose. Spores 14–18 μm, smooth to lightly papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Sphagnum compactum DC. ex Lam. & DC., Fl. Franç. 2: 443. 1805.

Plants short, compactly tufted in small, rounded cushions, pale green or brownish, rarely red-brown or pinkish red; cortical cells in 2–3 layers, without fibrils or pores; wood cylinder brown. Stem leaves minute (rarely 1 mm long), concave, shortly lingulate to oblong-triangular, bordered in the lower half, sometimes slightly lacerate at the broad, rounded apex; hyaline cells not divided, without fibrils, on the outer surface without pores or gaps but with membrane pleats, on the inner surface with a membrane gap at the upper end of each cell, small and rounded below but irregular and nearly as large as the cell toward the leaf apex. Branches short, crowded in fascicles of 4–6 (2, rarely 3, spreading); cortical cells in 1 layer, each uniporose at the upper end. Branch leaves imbricate to squarrose, broadly elliptic to oblong-ovate, broadly truncate at an involute-concave or cucullate apex, denticulate along a marginal resorption furrow; hyaline cells slightly convex on both surfaces, on the outer surface with few to numerous round, ringed pores near the commissures, mostly partitioned off by a straight or ring-like fibril and also with few to numerous pseudopores similarly partitioned off, sometimes also with a few irregularly rounded median pores, often with membrane pleats, on the inner surface with more or less ringed corner pores, usually in 3's at adjacent angles, and occasional pseudopores at the commissures; green cells, in section, elliptic, central, and entirely included, the adjacent walls of hyaline cells smooth.

Sphagnum imbricatum Hornsch. ex Russ., Arch. Naturk. Liv- Ehst- Kurlands, Ser. 2, Biol. Naturk. 7: 99. 1865.

Plants often fairly robust, in pale green to dark yellow-brown cushions, hummocks, or carpets; cortical cells in 3–4 layers, fibrillose, the outer cells with few to many irregularly rounded pores, the inner walls of the innermost cells finely cross-striate; wood cylinder of stem brown. Stem leaves oblong to lingulate, rounded at the apex, finely fringed and hyaline at the margins; hyaline cells commonly divided, without fibrils and pores, almost entirely resorbed on the outer surface. Branches stout, normally in fascicles of 5 (2 spreading), cortical cells in 1 layer, fibrillose, 1–2)-porose, the inner walls finely cross-striate. Branch leaves broadly ovate, cucullate-concave, roughened at back of the apex and serrulate-bordered by a resorption furrow; hyaline cells very concave on the outer surface, nearly plane on the inner, on the outer surface with 2–5 1arge, ringed, elliptic pores, in 3's at adjacent angles, more numerous (11–17) and rounded-elliptic toward the middle of the leaf base, on the inner surface toward the leaf apex with small, ringed corner pores and also 1–6 very large, round, unringed pores in a single row or, toward the margins, as many as 12 in 2 rows; green cells in section equilateral-triangular, broadly exposed on the inner surface, the side walls of hyaline cells beset with comb fibrils (often present only near the leaf insertion).

Plants small and slender, 1–3 cm long, pale green to green, in loose or dense mats. Stems pros-trate, irregularly branched, whitish to yellowish when young, red with age; stems in cross section with 1–3 rows of somewhat enlarged, firm-walled epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of ini-tials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irreg-ularly branched. Leaves erect to erect-spreading, somewhat contorted to twisted when dry, erect-spreading, flexuose when wet. Dorsal and lateral leaves lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.4 mm long, gradually long-acute to broadly acuminate; margins coarsely serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth swollen, often bifid, serrate to subentire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, weakly diverging throughout or parallel, serrate on back, projecting at the apices; cells smooth, at times weakly prorate near apex, long-rectangular to elongate-fusiform, thin-walled, eporose, 25–50 X 4–6 µm, lower cells between the costae 40–50 X 4–6 µm; basal cells near the in-sertions enlarged, oblong-rectangular; alar cells short-rectangular, otherwise undifferentiated. Ventral leaves erect, lanceolate, symmetric; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, smooth on back, not projecting at the apex; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 8–15 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth throughout or at times roughened to scabrose below capsules. Capsules inclined to pendent, short-cylindric, 1.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, thick-walled, collenchymatous; sto-mata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli of 5–8 rows of cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peri-stome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae projecting laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface yellow above, red at base, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yellowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long

Plants small and slender, 1–3 cm long, green to pale green, in dense mats. Stems prostrate, irreg-ularly branched, yellowish when young, red with age; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; para-phyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia subfoliose, with thin-walled cells; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and ir-regularly branched. Leaves erect at base, falcate-secund above when dry, erect-spreading, flexuose when wet. Dorsal and lateral leaves lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 1.0–1.5 mm long, gradually long-acuminate; margins coarsely serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth swollen, often bifid, serrate to subentire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, weakly diverging throughout or parallel, serrate on back, projecting at the apices; cells densely prorate, upper and median cells long-rectangular, 15–30 µm long, firm-walled, eporose or porose, lower cells between the costae 14–40 X 2–6 µm; basal cells near the insertions enlarged, oblong-rectangular, often reddish brown across the base; alar cells short-rectangular, otherwise undifferentiated. Ventral leaves erect, lanceolate, symmetric; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, smooth on back, not projecting at the apices; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 12–22 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth below, somewhat roughened below capsules. Capsules inclined to pendent, short-cylindric, 1.5–2.0 mm long, neck well developed; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, lateral walls evenly thickened, horizontal walls collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; operculum and annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furrows, dorsal trabeculae project-ing laterally, secondary walls on dorsal (outer) surface dark red, densely and closely cross-striate below, coarsely papillose above, primary walls yellow, smooth, ventral (inner) surface hyaline to yel-lowish, deposition thin, lightly papillose; endostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly pa-pillose throughout, basal membranes high, segments broad, strongly keeled, not perforate, cilia absent. Plants small to medium-sized, 10–40 mm long, pale, yellowish green, or reddish yellow, in thin mats. Stems prostrate, irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, somewhat complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with weakly differentiated 1–3-stratose hyalo-dermis, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyl-lia foliose; axillary hairs fugacious, 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids sparse, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves contorted when dry, wide-spreading when wet. Lateral leaves asymmetric, oblong to oblong-ovate, 1.5–2.5 mm long, short-acuminate, concave; margins serrate to denticulate, broadly inflexed below on one side, strongly bordered by 4–7 rows of narrow, elongate cells, confluent in the apices; costae double, ending 2/3–7/8 the leaf length, diverging throughout, occasionally projecting at the apices, smooth on dorsal surface, often confluent with leaf border on one side; cells smooth, upper cells irregularly rounded-hexagonal, 8–28 # 12–20 µm, laxly bulging, median and lower cells oblong-rectangular to long-rectangular; alar cells undifferentiated. Ventral and dorsal leaves symmetric, ovate. Asexual reproduction absent. Dioicous. Perigonia sessile on stems, bud-like, 1 mm long. Perichaetia and sporophytes unknown.

Pilopogon guadeloupensis (Brid.) Frahm, Fl. Neotrop. Monogr. 54: 206. 1991. Dicranum guadeloupense Brid., Muscol. Recent. Suppl. 1: 213. 1806. Campylopus guadeloupensis (Brid.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 77. 1869. Type. Guadeloupe, Balby s.n.

Didymodon gracilis Hook., Musci Exot. 1: 5. 1818. Pilopogon gracilis (Hook.) Brid., Bryol. Univ. 1: 519. Type. Colombia, in monte Quindiu, Andes de Cundinamarcae, Humboldt & Bonpland.

Pilopogon gracilis var. bernoullii C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 185. 1897. Pilopogon bernoullii (C. Müll.) C. Müll., Gen. Musc. Frond. 256. 1900. Type. Guatemala, Toyahay, Bernoulli & Cario 1870.

Plants variable in size, slender to medium or large, forming dense or loose turfs, yellowish green; stems erect, 1–15 cm long. Leaves evenly spaced, appressed wet or dry, subulate from a narrowly oblong base, 3–6 mm long; margins erect to incurved, entire except denticulate at apex; costa excurrent (upper leaves at times with costa excurrent, as long as the lower leaves), occupying 1/2 the leaf width at base, ribbed at back; upper leaf cells elongate-oval to oblong, incrassate, not pitted; median cells narrowly oblong; basal cells rectangular, hyaline, thin-walled, extending upward along the basal margins in a V-shaped pattern. Perichaetial leaves long sheathing, setaceous above, convolute at base, reaching from 1/2 to nearly the entire length of the seta. Setae 10–20 mm long, smooth below, papillose at apex; capsules erect to inclined, cylindrical, 2–3 mm long, smooth; peristome teeth filiform, densely papillose, 300 µm high; opercula 1.0–1.5 mm long.

Cynodontium guatemalensis (Bartr.) Crum, Bryologist 87: 203. 1984. Oncophorus guatemalensis Bartr., Bryologist 49: 111. 1946. Type. Guatemala, Quezaltenango, Steyermark 34872 (F, FH). Paratype. Steyermark 34869c (F, FH).

Plants yellowish green above, brown below; stems to 3 cm long. Leaves erect at base, flexuous-spreading when wet, crispate when dry, keeled above, narrowly lanceolate, 5–6 mm long, acute; margins recurved below, irregularly doubly serrulate above; costa ending below the apex; upper leaf cells irregularly rounded-quadrate, thick-walled; basal cells rectangular, thick-walled, yellowish. Inner perigonial bracts acuminate. Setae 3–4 mm long, cygneous when wet, yellow; capsules erect, oblong-cylindrical, 1.0–1.5 mm long, erect, not strumose, furrowed when dry; peristome teeth red, divided 1/2 their lengths; opercula 0.5–1.0 mm long.

Pilopogon laevis (Tayl.) Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 9: 12. 1936. Campylopus laevis Tayl., London J. Bot. 5: 47. 1846. Pilopogonella laevis (Tayl.) Bartr., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 6: 10. 1934. Type. Ecuador, Mt. Pichincha, Jameson (FH).

Plants small, forming loose, reddish yellow to red brown tufts; stems erect, to 10 mm high. Leaves erect-appressed to erect-spreading, narrowly lanceolate, 3–4 mm long, subulate; margins incurved above, entire; costa in upper leaves long-excurrent into hyaline, denticulate awns, dorsal surface above with lamellae 1 cell high; upper and median cells oval to rhomboidal, incrassate, non-porose; basal cells elongate rectangular, hyaline, thin-walled, extending up the basal margins in a V-shaped pattern. Dioicous. Sporophytes not seen, description from Frahm (1983). "Seta to 1 cm; capsule 2 mm long, dark brown, longly rostrate; peristome teeth 16, split to the base into filiform prongs. Spores yellowish, ca. 13 µm in diameter, smooth. Calyptrae cucullate, ciliate at base."

Philonotis sphaericarpa (Hedw.) Brid., Bryol. Univ. 2: 25. 1827.

Mnium sphaericarpon Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 197. 1801. Bartramia sphaericarpa (Hedw.) P.-Beauv., Prodr. Aethéog. 44. 1805. Protologue: Jamaica. In Jamaica sin coll.

Philonotis sphaericarpa var. latirevoluta Card., Rev. Bryol. 38: 36. 1911. Protologue: Mexico. Etat de Puebla: Honey-station (Pringle, 1908, n°15317).

Plants small, medium, or large sized, in loose or dense, yellowish‑green or green, glaucous tufts, to 25 mm high. Stems red; rhizoids at base, reddish brown, smooth to lightly roughened. Leaves 1.2–2 mm long, erect, erect-spreading or spreading when dry, erect-spreading when wet, straight or secund, ovate-lanceolate; apices acuminate; margins narrowly revolute, singly or doubly serrate; costa short- to long-excurrent, excurrent part toothed; cells papillose, papillae at upper cell ends, upper cells rectangular, firm‑walled, 20–40 x 6–8 μm, basal cells rectangular, to 55 x 15 μm, alar cells quadrate. Dioicous.  Perigonia gemmiform. Setae 15–25 mm long, red. Capsules 1.5–2 mm long, brown, subglobose, inclined to pendent; exothecial cells thick-walled; opercula 0.5 mm long, conic‑mammillate; peristome double, exostome teeth red, on outer surface densely and thickly papillose above, finely and evenly papillose below, trabeculae thin, inner surface smooth, trabeculae thick, endostome nearly as long as the exostome, yellowish, finely papillose granulose below, segments split along the median line and each half diverging toward the cilia, cilia 2–3, well-developed. Spores reniform, 22–30 μm, papillose.

Anisothecium vaginatum (Hook.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 39. 1869. Dicranum vaginatum Hook., Musci Exot. 2: Pl. 141. 1820. Aongstroemia vaginata (Hook.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 608. 1851. Dicranella vaginata (Hook.) Card., Wiss. Ergebn. Schwed. Südpol. Exp. 1901–1903, 4(8): 60. 1908. Type. Colombia, Humboldt & Bonpland.

Plants large for the genus, gregarious or in loose tufts, dull green to yellowish; stems slender, 15–30(–40) mm high, with a julaceous appearance due to strongly clasping leaf bases. Leaves 3–4 mm long, obovate, strongly clasping at base, abruptly narrowed above to a widely spreading to squarrose, setaceous limb about the same length as the basal part of the leaf; margins entire below, slightly serrulate at the apex; costa percurrent and nearly filling the upper limb; lower leaf cells pale, rectangular, thin-walled, those at the shoulder smaller, subquadrate to transversely elongated, incrassate. Perichaetial leaves identical to vegetative leaves except the clasping base somewhat longer. Setae 10–12 mm long, erect, weakly flexuous to straight, red; capsules 1.5 mm long, erect, oblong; stomata in 1 or 2 rows at base of capsule; opercula 1.5–1.7 mm long, long subulate-rostrate; peristome teeth 16, reddish brown below, hyaline above, densely papillose, from a low, smooth, thickly trabeculate basal membrane, deeply divided into terete forks, 250 µm long. Calyptrae smooth, entire at base, 2.0 mm long. Spores roughened, 20 µm wide.

Plants small in dull, dark green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched; leaves reduced,
0.4 mm long, well spaced, scale-like, oblong-ligulate from an ovate base, wide-spreading to
squarrose at tips, cells more or less smooth below, densely papillose above; rhizoids red brown, in
clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or weakly and irregularly branched. Secondary stems
erect-ascending, to 2 cm long, irregularly branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of
small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, firm- or thick-walled,
central strand absent; paraphyllia and pseudoparaphyllia absent. Secondary stem leaves erect-imbricate
when dry, spreading to widely spreading, complanate when wet, oblong-ligulate from an ovate base,
0.8–1.4 mm long, rounded to rounded-obtuse, not apiculate, at base one side narrow, margins broadly
incurved, the other side wide, margins plane, weakly decurrent; margins papillose-crenulate; costae
single, ending well below the apex, yellow, often branched above, channeled on ventral surface, upper
dorsal costal cells elongate, often seriate papillose, in cross section cells homogeneous, thick-walled;
juxtacostal cells in lower part of leaf bistratose, upper cells unistratose with occasional, scattered
bistratose patches, quadrate, oblate, or irregularly hexagonal, 5–10 μm, densely pluripapillose by
thick, branched, or C-shaped papillae, juxtacostal cells near the insertion on one side short-rectangular,
quadrate, or oblate, 4–10 papillose, on the other long-rectangular, to 20 μm long, smooth, not porose.
Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown.
