Plants small, caespitose, green to yellowish green or brown with age, saxicolous or terricolous. Stems 5–20 mm high, irregularly branched, central strand absent, cortical cells thin-walled, hyaline, uniform throughout; rhizoids scattered on stem, smooth or verrucose. Axillary hairs 5–6 cells long, lower 1–2 cells brown. Leaves 1.5–2.5 mm long, ligulate to lingulate, erect to spreading at base, weakly keeled, flexuose when dry, erect when wet; apices acute to short-acuminate or rounded-obtuse; margins entire, plane above, recurved at base; costa narrow, subpercurrent to percurrent, surface cells rectangular, smooth on both surfaces, median guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band well-developed, ventral surface layer of enlarged cells present; upper cells rounded-quadrate or oblate, 4–8 x 4–10 μm, firm-walled, smooth to somewhat bulging on both sides, basal cells rectangular, thin-walled, smooth, 14–30 x 12–16 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia terminal. Setae smooth, 2–5 mm long, yellowish brown. Capsules short-cylindrical, erect, 1.0–1.2 mm long, smooth, yellowish brown; exothecial cells quadrate to rectangular, thin-walled; stomata in neck; opercula rostrate, beak erect, 1 mm long; annuli persistent, clinging to the capsule mouth after dehiscence; peristome absent. Spores 12–14 μm, granulate. Calyptra not seen.

Bryoerythrophyllum calcareum (Thér.) Zand., Bryologist 83: 232. 1980.

Barbula calcareum Thér., Smithsonian Misc. Collect. 85(4): 20. 1931. Protologue: Mexico. Morelia: Loma Santa María, on calcareous rocks ([Arsène] 4891). Valle de México: Desierto (Bro. Amable 1620).

Barbula linguaefolia Bartr., Bryologist 50: 204. 1947. Protologue: Guatemala. Suchiate: Finca El Naranjo, near Chicacoa, Ruth D. Svihla 2879a (FH).

 

Plants small, reddish green, to 10 mm high. Stems red, erect, not or irregularly branched,  sclerodermis present, central strand exceptionally well-developed; rhizoidal initials in serial rows, rhizoids red, coarsely papillose. Leaves 1.5–2 mm long, erect-incurved to erect-spreading when dry, spreading when wet, lingulate; apices obtuse; margins unistratose, narrowly recurved to near the apex, entire, not bordered, decurrent at base; costa sub-percurrent, smooth at back, ventral superficial cells elongate, guide cells present, ventral stereid band weakly developed, dorsal stereid band present, ventral and dorsal epidermal layers enlarged; upper cells 6–12 x 4–10 μm, firm-walled, oblate to irregularly quadrate, rounded-hexagonal, or short-rectangular, pluripapillose by thick, c-shaped papillae, basal cells 30–75 x 10 μm, long-rectangular, smooth, thin-walled, alar cells not differentiated. Dioicous. Perichaetia terminal; perichaetial leaves convolute. Setae smooth, 10–12 mm long, red. Capsules cylindric, curved when dry, 2.0 mm long, smooth; stomata in neck; opercula erect, long-conic, 1 mm long; exothecial cells long-rectangular; annuli persistent, of 2 rows of vesiculose cells; peristome of 32 red, filamentous, densely spiculose teeth, basal membrane low, teeth spirally twisted. Spores 6–8 μm, smooth to lightly papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, smooth, 2.0 mm long.

Micromitrium austinii Aust., Musci Appalach. 45. 1870.

Nanomitrium austinii (Aust.) Lindb., Not. Sällsk. Fauna Fl. Fenn. Förh. 13: 408. 1874. Protologue: U.S.A. On wet broken ground in woods, Closter, New Jersey. Austin, Musc. Appal. 45 (F, MO).

Ephemerum capituligerum C. Müll., Hedwigia 39: 235. 1900. Nanomitrium capituligerum (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 515. 1903. Protologue: Brazil. Brasilia, Rio de Janeiro, in terra humida prope Jacurepagua, Aug. 1894: E. Ule leg., dedit 1898. 

Plants yellow-green, from sparse protonemata. Leaves to 2.1 mm long, 0.15 mm wide, narrowly to broadly acute to acuminate; margins more or less entire below, bluntly serrulate above; costae absent; leaf cells largest at midleaf, to 155 μm long, 25 μm wide, marginal cells shorter. Capsules dark brown-black, minute, to 0.18 mm long, with median dehiscence; exothecial cells unistratose, estomatose. Spores 29–36 μm, densely papillose. Calyptrae centric.

Splachnobryum obtusum (Brid.) C. Müll., Verh. Zool.-Bot. Ges. Wien 19: 504. 1869. 

Weisia obtusa Brid., Muscol. Recent. Suppl. 1: 118. 1806.  Syrrhopodon obtusus (Brid.) Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond., Suppl. 2 (2): 106. 1827. Protologue: Hispaniola, Poiteau ('Boiteau').

Splachnobryum bernoullii C. Müll., Verh. Zool.-Bot. Ges. Wien 19: 505. 1869. Protologue: Guatemala; Dr. Gustav Bernoulli (NY).

Splachnobryum crenulatulum Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 86. 1909. Protologue: Mexico, Morlos, murs près de Cuernavaca, Pringle 10532 (NY, US); Jalisco, Etzatlán, 1908, Pringle 15272.

Splachnobryum ligulifolium Card., Rev. Bryol. 36: 86. 1909. Protologue: Mexico, Jalisco, Guadalajara, 1908, Pringle 15243 (NY). 

Stems to 12 mm long; axillary hairs of 2–3 colorless cells, apical cell clavate; propagula often present, stalked, axillary, branched, filamentous; rhizoidal tubers irregularly shaped, sometimes in substrata. Leaves 1–2 mm long, ovate to lingulate; apices obtuse to rounded; margins entire to crenulate, particularly in distal half, plane or narrowly recurved in distal half; costa ending 4 cells below apex to percurrent, with small central substereid band, 2–3 ventral and 3–5 dorsal surface cells enlarged; leaf cells smooth, occasionally bulging-mammillose, upper cells rhombic, 1–2:1, median cells 2–4:1, basal cells oblong. Setae yellow to reddish brown, 3–6 mm long. Capsules 0.6–2.0 mm long; opercula conic. Spores 13–17 μm, smooth.

Plants robust, to 11 cm long and 0.8–1.3 cm wide, yellow green above, red to burgundy below, in glossy epiphytic masses. Stems creeping, irregularly branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, be-coming reddish with age, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 3–4 rows of small, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia ab-sent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2–4 cells long, basal 1–3 cells short-rectangular, red-dish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids in sparse groups from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect, strongly undulate above, plicate below when dry, erect-spreading when wet, symmetric or weakly asymmetric, concave, broadly ovate-lanceolate, long-acuminate, 6–8 X 2–3 mm; margins en-tire below, weakly serrate above, plane; costae double, thin, ending 1/2–3/4 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth on back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, incrassate, porose, apical cells rhomboidal to elongate-rhomboidal, 39–69 X 9–12 µm, median cells linear-rhomboidal, 55–115 X 7–9 µm, cells across the base reddish orange, rectangular, strongly porose; alar cells shortly rectan-gular, 23–55 X 13–21 µm. Dioicous. Perigonia sessile along stems and branches. Perichaetia termi-nal on lateral buds. Setae elongate, 2.5–3.0 cm long, dark red, scabrous above. Capsules more or less inclined, symmetric and cylindric, neck moderately developed, 2.5–3.5 mm long; exothecial cells rounded-rectangular, incrassate, more or less collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula long-rostrate, conic at base, 1.5–2.0 mm long; annuli massive, persistent, of 4–8 rows of yellowish, hexagonal cells; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth narrowly triangular, with broad median furrows, densely and closely striate below, coarsely papillose above, ventral surface hyaline to yellowish, smooth; en-dostome as long as the exostome, yellowish, lightly papillose throughout, basal membranes high, seg-ments broad, strongly keeled, not perforate, cilia absent. Spores rounded, 23–35 µm,

Plants small and slender, 1–2 cm long, yellowish green to green, in loose or dense mats. Stems pros-trate, irregularly branched, whitish to yellowish when young, red with age, somewhat complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with 1–3 rows of somewhat small, firm-walled epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axil-lary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves erect, erect-spreading, somewhat flattened, lightly contorted to twisted when dry, erect-spreading, flexuose when wet. Dorsal and lateral leaves lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, 0.8–1.4 mm long, gradually acute to broadly acute; margins coarsely serrate to dentate in upper 2/3, teeth at times swollen and bifid, serrate to subentire below, plane to erect; costae double, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, weakly diverging throughout or parallel, serrate on back, projecting at the apices; cells smooth, at times weakly prorate near apex, upper and median cells long-rectangular to elongate-fusiform, thin-walled, eporose, 30–60 X 4–6 µm, lower cells be-tween the costae 30–50 X 4–6 µm; basal cells near the insertions enlarged, oblong-rectangular; alar cells short-rectangular, otherwise undifferentiated. Ventral leaves erect, ovate-lanceolate, symmetric; margins serrate in upper 2/3, teeth elongate, rarely bifid, entire below; costae double, slender, ending 2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, unequal, smooth on back, not projecting at the apices; upper cells elongate-flexuose. Autoicous. Setae elongate, 6–12 mm long, red, flexuose, smooth below, lightly papillose below capsules. Capsules inclined to pendent, short-cylindric, 1.0 mm long, neck well de-veloped; exothecial cells quadrate to oblate in 2–3 rows at mouth, those below oblong to rectangular, thick-walled, collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–4-celled, on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous, exostome narrowly triangular with broad median furro

Eucamptodontopsis brittoniae (Bartr.) Allen var. brittoniae, Trop. Bryol. 3: 60. 1990. Dicranoloma brittoniae Bartr., Contr. U.S. Natl. Herb. 26: 69. 1928. Type. Costa Rica, Prov. Heredia, Standley & Valerio 50505 (F, FH, NY, US).

 

Plants medium to large; stems 10–12 cm long. Leaves evenly spaced, moderately crowded, erect-spreading below, spirally contorted above when dry, concave to tubulose, linear-lanceolate, 10–15 mm long, apex tubulose-setaceous, base shortly clasping; margins broadly incurved, remotely crenulate above, entire below; costa smooth to slightly roughened at back above, percurrent; upper leaf cells linear-rectangular, those at the margins distinctly shorter, more or less rhomboidal, incrassate and pitted, smooth; basal cells linear-rectangular, not sharply differentiated from the upper leaf cells, incrassate and pitted; alar cells strongly differentiated, incrassate, short-rectangular, reddish brown, weakly pitted. Sporophytes unknown.

Racomitrium crispipilum (Tayl.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 96. 1874.

Trichostomum crispipilum Tayl., London J. Bot. 5: 47. 1846. Grimmia crispipila (Tayl.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 1: 808. 1849. Protologue: Ecuador. Summit of the Quitinian Andes, Prof. William Jameson, 1845 (NY).

Grimmia contermina C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 655. 1851. Racomitrium conterminum (C. Müll.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 98. 1874. Protologue: Costa Rica. America centralis, Costa-Rica, alt. inter 5000–8000', Febr. lg. A. S. Oersted (NY). 

Plants robust in loose tufts, brown below, olive‑green to yellow-green above, often hoary. Stems erect, fasciculate branched, to 10 cm high; rhizoids sparse. Leaves appressed to homomallous or falcate when dry, erect‑spreading to reflexed when wet, 3–4 mm long, ovate‑lanceolate; apices acuminate, hair‑point usually long, but also short or absent on some leaves, weakly decurrent; margins unistratose, revolute, erect or plane; costa thin, percurrent, dorsally flat to rounded in lower half, with 2–3 enlarged, ventral surface cells; laminae unistratose, cells smooth; upper cells 12–25 μm, short‑rectangular, thick‑walled, basal cells 38–60 μm long, elongate, alar cells moderately differentiated, basal margins often with 10–20 enlarged, hyaline, thin‑walled, esinuose cells. Dioicous. Setae single or multiple, red, 6–10 mm long. Capsules 2–3 mm long, cylindric, erect; stomata in neck; opercula long rostrate; peristome teeth linear, coarsely papillose, basal membrane absent. Spores 12–14 μm, finely papillose. Calyptra not seen.

Grimmia longirostris Hook., Musci Exot. 1: 62. 1818.

Protologue: Ecuador. Locis scopulosis, apricis, in declivitate montis Chimborazo, altit. 2380 hexapod. super porphyrite (Regnum Quitense.) Humboldt et Bonpland (BM). 

Grimmia affinis Hornsch., Flora 2: 443. 1819 [July], nom. illeg. non Hornsch. 1819, Flora 2: 85 [February] (= G. fuscolutea Hook.). Protologue: Austria. Windissmattrey Tauern, Hornschuch s.n. (B).

Grimmia breviexserta C. Müll., Bull. Herb. Boissier 5: 200. 1897. Protologue: Guatemala. Quezaltenango, Coll No. 115 cum Grimmia Bernoullii associata [Bernoulli & Cario] (PC). 

Plants small in dense or loose cushions or tufts, brown below, yellowish green to olive‑green above, often hoary due to long hair‑points. Stems erect, fastigiate branched, 5–20 mm high, central strand present; rhizoids sparse. Leaves stiffly erect, imbricate, or erect‑patent when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 2.5–3 mm long, lanceolate, keeled, gradually acuminate, hair‑point long, short, or absent, weakly denticulate; margins multistratose, recurved on one side below, otherwise plane, entire; costa percurrent, with 2–4 guide cells, reniform; laminae bistratose in upper 1/2 to 1/3, cells smooth, upper cells 8–10 x 6 μm, irregularly quadrate to short‑rectangular or transversely rectangular, incrassate, with straight or sinuose walls, basal cells near costa 30–40 x 8 μm, elongate‑rectangular, strongly sinuose, basal marginal cells 8–20 x 12 μm, quadrate to rectangular, with thick transverse walls and thin longitudinal walls. Autoicous. Seta straight, 3–4 mm long, twisted when dry. Capsules emergent to exserted, 1.2–2 mm long, ovate, oblong, or cylindrical, erect, smooth; stomata superficial in neck; opercula erect‑ or oblique‑rostrate, 0.5–1.5 mm long; peristome teeth 16, narrowly triangular, red, densely papillose, entire or irregularly cleft into 2–3 parts, 200 μm long. Spores 8–10 μm, smooth to finely papillose. Calyptrae yellow, mitrate, 1.5 mm long.

Grimmia trichophylla Grev., Fl. Edin. 235. 1824.

Protologue: Scotland. Edinburgh, s. coll.; Arthur's Seat and coast of Fife, Arnott; Lanark Road, Edinburgh, s. coll.; walls between Colinton and the Pentland Hills, s. coll. Lectotype (Geissler & Maier 1995). [Great Britain] near Edinburgh. 1821 (E). 

Plants small to large in dense or loose cushions or tufts, brown below, yellowish green to olive‑green, often hoary due to long hair‑points. Stems erect, fastigiate branched, 5–30 mm high, central strand present; rhizoids sparse. Leaves erect to erect‑patent, somewhat twisted when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 2–2.5 mm long, linear‑lanceolate from a narrowly ovate‑lanceolate base, keeled, long-acuminate, hair‑point long, short or absent, entire or weakly denticulate; margins bistratose, occasionally unistratose, recurved on one or both sides, entire; costa percurrent, terete at back; laminae unistratose except at extremely apex or bistratose in scattered patches; cells smooth, upper cells 6–8 x 6 μm, irregularly quadrate to short‑rectangular or transversely rectangular, incrassate, with straight or sinuose walls, basal cells near costa 20–40 x 6–8 μm, elongate‑rectangular, strongly sinuose, basal marginal cells 8–20 x 12 μm, quadrate to rectangular, with thick transverse walls and thin longitudinal walls. Gemmae usually present, sessile on the dorsal side of the upper lamina. Dioicous. Setae cygneous or flexuose, 2–5 mm long, twisted when dry, yellow. Capsules exserted, 1.5–2 mm long, oblong, horizontal to pendent, furrowed; stomata superficial in neck; opercula erect‑ or oblique‑rostrate, 0.5–1 mm long; peristome teeth 16, narrowly triangular, red, densely papillose, entire or irregularly cleft into 2–3 parts, 200–300 μm long. Spores 10–15 μm, papillose. Calyptrae yellow, mitrate, 1.5 mm long.

Schistidium apocarpum (Hedw.) Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G., Bryol. Eur. 3: 99. 1845.

Grimmia apocarpa Hedw., Sp. Musc. Frond. 76. 1801. Protologue: Germany. Lipsiae ad piscinam Lindenthalensem, Gothanam versus Ileburgum, Dresdae ad rivulum Weiseriz ubertim. 

Grimmia gracilis Schleich., Cat. Plant Helv. (Ed. 2) 29. 1807, nom. nud. Grimmia gracilis Schleich. ex Schwaegr., Sp. Musc. Frond. 1(1): 98.1811, hom. illeg. Grimmia apocarpa γ gracilis Web. & Mohr ex Nees et al., Bryol. Germ. 96. 1827. Schistidium apocarpum var. gracile (Web. & Mohr ex Nees et al.) Bruch & Schimp. in B.S.G., Bryol Eur. 3: 99 (fasc. 257 1845. Schistidium gracile (Web. & Mohr ex Nees et al.) Schleich. ex Limp., Laubm. Deutschl. 705. 1889. Lectotype (Deguchi 1978, see Bremer 1980, Blom 1996): Switzerland, Schleicher Plantae Cryptogamicae Helveticae Century 3, n° 14 (G). 

Plants medium-sized, blackish green to red‑brown, 1.5–4 cm high. Leaves 1.6–1.8 mm long, erect to erect‑imbricate when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, ovate‑lanceolate, keeled in cross‑section; apices muticous or ending in short, hyaline, spinulose hair-points; margins entire or repand‑denticulate above, narrowly recurved throughout, bistratose;; costa percurrent, prominent at back, smooth or coarsely papillose above, in cross‑section costal cells more or less homogeneous; upper cells 8–12 μm, at times bistratose, irregularly rounded‑quadrate, straight‑walled or sinuose, medium leaf cells 8–14 μm long, oblong, sinuose, basal cells near costa not differentiated, 12–34 μm long, rectangular, straight‑walled or sinuose. Autoicous. Perichaetial leaves to 3 mm long. Setae 0.5 mm long, straight. Capsules 1 mm long, immersed, erect, ovoid‑ellipsoid to oblong, wide‑mouthed, smooth or weakly furrowed when dry; opercula obliquely short‑rostrate, 0.6–0.7 mm long; peristome teeth lanceolate, entire, papillose. Spores 8–10 μm, lightly papillose to smooth. Calyptrae mitrate or cucullate, 0.5 mm long.

Plants medium-sized, 4–7 cm long, yellow green to pale green. Stolons creeping; leaves ap-pressed to spreading, oblong-triangular, 0.4–0.6 mm long, costae strong and double, dark red across the leaf insertions; rhizoids smooth, reddish brown, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf inser-tions, densely present on stolons, and at the base of primary stems. Stems erect to pendent, regularly pinnately to bipinnately branched, evenly foliate; stems in cross section with unistratose hyalodermis, subsclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, very thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, firm- to thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia narrowly foliose to fila-mentous. Stem and branch leaves erect-incurved or catenulate when dry, erect-spreading when wet. Stem leaves ovate to ovate-triangular, 0.8–1.2 mm long, acute to rounded-acute, narrowly decurrent; margins minutely serrulate at apex, or subentire throughout, plane above, recurved at base; costae strong, double, reaching 0.8–0.9 the leaf length, not crested or crest low (one cell high) and confined to the uppermost part, irregularly toothed in upper 1/2, stoutly toothed at apex; cells smooth or in-conspicuously prorate, oval to oblong, 4–15 µm long, thick-walled, occasionally porose; alar cells not or weakly differentiated, cells across the insertions reddish, porose. Branch leaves ovate to broadly ovate, acute or obtuse and mucronate at the apex, 0.5–1.0 mm long, narrowly decurrent; margins minutely serrulate at apex, or subentire throughout, plane above, reflexed at base; costae strong, dou-ble, reaching 0.8–0.95 the leaf length, not crested or crest low (1–3 cells high), confined to the uppermost part, irregularly toothed in upper 1/2, stoutly toothed at apex; cells smooth or inconspicu-ously prorate, oval to oblong, 4–18 µm long, thick-walled, occasionally porose; alar cells not or weakly differentiated, cells across the insertions reddish, porose. Asexual propagula occasionally present on upper, dorsal surface of the costae. Dioicous. Perichaetia and perigonia on short lateral branches on stems and branches; perigonial leaves ovate-lanceolate, 0.8–1.0 mm long, perichaetial leaves lanceolate, 1.0–1.2 mm long, in both costae strong and double. Setae short, flexuose, 1.5–2.0 mm, smooth. Capsules exserted, erect, oblong-cylindric,

Campylopus oerstedianus (C. Müll.) Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 81. 1869. Dicranum oerstedianum C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 9: 259. 1851. Type. Costa Rica, Volcán de Irazu, Oersted (NY).

 

Plants small, densely tufted, yellowish green above, brownish below; stems densely red-tomentose below, to 1.0 cm high. Leaves erect-appressed, subtubulose above, occasionally tightly appressed on stems and comal tufted above, 2–4 mm long, oblong-lanceolate and gradually narrowed to a moderately long subula, usually ending in a short, hyaline tip, the perichaetial leaves ending in a long serrate awn; margins above the shoulders narrowly incurved, sharply serrulate; costa percurrent to short-excurrent (perichaetial leaves excurrent as an awn), in cross section with ventral hyalocysts equal to or smaller than the guide cells, dorsal stereid band well-developed; upper cells irregularly trapezoidal to short-rhomboidal, obliquely oriented, basal cells enlarged, long-rectangular becoming abruptly short-rectangular to nearly quadrate, typically firm-walled, occasionally thin-walled; alar cells weakly differentiated, reddish or hyaline in slightly auriculate groups. Sporophyte unknown.

Bryum leptocladon Sull., Proc. Amer. Acad. Arts 5: 282. 1861. 

Anomobryum leptocladon (Sull.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 563. 1903. Protologue: Cuba. Moist places on the ground, Wright 62. 

Plants small, green to yellow‑green in loose tufts to 3 mm high; rhizoids sparse at base. Leaves 0.5–0.9 mm long, imbricate, firm not contorted when dry, erect when wet, oblong‑ovate; apices short‑acuminate; margins plane throughout, not or indistinctly bordered, entire; costae percurrent to short‑excurrent; upper cells rhomboidal to rhomboidal‑hexagonal, thin‑walled, to 60 μm long, basal cells rectangular, firm‑walled, to 70 μm long. Dioicous. Setae 5–10 mm long, orange‑brown to red. Capsules 1–2 mm long, orange‑brown, suberect to horizontal, oblong‑pyriform, abruptly contacted to a slender neck nearly as long as the capsule; opercula 0.5 mm long, conic apiculate; annuli compound; exostome teeth yellow, densely papillose, endostome hyaline, lightly papillose, basal membrane to ½ of exostome teeth length, segments well-developed, narrowly perforate, cilia short, irregular, nodose, frequently rudimentary. Spores 14–18 μm, nearly smooth. Calyptra not seen.

Plants small and slender to medium-sized, in green to yellow green, glossy, lax to dense, silky mats, at times pendent. Primary stems creeping to 10 cm long with erect to imbricate, distantly spaced leaves; stems in cross section with sclerodermis of 1–2 rows of small, reddish yellow, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellowish to hyaline, thin-walled, central strand small; paraphyllia ab-sent; pseudoparaphyllia filamentous to subfoliose; rhizoids red brown, roughened, irregularly branched from small clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions; leaves erect to imbricate, dis-tantly spaced, 1.0–2.0 mm long. Secondary stems irregularly spaced, erect or pendent, 1–2 cm long, not branched but branch primordia present, often becoming flagellate, or transformed to stoloniferous stems, more or less complanate-foliate; leaves closely spaced, erect-spreading to wide-spreading, 1.6–4.0 mm long, linear to slenderly long-lanceolate, plicate, long-acuminate to hair-pointed, con-cave, subauriculate at base, not decurrent; margins serrate to serrulate throughout, with prominent, wide-spreading teeth at base, plane to narrowly recurved below; costae absent; cells linear, to 100 # 4 µm at base, smooth, thick-walled, conspicuously porose; alar cells weakly developed, of 2–5 short-rectangular to subquadrate, porose cells. Asexual reproduction by deciduous flagellate branches with microphyllous leaves and brown, papillose, uniseriate, septate propagula either arising from rhizoidal initials at the abaxial side of the leaf insertions or clustered around branch primordia. Dioicous. Sporophytes unknown from Central America, not seen, description from Britton (1913) and Buck (1998). Setae elongate, straight or flexuose, smooth, red, 15–25 mm long. Capsules erect, ovoid-cylindrical, 2–3 mm long; exothecial cells oblate below the mouth, short-rectangular below, not col-lenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula obliquely long-rostrate, 1 mm long; annuli rudimentary, of 2–3 rows of firm-walled cells; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth brown, narrowly triangular, papillose, weakly trabeculate; endostome paler, papillose, nearly as long as the exostome, basal mem-branes short, segments narrow, keeled, not or scarcely perforate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores 5–16 µm, round, lightly papillose. Calyptrae cucullate, naked, smooth or slightly roughened above, 2–3 mm long.

Plants medium-sized, in green or yellow green mats. Primary stems creeping, irregularly branched;
rhizoids from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions, red, smooth, unbranched or rarely irregularly
branched. Secondary stems horizontal or erect and loosely spreading, to 10 cm long, irregularly
branched; cross section with sclerodermis of 3–6 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells,
cortical cells enlarged, yellow to hyaline, very thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent;
pseudoparaphyllia filamentous or subfoliose and with scale leaves. Secondary stem and branch leaves
ovate-lanceolate, 1.2–2.4 mm long, imbricate to loosely imbricate, at times wrinkled when dry,
spreading when wet, gradually acuminate, decurrent; margins revolute in lower 3/4 or less, serrate to
denticulate above; costae strong, 0.7–0.8 the leaf length; cells smooth and thick-walled, cells in apex
fusiform, upper cells narrowly elliptic, 13–26 μm long, median cells elliptic, 10–20 μm long; basal
cells near costa in lower 1/6 of leaf elongate to linear, to 40 μm long; alar cells short-rectangular, subquadrate,
or oblate, 6–16 μm. Autoicous. Perichaetia and perigonia lateral. Perigonial leaves ovate,
ecostate; perichaetial leaves oblong, inner ones abruptly narrowed to a long, smooth or lightly roughened
awn equal to or somewhat shorter than the leaf lamina, costae discontinuous, stoutly filling the
apex, absent at base. Setae short, 0.1–0.2 μm long, cells quadrate. Capsules immersed, ellipsoid,
1.0–1.5 mm long, smooth, light brown, narrowed at the mouth, abruptly rounded-indented to the
setae; exothecial cells small, red, in 2–3 rows below the mouth, irregularly short-rectangular below;
stomata not seen; opercula conic-rostrate, smooth, to 0.5 mm long; annuli compound; peristome
diplolepideous, inserted within the mouth; exostome teeth narrowly triangular to linear, whitish yellow,
dorsal (outer) surface smooth below, papillose above, to 0.40 mm long; endostome segments linear,
papillose, shorter than the exostome, cilia absent, basal membranes very low. Spores massive,
spherical or irregularly oblong, lightly papillose, 40–60 μm. Spores endosporically germinated within
the capsule. Calyptrae mitrate, smooth, 0.4–0.6 mm long.

Plants small to medium-sized, 0.5–3.5 cm long, light green to yellowish green. Stems erect to ascending, sparsely and irregularly branched, complanate-foliate, red brown below, light green above; stems in cross section with moderately enlarged epidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand weak; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia subfoliose; axillary hairs 3–4 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, upper cells short and bulging, all cells hyaline; rhizoids densely felting at base of stems, smooth, reddish brown, from scattered initials on stems and around branch primor-dia, intricately pinnately branched. Leaves weakly dimorphic: lateral leaves wide-spreading, asym-metric, oblong-ovate, 2–3 mm long; dorsal leaves erect, more or less symmetric, oblong-ovate, 1.5–2.0 mm long. Leaves abruptly short-acuminate, not decurrent; margins plane, bordered by 1–3 rows of narrow, elongate, firm-walled cells, serrate above, entire to subentire below; costae short and double, greenish yellow, in cross section cells enlarged, firm-walled; upper cells hexagonal to long-hexagonal, smooth, thin-walled, 52–96 X 16–32 µm long; basal cells long-rectangular, 60–160 µm long; alar cells not differentiated, occasionally with 1–3 subquadrate cells. Asexual propagula absent. Autoicous. Setae elongate, curved above, 2–4 mm long, spinose below, setaceous above with 1–8-celled hairs. Capsules exserted, horizontal to pendent, ovoid to subglobose, constricted at the neck, symmetric, 1 mm long; exothecial cells enlarged, rounded to subquadrate at mouth, lower cells strongly collenchymatous; stomata on neck; opercula conic-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli rudimen-tary; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth reddish yellow, narrowly triangular, dorsal surface cross-striate, strongly furrowed, trabeculae projecting laterally, median line faint; endostome yellow, lightly papillose, basal membranes high, segments keeled and perforate, cilia rudimentary or absent. Spores rounded, 10–14 µm, smooth to lightly papillose. Calyptrae mitrate, densely ciliate-fringed at base, hairy above, 1 mm long.

Plants medium-sized, 1.0–3.5 cm long, glossy, yellowish green. Stems erect, sparsely and irreg-ularly branched, evenly foliate, dark red; stems in cross section with hyalodermis of enlarged, reddish cells, subepidermis of 1–3 rows of small, thick-walled, red cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, cen-tral strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2 cells long, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong-elongate, hyaline; rhizoids at base of stems, around branch primordia, and at times along the stems, smooth, reddish brown, from initials abaxial to the leaf insertions and from scattered initials, at times pinnately branched. Leaves isophyllous, laxly erect-imbricate, somewhat flexuose when dry, erect-spreading when wet, narrowly ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 2.5–3.0 mm long, 0.5–0.9 mm wide at base, deeply keeled in lower 1/2, acute to somewhat acuminate, decurrent; margins narrowly recurved, bordered by elongate, thick-walled cells, 8–11 cells wide below, entire throughout, rarely minutely denticulate near the apices; costae single, strong, often flexuose, ending 3/4 the leaf length, in cross section cells homogeneously thick-walled; upper cells rounded-rhomboidal to elongate-fusiform, 18–35 X 7–10 µm, smooth, firm-walled, median cells similar but somewhat larger; basal cells rounded-rectangular, firm-walled, 18–40 X 7–12 µm, juxtacostal cells linear, similar to the border cells, forming a distinct band along the costa from the base into the apex, cells across the insertions enlarged, irregularly rectangular to subquadrate, reddish brown, porose. Asexual structures not seen. Autoicous. Perichaetia lateral on stems. Setae elongate, 10–12 mm long, red, scabrose above, smooth below. Capsules erect, ovoid to oblong, more or less constricted at the neck, symmetric, 1.0–1.5 mm long; exothecial cells at the mouth oblate in 3–4 rows, lower cells larger, oblate, rounded-quadrate, or subrectangular, collenchy-matous; stomata on neck; operculum and annulus not seen; peristome diplolepideous; exostome teeth reddish yellow at base, recurved when wet, incurved when dry, narrowly triangular, both surfaces pa-pillose throughout, dorsal trabeculae and median line thick, ventral trabeculae faint; endostome yel-lowish white, spiculose-papillo<

Plants small to medium-sized, 2–6 cm long, glossy, dark green, green, yellowish green, or red-dish, in lax tufts. Primary stems prostrate and creeping. Secondary stems erect-ascending, or pendent, sparsely and irregularly branched, branches at times attenuate-foliate, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming reddish with age, loosely or strongly complanate-foliate; stems in cross section with well-developed hyalodermis, 1–3 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells en-larged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphylliaabsent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on primary stems and at base of secondary stems, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves distantly or closely spaced, weakly dimorphic, loosely or strongly flattened. Lateral leaves spreading, flat or sometimes crispate when dry, falcate-spreading when wet, oblong to oblong-lanceolate, 2–4 mm long, asym-metric, falcate to sigmoid, short-acute to short-acuminate; margins serrate to serrulate, at times suben-tire above, plane, often broadly infolded on one side at base, elimbate or obscurely bordered by a single row of elongate cells; costae double, slender, 1/4–1/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, upper cells narrowly or broadly linear-fusiform, 80–120 X 10–15 µm, thin-walled, not porose, becoming oblong-rectangular to oblong-fusiform below; alar cells not differentiated. Dorsal leaves erect to appressed, ovate to oblong-lanceolate, symmetric, 2–3 mm long. Asexual reproduction by deciduous leaves or fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate propag-ula from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae. Autoicous or synoicous. Setae elongate, 4–10 mm long, red to reddish orange, papillose throughout. Capsules erect to suberect,

Plants medium-sized to robust, 4–9 cm long, green, dark green, or yellowish brown, in lax or dense tufts. Stems prostrate and creeping, irregularly and sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming darker with age; stems in cross section with a moderate-sized 1–3-stratose hyalodermis, 1–2 layers of smaller, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on stems when in contact with substrate, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves crowded to somewhat distant, crispate when dry. Lateral leaves wide-spreading, oblong-lanceolate or oblong-lingulate, 3.5–5.0 mm long, asymmetric, obtuse or rounded, apiculate or short-acuminate; margins serrulate to serrate above, entire below, limbate, by 2–4 rows of elongate cells, plane above, usually broadly infolded on one side at base; costae double, thin, ending 2/3–3/4 the leaf length, diverging throughout, in lateral leaves one fork often approaching the margins, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, median cells broadly hexagonal, 100–50 X 44–15 µm, thin-walled, lower cells oblong to rec-tangular; alar cells not differentiated. Dorsal leaves erect when wet, ovate to ovate-lanceolate, 3–4 mm long, symmetric, short-acuminate, margins serrulate to serrate above, entire below, limbate, by 2–4 rows of elongate cells, plane. Asexual propagula fusiform, multicellular, uniseriate, arising from clus-ters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae. Dioicous. Sporophytes not known from Central America or seen, description from Churchill (1988). Setae short, 3.5 mm long, papillose throughout. Capsules 1.0 mm long. Calyptrae mitrate, 1.5 mm long, short-campanulate, hairy.

Plants small, medium-sized, or robust, 2–8 cm long, green, dark green, or yellowish brown, in lax or dense tufts. Stems prostrate and creeping, irregularly and sparsely branched, hyaline to yellowish when young, becoming darker with age; stems in cross section with a moderate-sized hyalodermis, 1–2 layers of small, thick-walled subepidermal cells, cortical cells enlarged, thin-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-celled, basal cell short-rectangular, reddish brown, upper cell oblong, hyaline; rhizoids on stems when in contact with sub-strate, from clusters of initials abaxial to the leaf insertions at base of costae, smooth, reddish brown, not or sparsely and irregularly branched. Leaves crowded to somewhat distant, crispate to tortuose when dry. Lateral leaves wide-spreading, obovate, ovate-oblong, or oblong, 2–3 mm long, asymmet-ric or symmetric, obtuse or rounded, apiculate or short-acuminate; margins serrulate to serrate above, entire below, limbate, by 2–5 rows of elongate cells, plane above, at times broadly infolded on one side at base; costae double, thin, ending 1/3–2/3 the leaf length, diverging throughout, one fork often approaching the margins, smooth at back, not projecting at the apices; cells smooth, median cells broadly hexagonal to rhomboidal, 40–60 X 25–35 µm, thin-walled, lower cells rectangular; alar cells not differentiated. Dorsal leaves erect when wet, ovate, oblong-ovate, or suborbicular, 2 mm long, symmetric, short-acuminate; margins serrulate to serrate above, entire below, limbate, by 2–5 rows of elongate cells, plane. Asexual propagula not seen. Dioicous. Setae elongate, 10–12 mm long, red to reddish orange, densely papillose throughout. Capsules erect, ovoid to oblong-cylindrical, 1.0–1.5 mm long, neck weakly developed; exothecial cells reddish, oblate in 4–6 rows at mouth, those below long-rectangular, evenly firm- to thick-walled, not collenchymatous; stomata rudimentary, 3–6-celled, on neck; opercula high-conic, 0.7–1.0 mm long; annuli of 7–12 rows of thin-walled cells, separating from capsule along dehiscent zone at base and persistent on the operculum; peristome diplolepideous, exostome very narrowly triangular, median furrow absent, dorsal (outer) surface broad, whitish yel-low, lightly papillose throughout, trabeculae thin, median lines faint,

Ditrichum difficile (Duby) Fleisch., Musci Fl. Buitenzorg 1:300. 1904. Trichostomum difficile Duby in Moritzi, Syst. Verz. 134. 1846. Type. Java, Zollinger 411.

Leptotrichum rufescens Hampe, Linnaea 31: 521. 1862. Ditrichum rufescens (Hampe) Hampe, Flora 50: 182. 1867. Type. Colombia, Bogotá, Lindig 2137 (NY), syn. nov.

Plants slender, silky, densely tufted, yellowish green; stems 1–2 cm high, sparsely to densely tomentose. Leaves erect, flexuous, 2–3 mm long, lanceolate-subulate, from a narrow subclasping base; margins erect to narrowly incurved, entire or faintly serrulate; costa percurrent to shortly excurrent with a few blunt teeth at the apex; cells firm-walled to incrassate, basal cells linear, 32–57 µm long, upper cells short-rectangular, 11–22 µm long. Autoicous. Setae 12–20 mm long, yellow becoming reddish with age; capsules erect to inclined, cylindric, 2.0 mm long; opercula conic-rostrate, 1 mm long, red; peristome teeth 0.5–0.6 mm long, divided nearly to the base into filiform, yellow or red, densely papillose, filiform divisions. Spores nearly smooth, 15 µm.

Entosthodon attenuatus (Dicks.) Bryhn, Kongel. Norske Vidensk. Selsk. Skr. (Trondheim) 1908(8): 25. 1908.

Bryum attenuatum Dicks., Fasc. Pl. Crypt. Brit. 4: 8. 1801. Funaria attenuata (Dicks.) Lindb., Not. Sällsk. Fauna Fl. Fenn. Förh.11: 633. 1870. Protologue: Scotland. Habitat in paludibus montosis Scotiae. 

Plants yellow‑green, usually gregarious in lax to dense tufts. Stems erect, 2–5 mm tall, sparsely branching by subperigonial innovations, usually naked at very base (except for rhizoids), the leaves more or less clustered toward stem apices, with a single‑layered sclerodermis over 1–2 rows of small reddish thick‑walled cells, subtended by abruptly larger thin‑walled cells, central strand well developed. Leaves erect‑spreading when dry, slightly contorted, wide‑spreading when moist, oblanceolate to oblong‑obovate, cuspidate, 1–2 mm long, concave, not decurrent; margins bluntly serrulate above, subentire below, plane; costa subpercurrent; upper cells subquadrate to hexagonal to short‑rectangular, thin‑walled, smooth, (34–)51–85 x 20–42 μm, differentiated at the margins with 1–2(–3) rows of narrow, elongate, yellowish cells, more or less confluent in the apex, disappearing toward the insertion, basal cells long‑rectangular, 100–240 x 34–57 μm, sometimes more or less inflated, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae orange to reddish brown, straight to slightly flexuose, weakly hygroscopic, smooth, 0.8–1.4 cm long. Capsules reddish brown, narrowly oblong‑pyriform, neck 1/2 the capsule length, erect to inclined, somewhat asymmetric from a bend in the neck, somewhat constricted below the mouth when dry, wrinkled to sulcate in the neck, smooth above, 2–2.8 mm long; stomata phaneroporous, numerous in neck; opercula plano‑convex, cells subquadrate, thick‑walled, in more or less regular, straight vertical rows; annuli simple; peristome double, inserted well below the mouth, exostome teeth red‑brown, straight, 150 x 40 μm, acute or irregular at apex, papillose to papillose‑striate, endostome rudimentary, hyaline and weakly papillose, basal membrane short, segments short and blunt, projecting just above the capsule mouth, segments wider than teeth. Spores more or less angular, (22–)28–34 μm in diameter, very finely but densely roughened, without trilete scars. Calyptrae cucullate‑rostrate, 2–2.5 mm long, naked, smooth.

Entosthodon jamesonii (Tayl.) Mitt., Hooker's J. Bot. Kew Gard. Misc. 3: 354. 1851. 

Physcomitrium jamesonii Tayl., London J. Bot. 6: 329. 1847. Amphoritheca jamesonii (Tayl.) Hampe, Ann. Sci. Nat. Bot. sér. 5, 3: 340. 1865, not Funaria jamesonii Tayl., London J. Bot. 7: 189. 1848 [= Entosthodon laevis (Mitt.) Fife]. Protologue: Ecuador. On Pichincha, Prof. W. Jameson, Nov. 1846.

Gymnostomum acidotum Tayl., London J. Bot. 7: 279. 1848. Entosthodon acidotus (Tayl.) C. Müll., Syn. Musc. Frond. 2: 547. 1851. Amphoritheca acidota (Tayl.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 219. 1874. Funaria acidota (Tayl.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 523. 1903. Protologue: Ecuador. On Pichincha; near the limits of perpetual snow. Prof. W. Jameson. 5th July 1847. 

Plants yellow‑ to brownish green, usually gregarious in lax to dense tufts. Stems erect, 3–8(–20) mm tall, branching by subperigonial innovations, more or less naked at very base (except for rhizoids), the leaves otherwise evenly placed, not conspicuously clustered toward stem apices, with a single‑layered sclerodermis, central strand well-developed. Leaves erect when dry, little altered when moist, lanceolate‑triangular to ovate‑lanceolate, acute to acuminate, 0.8–1.5 mm long, concave or subtubulose, not decurrent; margins subentire throughout, plane to narrowly incurved above, plane below; costa subpercurrent; upper cells oblong to short‑rectangular, thin‑ to firm‑walled, smooth, (25–)55–90 x (12–)18–21 μm, not differentiated at the margins or toward the insertion, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae reddish brown, straight to slightly flexuose, twisted to the right throughout, weakly hygroscopic, smooth, 1.2–2 cm long. Capsules reddish brown, narrowly to broadly oblong‑pyriform with the neck about 1/2 the capsule length, erect, symmetric, somewhat constricted below the mouth when dry, sulcate in the neck, smooth above, (1–)1.5–2(–2.5) mm long; exothecial cells irregularly shaped, mostly fusiform‑rectangular, becoming oblate and thick‑walled in 3–6 rows at the mouth; stomata phaneroporous; opercula plano‑convex, with a slightly paler margin, cells subquadrate to oblate, thick‑walled, in regular, straight vertical rows; annuli simple; peristome absent or reduced to irregular membrane not or scarcely projecting above mouth. Spores subspherical to more or less reniform, often appearing angular, 28–38 μm in diameter, coarsely verrucate‑bullate, with conspicuous trilete scars. Calyptrae cucullate‑rostrate, 2–2.5 mm long, naked, smooth.

Entosthodon obtusifolius Hook. f. in Hook., Icon. Pl. 3: 245A. 1840.

Physcomitrium obtusifolium (Hook. f.) C. Müll., Linnaea 18: 697. 1844 [1845]. Amphoritheca obtusifolia (Hook. f.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 220. 1874. Funaria obtusifolia (Hook. f.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 524. 1903, hom. illeg., not Weinm., Bull. Soc. Imp. Naturalistes Moucou 18(2): 438. 1845 [= Meesia uliginosa Hedw.]. Funaria hookeriana Thér., Rev. Bryol. Lichénol. 4: 177. 1931 [1932]. New name for Funaria obtusifolia (Hook. f.) Broth. Protologue: Peru. Moist places, Lomas of Amancaes, near Lima, Peru. Mathews (n. 958).

Entosthodon acutifolius Hampe ex C. Müll., Bot. Zeitung (Berlin) 17: 198. 1859.  Funaria acutifolia (C. Müll.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 524. 1903. Protologue: Venezuela. Venezuela, Mt. Galipano, 6000 pedes altus: A. Trumpff.

Entosthodon longicollis Mitt., J. Linn. Soc., Bot. 12: 244. 1869. Amphoritheca longicollis (Mitt.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 220. 1874. Protologue. Ecuador. Andes Quitenses, Baños (6000 ped.), Spruce, n. 448 (NY).

Entosthodon longisetus Schimp. ex Besch., Mém. Soc. Sci. Nat. Cherbourg 16: 192. 1872. Amphoritheca longiseta (Besch.) Jaeg., Ber. Thätigk. St. Gallischen Naturwiss. Ges. 1872–73: 221. 1874. Funaria longiseta (Besch.) Broth., Nat. Pflanzenfam. 1(3): 523. 1903. Protologue: Mexico. San Cristobal (F. Müller). (NY). 

Plants yellow‑ to brownish green, usually gregarious in lax to dense tufts. Stems erect, 2–8 mm tall, simple or with a single subperigonial innovation, usually more or less naked at very base (except for rhizoids), the leaves usually clustered toward stem apices, with a single‑layered sclerodermis, central strand well-developed. Leaves erect‑spreading when dry, slightly contorted, little altered when moist, oblong‑ovate to obovate, acute to obtuse, 1–2.5 mm long, concave, not decurrent; margins subentire throughout, plane; costa subpercurrent; upper cells subquadrate to hexagonal to short‑rectangular, thin‑walled, smooth, (37–)43–85 x 17–25(–42) μm, not differentiated at the margins, toward the insertion becoming long‑rectangular, (85–)114–185(–243) x 37–55 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Autoicous. Setae reddish brown, straight to slightly flexuose, twisted to the right throughout, weakly hygroscopic, smooth, (0.7–)1–2 cm long. Capsules reddish brown, narrowly oblong‑pyriform with the neck about ½ or more the capsule length, erect, symmetric, somewhat constricted below the mouth when dry, wrinkled to sulcate in the neck, smooth above, 1.5–2 mm long; exothecial cells fusiform‑ rectangular to long‑hexagonal, 55–85 x 11–17(–23) μm, thin‑walled, shorter in the neck, becoming oblate and thick‑walled in 2–4(–8) rows at the mouth; stomata phaneroporous; opercula plano‑convex, with a slightly paler margin, cells subquadrate to oblate, thick‑walled, in regular, straight vertical rows; annuli simple; peristome single, exostomial, inserted well below the mouth, teeth straight, sometimes united in pairs by appendiculae, 120–170 x 30–40 μm, acute or irregular at apex, irregularly striate throughout. Spores appearing angular, 28–38 μm in diameter, very finely but densely roughened, with inconspicuous trilete scars. Calyptrae cucullate‑rostrate, 2–2.5 mm long, naked, smooth.

Plants medium-sized to robust, in green to yellow green, dense, hoary, rigid tufts or mats. Primary
stems short, creeping, irregularly branched; leaves well spaced, ovate, abruptly acuminate, erect
below, recurved above, apex not hyaline, 0.7–1.0 mm long; rhizoids red brown, in sparse clusters at
abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or rarely branched. Secondary stems erect and loosely spreading,
2–6 cm long, irregularly branched, rarely with lateral stolons; cross section with sclerodermis of 2–4
rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow, thick-walled, central
strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Secondary stem and branch leaves erectappressed,
apices at times wide-spreading or secund when dry, erect-spreading to spreading when
wet, not plicate, oblong-ovate, 2.0–2.5 mm long, acute to acuminate, apices ending in long, broad,
hyaline, pluripapillose acumina, sparsely spinose-serrate at the apices, shortly decurrent; margins
plane or narrowly recurved at base, plane at midleaf, narrowly incurved below apex; costa absent;
upper cells short-rectangular to subquadrate, 8–16 x 5–7 μm, thick-walled, papillae 1–2(–3) on the
abaxial surface, stout, at times branched; basal median cells long-rectangular, 40–70 x 2.5–7 μm,
very thick-walled, porose, pluripapillose, hyaline to yellow orange at base; alar cells in numerous
rows at basal angles short-rectangular, quadrate, or oblate, very thick-walled, papillose, reddish
brown, at times yellow orange, 8–18 x 7–10 μm. Autoicous. Perigonia gemmate, sessile on secondary
stems and branches. Perichaetia terminal, perichaetial leaves erect, elongate, overtopping the capsules,
upper margins with long, hyaline, pluripapillose cilia. Setae short, to 1.0 mm long. Capsules
immersed, erect, cupulate, 1 mm long, smooth, red brown, wide-mouthed, tapering to a short wrinkled
neck; exothecial cells small, reddish brown, in 5–10 rows below the mouth, larger, oblate, irregularly
subquadrate below, neck cells small; cryptoporic stomata in neck; opercula plano-convex, at
times umbonate, 0.5 mm high; annuli rudimentary; peristome absent. Spores vermiculate-papillose,
irregularly shaped, 22–26 μm, brown. Calyptrae conic-cucullate, smooth, naked, 1 mm long.

Plants medium-sized to somewhat robust, in green, yellow green, or reddish yellow, loose or
dense tufts or mats. Primary stems short, creeping, irregularly branched; leaves well spaced, ovate,
abruptly long-acuminate, erect below, squarrose-recurved above, 0.6–0.8 mm long; rhizoids red
brown, in sparse clusters at abaxial side of leaf insertions, not or rarely branched. Secondary stems
erect and loosely spreading, 2–10 cm long, irregularly branched, often with lateral stolons; cross section
with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow,
thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia foliose. Secondary
stem and branch leaves erect-imbricate when dry, erect-spreading when wet, oblong-ovate, 1.5–2 mm
long, slenderly acuminate, apices concolorous or hyaline-tipped, shortly decurrent, not or weakly plicate,
lateral stolon leaves often long hair-pointed; apices sparsely serrate; margins narrowly recurved
to near the apex; costa absent; upper cells short-rectangular to subquadrate or oblate, 6–14 x 4–6 μm,
very thick-walled, sinuose, pluripapillose; basal median cells long-rectangular, 40–64 x 4 μm, very thickwalled,
porose, pluripapillose, yellow; alar cells in numerous rows at basal angles short-rectangular,
quadrate, or oblate, very thick-walled, smooth, dark reddish brown. Autoicous. Perigonia lateral. Perichaetia
terminal, perichaetial leaves erect, elongate, overtopping the capsules. Setae short, yellow becoming
red with age, 1 mm long. Capsules immersed, erect, broadly oblong to subglobose, 1.5–2.0 mm
long, strongly furrowed when wet or dry, red brown, slightly narrowed at the mouth, tapering to the seta;
exothecial cells small, reddish brown, in 5–10 rows below the mouth, larger, oblate, irregularly subquadrate
below, neck cells small; stomata in neck; opercula obliquely conic-rostrate, 0.5 mm long; annuli
rudimentary; peristome absent. Spores vermiculate-papillose, irregularly shaped, 20–24 μm,
brown. Calyptrae conic-mitrate, 2–3-lobed, reddish yellow, smooth, 1.5 mm long.

Macromitrium sharpii Crum ex Vitt, Bryologist 82: 4. 1979.

Protologue: Mexico. Durango: on Juniperus, 8850 ft. (2700 m) elev., 45 km W of El Salto. 30 Dec. 1944. Sharp 1859 (TENN).

Plants slender, yellow‑green. Stems strongly creeping, branches 1–3 cm long, densely red tomentose. Leaves moderately keeled, erect below, crispate to flexuose‑contorted above when dry, erect‑spreading when wet, 1.5–2.2 x 0.5 mm, lanceolate; apices apiculate, acute, or acuminate; margins entire or crenulate by bulging cell walls, recurved or plane below, plane above, enlarged basal teeth at leaf insertion absent; costae subpercurrent, percurrent or excurrent into an apiculus; upper interior cells 6–12 μm, rounded-hexagonal, bulging mammillose, upper marginal cells not differentiated, basal cells to 40 μm long, long‑rectangular, incrassate and porose, densely to moderately tuberculate. Setae 5–10 mm long, smooth. Plants small, green to golden or reddish brown, in dense tufts, 1–3 mm high. Stems simple or forked, reddish yellow, erect, epidermal cells short-rectangular, sclerodermis present to weakly present, central strand well-developed; rhizoids sparse. Leaves 0.3–0.8 mm long, oval, oblong or elliptic, spreading at base, rosulate, somewhat tumid, appressed-imbricate when dry, erect to erect-incurved when wet; apices obtuse, cucullate; lamina unistratose; margins entire, plane to erect; costa stout, subpercurrent, often spurred above, upper ventral superficial cells quadrate to short-rectangular, bulging, guide cells and single (dorsal) stereid band present, ventral surface layer enlarged, bulging near apex; cells smooth, upper cells round, quadrate, short-rectangular, triangular or oblate, 6–10 x 2–8 μm, thick-walled, basal cells quadrate, short or long-rectangular, hyaline, 10–20 x 6–10 μm, alar cells not differentiated. Plants small, dull, green above, brown below, in tufts, 4–10 mm high. Secondary stem and branch leaves differing only in size, leaves long, narrowly lanceolate from an ovate base, plicate, apices fragile, often detached, 7–10(–12) mm long, erect at base, erect to wide-spreading above when dry, wide-spreading to subsquarrose when wet, decurrent, narrowly acute to acuminate; margins plane, some-times narrowly recurved below, coarsely serrate above, teeth uni- or multicellular; costae single, sub-percurrent, at times wavy above, in cross section at base with two rows of guide cells, dorsal and ventral stereid cells in multiple rows; cells unipapillose, typically elongate and porose throughout, at times upper cells fusiform, 20–60 # 4–8 µm; alar cells usually elongate and porose, occasionally with a few scattered quadrate to oblate cells, 12–30 # 4–6 µm. Plants medium-sized, in glaucous green, greenish yellow, or reddish yellow mats. Primary stems
inconspicuous, creeping, sympodially branched, leaves reduced and distantly spaced; rhizoids rare,
densely clustered at base of sympodial branches, red, smooth, more or less unbranched. Secondary
stems prominent, prostrate or erect, irregularly branched from all sides of the stems; cross section
with sclerodermis of 2–5 rows of small, red brown, thick-walled cells, cortical cells enlarged, yellow,
thick-walled, central strand absent; paraphyllia absent; pseudoparaphyllia absent; axillary hairs 2-
celled, upper one oblong, lower one subquadrate, red. Secondary stem and branch leaves oblong to
broadly elliptic, often panduriform, 1–2 mm long, erect to erect-spreading when dry, erect-spreading
when wet, short to long apiculate, decurrent; margins narrowly recurved at base, broadly incurved
above, serrulate; costa absent; cells linear-flexuose, 40–60 x 6 μm, thick-walled, porose, densely
covered by a finely papillose reticulum; marginal cells longer, narrower, smooth, forming a distinct
border; cells at the insertions smooth, linear, strongly porose, yellow to red; alar cells extensively developed,
oblong to subquadrate, extremely thick-walled, porose, smooth. Dioicous. Perigonia gemmate,
lateral on secondary stems and branches, 1–2 mm long. Perichaetia terminal, 3 mm long; leaves
erect, elongate, cells elongate-flexuose, strongly porose, smooth to prorate from both ends, yellow

stomata deeply immersed on neck; operculum not seen; annulus not seen; peristome absent. Spores
tetrahedral, warty papillose on one side, with trilete scar on opposite side, 14–16 μm. Immature calyptrae
cucullate, reddish brown, smooth, 3–4 mm long.
